30f3d3f2-be9c-4877-aa64-69c887da4863.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples
30f3d3f2-be9c-4877-aa64-69c887da4863.description:
Aboriginal Peoples are the Traditional custodians of Australia and are represented by more than 250 language groups, each connected with a particular Country. Torres Strait Islander Peoples are represented by 5 major island groups and are connected with islands to the north of Australia’s Cape York which were annexed by Queensland in 1879. 

An Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person is someone who: 

  • is of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent 
  • identifies as an Aboriginal person and/or Torres Strait Islander person, and 
  • is accepted as such by the Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Community(ies) in which they live.

3a870154-5d78-4fc3-af2c-8113f41ed342.title: culture
3a870154-5d78-4fc3-af2c-8113f41ed342.description: The customs, habits, beliefs/spirituality, social organisation and ways of life that characterise different groups and communities. Cultural characteristics give a group or individual a sense of who they are and help them make sense of the world in which they live. Culture is a shared system but inherently diverse – there can be individual and group differences within cultures. Everyone has culture – it is a lens through which we see the world.

67122a51-b3f5-464a-bac8-d75cb8e0f86e.title: diversity
67122a51-b3f5-464a-bac8-d75cb8e0f86e.description: Differences that exist within a group, for example, age, sex, gender, gender expression, sexuality, ethnicity, ability/disability, body shape and composition, culture, religion/spirituality, learning differences, socioeconomic background, values and experiences.

4f988065-71ac-4c02-89d5-c9e6c8c0768f.title: language revival
4f988065-71ac-4c02-89d5-c9e6c8c0768f.description: The process and range of strategies for increasing knowledge and use of a language that is no longer spoken fluently across all generations in the context of language loss or language dispossession caused by colonisation. Aboriginal Languages and Torres Strait Islander Languages are being revived through community initiatives, linguistic research and school programs. ‘Language revival’ may be used as an overarching term that could also include ‘reclamation’, ‘revitalisation’, ‘renewal’ and ‘reawakening’.

68cb9d20-6052-4706-93bd-43cbefe9981b.title: signage
68cb9d20-6052-4706-93bd-43cbefe9981b.description: The use of words, graphic designs and/or symbols used to communicate a message, eg information signs, plaques, warning signs, road signs, signs that show direction.

c2193cf9-a042-45a3-bb21-1f01b7f86f6e.title: communication forms
c2193cf9-a042-45a3-bb21-1f01b7f86f6e.description: The ways people communicate and the communicative behaviours they use. Communication forms can be non-symbolic and/or symbolic. Non-symbolic forms include sounds, gestures, facial expressions and eye movements. Symbolic forms can be aided or non-aided. Aided forms of symbolic communication include objects, symbols, photographs and drawings. Aided forms can be digital. Non-aided forms of symbolic communication include formal gestures; speech; and signs, such as Key Word Sign.

5ca9676c-7efb-4e25-ab1a-04b8c8586bd2.title: accessibility
5ca9676c-7efb-4e25-ab1a-04b8c8586bd2.description: The extent to which a system, environment or object may be used irrespective of a user’s capabilities or abilities. For example, the use of assistive technologies (AT) to allow people with disability to use computer systems, or the use of icons in place of words to allow young children to use a system.

c3fb5105-ad4f-4a1e-9a9e-c852617d8ab1.title: intellectual property
c3fb5105-ad4f-4a1e-9a9e-c852617d8ab1.description:
Non-material assets such as forms of cultural expression that belong to a particular individual or community. Intellectual property rights refer to the rights that the law grants to individuals for the protection of creative, intellectual, scientific and industrial activity, such as inventions. 

See Indigenous cultural and intellectual property (ICIP), and copyright

f2caa95c-15c9-4596-a628-65159bdff2c6.title: Aboriginal Songline(s)
f2caa95c-15c9-4596-a628-65159bdff2c6.description: Texts that describe landscapes and directions of the tracks forged in lands, waters and skies by Creator Spirits during the Dreaming.

765611ae-67e2-43fa-8d2e-d1bb37f6e106.title: d/Deaf
765611ae-67e2-43fa-8d2e-d1bb37f6e106.description: When referring to deaf people who belong to a linguistic and cultural minority known as the Deaf community, the 'D' may be capitalised in reference to the individual, the group, or the culture in order to accord respect and deference, for example, the Deaf community. When referring simply to audiological status or when cultural affiliation is not known, as in the case of a person with a hearing loss in general, the lowercase 'd', as in 'deaf' is the more common usage.

25bc4c40-d17d-4686-b723-a7f032827e75.title: yarning circle
25bc4c40-d17d-4686-b723-a7f032827e75.description: Yarning circles are an important cultural practice for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples to learn within the collective group. Knowledge and information are shared in harmony and respect with all individuals.

4b808e71-8de7-49ee-937a-ae131d8fcedb.title: Aboriginal English
4b808e71-8de7-49ee-937a-ae131d8fcedb.description: A recognised dialect of English which is the first, or home language, of many Aboriginal people. It differs from other dialects of English, such as Standard Australian English, in systematic ways including sounds, grammar, words and their meanings, and language use. Aboriginal English is a powerful vehicle for the expression of Aboriginal identity. Aboriginal English is not a target language study option for NSW Aboriginal Languages syllabuses.

e2f9a304-ddc9-43f8-b104-29135dab4732.title: assistive technology (AT)
e2f9a304-ddc9-43f8-b104-29135dab4732.description: A device or system whose primary purpose is to maintain or improve an individual's functioning and independence to facilitate participation and enhance overall wellbeing. This includes technologies specifically designed to meet an individual's needs, eg eye gaze technology, as well as more general technologies that can be used by anyone, eg speech-to-text applications. Assistive technology can also be referred to as inclusive technology.

1d59c866-5720-4557-809b-6011fe3c8859.title: augmentative and alternative communication (AAC)
1d59c866-5720-4557-809b-6011fe3c8859.description:
An umbrella term that encompasses the communication methods used to supplement or replace speech or writing. AAC can be unaided, such as gestures, body language and sign language, or aided such as pictures, symbols, objects or speech generating devices.

See communication systems

a443b161-99de-4984-a128-3286e1d9cf8c.title: Country/Place
a443b161-99de-4984-a128-3286e1d9cf8c.description:
Country is used to describe a specific area of a nation or clan including physical, linguistic and spiritual features. Aboriginal communities’ cultural associations with their Country may include or relate to languages, cultural practices, knowledge, songs, stories, art, paths, landforms, flora, fauna and minerals. These cultural associations may include custodial relationships with particular landscapes such as land, sea, sky, rivers as well as the intangible places associated with the Dreaming(s). Custodial relationships are extremely important in determining who may have the capacity to authentically speak for their Country. 

Place is a space mapped out by physical or intangible boundaries that individuals or groups of Torres Strait Islander Peoples occupy and regard as their own. It is a space with varying degrees of spirituality.

609822c4-eade-4974-ac3f-88eb9006855e.title: custodians
609822c4-eade-4974-ac3f-88eb9006855e.description: In Aboriginal communities, an individual charged with maintaining and passing on particular elements of cultural significance, eg language, stories, songs, rituals and imagery.

0df4f33e-0075-431b-9e30-e1dcf8667ccb.title: Deaf
0df4f33e-0075-431b-9e30-e1dcf8667ccb.description: A cultural identity for people with hearing loss who share a common culture and who usually have a shared sign language.

9c5d8d3a-2cb8-4fbc-b9b3-873da95325de.title: disability
9c5d8d3a-2cb8-4fbc-b9b3-873da95325de.description:
An umbrella term for any or all of the following components: 

  • impairments: challenges in body function or structure
  • activity limitations: difficulties in executing activities
  • participation restrictions: challenges an individual may experience in involvement in life situations. (World Health Organization)

55c5b3f1-a4c5-443b-b00c-de047b03d98e.title: Dreaming
55c5b3f1-a4c5-443b-b00c-de047b03d98e.description: The Dreaming has different meanings for different Aboriginal groups. The Dreaming can be seen as the embodiment of Aboriginal creation which gives meaning to everything; the essence of Aboriginal beliefs about creation and spiritual and physical existence. It establishes the rules governing relationships between the people, the land and all things for Aboriginal Peoples. The Dreaming is linked to the past, the present and the future. Where appropriate, refer to Aboriginal names for the Dreaming.

d5dfb36e-072e-4aca-b2f9-6f284ba50f98.title: Elders
d5dfb36e-072e-4aca-b2f9-6f284ba50f98.description: The custodians of knowledge and lore. They are chosen and accepted by their own communities as people who have the permission to disclose cultural knowledge and beliefs. Recognised Elders are highly respected people within Aboriginal communities. Proper consultation with local Aboriginal communities will often direct schools to recognised Elders.

6b89c8fe-25c0-4e5c-bca0-9bc3bb633f0d.title: first language(s)
6b89c8fe-25c0-4e5c-bca0-9bc3bb633f0d.description: The first language(s) that a person learns to speak.

84bcafed-8c0e-4b92-a657-3f9ebf9abca1.title: Indigenous
84bcafed-8c0e-4b92-a657-3f9ebf9abca1.description:
An internationally recognised term for the first peoples of a land. In NSW the term Aboriginal person/Peoples is preferred.

See Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

d594fc47-7229-42f7-9f79-8cac41711b21.title: Indigenous cultural and intellectual property (ICIP)
d594fc47-7229-42f7-9f79-8cac41711b21.description:
Includes, but is not limited to, objects, sites, cultural knowledge, cultural expression and the arts, that have been transmitted or continue to be transmitted through generations as belonging to a particular Indigenous group or Indigenous people as a whole or their territory. 

See intellectual property

664a1694-d4ac-43a5-9c04-dab964482129.title: kinship
664a1694-d4ac-43a5-9c04-dab964482129.description: A key aspect of Aboriginal cultures and values. It includes the importance of all relationships and of being related to and belonging to the land.

3af61696-fac2-4b46-9265-5c38336c6634.title: language group
3af61696-fac2-4b46-9265-5c38336c6634.description: An Aboriginal community identified with a common language, both verbal and nonverbal, and with a particular territory. Used in preference to the term ‘tribe’.

1a7c334d-af48-4df1-95ae-9444cc417384.title: local Aboriginal community
1a7c334d-af48-4df1-95ae-9444cc417384.description:
A local Aboriginal community is constituted by those people who are Aboriginal and who reside in the near locality. Aboriginal communities will have a rich and diverse history that has been seriously affected by dispossession and relations, which sees families with spiritual connection to Country residing beside those who have been forced to move from other locations. The notion of locality is complex and multilayered: schools should seek advice from a range of people and/or organisations representing local interests. 

See community(ies)

4f8c39f9-a256-4ef6-8390-c6bd2bbb0c85.title: off-Country
4f8c39f9-a256-4ef6-8390-c6bd2bbb0c85.description:
Taking place away from Aboriginal land or Country of origin. 

See Country/Place

44dc6bff-7faf-4327-9c64-8b8308a72598.title: on-Country
44dc6bff-7faf-4327-9c64-8b8308a72598.description:
Taking place on Aboriginal land or Country of origin.

See Country/Place

d53d7a97-cf23-48af-89bc-39679d026157.title: protocols
d53d7a97-cf23-48af-89bc-39679d026157.description: The appropriate ways of behaving, communicating and showing respect for diversity of history and culture. This involves appreciation of the knowledge, standing and status of people within the local Aboriginal community and the school community. Protocols inevitably vary between communities, and between people within a community. In establishing a partnership between schools and Aboriginal communities, it is especially important that protocols are acknowledged and respected.

bbddc190-01b0-4f28-b8a2-8ece83b97685.title: sign
bbddc190-01b0-4f28-b8a2-8ece83b97685.description: Hand signs (or hand talk) used to supplement or replace oral language. Signs form part of nonverbal communication for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and may be used by people who are hearing, or d/Deaf or hard of hearing. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Sign Languages may be used in some areas. Some Sign Languages may be associated with sacred ceremonial practices.

e00cf5b4-3d52-4f2f-9116-60634685c663.title: Key Word Sign
e00cf5b4-3d52-4f2f-9116-60634685c663.description: A communication strategy that incorporates signing with speech. It is used to support language development for people with communication difficulties. Although Key Word Sign uses a simplified form of manual signing, it is different to Auslan, as it is not a signed language.

a3e700d1-e83e-427c-9278-f7a67eb7be2e.title: copyright
a3e700d1-e83e-427c-9278-f7a67eb7be2e.description: The protection provided to the creators of original works and makers of sound recordings and films, that offers a legal framework for the control and reproduction or transmission of their literary, dramatic, artistic or musical works.

795a52b0-9fcf-4b35-a4e0-e1fdb3505421.title: switch
795a52b0-9fcf-4b35-a4e0-e1fdb3505421.description:
A type of assistive technology that enables people with cognitive and/or physical disability to access a range of devices, including computers and communication devices. Switches can be activated by touch, or triggered without contact, such as through eye gaze, sound or blowing.

See assistive technology (AT)

04a1acd8-9e16-49ed-8066-1106b1e4e544.title: colonisation
04a1acd8-9e16-49ed-8066-1106b1e4e544.description: A process by which a different system of government is established by one nation over another group of Peoples. It involves the colonial power asserting and enforcing its sovereignty or right to govern according to its own laws rather than by laws of the colonised.

fc196476-a9de-4220-b8a5-5d133845eab2.title: Community(ies)
fc196476-a9de-4220-b8a5-5d133845eab2.description:
Community(ies) is about interrelatedness and is central to shared conceptions of belonging. Aboriginal Peoples may belong to more than one Community. Important elements of Community are identification with Country or location, family ties and shared experience.

See local Aboriginal community

58e550d9-f830-4e27-a111-1654c2762a81.title: consultation
58e550d9-f830-4e27-a111-1654c2762a81.description: The involvement of representatives from the relevant Aboriginal Community(ies) in the planning, appropriate implementation and assessment of the syllabus. To pursue the idea of teaching an Aboriginal Language, a wide range of local Aboriginal organisations should be approached in person. To ensure that all owners and Custodians are reached, the consultation process should be ongoing and will take time.

a469d8cd-2385-4c8f-a012-006064fdfa70.title: context
a469d8cd-2385-4c8f-a012-006064fdfa70.description: An environment or situation (social, cultural or historical) in which a text is responded to or created. Or wording surrounding an unfamiliar word, which a reader or listener uses to understand its meaning.

6212df83-b71d-482f-b99b-c887a93ada96.title: conventions
6212df83-b71d-482f-b99b-c887a93ada96.description: Accepted practices or features that help define textual forms, creative forms, styles and meaning.

025341f0-4a76-4ac1-96d9-c8f9fc22cdbd.title: critically analyse/evaluate
025341f0-4a76-4ac1-96d9-c8f9fc22cdbd.description: Add a degree or level of accuracy, depth, knowledge and understanding, logic, questioning, reflection and quality to (analyse/evaluate).

912a98f3-eda6-4802-a8ed-45269a79ce18.title: Customary
912a98f3-eda6-4802-a8ed-45269a79ce18.description:
Relating to customs or practices associated with a particular culture, society, place or set of circumstances. Similar to the term 'traditional', 'Customary' is used in reference to aspects of Aboriginal Cultures in pre-invasion contexts.

See traditional

a02912d0-3559-4600-b599-218f611290e5.title: ecology
a02912d0-3559-4600-b599-218f611290e5.description: In a languages context, ecology is used to describe the view that languages can be studied as living entities that are interrelated and that relate to their environments.

e39b478b-e951-404f-9c53-55b266bed888.title: evaluate
e39b478b-e951-404f-9c53-55b266bed888.description: Make a judgement based on criteria; determine the value of.

a5fd6c73-a407-41de-a231-6e5539feafc4.title: handshape
a5fd6c73-a407-41de-a231-6e5539feafc4.description: The held position of the hand and fingers in producing a particular sign.

a65b4d86-bedd-4c63-b211-672509c3802c.title: identity
a65b4d86-bedd-4c63-b211-672509c3802c.description: A person’s conception and expression of individuality or group affiliation, self-concept and self-representation. It is closely connected to culture and language.

7bfd65bd-417c-468a-92ec-f87d3d2de191.title: language awareness
7bfd65bd-417c-468a-92ec-f87d3d2de191.description: A type of language program that develops an understanding of the forms of a language rather than the capacity to use it to communicate. For Aboriginal Languages, this program typically occurs in locations where historical language loss is extreme and few tangible records have survived.

b60ee5fb-b05b-4839-b2fc-de9595ac4396.title: language maintenance
b60ee5fb-b05b-4839-b2fc-de9595ac4396.description: Situation where a speaker, group of speakers or community of speakers continue to use their language despite competition with a dominant or majority language.

bb55409e-5b50-41f4-9dda-e8ddc6851ceb.title: language reclamation
bb55409e-5b50-41f4-9dda-e8ddc6851ceb.description: The process of restoring, preserving, recording and promoting Aboriginal Languages.

a237657e-dcab-4b6a-ba78-f9a1225002ec.title: language renewal
a237657e-dcab-4b6a-ba78-f9a1225002ec.description: A type of language program in which the target language is known and used by a community in part rather than in its entirety or ‘right through’.

cf026eab-c63c-42e5-bff5-da5c00dd1255.title: language revitalisation
cf026eab-c63c-42e5-bff5-da5c00dd1255.description: A type of language program in which the goal is to encourage younger speakers to use the target language as fluently as older speakers.

390cd93c-2d6d-4893-8150-b7edf0995f9c.title: linguistic
390cd93c-2d6d-4893-8150-b7edf0995f9c.description: Relating to the systematic study of language.

93a2be47-fbf8-497c-bb96-2d753c604d01.title: metalanguage
93a2be47-fbf8-497c-bb96-2d753c604d01.description: Technical terms used to describe and discuss how language and texts function.

1069cf6f-0b16-4e99-831f-44c7c7cd84ba.title: nonverbal communication
1069cf6f-0b16-4e99-831f-44c7c7cd84ba.description: Manually coded forms of communication in which the body is manipulated to convey meaning. These are often used in place of spoken languages. For Aboriginal Peoples nonverbal communication exists alongside spoken language(s) and are usually associated with particular Cultural protocols, e.g. relationships, ceremony, local Community.

33fbccc7-9ad8-4d2d-91fa-32c7d5a56df6.title: observe/observing
33fbccc7-9ad8-4d2d-91fa-32c7d5a56df6.description: To see, watch, perceive or notice. Observations can be made using all 5 senses as well as digital and non-digital tools that extend our senses.

01e973d8-3f16-4351-92ac-0311820b12e4.title: perspective
01e973d8-3f16-4351-92ac-0311820b12e4.description: A way of regarding situations, facts and texts, and evaluating their relative significance.

a999fade-f61b-4773-a406-33ff8d5ccf9e.title: phonology
a999fade-f61b-4773-a406-33ff8d5ccf9e.description: The study of the sound system of a language, especially regarding speech sounds such as phonemes.

5547fc5a-e83a-47c0-966f-fc4414a40b2c.title: principles
5547fc5a-e83a-47c0-966f-fc4414a40b2c.description: The guiding requirements and obligations of right conduct.

7b7b81ef-71d0-42f4-abe7-b078f836c071.title: scaffold
7b7b81ef-71d0-42f4-abe7-b078f836c071.description: A framework to support the production of original text.

15687960-6788-41c9-8b79-b8551d42e244.title: strengthening (of languages)
15687960-6788-41c9-8b79-b8551d42e244.description: Improving the status and recognition of Aboriginal Languages, including the allocation of funding and resources, raising the prestige of the target language and the development of new words, where applicable.

6e6da676-79b0-4e5f-9868-f755d531ae2d.title: symbols
6e6da676-79b0-4e5f-9868-f755d531ae2d.description: The written representations of a language such as letters, characters, marks, accents; identifiable aspects of culture such as flags, artefacts, costumes, landmarks.

c0757cd6-43b2-4958-abd9-bbb98b475ee7.title: target language
c0757cd6-43b2-4958-abd9-bbb98b475ee7.description: The Aboriginal Language in which it is intended that a student will gain proficiency.

311614b9-09ab-4956-9f8b-14e7cd440bc0.title: traditional
311614b9-09ab-4956-9f8b-14e7cd440bc0.description:
A term widely used to refer to pre-invasion Aboriginal life, Culture and social organisation, or the continuation of aspects of Aboriginal Cultures. The term ‘traditional’ must be used with care, as individuals and groups may find this term offensive. The word ‘Customary’ is often used to convey a similar message.

See Customary

80b0c7ae-226d-4ebd-a158-d53a89a42e07.title: view/viewing
80b0c7ae-226d-4ebd-a158-d53a89a42e07.description: Observing and comprehending a visual text, e.g. diagram, illustration, photograph, film, television documentary, multimedia. This sometimes involves listening to and reading accompanying written text.

b394eef2-1212-43a8-af9a-7b5217a1e0ae.title: compare
b394eef2-1212-43a8-af9a-7b5217a1e0ae.description: Show how things are similar or different.

4cb7eebb-063b-4d24-b94d-1fbffbe31791.title: access content points
4cb7eebb-063b-4d24-b94d-1fbffbe31791.description: Content for students with significant intellectual disability who are working towards the Early Stage 1 outcomes. Teachers can use the access content points on their own, or in combination with the content for each outcome.

0822ad61-50b9-44d9-b410-7f198ac1c28b.title: genre
0822ad61-50b9-44d9-b410-7f198ac1c28b.description:
The categories into which texts are grouped based on similarities in premise, structure and function. The ‘genre’ of a text describes larger recurring patterns of subject matter and textual structures observable between texts, such as typical plots, characters and setting.

‘Genre’ can also describe categories of form and structure in texts.

e764f3ae-31d3-4a29-8974-0e376f364e50.title: rhotics
e764f3ae-31d3-4a29-8974-0e376f364e50.description: Pronouncing the letters r, rr, rl when they occur after a vowel or at the end of a syllable.

817b8116-28d5-4bbf-8b88-7cc8c212c29a.title: stakeholder
817b8116-28d5-4bbf-8b88-7cc8c212c29a.description:
A person, group or organisation that has interest or concern.

See custodians and consultation

93a278c1-92e0-4594-8397-f9c2871624aa.title: morpheme
93a278c1-92e0-4594-8397-f9c2871624aa.description: The smallest unit of meaning in a word, e.g. jumps has 2 morphemes: jump + s.

62028eef-6753-4184-9827-80e911e8514a.title: phoneme
62028eef-6753-4184-9827-80e911e8514a.description:
The smallest unit of speech sound.

Examples include:

  • Cat has 3 phonemes: c/a/t
  • Truck has 4 phonemes: t/r/u/ck.

9f451bcf-17da-40fa-8bf0-2c6fdb43d234.title: interpret
9f451bcf-17da-40fa-8bf0-2c6fdb43d234.description: The act of translation from one language to another, the process of understanding and explaining.

a9b597af-336f-4e4e-9220-151ee98ccff7.title: intonation
a9b597af-336f-4e4e-9220-151ee98ccff7.description: The pattern or melody of pitch changes in connected speech, especially the pitch pattern of a sentence.

ffd6d1d6-c7d3-4222-877f-cbeb2c6c0644.title: collaborate
ffd6d1d6-c7d3-4222-877f-cbeb2c6c0644.description: Working with others towards a shared goal, through a variety of modes of communication. This may be achieved using a range of technologies, tools and processes.

75f74bb4-a756-4763-a616-2340d8ccc28b.title: synthesise
75f74bb4-a756-4763-a616-2340d8ccc28b.description: Put together various elements to make a whole.

ee9b8632-ca6b-4ebe-9c97-afa97bae46ee.title: Aboriginal-controlled
ee9b8632-ca6b-4ebe-9c97-afa97bae46ee.description: Local Aboriginal Community management of processes guided by locally endorsed Cultural protocols.

42e18fdb-b4b4-4e1e-9e51-173fe37b54e4.title: Aboriginal enterprise
42e18fdb-b4b4-4e1e-9e51-173fe37b54e4.description: These can be owned by individuals, Communities or can be an extension of an Aboriginal organisation, and are usually staffed by Aboriginal People. Aboriginal enterprises can be social enterprises or based on certain protocols such as benefit-sharing.

64c1f108-6171-422a-aae3-45560c5e8728.title: Aboriginal organisation
64c1f108-6171-422a-aae3-45560c5e8728.description: An entity with a particular purpose, which is initiated, managed and maintained by Aboriginal People. Aboriginal organisations usually provide services for the direct or indirect benefit of Aboriginal People. They are usually not-for-profit, and may be reliant on Aboriginal Community member volunteers.

0a3bd895-0f86-4837-b87c-1ec933634d1a.title: Custodianship
0a3bd895-0f86-4837-b87c-1ec933634d1a.description: In Aboriginal Communities, the practice of maintaining and passing on particular elements of Cultural significance, e.g. Language, stories, songs, rituals and imagery.

e1c879f9-0345-451c-aece-fd134429918c.title: Customary law
e1c879f9-0345-451c-aece-fd134429918c.description:
Aboriginal Peoples have a complex system of laws that represent accepted Practices, responsibilities and interactions. As there are no formal codified laws or formal courts under Customary law, problems regarding the law are handled by Elders – the most knowledgeable people in the Community.

See Customary Lore

1686d9cd-2fee-41df-8686-ff4ac6a85f09.title: Customary Lore
1686d9cd-2fee-41df-8686-ff4ac6a85f09.description:
The learning and transmission of Cultural heritage by observing Customs, ceremonies and songs. Customary Lore is connected to the Dreaming and provides protocols and Practices for how people interact with Country, Kinship and Community.

The term ‘Customary’ must be used with care. Some individuals and groups could find this term offensive, and may prefer to use Aboriginal Language terms or ‘law’. The term ‘folklore’ is not appropriate.

See Customary law

716d7c33-f61a-4172-91cb-0fac9cf698e2.title: handtalk
716d7c33-f61a-4172-91cb-0fac9cf698e2.description: A form of communication that consists of hand signs, gestures and expressions.

488c4231-97fa-4d8e-b9b0-2ebcbad8a902.title: land
488c4231-97fa-4d8e-b9b0-2ebcbad8a902.description:
Used by Aboriginal Peoples to describe their spirituality, ecosystems, Dreaming(s), all living things, including totems, all physical factors such as sacred sites, water, air and geographical factors.

See Country/Place

9d8aec29-aa74-4139-aad6-edd396efe005.title: land rights
9d8aec29-aa74-4139-aad6-edd396efe005.description:
The evolving struggle of Aboriginal Peoples, Torres Strait Islander Peoples, and international Indigenous Peoples for the absolute legal and moral acknowledgement of prior ownership of their land and recognition of all accompanying rights and obligations which flow from this association. ‘Land Rights’ (capitalised) refers to the legislation.

See land

0650f026-5f34-42d2-9278-da09a9fcf1ba.title: missions
0650f026-5f34-42d2-9278-da09a9fcf1ba.description: Living areas established initially by churches and later by the Aborigines Welfare Board, and ruled under the provisions of the Aborigines Protection Act.

ede22e48-d115-4d37-a6e7-b4d77236113e.title: Peoples
ede22e48-d115-4d37-a6e7-b4d77236113e.description:
The term ‘Peoples’ acknowledges the plurality and diversity of Aboriginal Cultures, Torres Strait Islander Cultures, and international Indigenous Cultures.

See Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

407adb78-c3ea-4df9-ac8b-158eb7087fff.title: racism
407adb78-c3ea-4df9-ac8b-158eb7087fff.description:
Prejudice, discrimination or unconscious bias on the basis of colour, culture or national origin.

See discrimination

ab2f81d9-c1dc-4ca3-8f85-9fe360773c92.title: research methodology
ab2f81d9-c1dc-4ca3-8f85-9fe360773c92.description:
The methods used to identify and analyse a specific topic of research.

Indigenous Research methodology is centred on ethics, undertaken with Indigenous Peoples on collaborative projects.

2645566f-1f52-4e84-9118-04f580af1dba.title: reserves
2645566f-1f52-4e84-9118-04f580af1dba.description: Land reserved by the Crown for Aboriginal Peoples, established in the 19th century, administered and controlled by governments. In NSW the regulatory body was the Aborigines Protection Board.

c8fe94e6-4c6e-420f-85fe-ace745c502c9.title: self-determination
c8fe94e6-4c6e-420f-85fe-ace745c502c9.description: Involves the effective participation of Aboriginal Peoples in all decision-making that affects them.

0cc81374-a733-42c9-9ad1-8ada323b56f2.title: spirituality(ies)
0cc81374-a733-42c9-9ad1-8ada323b56f2.description:
Refers to individual and collective aspects of Aboriginal Peoples’ interconnectedness with the world. Spirituality is deeply linked to Country, Dreaming(s), Kinship and identity, and often incorporates concepts of ‘Customary law’/‘Customary Lore’.

See Country/Place, Dreaming, kinship, Customary law, Customary Lore

412986cc-1447-47a2-b5b5-f44f71957dc7.title: Legends of the Torres Strait
412986cc-1447-47a2-b5b5-f44f71957dc7.description: Central to Torres Strait Islander Peoples' beliefs about creation and spiritual and physical existence. Stories about the beginning of all things, passed down through oral traditions, songs and ceremonies for millennia.

ee3e37bf-3f17-49e5-b4fe-402c35117359.title: invasion
ee3e37bf-3f17-49e5-b4fe-402c35117359.description: The forced takeover of land and people.

1a7619ee-10c7-42ea-9177-6c55b3789545.title: Native Title
1a7619ee-10c7-42ea-9177-6c55b3789545.description: Native Title in Australia recognises Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ rights to land and waters based on traditional laws and customs.

2edbe9af-55b0-4f84-b6bf-5986bef5e311.title: social justice principles
2edbe9af-55b0-4f84-b6bf-5986bef5e311.description: Principles aimed at decreasing or eliminating inequity; promoting inclusiveness of diversity; and establishing environments that are supportive of all people. The principles include: participation, equity, access and rights.

1d31e8fd-c603-4b31-9a99-ed6fafecd30b.title: Knowledges
1d31e8fd-c603-4b31-9a99-ed6fafecd30b.description: The collective intelligence, developed over generations, of multiple facts, information, awareness, familiarity, experiences, skills and understandings.

f462fc3b-b47c-4c42-ac5b-79afe64661e6.title: discrimination
f462fc3b-b47c-4c42-ac5b-79afe64661e6.description: An unjust or prejudicial treatment of someone because they belong to a particular group of people or have a particular characteristic.

19bbddf5-0e1f-4d5c-83ab-e27279916825.title: dispossession
19bbddf5-0e1f-4d5c-83ab-e27279916825.description: The removal of people from their lands which had been occupied and cared for by their ancestors over thousands of years.

382826e1-7645-414c-a12e-2ea980d53771.title: terra nullius
382826e1-7645-414c-a12e-2ea980d53771.description: A concept in international law meaning ‘a territory belonging to no-one’ or ‘over which no-one claims ownership’.

5e08543f-a7cb-419e-8261-bbfe51f97c69.title: Agtech
5e08543f-a7cb-419e-8261-bbfe51f97c69.description: The collective term for innovation in agricultural practice through new and improved tools, technologies and processes, including devices, networks, sensors, robotics, automation and artificial intelligence.

ffc6dd63-791d-4d24-9d98-19776c7fa61c.title: biosecurity
ffc6dd63-791d-4d24-9d98-19776c7fa61c.description: Measures taken to prevent the spread of disease to plants or animals in a specific region.

71e1bf44-9d8b-4dd4-88a7-f3180ca414bb.title: extensive (production system)
71e1bf44-9d8b-4dd4-88a7-f3180ca414bb.description: Agricultural production spanning large areas of land. Carrying capacity and crop capability are dependent on animal behaviour, topography, soil quality; farmed using less labour and fewer resources.

c4531fc8-bbcc-420e-96f9-41f2087be888.title: intensive (production system)
c4531fc8-bbcc-420e-96f9-41f2087be888.description: Agricultural production using small areas of land or spaces. Carrying capacity and crop capability require greater inputs, including labour and resources, to increase income and yield.

b8d559f6-2d7d-4545-b78e-cc13eadc6287.title: propagation
b8d559f6-2d7d-4545-b78e-cc13eadc6287.description: The process of creating new plants from seed or vegetative parts of original plants, such as leaves, stems and roots.

308dd39f-7634-4619-98dd-2ac6a4537ff6.title: biotic
308dd39f-7634-4619-98dd-2ac6a4537ff6.description: Involving the living components of the environment.

c2b37f93-1816-4ed7-b496-a0bf3ccdc61f.title: species
c2b37f93-1816-4ed7-b496-a0bf3ccdc61f.description: A single, specific type of living organism.

d59d6193-2e52-4de9-96b2-86092ee6f507.title: ancient
d59d6193-2e52-4de9-96b2-86092ee6f507.description: In the study of Ancient History in Stage 6, the ancient period covers history from the development of early human communities to the end of late antiquity (around AD 650).

963742b9-63ff-491c-87cb-74ce4d4b1111.title: causation
963742b9-63ff-491c-87cb-74ce4d4b1111.description: A process that includes a range of possible reasons for an historical event, situation or development.

f24ba0df-fb32-4860-90cb-f93f3d7d4759.title: chronology
f24ba0df-fb32-4860-90cb-f93f3d7d4759.description: The order in which a series of events happened, or a list of these events in the order in which they happened.

752be3bd-b284-4985-ac9c-dacc7e85fa98.title: colonisation
752be3bd-b284-4985-ac9c-dacc7e85fa98.description:
In Modern History – a process by which a different system of government is established by one nation over another group of peoples. It involves the colonial power asserting and enforcing its sovereignty or right to govern according to its own laws rather than by laws of the colonised.

In Ancient History – a process by which ancient societies establish settlements in other lands and establish trading connections.

4db4a167-2c0d-444b-b2e8-f84bd61be0d1.title: concepts
4db4a167-2c0d-444b-b2e8-f84bd61be0d1.description: The key ideas that shape the practice of the discipline of history, e.g. causation, continuity and change, contestability, perspectives and significance. They provide the scope for judgement, interpretation and argument and are the major means by which knowledge is constructed, analysed, questioned and represented.

38cdf25e-c5c9-4d77-9074-a1e6cb81d636.title: contestability
38cdf25e-c5c9-4d77-9074-a1e6cb81d636.description: An examination of how interpretations and representations of the past differ, e.g. as a result of using differing evidence or resulting from different perspectives.

5626ff43-4b48-44e0-a577-6a3d5ae70058.title: continuity and change
5626ff43-4b48-44e0-a577-6a3d5ae70058.description: Aspects of the past that have remained the same over a period of time or have changed over time. Change can be understood as a 'process'.

af7f8738-bcb1-437b-9d8d-893b7940a882.title: evidence
af7f8738-bcb1-437b-9d8d-893b7940a882.description: The information elicited and interpreted from a source that is used to support arguments or inform a specific inquiry.

96d80d78-3776-4145-a697-b0fab58c30be.title: heritage
96d80d78-3776-4145-a697-b0fab58c30be.description: Tangible or intangible aspects of the past that are valued by an individual, group, community or nation as a result of birth, inheritance or membership. It can also be applied to significant examples of the human or natural environment.

a898e13e-4d64-42fb-a9b4-0c67c60cdf1d.title: historical authentication
a898e13e-4d64-42fb-a9b4-0c67c60cdf1d.description: A process of verifying the origins of an artefact or object and establishing it as genuine.

a973c2e4-cda9-4b7a-8074-26978ee57e8a.title: historical inquiry
a973c2e4-cda9-4b7a-8074-26978ee57e8a.description: The process of developing knowledge and understanding by posing questions about the past, and applying skills associated with locating, analysing, evaluating and using sources as evidence to develop an informed argument or interpretation.

598c00a0-9529-4541-afe5-09461d892594.title: historiography
598c00a0-9529-4541-afe5-09461d892594.description: The study of how history is constructed. It involves the critical analysis and evaluation of historical methodologies and the way history has been written over time.

408f7498-cfb8-4c3e-afd5-7d74cbe9f3bc.title: ideology
408f7498-cfb8-4c3e-afd5-7d74cbe9f3bc.description: A framework of beliefs that guides actions, e.g. fascism and communism.

e1612073-3694-4eaa-b118-9ee3b5749c8e.title: interpretation
e1612073-3694-4eaa-b118-9ee3b5749c8e.description: A way of understanding and explaining what has happened in the past. The discipline of History acknowledges that there is often more than one view of what happened in the past.

77fb387e-ed10-47dd-b8fa-e9ed0e29d444.title: modern
77fb387e-ed10-47dd-b8fa-e9ed0e29d444.description: In the study of Modern History in Stage 6, the period of time in the modern world – generally between 1750 and the present.

e1652691-111e-4327-9ade-087e6d4488ac.title: perspective
e1652691-111e-4327-9ade-087e6d4488ac.description: A point of view from which historical events, problems and issues can be analysed, e.g. the perspective of an individual or group in the past. This may involve empathetic understanding – the capacity to enter into the world of the past from the point of view of a particular individual or group from that time, including an appreciation of the circumstances they faced, and the motivations, values and attitudes behind their actions.

96374323-06f0-4478-a50d-92c275d4ab14.title: reconstruction
96374323-06f0-4478-a50d-92c275d4ab14.description: A process of piecing together evidence from sources to develop an understanding or picture of the past. It may include the physical reconstruction of ancient sites.

dd537daf-69c8-4da7-ac65-f6a3a16dc0b3.title: reliability
dd537daf-69c8-4da7-ac65-f6a3a16dc0b3.description: Consideration of the context, purpose, origin and audience of a source to determine how accurately an area of historical study is represented. A source is neither reliable nor unreliable in and of itself. It can only be judged reliable or useful for the question that is asked. Reliability requires an understanding of perspective.

c846cbd5-1935-4c10-afef-47efeb5453a1.title: representation
c846cbd5-1935-4c10-afef-47efeb5453a1.description: A portrayal of the past that may reflect a popular view within society, past or present, or that may be constructed by historians.

74c18b84-67b5-4d01-b3bb-d9a8a33e7581.title: significance
74c18b84-67b5-4d01-b3bb-d9a8a33e7581.description: The importance attributed to a particular aspect of the past such as an individual or event. Significance involves an understanding of the various considerations which cause different groups at different times to judge aspects of the past more or less historically significant.

5e6c3ca3-31b7-43e2-83fe-efe425daa9de.title: source
5e6c3ca3-31b7-43e2-83fe-efe425daa9de.description:
Any written or non-written materials that can be used to investigate the past.

Extended in 7–12 History Syllabuses: A source is used to elicit ‘evidence’ in order to answer a specific historical question, inform a historical inquiry, or to support or refute an interpretation.

3558f51c-6b1d-41ac-b0b7-610b68064c1c.title: terms
3558f51c-6b1d-41ac-b0b7-610b68064c1c.description: A word or phrase used to describe abstract aspects or features of the past, e.g. imperialism, democracy or republic; and more specific features, such as trench warfare, or a dictator, gladiator or vizier.

2b3d49e6-3f25-45ac-8c1e-29d7acea919a.title: archaeology/archaeological
2b3d49e6-3f25-45ac-8c1e-29d7acea919a.description: The practice of excavation and the study of the material remains of past human life and activities, e.g. pottery, jewellery, tools, monuments and human remains.

2d6d6086-949d-41bc-96fb-9e7068fe9ada.title: artefact
2d6d6086-949d-41bc-96fb-9e7068fe9ada.description: An object made by a person, e.g. a tool, weapon, or ornament.

7e0f3b71-b845-4fe6-a1fb-b76696555961.title: legacy
7e0f3b71-b845-4fe6-a1fb-b76696555961.description: The long-lasting impact, influence or significance of a person, action or event from the past.

5d6aaa44-97ae-4825-993f-562078414a12.title: preservation
5d6aaa44-97ae-4825-993f-562078414a12.description: Actions taken to minimise deterioration of an object and maintain it in its existing condition.

68cefcba-3da6-40df-af3d-2fe3b2e0edb5.title: site
68cefcba-3da6-40df-af3d-2fe3b2e0edb5.description: A location, building or structure of historical significance.

65cb3b5d-520d-4346-a103-d3628b3a1464.title: aquaculture
65cb3b5d-520d-4346-a103-d3628b3a1464.description: The farming of aquatic animals and plants, especially fish, shellfish and seaweed, in natural or controlled marine or freshwater environments.

07e89758-5167-4fc7-870f-1c46115b285c.title: biofouling
07e89758-5167-4fc7-870f-1c46115b285c.description: The accumulation of microorganisms, plants, algae, or small animals on surfaces, such as ships' hulls, pipes or underwater sensors, particularly in aquatic environments.

c41c8143-1829-431d-8829-ef931146a2bb.title: brackish
c41c8143-1829-431d-8829-ef931146a2bb.description: Describes a mixture of freshwater and saltwater. Brackish water has a higher salt content than freshwater but a lower salt content than seawater.

c16dc9af-671b-4d14-90cf-b097f0f87476.title: carbon sink
c16dc9af-671b-4d14-90cf-b097f0f87476.description: A natural system, like forests, oceans, lakes or wetlands, that absorbs and stores carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. This process helps mitigate the effects of climate change.

86595017-0bb8-4ddf-9381-71ea5544f902.title: dissolved oxygen
86595017-0bb8-4ddf-9381-71ea5544f902.description: The amount of oxygen present in water, essential for the survival of aquatic life. It enters the water from the air or through photosynthesis by aquatic plants.

1898a67c-9098-4a0e-a6d3-751e4d586c33.title: fish finder
1898a67c-9098-4a0e-a6d3-751e4d586c33.description: An electronic device used on a boat to detect and locate fish underwater. It uses sonar technology to send sound waves into the water and displays the results on a screen.

2f583cd0-3cdc-489b-a2ad-f076c2f4c221.title: mariculture
2f583cd0-3cdc-489b-a2ad-f076c2f4c221.description: A type of aquaculture involving farming marine organisms, such as fish, shellfish and seaweed in oceans, coastal areas and estuaries. Species are raised in either natural or controlled conditions for food, materials or other products.

855ac9d5-c652-4995-9fdb-117158b8acde.title: propagation
855ac9d5-c652-4995-9fdb-117158b8acde.description: The process of breeding and growing new plants or animals.

204f0fa3-b3b8-4016-9657-8697ffcacf83.title: riparian zones
204f0fa3-b3b8-4016-9657-8697ffcacf83.description: An area of land along the edge of a river, stream or other body of water. These zones are important for supporting diverse plant and animal life and help protect water quality.

34642c64-6572-4725-9067-f5a2598c0eb3.title: sounder
34642c64-6572-4725-9067-f5a2598c0eb3.description: An electronic device used on a boat to measure the depth of water beneath it. It sends sound waves to the bottom and calculates the distance based on how long it takes for the sound to bounce back.

96c00021-1dc1-41eb-b3f5-ded9155c40d9.title: tackle
96c00021-1dc1-41eb-b3f5-ded9155c40d9.description: The equipment used for fishing, such as rods, reels, lines and hooks. It includes all the tools and gear needed to catch fish.

0367332f-76f1-4219-a2ce-a00d760e0441.title: turbidity
0367332f-76f1-4219-a2ce-a00d760e0441.description: How cloudy or murky water is due to particles like dirt, algae or other materials floating in it. Higher turbidity means the water is less clear.

fe34723f-8fd8-4ac5-ae79-bf2a0337d8d8.title: watercraft
fe34723f-8fd8-4ac5-ae79-bf2a0337d8d8.description: Any vehicle used for traveling on water, including surfboards, kayaks, boats and ships.

1d5c4718-63f8-4106-947f-61baf8ad9b97.title: biodiversity
1d5c4718-63f8-4106-947f-61baf8ad9b97.description: The variety of living organisms within a particular habitat, ecosystem, biome, or globally.

87884c39-7ca0-4f49-8872-6d1e7d5d6bc0.title: ecosystem
87884c39-7ca0-4f49-8872-6d1e7d5d6bc0.description:
A system formed by the interaction of biotic organisms with each other and with the abiotic components of the environment in which they live.

While an ecosystem may be synonymous with a specific environment, the ‘system’ approach enables a focus on the various components and their interconnected nature.

c2645ea8-a93b-4e9d-842f-381a31cefe57.title: sustainability
c2645ea8-a93b-4e9d-842f-381a31cefe57.description: The patterns of activities that meet the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

f86cd118-0074-4d1c-b2d9-89749121da17.title: food web
f86cd118-0074-4d1c-b2d9-89749121da17.description: A series of interconnected food chains that outlines feeding relationships in an ecosystem.

7e36c0c1-8147-4e35-8e3f-f30359554017.title: project
7e36c0c1-8147-4e35-8e3f-f30359554017.description: An individual or collaborative problem-solving activity undertaken by students that is planned to achieve an articulated aim.

b6fb6962-e40d-409a-a9ad-55f4bc411de1.title: access
b6fb6962-e40d-409a-a9ad-55f4bc411de1.description: Listen to, read and/or view texts to understand meaning.

d97529ed-3d57-468d-907b-b8030ac4a713.title: visual–gestural languages
d97529ed-3d57-468d-907b-b8030ac4a713.description: Signed languages are described as visual–gestural because they are received through vision and signed with hands, compared to spoken languages which are described as auditory–oral languages, as they are received through hearing and spoken with the mouth. The term does not equate signed languages with gesture in general.

35fe6b2b-08bf-4894-b874-90aa1809d72d.title: adapted forms
35fe6b2b-08bf-4894-b874-90aa1809d72d.description: Adapted forms of Auslan, sign language and fingerspelling are used by people who are deafblind. The most common forms are visual frame or box signing, close vision, tracking, tactile signing, tactile fingerspelling or deafblind alphabet and short-cut signs.

8e2534ed-5279-4902-b8ec-3e6581a662ba.title: backchannel
8e2534ed-5279-4902-b8ec-3e6581a662ba.description: Responses given by the receiver of a message in a conversation that serve a social function, such as showing attention or nodding without interrupting the signer or giver of the message.

89d92452-dcf8-47c9-91c4-facf4cb5a4ec.title: communication
89d92452-dcf8-47c9-91c4-facf4cb5a4ec.description: A mutual and reciprocal exchange of meaning.

88d8183f-cce0-4577-a196-bd9d6941ea39.title: constructed action
88d8183f-cce0-4577-a196-bd9d6941ea39.description: A discourse strategy used in signed languages when signers use their own face and body to represent actions, signs, thoughts or feelings of a referent in a text. The referent can be themselves at another time, a different character, or something thought of as an animate entity.

f19249a7-24b3-4365-9f55-160d1ebcdde7.title: Deaf community
f19249a7-24b3-4365-9f55-160d1ebcdde7.description: A local, national or transnational network of people who share the language and culture of Deaf people and a history of common experiences. A primary unifying factor in Deaf communities is the use of sign language.

fce0d6b0-e8eb-4141-9d78-53ad97d36c8b.title: Deaf culture
fce0d6b0-e8eb-4141-9d78-53ad97d36c8b.description:
The beliefs, values, traditions, history, social norms, literary traditions and art shared by d/Deaf people who belong to the Deaf community. Culture is understood as a framework in which things come to be seen as having meaning. It involves the lens through which people:

  • see, think, interpret the world and experience
  • make assumptions about self and others
  • understand and represent individual and community identity.

See culture

b7437bae-fed9-453a-ad24-e4288a21ca99.title: Deaf gain
b7437bae-fed9-453a-ad24-e4288a21ca99.description: Used to reframe the term ‘deaf’, from the traditional pathological perspective of ‘hearing loss’ often held by wider society to a view of deafness through the lens of bicultural diversity. Being deaf is seen as an individual and social gain and as a positive form of diversity that involves cognitive and sensory changes that have the potential to contribute to the greater good of humanity.

64acfa24-887c-4958-a721-ad65ff9d11cf.title: depicting signs
64acfa24-887c-4958-a721-ad65ff9d11cf.description:
A partly-lexical sign that is highly iconic and can be modified in a gradient way by a signer. Depicting signs can act as verbs or nouns depending on their use in context.

See entity depicting signs, handling depicting signs, size and shape specifier depicting signs

891cd193-6f7f-4eee-91fd-69f29ec055ae.title: enacting
891cd193-6f7f-4eee-91fd-69f29ec055ae.description: Showing or constructing the action, thoughts or language of a referent using the whole body or part of the body. Enactments are context-dependent for meaning.

49f79f37-f4e3-4f10-8abc-c6134fadde02.title: entity depicting signs
49f79f37-f4e3-4f10-8abc-c6134fadde02.description:
Signs in which the handshape represents an object, and the object can move around or be located in space mirroring real-world movement and location.

See depicting signs

796d9d72-3f84-4552-8eed-74ead1026823.title: eye gaze
796d9d72-3f84-4552-8eed-74ead1026823.description: The direction in which a signer is looking, which can have conventional associated meanings in Auslan, such as marking a shift into character in constructed action.

60f68def-15c9-48e9-8bfc-48edf603069b.title: fingerspelling
60f68def-15c9-48e9-8bfc-48edf603069b.description: The manual representation of the letters of the alphabet of a spoken language. In Australia, a 2-handed fingerspelling system is used to fingerspell English letters.

62de1b34-7aa8-4aa7-abf3-eef106ff0b08.title: fully-lexical signs
62de1b34-7aa8-4aa7-abf3-eef106ff0b08.description: Signs with a form that is fully specified, that is, the handshape, movement and location are conventional. Lexical signs make up a large proportion of the signs in a sign language dictionary.

7de0c1f6-08c1-4309-89b3-b8fe9dc4de43.title: gesture
7de0c1f6-08c1-4309-89b3-b8fe9dc4de43.description: A way of communicating with the hands that uses largely unconventional forms (except for conventional gestures such as the thumbs up for good), and that represents more imagistic thought of a speaker or signer. In spoken languages, gestures co-occur with speech, and in signed languages they form gestural overlays.

532b6fe2-815f-4097-8d72-120dbf741ca3.title: handling depicting signs
532b6fe2-815f-4097-8d72-120dbf741ca3.description:
Signs where the handshape represents how a human hand holds or touches an object and the movement shows how something is moved around or located in space.

See depicting signs

0ef8bbb3-9147-45a3-997e-d650a87d208a.title: iconicity
0ef8bbb3-9147-45a3-997e-d650a87d208a.description: See arbitrary signs, translucent signs and transparent signs

3e8b2a9b-3cfa-403e-9bd3-dc15401277f4.title: indicating verbs
3e8b2a9b-3cfa-403e-9bd3-dc15401277f4.description: A subset of verbs which can have their start or end location modified or be moved around in space to show who, what or where is involved in the verb. Directional indicating verbs can be moved meaningfully in space. Locatable indicating verbs cannot change direction, but can be meaningfully signed in a non-neutral location.

40129fc7-588e-4c27-9edf-f08bc73b1f4a.title: list buoys
40129fc7-588e-4c27-9edf-f08bc73b1f4a.description: A sign where the fingers on the non-dominant hand are used to represent the items in a list while the dominant hand signs something about those items.

8c0102f7-e630-4fec-ab8e-2a8fa063fee3.title: modality
8c0102f7-e630-4fec-ab8e-2a8fa063fee3.description: Referring to visual–gestural languages as opposed to auditory–verbal languages.

50a1e763-3dbd-4838-884f-f2ddefbdfda1.title: non-body-anchored signs
50a1e763-3dbd-4838-884f-f2ddefbdfda1.description: Signs that are made in neutral space and do not make contact with a location on the body. These signs can easily be moved around in space.

82765d75-7ac3-437a-8cf3-666a05ee9d49.title: non-lexical signs
82765d75-7ac3-437a-8cf3-666a05ee9d49.description: Symbolic units of meaning that are created on the spot in a particular context, particularly in constructed action but also gesturing. These signs cannot be listed in a dictionary.

32d6e48f-e02d-476d-a8c9-6a83a490a2c9.title: non-manual features
32d6e48f-e02d-476d-a8c9-6a83a490a2c9.description: Elements of a sign that contribute to the meaning but are not made with the hands, e.g. eyebrow position or mouth gestures.

cb2afac4-7157-4ab1-ac05-e608840790aa.title: orientation
cb2afac4-7157-4ab1-ac05-e608840790aa.description: The direction the palm or fingers of a handshape point in a given sign.

700eac8f-daf6-4bec-af61-5aca43157d2b.title: partly-lexical signs
700eac8f-daf6-4bec-af61-5aca43157d2b.description: Signs with a form that is not fully specified. The handshape, movement and/or location can change, e.g. in pointing signs (direction or handshape can be modified), or depicting signs (movement and location are often created on the spot).

43d3b467-da07-4550-9930-103b93a4e5ba.title: path movements
43d3b467-da07-4550-9930-103b93a4e5ba.description: Movement of the hands from one location in space to another while producing a sign.

2f9e84f0-5604-4a45-82d9-923cfa7e793b.title: referent
2f9e84f0-5604-4a45-82d9-923cfa7e793b.description: The person or thing being talked about with a sign or phrase.

7f9e6484-6c89-4a6b-8615-044e785d922c.title: sign languages
7f9e6484-6c89-4a6b-8615-044e785d922c.description:
Visual–gestural languages which evolve naturally in Deaf communities, such as Auslan. They are neither universal nor based on the spoken language of the country or region. Sign languages have their own lexicon and grammar and are equally complex and sophisticated as spoken languages. Adapted forms of sign language can be used for people who are deafblind.

See adapted forms

e8636364-f1bb-4d38-af7c-2c2778e7df69.title: signing space
e8636364-f1bb-4d38-af7c-2c2778e7df69.description: The area around a signer in which signs are articulated and can be modified.

33b421b1-3ac2-4e5a-a885-e90b0ee985ad.title: size and shape specifier depicting signs
33b421b1-3ac2-4e5a-a885-e90b0ee985ad.description:
Depicting signs in which the handshape and movement are used to outline the size or shape of an object. The handshape is formed as if handling the actual entity being described (or a miniature of it) and the movement is a mirror of the hands, as if they are tracing the size and shape of the object.

See depicting signs

0662855a-7c90-4649-b6ac-7c343aee257f.title: spatial locations
0662855a-7c90-4649-b6ac-7c343aee257f.description: Locations in the signing space that are associated with particular absent referents so that they can be referred back to in place of naming a referent.

c4ab48ea-016b-4801-9998-38ad6051a9be.title: visual vernacular
c4ab48ea-016b-4801-9998-38ad6051a9be.description: A highly visual form of performance often incorporated into storytelling which uses features of mime, gesture, non-manual features and specific cinematic techniques in the production of signs. Techniques include close and distant focus, dissolving of visual images and cutting between scenes, objects and characters, and time distortion in the 3-dimensional delivery of visually presented information.

74220373-c9ec-4692-86a6-4c29e99d6116.title: cohesion
74220373-c9ec-4692-86a6-4c29e99d6116.description: The use of a range of language features to link parts of a signed text to make it easy to follow and understand referents in the text.

6945d7ec-bb3f-4080-854b-93fb654c061c.title: create
6945d7ec-bb3f-4080-854b-93fb654c061c.description:
Develop and/or produce signed, spoken, written or multimodal texts in print, visual, oral or digital forms.

See compose

c17b76d3-bc1f-4515-afd6-63a13870b638.title: dialect
c17b76d3-bc1f-4515-afd6-63a13870b638.description: A variant of a language that is characteristic of a region or social group.

09dbc282-10eb-4909-96b3-a9c8f35506db.title: multimodal text/presentation
09dbc282-10eb-4909-96b3-a9c8f35506db.description: A text that combines 2 or more expressive modes to communicate.

ca4865bf-7f66-48e5-857e-c377305de304.title: narrative
ca4865bf-7f66-48e5-857e-c377305de304.description: An account of events or experiences, which are real or imagined. In English literary theory, narrative includes a story (what is narrated) and a discourse (how it is narrated). Narrative can present as an explicit sequencing of events (type of text) or it can be an implied or inferred component in a text.

aaadf8f5-2310-49af-9075-9d98f6d1542d.title: register
aaadf8f5-2310-49af-9075-9d98f6d1542d.description: The degree of formality or informality of language used for a particular purpose or in a particular social setting.

d707259f-4309-4dfa-a141-96e04f550e8b.title: audience
d707259f-4309-4dfa-a141-96e04f550e8b.description: Readers, listeners or viewers who engage with a text.

a0fc5cc0-913e-4181-9d20-24b239cf50e2.title: formulaic phrases or expressions
a0fc5cc0-913e-4181-9d20-24b239cf50e2.description: Words or expressions which are commonly used in fixed patterns and learnt as such without grammatical analysis. For example: Once upon a time (story-starter).

a170a605-d2f5-4247-9de9-b1b0dbe8ab0f.title: language
a170a605-d2f5-4247-9de9-b1b0dbe8ab0f.description: A structured system of communication. The structure of a language is its grammar and the free components are its vocabulary. Languages are the primary means of communication of humans, and can be conveyed through speech (spoken language), sign or writing.

047ac55c-067f-4853-ac53-4c2d17ab6e92.title: linguistic features/structures
047ac55c-067f-4853-ac53-4c2d17ab6e92.description: Grammatical, lexical, phonological or structural characteristics of a language or a text.

320e1250-26e4-4c68-a97d-d285de0155cf.title: modelled language
320e1250-26e4-4c68-a97d-d285de0155cf.description: Language that has been modelled or previously taught by the teacher. It can be used by students as a scaffold in structured situations.

5c00cc85-39c6-4056-83e2-3151b79e2d1b.title: responding
5c00cc85-39c6-4056-83e2-3151b79e2d1b.description: Engaging with a text. ‘Responding’ involves identifying, selecting, describing, comprehending, imagining, interpreting, explaining, analysing and/or evaluating.

aa942a7c-0e96-475b-8650-05b26c0b0ba9.title: simple text
aa942a7c-0e96-475b-8650-05b26c0b0ba9.description: A text in which the vocabulary and language structures are very familiar and straightforward, with mostly simple sentences. Comprehension may be supported by the use of visuals and/or word lists.

782911b0-1131-4269-b0ad-683cdd317d5c.title: translation
782911b0-1131-4269-b0ad-683cdd317d5c.description: A process of translating signs/words/text from one language into another, recognising that the process involves movement of meanings and attention to cultural context as well as the transposition of individual words.

afeb9462-8c3d-40c7-bcdd-b1b617b7183c.title: transect (sampling)
afeb9462-8c3d-40c7-bcdd-b1b617b7183c.description: A straight line or narrow strip through a natural environment along which observations or measurements are made to study the distribution and abundance of organisms or environmental features.

057572dd-da6d-4610-a70f-1a69de86c69a.title: model
057572dd-da6d-4610-a70f-1a69de86c69a.description: A mathematical, conceptual or physical representation that describes, simplifies, clarifies or provides an explanation of the structure, workings or relationships within an object, system or idea. Models can provide a means of testing and predicting behaviour within limited conditions. Models may be physical or exist in digital form.

883c4322-f5fd-41c5-9f69-669f925c9230.title: endocytosis
883c4322-f5fd-41c5-9f69-669f925c9230.description: The process by which material is ingested into a cell by the folding of the cell membrane to form a vesicle.

dde983c8-a11c-4be8-97ba-f94c3b7f70c4.title: mRNA (messenger ribonucleic acid)
dde983c8-a11c-4be8-97ba-f94c3b7f70c4.description: An intermediate single-stranded RNA molecule used during polypeptide synthesis that is transcribed from DNA and translated into proteins.

834c6770-8aee-4408-aa78-bbbbd01e5a16.title: mutagen
834c6770-8aee-4408-aa78-bbbbd01e5a16.description: A chemical, biological or physical agent capable of causing changes in DNA.

335a0a47-394d-4835-b758-4171d7631b7a.title: cytokinesis
335a0a47-394d-4835-b758-4171d7631b7a.description: The process following mitotic and meiotic division in which the cytoplasm divides, separating into daughter cells.

2a31344b-45dc-43be-a93f-058fe2114fe2.title: nonsense mutation
2a31344b-45dc-43be-a93f-058fe2114fe2.description: A mutation that occurs in DNA when a sequence change gives rise to a stop codon rather than a codon specifying an amino acid.

f253dafe-2937-4958-99aa-6f7730803481.title: amino acid
f253dafe-2937-4958-99aa-6f7730803481.description: An organic compound considered the building block from which proteins are formed.

130426a7-5f53-41a4-997f-da9ceaea3fb2.title: epigenetics
130426a7-5f53-41a4-997f-da9ceaea3fb2.description: Changes in the way a gene functions within an organism that are heritable but do not alter the genetic code itself; changes that affect the phenotype without changing the genotype.

21306afb-2c7f-4b3a-8913-ff8834d7b5de.title: biotechnology
21306afb-2c7f-4b3a-8913-ff8834d7b5de.description: The development or creation of products from biological systems, processes or living organisms.

9f57dc63-1483-4225-9db2-56eee9b6c472.title: carrying capacity
9f57dc63-1483-4225-9db2-56eee9b6c472.description: The largest amount of individuals of a species that can be supported by an environment. The number is based on resources, such as food, water and shelter, and how accessible they are.

5a6bbd60-4081-4058-92db-5d97cf5d1ad1.title: trend
5a6bbd60-4081-4058-92db-5d97cf5d1ad1.description: A general direction or pattern in data or observations that shows how something changes over time or under different conditions.

1ea6c033-865e-4d7b-825d-3df428ee1ec3.title: dominant
1ea6c033-865e-4d7b-825d-3df428ee1ec3.description: A trait expressed in a heterozygous organism or a homozygous-dominant organism.

f1675f7c-6853-4b56-9a7e-91cae910a470.title: predation
f1675f7c-6853-4b56-9a7e-91cae910a470.description: A biological interaction where a predator hunts and kills prey, usually for nutrition.

c49c6550-71cb-44b9-91e8-a2cf0d9672c9.title: exocytosis
c49c6550-71cb-44b9-91e8-a2cf0d9672c9.description: The process of expelling unwanted molecules from a cell through the cell membrane to the outside space by vesicles.

01e84aab-48c7-4986-a18b-bfb88ed107e5.title: control centre
01e84aab-48c7-4986-a18b-bfb88ed107e5.description: A region of the brain that maintains homeostasis by processing messages received from receptors and sending responses to effectors to counteract a stimulus.

469c7f12-d87f-4b3e-b215-74c408e141b3.title: effector
469c7f12-d87f-4b3e-b215-74c408e141b3.description: A muscle or gland that carries out a response.

30531489-4561-4629-bab3-638c27152918.title: mutualism
30531489-4561-4629-bab3-638c27152918.description: A symbiotic relationship between organisms of 2 different species where each benefit from the interaction.

e625546b-73fa-43a8-8f10-ea25b6732dab.title: parasitism
e625546b-73fa-43a8-8f10-ea25b6732dab.description: A symbiotic relationship in which a parasite lives on or within a host and benefits at the host’s expense.

a5478ec4-c06b-4f03-94e5-3952cee7d877.title: receptor
a5478ec4-c06b-4f03-94e5-3952cee7d877.description: A group of sensory cells within the body that detects a change in a particular component of the internal and/or external environment.

6555f51d-244d-47aa-a3ae-f1d6b2017d20.title: mitosis
6555f51d-244d-47aa-a3ae-f1d6b2017d20.description: The process that takes place as part of the cell cycle in which cellular division takes place, resulting in 2 genetically identical daughter cells.

2f13b6ee-a72d-4f29-be40-be50de995103.title: phylogenetic tree
2f13b6ee-a72d-4f29-be40-be50de995103.description: A branching diagram that visually represents the evolutionary relationships between different species or groups of organisms.

c96ca3dc-1acb-44d7-a8b9-93d689f11278.title: B cell
c96ca3dc-1acb-44d7-a8b9-93d689f11278.description: Lymphocytes produced in the bone marrow that develop into plasma cells responsible for making antibodies.

ac235043-1850-4148-9b10-440c96f4a74b.title: correlation
ac235043-1850-4148-9b10-440c96f4a74b.description: A statistical measurement of the relationship between 2 variables, indicating the size and direction.

4537f4c3-79f4-492e-9e0f-6542a6a01aa6.title: transpiration
4537f4c3-79f4-492e-9e0f-6542a6a01aa6.description: The process by which plants evaporate water into the atmosphere, usually via the stomata found within the leaves of a plant.

e54e60f7-5708-4da6-8f21-3b764c49d5f6.title: single nucleotide polymorphism
e54e60f7-5708-4da6-8f21-3b764c49d5f6.description: A single nucleotide base change at a particular locus on DNA in the genome of at least one per cent of individuals within a population.

74623030-ef08-4cfd-bf19-ae1a03862acd.title: eukaryotic cell
74623030-ef08-4cfd-bf19-ae1a03862acd.description: A cell which has DNA in its clearly defined nucleus, and also contains membrane-bound organelles.

f2e71f7a-a8ac-4a04-a06b-815411f3c66b.title: base substitution
f2e71f7a-a8ac-4a04-a06b-815411f3c66b.description: The replacement of one nucleotide base with a different one.

1918037a-b9c3-4832-ab58-51af371c3114.title: silent mutation
1918037a-b9c3-4832-ab58-51af371c3114.description: A point mutation which includes a change in the DNA sequence that does not change the amino acid produced during protein synthesis.

53805c3b-4efb-42d9-be10-fecd44fc0de2.title: genetic drift
53805c3b-4efb-42d9-be10-fecd44fc0de2.description: A change in allele frequency within a population due to random chance/causes.

5a08c715-db5f-4c48-a497-c3f2b5225dcc.title: phagocytic leukocyte
5a08c715-db5f-4c48-a497-c3f2b5225dcc.description: A type of white blood cell that ingests and digests foreign particles, microorganisms and cellular debris.

a023184a-65a1-4444-85b2-8989b9f98092.title: hypotonic
a023184a-65a1-4444-85b2-8989b9f98092.description: Denoting a solution that has a lower concentration of solutes compared to another solution.

45d45fe3-4f89-4d07-9349-b0766dfe5265.title: allele
45d45fe3-4f89-4d07-9349-b0766dfe5265.description: The alternative form of a gene at identical loci of homologous chromosomes.

a80ad3b1-5d66-4371-8c9f-60ed47f502ea.title: exon
a80ad3b1-5d66-4371-8c9f-60ed47f502ea.description: The coding section of DNA that remains in a mature mRNA molecule to be translated to form a protein.

19b683e1-3608-4908-9fdc-bde89b64831b.title: active transport
19b683e1-3608-4908-9fdc-bde89b64831b.description: The process of transporting molecules or ions across a cell membrane from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration using energy.

a58c2003-6cf9-49d7-a78d-b58555d324ac.title: binary fission
a58c2003-6cf9-49d7-a78d-b58555d324ac.description: An asexual reproduction method of division into 2 identical daughter cells.

a99bfd3f-16b7-489f-8d09-67bdf951c788.title: protein
a99bfd3f-16b7-489f-8d09-67bdf951c788.description: A large molecule made up of polypeptide chains found within cells.

39f1f37e-3850-48cb-aa2a-113baeb5b83d.title: immune response
39f1f37e-3850-48cb-aa2a-113baeb5b83d.description: The body’s co-ordinated defence mechanism characterised by both the innate immune system and the adaptive immune system.

9881cce6-6dcd-41b2-a9ba-e71a8aeee891.title: transgenic organisms
9881cce6-6dcd-41b2-a9ba-e71a8aeee891.description: A species that has artificially inserted genes from another species into their genome using genetic engineering techniques.

4c0b96d1-8949-4cbc-bbe1-9228d12aaea9.title: gene expression
4c0b96d1-8949-4cbc-bbe1-9228d12aaea9.description: The process by which the information encoded in a gene is turned into a function.

82078493-20ae-4f89-ba95-95511aec01c6.title: allele frequency
82078493-20ae-4f89-ba95-95511aec01c6.description: A percentage measure of the allele composition within a population’s gene pool.

5679e049-3577-4922-82a4-29947f7bc205.title: punctuated equilibrium
5679e049-3577-4922-82a4-29947f7bc205.description: A theory of evolution stating that species experience long periods of little or no evolutionary change, interrupted by brief periods of rapid change that lead to the formation of new species.

575b87f1-019d-4513-be86-bcfd2d89ff06.title: selective reabsorption
575b87f1-019d-4513-be86-bcfd2d89ff06.description: The process in which substances required by the body move from the renal tubules back into the blood in the capillaries by diffusion or active transport.

430a42aa-b730-4737-9981-e87e7430f0f4.title: recombinant DNA
430a42aa-b730-4737-9981-e87e7430f0f4.description: DNA that has been artificially constructed by combining genetic material from 2 or more different genomes.

62d35e07-f192-4a9f-94a1-07fd7eec9275.title: germline variant
62d35e07-f192-4a9f-94a1-07fd7eec9275.description: A DNA variation that occurs in the sexual reproductive cells (eggs and sperm) which can be passed on to the offspring.

2dd19b93-a764-4a32-aba2-19ee7fb37c03.title: replication fork
2dd19b93-a764-4a32-aba2-19ee7fb37c03.description: The Y-shaped region formed by the unwinding and partial separation of the DNA double helix during replication.

44284e53-88d8-42ee-97f2-6f39c9415e3c.title: ectotherm
44284e53-88d8-42ee-97f2-6f39c9415e3c.description: An organism that has a variable body temperature which is dependent on the ambient temperature.

fa5d013f-62ad-45f8-9f34-69b1f440ea84.title: secretion (within the nephron)
fa5d013f-62ad-45f8-9f34-69b1f440ea84.description: Part of a process within the nephron of moving unwanted substances from the blood capillaries into the renal tubules, mostly via active transport.

1d27bb4c-3ccc-47b7-8d79-be7fe1579052.title: codon
1d27bb4c-3ccc-47b7-8d79-be7fe1579052.description: A triplet sequence of nucleotides in mRNA that codes for a specific amino acid.

8e70609a-bed9-4cba-a535-2b490686e724.title: enzyme
8e70609a-bed9-4cba-a535-2b490686e724.description: A biological catalyst that increases the rate of a chemical reaction.

ae55b99d-5723-42b1-8254-2a765805fd8d.title: fluid mosaic model
ae55b99d-5723-42b1-8254-2a765805fd8d.description: A model used to describe the structure and function of the cell membrane.

c37c7519-ff20-4e5f-9690-8d93b12ba369.title: random segregation
c37c7519-ff20-4e5f-9690-8d93b12ba369.description: The separation of allele pairs by chance during the formation of gametes.

d1dfc0bb-5bcf-4a43-af64-ddd11588b306.title: endotherm
d1dfc0bb-5bcf-4a43-af64-ddd11588b306.description: An organism that maintains body temperature within a narrow range of tolerance despite any variation in the ambient temperature.

36aa517b-e5f3-47e7-b663-d3c37030265c.title: bioinformatics
36aa517b-e5f3-47e7-b663-d3c37030265c.description: The science of collecting and analysing biological data using computer technology.

57d0bac8-1ffd-4831-bd0b-5a83334310d6.title: glomerular filtrate
57d0bac8-1ffd-4831-bd0b-5a83334310d6.description: The fluid that passes through the walls of the capillaries in the glomerulus into the renal tubules of the Bowman’s capsule.

392ed884-b065-428a-8938-2d44eb4c0ad5.title: point mutation
392ed884-b065-428a-8938-2d44eb4c0ad5.description: A single nucleotide base change in the DNA or RNA sequence.

63e37e45-3664-417e-84c5-4842693c2d36.title: antibody
63e37e45-3664-417e-84c5-4842693c2d36.description: A type of blood protein produced in response to a specific antigen in order to counteract it. Also known as immunoglobin.

43e28119-53c5-4358-a7c3-7a7f288bccc2.title: interleukin
43e28119-53c5-4358-a7c3-7a7f288bccc2.description: A group of proteins, mainly secreted by leukocytes, responsible for the activation and differentiation of immune cells during an immune response.

6372985c-6ba2-4220-beb6-59e1c3f7e30c.title: transcription
6372985c-6ba2-4220-beb6-59e1c3f7e30c.description: A process within polypeptide synthesis in which a segment (gene) of DNA is copied into mRNA within the nucleus.

9ec52c16-ad44-4425-b463-e2459ff80041.title: intron
9ec52c16-ad44-4425-b463-e2459ff80041.description: The sequence of bases that are spliced out from the mRNA molecule also known as the non-coding section of DNA.

c687a0e8-4bda-4421-8f47-80b264ea1e6f.title: tubules (kidney)
c687a0e8-4bda-4421-8f47-80b264ea1e6f.description: Tiny tubes within the kidney that filter blood to form urine, including the proximal convoluted tubule, the Loop of Henle, the distal convoluted tubule and the collecting duct.

4523650f-6345-4138-ba7f-d38fcc07db98.title: prokaryotic cell
4523650f-6345-4138-ba7f-d38fcc07db98.description: A simple, single-celled organism containing single-strand DNA and without a distinct nucleus or membrane-bound organelles.

ea5562a5-910a-4867-8518-f841390f8358.title: isotonic
ea5562a5-910a-4867-8518-f841390f8358.description: A solution which has the same concentration of solutes as another solution.

6e7e9788-ebc1-47a4-8789-ea53e6328ab7.title: genetically modified organism (GMO)
6e7e9788-ebc1-47a4-8789-ea53e6328ab7.description: A plant, animal or microbe in which one or more changes have been made to the genome using biotechnology to alter its characteristics.

bf359623-169a-402c-9e50-19ad2b9fc9f3.title: budding
bf359623-169a-402c-9e50-19ad2b9fc9f3.description: An asexual reproduction method where part of the adult organism divides through mitosis to produce a small genetically identical bud.

ccc494f0-0310-4308-90c8-b7445b5325d3.title: gene flow
ccc494f0-0310-4308-90c8-b7445b5325d3.description: The natural transfer of genes between populations of the same species, affecting the allele frequency within a population.

ce16ace0-4bac-4a46-86ec-e5c7fdb6e011.title: frameshift mutation
ce16ace0-4bac-4a46-86ec-e5c7fdb6e011.description: A type of genetic mutation in which one or more nucleotides are inserted into or deleted from the DNA sequence, causing a shift in the reading frame of the genetic code during protein synthesis.

1a6ebdb0-e9bf-4935-a12d-7fe0856ab62f.title: parthenogenesis
1a6ebdb0-e9bf-4935-a12d-7fe0856ab62f.description: A form of asexual reproduction in which an embryo develops from an unfertilised egg without the need for fertilisation by a male sperm or pollen.

54670543-eb1a-41c7-9be5-d34b0cedf2ae.title: somatic variant
54670543-eb1a-41c7-9be5-d34b0cedf2ae.description: A change in a DNA sequence that occurs in body cells.

566e943e-83eb-40fe-99a6-c4665880ac9e.title: meiosis
566e943e-83eb-40fe-99a6-c4665880ac9e.description: A cell division process that halves the chromosome numbers to become haploid and results in gametes.

30d788f2-643c-4739-88c0-12706a81664c.title: tRNA (transfer ribonucleic acid)
30d788f2-643c-4739-88c0-12706a81664c.description: A small RNA molecule containing an anticodon that corresponds to the specific amino acid being carried used in translation.

7809d6dc-788f-4f64-b178-b2da909dac37.title: scientific investigation
7809d6dc-788f-4f64-b178-b2da909dac37.description: A scientific process of answering a question, exploring an idea or solving a problem, which requires activities such as planning a course of action, collecting data, interpreting data, reaching a conclusion and communicating these activities. Investigations can include practical and/or secondary-source data or information.

89457845-4338-4220-8cfa-d4b35e24ec1d.title: asexual reproduction
89457845-4338-4220-8cfa-d4b35e24ec1d.description: Reproduction involving only one parent and no sex cells.

cdd5ef67-1f73-4dd9-8d58-79df3908eba4.title: allelopathy
cdd5ef67-1f73-4dd9-8d58-79df3908eba4.description: The adverse effect one plant causes another through the release of chemicals into the soil.

a3208f54-323d-4eab-a009-589e0cb97ac5.title: comparative anatomy
a3208f54-323d-4eab-a009-589e0cb97ac5.description: The scientific study of the similarities and differences in the anatomical structures of different species of animals.

0dee777c-0a99-4e5f-b490-6e28953cd2ad.title: selection pressures
0dee777c-0a99-4e5f-b490-6e28953cd2ad.description: Environmental factors that influence which traits are advantageous for the survival and reproduction of organisms that drive evolution.

3b0832f3-d8d7-43e6-9b57-ce5e0e0ef277.title: cell-mediated response
3b0832f3-d8d7-43e6-9b57-ce5e0e0ef277.description: An immune response involving macrophages and T cells that eliminate intracellular pathogens.

9569fbd3-e0ad-4a71-ba56-f70087d287d6.title: stimulus
9569fbd3-e0ad-4a71-ba56-f70087d287d6.description: Something that causes a change in the internal or external environment that is detected by a receptor and triggers a response.

3ae40300-1e21-476f-ae0b-96877cee78f2.title: invasive species
3ae40300-1e21-476f-ae0b-96877cee78f2.description: A species which thrives in a habitat it is not native to and threatens the environment, economy or human health.

5b5c1ce0-463d-4158-922d-c4a7e01865bb.title: quadrat
5b5c1ce0-463d-4158-922d-c4a7e01865bb.description: A square or rectangular area used within a larger habitat to identify and count species, used as sampling technique.

cb1f6ada-5c3d-4dae-b109-45d08e5f2d32.title: hypertonic
cb1f6ada-5c3d-4dae-b109-45d08e5f2d32.description: Denoting a solution that has a higher concentration of solutes compared to another solution.

a31b9050-2c19-4ee9-836f-7f8cd4b662ec.title: gradualism
a31b9050-2c19-4ee9-836f-7f8cd4b662ec.description: The theory that species evolve slowly from existing ones over long periods of time.

425962ed-8845-4fb7-bd01-3e6686ff0934.title: T cell
425962ed-8845-4fb7-bd01-3e6686ff0934.description: A white blood cell, produced in bone marrow and matured in the thymus, which is responsible for the identification and killing of infected cells, the activation of other immune cells and the regulation of immune responses.

e4817f9c-7024-411a-bc5c-e9deefb8debd.title: commensalism
e4817f9c-7024-411a-bc5c-e9deefb8debd.description: A type of symbiotic relationship in which one organism benefits from living with, on or in another one without affecting the other organism.

147c2f50-b6aa-4a1f-9cc3-e1ffd288129e.title: gene pool
147c2f50-b6aa-4a1f-9cc3-e1ffd288129e.description: The total number of different alleles within all genes in a breeding population.

c0c913b0-862f-4335-b2ae-3256071057fe.title: incidence
