c0c913b0-862f-4335-b2ae-3256071057fe.description: The number of new cases (of an illness or event, and so on) occurring during a given period.

fbb22daf-9b6a-4455-92ef-1c67a4576a0b.title: accuracy
fbb22daf-9b6a-4455-92ef-1c67a4576a0b.description: The extent to which measurements are considered to be close to the true value.

46da7887-fd2b-4c9e-8704-5d3285c246fd.title: mean
46da7887-fd2b-4c9e-8704-5d3285c246fd.description: The sum of values in a dataset divided by the total number of values in the dataset. Also called the average.

4b51fe7c-376f-4cc5-b4a9-b165ac1f1b23.title: outlier
4b51fe7c-376f-4cc5-b4a9-b165ac1f1b23.description: A data value that appears to stand out from the other members of the dataset by being unusually high or low.

dc5b0da5-cfb4-420b-b29f-0ef39850ffef.title: percentage error
dc5b0da5-cfb4-420b-b29f-0ef39850ffef.description: The absolute error of a measurement expressed as a percentage of the recorded measurement.

39fb1b8a-ccbf-4f5e-8ffa-3aac94038663.title: standard deviation
39fb1b8a-ccbf-4f5e-8ffa-3aac94038663.description:
A measure of the variability or spread of a dataset. It gives an indication of the degree to which the individual data values are spread around their mean.

Extended in Mathematics Standard and Advanced: For a random variable, the standard deviation is the square root of its variance.

It provides a measure of the spread of the probability density function.

b1eba4e7-1b86-4872-b35b-f183fb46d653.title: pattern
b1eba4e7-1b86-4872-b35b-f183fb46d653.description: A pattern is made up of a number of elements that repeat or follow a rule.

f2fa89ad-22b2-4083-a964-c5dcb94e1188.title: cellular respiration
f2fa89ad-22b2-4083-a964-c5dcb94e1188.description: The process by which a living organism or cells break down organic molecules to release energy. Cellular respiration can be aerobic (with oxygen) or anaerobic (without oxygen).

4c4264ea-d5fc-4371-a9c0-e6b2ca34a113.title: chromosome
4c4264ea-d5fc-4371-a9c0-e6b2ca34a113.description: Chromosomes are tiny structures found in all living cells. They are made up of DNA and proteins, which contain the genetic information that determine how an organism develops and functions.

23d5304a-62a6-4249-933a-78f2e8d2c252.title: controlled variable
23d5304a-62a6-4249-933a-78f2e8d2c252.description: A variable that is kept constant (or changed in constant ways) during an investigation. For example, the same amount of water would be a controlled variable in an investigation comparing solubility.

172917fb-aa1d-4687-a1a9-1bfe14057386.title: dependent variable
172917fb-aa1d-4687-a1a9-1bfe14057386.description: The factor in an experiment that changes in response to changes to the independent variable.

b5236910-8ed1-4470-9dc4-bbc26c77c560.title: DNA
b5236910-8ed1-4470-9dc4-bbc26c77c560.description: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is a molecule found in cells that carries the genetic instructions for the development, functioning, growth, and reproduction of all living organisms including viruses.

dd6d3782-54ef-47ff-8568-028bc4eb778e.title: experimental control
dd6d3782-54ef-47ff-8568-028bc4eb778e.description:
The sample in an experiment to which all the other samples are compared.

Extended in Science 11–12: The sample in an experiment that does not receive the independent variable.

02c60955-d27d-4281-b7f7-607e832ad928.title: fossil
02c60955-d27d-4281-b7f7-607e832ad928.description: The preserved remains or traces of an organism, such as a skeleton, or a footprint, from a past geological age, typically found in sedimentary rock layers.

df100853-717f-4099-b22f-d6cbaa5edde0.title: genetic variation
df100853-717f-4099-b22f-d6cbaa5edde0.description: The diversity in genetic makeup within a population or species, resulting from differences in the genetic information carried by individuals.

aa026ca6-7589-4397-8d13-28511df46bff.title: homeostasis
aa026ca6-7589-4397-8d13-28511df46bff.description: The ability of an organism to maintain stable internal conditions despite external changes.

3acb684d-c6a7-4300-8865-f5187a3ae83d.title: independent variable
3acb684d-c6a7-4300-8865-f5187a3ae83d.description: The variable that is deliberately changed, often through a series of pre-set values.

f42984d6-c2b2-4468-a279-0c75dbcd2083.title: mutation
f42984d6-c2b2-4468-a279-0c75dbcd2083.description:
A change in genetic material (DNA).

Extended in Biology 11–12: Occurs due to an error during DNA replication.

bba5121c-2e1e-4d98-8dfc-b01df4043874.title: natural selection
bba5121c-2e1e-4d98-8dfc-b01df4043874.description: The process by which organisms with traits that are better suited to their environment survive and reproduce more successfully than those with less favourable traits. This leads to the gradual change or adaptation of a population over time.

f038a017-4c60-4c31-98a8-87e39eb1304f.title: phloem
f038a017-4c60-4c31-98a8-87e39eb1304f.description: A tissue in vascular plants that transports organic nutrients, particularly sugars, from leaves to other parts of the plant, including roots, stems and developing fruits.

b5cd04a0-f03f-4acf-b3d8-50d67395c814.title: photosynthesis
b5cd04a0-f03f-4acf-b3d8-50d67395c814.description: A chemical process that uses sunlight and chlorophyll to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose, oxygen and water.

b03e3232-2b7f-4dcf-ace4-0fa134fbeeb3.title: precision
b03e3232-2b7f-4dcf-ace4-0fa134fbeeb3.description: The extent to which repeated measurements of the same item are close to each other.

3aa3762d-40a9-435d-a851-c7b64486faa8.title: prediction
3aa3762d-40a9-435d-a851-c7b64486faa8.description: A statement or estimate about what will happen in the future, often based on available evidence, past experiences or statistical analysis.

dad16806-8ef2-4d3c-a4f6-4cc07ed9b273.title: qualitative
dad16806-8ef2-4d3c-a4f6-4cc07ed9b273.description: To use descriptive explanations involving features, characteristics or properties to identify important components. Data and information that is not numerical in nature.

d34bbe1b-441a-40dd-9c3d-31de49066851.title: quantitative
d34bbe1b-441a-40dd-9c3d-31de49066851.description: Data or components that can be expressed or measured numerically, including chemical formulae or numbers.

6cd7a6f3-12de-47e7-8b61-ec640dae3247.title: range (of a dataset)
6cd7a6f3-12de-47e7-8b61-ec640dae3247.description: The difference between the highest and lowest values in a dataset.

b049755e-fe68-412a-bb1d-02ae7d63d2b1.title: reliability
b049755e-fe68-412a-bb1d-02ae7d63d2b1.description: An extent to which repeated observations and/or measurements taken under identical circumstances will yield similar results.

2cbba6f8-94e8-44a6-8b8a-62fd87561028.title: validity
2cbba6f8-94e8-44a6-8b8a-62fd87561028.description: The extent to which the processes and resultant data measure what was intended.

25e5c788-254e-4682-ba52-05c1d6b2cc13.title: conservation
25e5c788-254e-4682-ba52-05c1d6b2cc13.description: The careful management and protection of natural environments, including landscapes, ecosystems, habitats and geological or archaeological sites that hold historical, cultural, ecological, or scientific importance.

20d5398c-9729-4361-aa3f-8e86bbdcf2e8.title: hazard
20d5398c-9729-4361-aa3f-8e86bbdcf2e8.description: A source that poses a potential risk of harm or injury.

c32e0a01-49d6-465c-a876-1b0a3cd6408b.title: morbidity
c32e0a01-49d6-465c-a876-1b0a3cd6408b.description: The ill health of an individual and levels of ill health in a population or group.

6e3950a2-d4a0-45ef-9767-611dfd4d9fe9.title: mortality
6e3950a2-d4a0-45ef-9767-611dfd4d9fe9.description: Number or rate of deaths in a population during a given time period.

bac96eb3-0a4e-4a6b-b777-71771c8dd77c.title: prevalence
bac96eb3-0a4e-4a6b-b777-71771c8dd77c.description: The number or proportion (of cases, instances, and so forth) in a population at a given time. For example, in relation to cancer, refers to the number of people alive who had been diagnosed with cancer in a prescribed period (usually 1, 5, 10 or 26 years).

8bf1f85b-ab84-4d28-abbb-1b2c69679988.title: cool burning
8bf1f85b-ab84-4d28-abbb-1b2c69679988.description: A land management Practice used by Aboriginal Peoples using small, low-temperature fires to promote the regeneration of bushland and reduce the risk of intense, uncontrolled bushfires.

7dc51d10-2b96-4f5a-8b38-b7527511043c.title: bush medicine
7dc51d10-2b96-4f5a-8b38-b7527511043c.description: Medicines developed and used by Aboriginal Peoples in healing illness and infection.

b46db133-0aee-4c68-8b80-74df9ce946c6.title: causation
b46db133-0aee-4c68-8b80-74df9ce946c6.description: A relationship in which one event or action directly results in another.

5bcea525-4b40-4c2e-ba1f-34c916a76e1c.title: artificial selection
5bcea525-4b40-4c2e-ba1f-34c916a76e1c.description: The process by which humans intentionally breed plants or animals based on desirable traits.

7147753f-9de8-432b-b1e5-eb421cc0e6b6.title: genetic trait
7147753f-9de8-432b-b1e5-eb421cc0e6b6.description: Characteristics and qualities that offspring inherit from their parents.

5188f2de-54cb-4ef4-86cb-eb12f3efac9a.title: sedimentary (rock)
5188f2de-54cb-4ef4-86cb-eb12f3efac9a.description: Relating to rocks formed by the deposition and compaction of sediments – particles of minerals, organic matter or fragments of other rocks – that are deposited by water, wind, ice or biological activity.

20f333f3-889e-4edf-863d-cf0771611e0f.title: bush tucker
20f333f3-889e-4edf-863d-cf0771611e0f.description: Edible bush foods, including meat, fish, seafood, nuts, seeds, spices and fruits consumed by Aboriginal Peoples.

d5c7697c-2be4-44ac-9aa6-7fdc8ce3b6fc.title: observation
d5c7697c-2be4-44ac-9aa6-7fdc8ce3b6fc.description: To see, watch, perceive or notice. Observations can be made using all 5 senses as well as digital and non-digital tools that extend our senses.

f34e40ca-a636-4690-9cf6-65ff80018a6a.title: variable
f34e40ca-a636-4690-9cf6-65ff80018a6a.description: A factor that can be changed, kept the same or measured in an investigation.

1b0e54f9-3e49-4d63-a160-a91af24cb495.title: acid–base indicator
1b0e54f9-3e49-4d63-a160-a91af24cb495.description: A substance used to indicate an acidic or basic solution.

4aa9eca9-f920-4e54-a108-413f8137f1e6.title: substance
4aa9eca9-f920-4e54-a108-413f8137f1e6.description: Matter in the form of elements, compounds, or mixtures.

14074995-a37b-4b13-aecc-8900ab532c1d.title: mass
14074995-a37b-4b13-aecc-8900ab532c1d.description: The amount of matter in an object.

25a11560-268b-4ac1-8649-7ff367aa8ac5.title: complete combustion
25a11560-268b-4ac1-8649-7ff367aa8ac5.description: A chemical reaction in which a fuel reacts with unlimited oxygen gas (O2) resulting in the production of carbon dioxide (CO2), water (H2O), and heat.

08581114-36ca-48d6-aef5-ef30e266e04f.title: element
08581114-36ca-48d6-aef5-ef30e266e04f.description: One of a class of substances which consists entirely of atoms of the same atomic number, and which cannot be further divided by chemical methods.

cd390ad5-80de-43a3-94e4-10bb705d8e13.title: incomplete combustion
cd390ad5-80de-43a3-94e4-10bb705d8e13.description: A chemical reaction in which a fuel reacts with limited oxygen gas (O2). Can lead to the formation of carbon, as soot (C), or carbon monoxide (CO).

c2e70955-6d0c-411a-88bb-a04ecefd24de.title: matter
c2e70955-6d0c-411a-88bb-a04ecefd24de.description: A physical substance; anything that has mass and occupies space.

1627c5e1-92c9-4203-bc17-5ca653e129af.title: particle theory
1627c5e1-92c9-4203-bc17-5ca653e129af.description: The kinetic theory of matter that all matter consists of tiny indivisible particles that are constantly moving.

c708e0c2-f23a-4754-a94e-6caad60a2b71.title: periodic table
c708e0c2-f23a-4754-a94e-6caad60a2b71.description: A table in which all the known chemical elements are arranged in rows and columns so that elements with similar chemical properties lie in the same column.

51e392a2-d5a0-4a54-8b33-e6f34c5b8f68.title: solute
51e392a2-d5a0-4a54-8b33-e6f34c5b8f68.description: A substance that is dissolved by a solvent.

c75c7e9c-2350-45cf-aa0d-1d48fed6efeb.title: solution
c75c7e9c-2350-45cf-aa0d-1d48fed6efeb.description: A mixture made up of a solvent and a dissolved solute.

9edf7b3b-de91-420d-86a9-aba251625b05.title: solvent
9edf7b3b-de91-420d-86a9-aba251625b05.description: A substance, especially a liquid, that can dissolve other substances.

10ae30fc-2707-4553-b1fa-703a62417143.title: chemical reaction
10ae30fc-2707-4553-b1fa-703a62417143.description: A process in which the breaking and forming of chemical bonds transforms one or more reactants into different products and includes the release or absorption of energy.

c9c5dcc9-18be-4299-a319-7799cac69f71.title: acid dissociation constant (Ka)
c9c5dcc9-18be-4299-a319-7799cac69f71.description: The measure of the strength of an acid in solution.

633bcf35-26de-4731-b026-7e93e35fb499.title: addition reaction
633bcf35-26de-4731-b026-7e93e35fb499.description: A chemical reaction in which atoms are added to a molecule usually by the breaking of double or triple bonds.

45528e77-1f0c-4617-b4d4-216500395477.title: aliphatic hydrocarbon
45528e77-1f0c-4617-b4d4-216500395477.description: An organic compound arranged in straight chains, branched chains or non-aromatic rings (not benzene rings).

e29fd64c-085b-449f-b0c6-e56ab0af1866.title: amphiprotic
e29fd64c-085b-449f-b0c6-e56ab0af1866.description: A substance capable of accepting or donating a proton to act like either an acid or base.

c31ec4ae-2082-4315-b47a-9998d704ba62.title: atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS)
c31ec4ae-2082-4315-b47a-9998d704ba62.description: An analytical technique to determine and measure the unknown concentration of metal ions in a sample based on the amount of light it absorbs.

22acbbf4-4e9e-48a8-9b22-c1941b47313f.title: atomic emission spectroscopy (AES)
22acbbf4-4e9e-48a8-9b22-c1941b47313f.description: An analytical technique to determine and measure the unknown concentration of metal ions in a sample based on the amount of light it emits.

9f9628f8-5c24-4ecc-a614-504e7360c8e0.title: back titration
9f9628f8-5c24-4ecc-a614-504e7360c8e0.description: An analytical technique used to determine the concentration of a substance that is not able to be determined directly.

f1f0e3c4-928e-4498-ae2b-85aa8e460d38.title: base dissociation constant (Kb)
f1f0e3c4-928e-4498-ae2b-85aa8e460d38.description: The measure of the strength of a base in solution.

7a54e685-aaef-4436-8c82-ac07adf1f592.title: buffer
7a54e685-aaef-4436-8c82-ac07adf1f592.description: A solution that remains unchanged in its pH when small amounts of acid or base are added.

93dc1ca5-bc1e-4bb7-9449-41d17f4455e9.title: carbon (13C) NMR spectroscopy
93dc1ca5-bc1e-4bb7-9449-41d17f4455e9.description: An analytical technique used to determine the structure of organic compounds by observing the behaviour of carbon-13 nuclei in a magnetic field.

348b7965-1069-40fd-809a-ec654aa06dc2.title: cell potential
348b7965-1069-40fd-809a-ec654aa06dc2.description: The voltage difference between the 2 electrodes of an electrochemical cell.

a1c6b432-9ca2-4d43-83f6-689108b468da.title: chain isomer
a1c6b432-9ca2-4d43-83f6-689108b468da.description: Compounds with different arrangements of the substituents on the carbon chain and the same molecular formula.

6eb0ba29-9566-4b90-9801-2ac502d2b702.title: closed system
6eb0ba29-9566-4b90-9801-2ac502d2b702.description: A chemical system in which no substances are able to enter or leave.

fc09033d-22f8-4dd6-ba84-a0e5fc5e4e36.title: concentration of hydroxide [OH–]
fc09033d-22f8-4dd6-ba84-a0e5fc5e4e36.description: The number of moles of hydroxide ion in a litre of solution.

e5e4f43b-d6df-41ab-a95d-ddff922e6e55.title: conjugate acid–base pairs
e5e4f43b-d6df-41ab-a95d-ddff922e6e55.description: Two substances that differ by one proton where the acid donates a proton and becomes its conjugate base or the base accepts a proton and becomes its conjugate acid.

761b64db-d3be-4fbe-94fa-acd20c4d988d.title: covalent bond
761b64db-d3be-4fbe-94fa-acd20c4d988d.description: A chemical bond made when 2 atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

ebcdf588-3231-407e-b90a-89606602bedc.title: diprotic acid
ebcdf588-3231-407e-b90a-89606602bedc.description: An acid substance that can donate 2 protons per molecule in an aqueous solution.

2082003a-3efd-4a06-b153-d79bc8434620.title: dissociation constant
2082003a-3efd-4a06-b153-d79bc8434620.description: An equilibrium constant that describes the separation of a weak acid (Ka) or weak base with water (Kb).

7532cfe8-74f5-4bb2-993a-6d6e99102478.title: dissolution
7532cfe8-74f5-4bb2-993a-6d6e99102478.description: The dissolving of a gas, liquid or solid in a solvent to form a homogenous solution (gas or liquid).

c5f6b0bc-cc94-4d79-aa9f-70557a0360dc.title: dynamic equilibrium
c5f6b0bc-cc94-4d79-aa9f-70557a0360dc.description: A state in which there are no macroscopic changes to the system as the rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal and therefore the amount of reactants and products remain constant.

542cfd33-76c5-4200-a17b-88fd4f95c32c.title: electron configuration
542cfd33-76c5-4200-a17b-88fd4f95c32c.description: The arrangement of electrons in an atom’s orbitals, showing how electrons fill shells and subshells (s, p, d, f) according to energy levels.

ae8ec47f-66dc-4172-842c-5f39ebcca323.title: electronegativity
ae8ec47f-66dc-4172-842c-5f39ebcca323.description: The ability of an atom to attract bonding electrons toward itself to form a chemical bond.

162261a7-c275-4818-83ef-1b6b943ec1a6.title: empirical formulae
162261a7-c275-4818-83ef-1b6b943ec1a6.description: The chemical formula of a compound that gives the simplest whole-number ratio by atoms of each element in a compound.

0e2a9660-fbe6-4ef4-afcf-34f74fa2d736.title: endpoint (of titration)
0e2a9660-fbe6-4ef4-afcf-34f74fa2d736.description: The point at which the indicator changes colour to show the equivalence point has been reached.

11c2a056-35c1-4f81-a3aa-41266f435c22.title: enthalpy
11c2a056-35c1-4f81-a3aa-41266f435c22.description: A measure of the total heat content of a substance or system at a constant pressure.

fd20ebbe-d994-451a-93f7-debb29701be1.title: equivalence point
fd20ebbe-d994-451a-93f7-debb29701be1.description: The point in a titration when equal amounts of acid and base have reacted, meaning the moles of acid equals moles of base.

76b97d7f-8bc8-4474-8440-1e2ddb1de7a4.title: first ionisation energy
76b97d7f-8bc8-4474-8440-1e2ddb1de7a4.description: The amount of energy required to remove one electron from a neutral atom in the gaseous state to form a +1 ion.

511890de-4c7e-4a0b-a78e-03ff9ef96862.title: galvanic cell
511890de-4c7e-4a0b-a78e-03ff9ef96862.description: An electrochemical cell that generates electrical energy from a spontaneous redox reaction occurring within it.

e7a38958-8b64-4ee6-94c5-20c43e7af203.title: groups (within the periodic table)
e7a38958-8b64-4ee6-94c5-20c43e7af203.description: A vertical column of the periodic table.

f4b3cf3b-2a74-4381-8219-1306c1fc97d0.title: homologous series
f4b3cf3b-2a74-4381-8219-1306c1fc97d0.description: A family of organic compounds with the same functional group, similar chemical properties and general formula, where each successive member differs by a CH2 unit.

c09c578e-0de2-4f17-93ca-d4525f637303.title: hydrogen bonding
c09c578e-0de2-4f17-93ca-d4525f637303.description: A type of strong dipole–dipole interaction that occurs when a hydrogen atom bonded to a highly electronegative atom (N, O, or F) is attracted to the lone pair of electrons on another nearby electronegative atom.

21ac82bc-93b7-4189-85ac-05e3b9588891.title: ideal gases
21ac82bc-93b7-4189-85ac-05e3b9588891.description: A theoretical gas that perfectly follows the ideal gas law and assumes no interactions between particles and in which the particles occupy no volume.

92787eec-7ba0-4754-bbe2-f27db52c7638.title: infrared spectroscopy
92787eec-7ba0-4754-bbe2-f27db52c7638.description: An analytical technique that uses the interaction of infrared light with a sample to identify and characterise molecules.

185e928d-090f-45ac-b348-4d729aec75c9.title: intermolecular force
185e928d-090f-45ac-b348-4d729aec75c9.description: The attractions or repulsions between adjacent molecules.

c56f47b5-efa7-46d1-8e0f-dcd82b85393e.title: limiting reagents
c56f47b5-efa7-46d1-8e0f-dcd82b85393e.description: The reactant that is completely used up first in a chemical reaction, limiting the amount of product produced.

12f41a0e-f0e8-4ce5-ad50-370466987df2.title: molar concentration
12f41a0e-f0e8-4ce5-ad50-370466987df2.description: The number of moles of solute dissolved in one litre of solution.

9d3f310b-2fea-478f-b6d2-8a68a85c9af4.title: monoprotic acid
9d3f310b-2fea-478f-b6d2-8a68a85c9af4.description: An acid that can donate only 1 proton (H+) per molecule to a base

03be68be-1288-478f-8f4c-333f2e06a17e.title: open system
03be68be-1288-478f-8f4c-333f2e06a17e.description: A chemical system in which substances are able to enter or leave.

58e91129-4a00-4d34-8ac3-55b8c1bc7524.title: orbital
58e91129-4a00-4d34-8ac3-55b8c1bc7524.description: A region around an atom’s nucleus where there is a high probability of finding an electron.

6491899d-a813-45f6-8f80-bffd674e510b.title: percentage composition
6491899d-a813-45f6-8f80-bffd674e510b.description: Ratio by mass in which elements are present.

acd6b583-c000-4a24-963c-e6f0c372a18c.title: polymerisation
acd6b583-c000-4a24-963c-e6f0c372a18c.description: A chemical process where small molecules join together to form a large molecule.

4681bcf1-e271-44fc-8668-81387377003e.title: polyprotic acid
4681bcf1-e271-44fc-8668-81387377003e.description: An acid that can donate more than one proton (H+) per molecule.

7bc9396a-3375-411d-b450-cd2833c03810.title: primary standard solution
7bc9396a-3375-411d-b450-cd2833c03810.description: A solution made from a highly pure, stable and accurately weighable substance used to determine the concentration of another solution in titration.

8c2adc07-70f1-421d-b48c-d6cdb06ed011.title: proton (1H) NMR spectroscopy
8c2adc07-70f1-421d-b48c-d6cdb06ed011.description: An analytical technique used to determine the structure of organic compounds by studying how hydrogen nuclei (¹H) in a molecule absorb radiofrequency energy in a magnetic field.

51cca2fe-ec84-43a1-bb4b-8cdbceb8b876.title: reaction quotient (Q)
51cca2fe-ec84-43a1-bb4b-8cdbceb8b876.description: A value calculated using the concentrations (or partial pressures) of reactants and products at any point in a reaction (not necessarily at equilibrium).

a0b8239b-a4d6-444a-b518-6cff3db17ba2.title: redox reactions
a0b8239b-a4d6-444a-b518-6cff3db17ba2.description: A reaction in which oxidation and reduction is occurring.

8a76b265-d5b4-4807-95a0-6091255f4dd2.title: solubility product constant (Ksp)
8a76b265-d5b4-4807-95a0-6091255f4dd2.description: The equilibrium constant for the dissolution of a sparingly soluble ionic compound in water.

c2339e5a-6bf4-47d9-a7ed-71db0b37c74e.title: standard reduction potentials
c2339e5a-6bf4-47d9-a7ed-71db0b37c74e.description: The measure of the tendency of a chemical species to be reduced by gaining electrons measured under standard conditions.

121320f9-5d0b-4e90-a883-b8bea652c6c3.title: stoichiometry
121320f9-5d0b-4e90-a883-b8bea652c6c3.description: Study of quantitative relationships in chemical formulae and equations.

600bcf68-73ee-4003-bd65-bbed5bf0e0ed.title: substitution reaction
600bcf68-73ee-4003-bd65-bbed5bf0e0ed.description: A chemical reaction where an atom or functional group in a molecule is replaced by a different atom or group.

99cff91e-1a45-4852-b650-d6b5d97ace3b.title: titration curves
99cff91e-1a45-4852-b650-d6b5d97ace3b.description: A graph that represents the change in pH of a solution as a titrant is gradually added during a titration process.

8179340d-f94b-4fa6-90e2-86818b5dce79.title: triprotic acid
8179340d-f94b-4fa6-90e2-86818b5dce79.description: An acid that can donate 3 protons (H+) per molecule in a reaction.

775f4ff8-fd78-4327-9c04-bb9e413ce9b9.title: equilibrium constant (Keq)
775f4ff8-fd78-4327-9c04-bb9e413ce9b9.description: A numerical value that expresses the ratio of the concentrations of products to reactants at equilibrium for a reversible reaction.

037fae84-e6e7-4282-805f-46b2c25086be.title: crude oil
037fae84-e6e7-4282-805f-46b2c25086be.description: Oil as it is found naturally in underground reservoirs; a raw natural resource made from hydrocarbons that formed over millions of years from the remains of animals and plants.

3e419f2d-a525-4697-a914-a4de479610c0.title: decomposition
3e419f2d-a525-4697-a914-a4de479610c0.description: A chemical reaction in which a complex reactant (that consists of multiple components or molecules) breaks down into 2 or more simpler products.

fe2fe8b7-ba41-480e-932b-5178eadc06e7.title: electrostatic
fe2fe8b7-ba41-480e-932b-5178eadc06e7.description: Relating to electricity or fields that do not move in a current but are instead attracted to the surface of an object, as opposed to electric currents.

15c9120a-c137-4485-a1c0-a1090e3756b2.title: hydrocarbons
15c9120a-c137-4485-a1c0-a1090e3756b2.description: A group of compounds containing only hydrogen and carbon, such as methane (CH4), ethene (C2H4) and but-1-yne (C4H6).

45de7426-ff91-4019-abc6-13dde32da4bd.title: ionic (bond)
45de7426-ff91-4019-abc6-13dde32da4bd.description: A very strong chemical bond formed by the transfer of one or more electrons from one atom to another atom; the ions are held together by electrostatic attraction.

3218660a-0b02-4992-bfbe-033d145e601e.title: isotope
3218660a-0b02-4992-bfbe-033d145e601e.description: Variants of a chemical element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei.

5fe4bec7-df46-49c3-8048-97527c34e8d4.title: metallic bond
5fe4bec7-df46-49c3-8048-97527c34e8d4.description: A type of chemical bond formed between positively charged metal ions and the delocalised electrons surrounding them.

0ad7fc37-bb74-45ab-b24a-4d49450cbf8a.title: neutralisation reaction
0ad7fc37-bb74-45ab-b24a-4d49450cbf8a.description: The act of making a substance chemically neutral, so it is not an acid or a base.

07a26f38-41c1-412c-93dd-ba21413847ea.title: radioisotope
07a26f38-41c1-412c-93dd-ba21413847ea.description: An element that has the same atomic number and similar chemical properties, but different atomic masses.

b648632b-e782-4f7a-b742-3738f24f2285.title: saturated
b648632b-e782-4f7a-b742-3738f24f2285.description: A chemical solution which contains the maximum amount of solute that can be dissolved in a solution.

e2aa322c-c384-4c7b-a42a-fff247174968.title: period (within the periodic table)
e2aa322c-c384-4c7b-a42a-fff247174968.description: A horizontal row of the periodic table.

b06f9fb3-40d4-4e9b-bd69-a6ec2a9c362f.title: Cultural identity
b06f9fb3-40d4-4e9b-bd69-a6ec2a9c362f.description:
Central to Aboriginal ways of knowing, being and doing. Cultural identity includes values and Practices, connections to Country, family, Community, Dreaming, Lore, customs, art, dance and shared experiences.

See culture, Country/Place, Cultural Practices and language group

f9f4f01c-0241-4a31-9f2d-3a620876f511.title: mental health
f9f4f01c-0241-4a31-9f2d-3a620876f511.description: A state of mental wellbeing in which a person can function and manage ordinary stresses.

68939fd1-ba9a-4468-9ce9-0eda1ca7388a.title: milestones
68939fd1-ba9a-4468-9ce9-0eda1ca7388a.description: Behaviours or physical skills demonstrated by infants and children as they grow and develop.

985673bc-4546-4019-933f-6d07fef6158c.title: otitis media
985673bc-4546-4019-933f-6d07fef6158c.description: Infection of the middle ear. Otitis media is a leading cause of ear disease in Aboriginal children.

db925f3b-879b-4ed2-ad80-bcc98a415423.title: planetary health
db925f3b-879b-4ed2-ad80-bcc98a415423.description: The relationship between the health of the planet and the health of humans.

b099977b-421d-4136-a2c5-ce62fc55fa04.title: risky play
b099977b-421d-4136-a2c5-ce62fc55fa04.description: Play activities that involve a degree of challenge and allow children to test limits and explore boundaries.

aac836c8-74ff-4066-baf2-656d21e2375f.title: Cultural Practices
aac836c8-74ff-4066-baf2-656d21e2375f.description: Rules or behaviours and standards that guide Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ worldview. Cultural Practices guide spiritual beliefs, Customs, Lore, history and Tradition.

e0053dcd-a49d-41e7-8d08-a0ab6a288375.title: wellbeing
e0053dcd-a49d-41e7-8d08-a0ab6a288375.description: A sustainable state characterised by predominantly positive feelings, attitudes and relationships. It involves resilience, self-efficacy and a high level of satisfaction with self.

f25fd74a-b6e3-4bc8-a108-ab67b3c1970b.title: Classical language
f25fd74a-b6e3-4bc8-a108-ab67b3c1970b.description: Classical languages are any language with an independent literary tradition and a large and ancient body of written literature. They are no longer spoken as a first language.

6e8ffec6-a738-413c-a20c-e38586d49c15.title: cognate
6e8ffec6-a738-413c-a20c-e38586d49c15.description: A word which is directly related in origin to another; cognates have similar spellings and meanings.

2aca9010-43e8-4aa4-9a5e-5d47a95e4aa5.title: declension
2aca9010-43e8-4aa4-9a5e-5d47a95e4aa5.description: The inflection of nouns, and of words similarly inflected, for categories such as case and number.

6a337783-298d-433a-8184-df73643ad9f9.title: derivation
6a337783-298d-433a-8184-df73643ad9f9.description: A word which is formed from or based on another word.

4efb2d79-6fdc-4101-bf46-ee0495334dd6.title: lexical and grammatical chunks
4efb2d79-6fdc-4101-bf46-ee0495334dd6.description: A group of words that are commonly found together; a grammatical pattern, e.g. prepositional phrase, verb + infinitive.

875aaa28-9893-4ae7-a80c-8da796b069a8.title: morphological features
875aaa28-9893-4ae7-a80c-8da796b069a8.description: The patterns of word formation in a particular language, including inflection, derivation and composition.

83188252-d59f-42dd-be83-822e49f7df56.title: synthetic text
83188252-d59f-42dd-be83-822e49f7df56.description: Text in the target language written in modern times to assist reading comprehension for a diversity of learners.

1458452a-3c5c-4870-a1e7-7b38c1d7902b.title: tone
1458452a-3c5c-4870-a1e7-7b38c1d7902b.description: The attitude or feeling the writer expresses through choice of words and/or literary devices, e.g. solemn, playful, defensive or sinister.

1cdfac0c-39ad-4cd7-a10c-35bc5402df69.title: idiom
1cdfac0c-39ad-4cd7-a10c-35bc5402df69.description: A commonly used phrase or expression, usually figurative or non-literal, that has an understood meaning specific to a language or dialect, e.g. over the moon, half asleep, pull your socks up.

ba6b975e-44f6-4ddf-8bdd-909cfa1fa342.title: sentence
ba6b975e-44f6-4ddf-8bdd-909cfa1fa342.description:
A collection of words that conveys a complete thought, typically containing a subject and predicate. A sentence:

  • may express a statement, exclamation, command or question
  • comprises a main clause and sometimes one or more subordinate clauses
  • begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, exclamation mark or question mark.

See clause (main), simple sentence, compound sentence and complex sentence

7aaf762c-2d74-47b6-8380-7465b605a80d.title: communication
7aaf762c-2d74-47b6-8380-7465b605a80d.description: The purposeful interpretation and expression of meaning.

6f73864f-3eb0-4c5d-913c-975c80ecd56d.title: cues
6f73864f-3eb0-4c5d-913c-975c80ecd56d.description: Sources of information used to facilitate comprehension of language that may be visual, grammatical, gestural or contextual.

36f6cb04-21de-4d51-b5c2-87f7aa4e92ed.title: language systems
36f6cb04-21de-4d51-b5c2-87f7aa4e92ed.description: Includes the sounds, lexicon (vocabulary), grammar and alphabet/script of the language.

ea4eef4f-b34e-42e2-9647-53ee2f234bb7.title: moderately complex text
ea4eef4f-b34e-42e2-9647-53ee2f234bb7.description: A text in which the topic and/or type of text is familiar; however, it may be structurally and/or conceptually more challenging, with greater complexity of language. The text may require students to understand stated and implied meanings.

339b2901-cb9f-49f9-9007-70bd6aea5589.title: predictable text
339b2901-cb9f-49f9-9007-70bd6aea5589.description: A text in which the topic and/or type of text is very familiar; it contains mostly familiar language structures, but some unfamiliar language is present. Comprehension strategies may be used in conjunction with knowledge of language to understand the text.

53f89693-534d-419e-9df7-5f0203521237.title: pronunciation
53f89693-534d-419e-9df7-5f0203521237.description: A manner in which a syllable is uttered.

1af90774-bdbf-413c-be0e-5d7c4a50b3a8.title: read
1af90774-bdbf-413c-be0e-5d7c4a50b3a8.description: Process visual or tactile symbols (e.g. braille), words or actions in order to derive and/or construct meaning. Reading includes elements of decoding (of sounds and symbols), interpreting, critically analysing and reflecting upon meaning in a wide range of written, visual, print and non-print texts.

299abfd0-2bdd-4c11-801d-a20e60d73293.title: sound–symbol correspondences
299abfd0-2bdd-4c11-801d-a20e60d73293.description: A relationship between letters or characters and the sounds they make when pronounced.

8e001158-a24a-4082-a7b8-0852da79967b.title: sound system
8e001158-a24a-4082-a7b8-0852da79967b.description: Phonological components of the language, including intonation, pronunciation and stress.

dea2b1bf-c0d6-45ed-849e-4bbb47ea844e.title: stress
dea2b1bf-c0d6-45ed-849e-4bbb47ea844e.description:
An emphasis in pronunciation that is placed on a particular syllable of a word.

For example:

  • She will conduct the orchestra.
  • Her conduct is exemplary.

f3ddf64e-d051-43ec-89e7-346df74d2169.title: symbol
f3ddf64e-d051-43ec-89e7-346df74d2169.description: A letter, figure or other character or mark, or a combination of letters, used to represent something.

ce941859-72c4-40d6-adc1-1f91bf14025d.title: text types
ce941859-72c4-40d6-adc1-1f91bf14025d.description: Categories of text, classified according to the particular purposes they are designed to achieve, which influence the features the texts employ. For example, texts may be imaginative, informative or persuasive, or can belong to more than one category. Text types vary significantly in terms of structure and text features across different languages and cultural contexts.

6745bcfa-8a14-4f5d-ba8a-7086c1cc9689.title: visual
6745bcfa-8a14-4f5d-ba8a-7086c1cc9689.description: A visual item, such as a photograph or drawing; an image.

418709cf-0f33-4a29-9365-30eccbff7d4a.title: writing system
418709cf-0f33-4a29-9365-30eccbff7d4a.description: A method of visually representing verbal communication, based on an alphabet, characters and/or script.

636298c1-78e8-4fe7-a32a-381fd67eec1f.title: text
636298c1-78e8-4fe7-a32a-381fd67eec1f.description: Any written, spoken/signed, nonverbal, visual, auditory or multimodal communication. Texts may be extended unified works, a series of related pieces or a single, simple piece of communication.

369ecb62-25f2-4760-8f3b-6882df199ed0.title: text features
369ecb62-25f2-4760-8f3b-6882df199ed0.description: Structural or stylistic components that combine to construct meaning and achieve purpose. Can be recognisable as characterising particular types of texts.

1a3940e2-3898-4ddf-b0bb-bc7fa2b89d31.title: competition
1a3940e2-3898-4ddf-b0bb-bc7fa2b89d31.description: Rivalry between businesses that offer similar goods or services with each business aiming to gain a larger market share by attracting more customers.

756f0fb1-442e-4d77-ac7e-aaf89c74ee7b.title: competitive advantage
756f0fb1-442e-4d77-ac7e-aaf89c74ee7b.description: The ability of a business to outperform its rivals by differentiating its goods or services from those of its competitors or by operating at a lower cost.

e6af8df6-a6a6-45e1-88ff-e54894e189dd.title: consumer
e6af8df6-a6a6-45e1-88ff-e54894e189dd.description: A person or group who purchases goods and services to satisfy their needs and wants.

524d2d6d-8308-42fd-b484-3f5d16649fdd.title: consumer redress
524d2d6d-8308-42fd-b484-3f5d16649fdd.description: Options available for purchasers of goods or services to resolve issues that may arise when consumer guarantees are not met.

738a5865-3626-4361-87e6-02a6ce8f191b.title: corporate social responsibility
738a5865-3626-4361-87e6-02a6ce8f191b.description: When businesses consider the impact of their decisions on people, communities and the environment, in addition to focusing on financial performance.

3d79b47a-85c7-41bf-bd84-31fa2cfbc0de.title: credit score
3d79b47a-85c7-41bf-bd84-31fa2cfbc0de.description: A numerical rating showing a person’s financial reliability based on their debt repayment history, helping lenders predict the likelihood of timely loan repayments.

8ae33d96-3ead-4611-b9ef-a605ef919d55.title: demand
8ae33d96-3ead-4611-b9ef-a605ef919d55.description: The quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing and able to purchase at a particular price at a given point in time.

28a93a66-571d-45ab-8f19-454f9c0c86a3.title: elected official
28a93a66-571d-45ab-8f19-454f9c0c86a3.description: A person chosen through an electoral process to serve in parliament or at the local level in a council, representing voters and making decisions on their behalf.

126ccd71-d556-43dc-9292-bed027b2411d.title: entrepreneur
126ccd71-d556-43dc-9292-bed027b2411d.description: An innovative person who starts and grows a business by identifying and seizing market opportunities, and managing risks and rewards, with the aim of being successful and profitable.

78fb3e98-bf24-4f9d-aedc-a09ee6606c14.title: investment portfolio
78fb3e98-bf24-4f9d-aedc-a09ee6606c14.description: A collection of assets owned by an individual or an organisation. It is managed to achieve financial goals.

3b8f9ecd-71db-4ec8-aaab-ced2936e4eb4.title: legal capacity
3b8f9ecd-71db-4ec8-aaab-ced2936e4eb4.description: A person’s ability to make decisions that are recognised as valid and binding under the law.

18c720d6-4d56-473a-95f7-5cddb7cc2b1e.title: living standards
18c720d6-4d56-473a-95f7-5cddb7cc2b1e.description: The level of comfort, material wealth and wellbeing experienced by people, influenced by their income.

43858bd8-9459-4056-b33a-b125117f136f.title: minor
43858bd8-9459-4056-b33a-b125117f136f.description: A person under the age of 18 years.

93e5fc71-ba9c-4dc2-b141-cec14d5df619.title: non-legal rules
93e5fc71-ba9c-4dc2-b141-cec14d5df619.description: Guidelines set by an individual or a group that are not enforceable by law but govern behaviour within a specific context.

fd702942-1b01-478b-b94c-95d749ed6fa2.title: opportunity cost
fd702942-1b01-478b-b94c-95d749ed6fa2.description: What a person has to forgo if they choose to do A rather than B; the value of the next best alternative that is forgone whenever a choice is made.

b37a3d0f-944b-400a-979e-2ead8417bfae.title: public office
b37a3d0f-944b-400a-979e-2ead8417bfae.description: A position of authority within government filled through an election, where the elected individual represents the public and performs official duties.

312b4e5d-dd77-4f79-98a9-6f9f571a2c06.title: risk mitigation
312b4e5d-dd77-4f79-98a9-6f9f571a2c06.description: Action taken to reduce or manage potential negative impacts.

e88d2601-b949-4e37-a7bf-8486b8e9821c.title: scam
e88d2601-b949-4e37-a7bf-8486b8e9821c.description: A fraudulent scheme that tricks people into giving away money or personal details by misleading them about the nature or benefits of the transaction.

6be85e63-07a0-4b87-a2a1-121e3892aeab.title: sharing economy
6be85e63-07a0-4b87-a2a1-121e3892aeab.description: A system providing access to goods or services on a temporary basis as an alternative to purchasing, often through a digital platform.

79421981-cdaf-4205-8c71-b61571e84a1c.title: stakeholder
79421981-cdaf-4205-8c71-b61571e84a1c.description: A person, group or organisation that has an interest in or concern about something.

128c4f94-82d4-49a5-aab1-0231c4e0f972.title: supply
128c4f94-82d4-49a5-aab1-0231c4e0f972.description: The quantity of a good or service that businesses are willing and able to offer for sale at a particular price at a given point in time.

8ad2b4e2-a4a3-4e74-bfca-2b68d5319d40.title: target market
8ad2b4e2-a4a3-4e74-bfca-2b68d5319d40.description: The group of customers to whom a business intends to sell its goods and/or services.

c13be073-1596-4589-ab57-c0b77432775c.title: anthropometric data
c13be073-1596-4589-ab57-c0b77432775c.description: Measurements of the human body collected for the purpose of assessing physical properties, including size, shape and proportions.

697e49db-0fd6-4760-933a-8bc3b8ad30f0.title: axonometric projection
697e49db-0fd6-4760-933a-8bc3b8ad30f0.description: A drawing technique used to represent 3D objects using true scale, with one vertical axis and others angled, usually at 45° for architectural drawings.

ef1d97af-d795-4399-9c81-7dec3b84b203.title: cutaway view
ef1d97af-d795-4399-9c81-7dec3b84b203.description: A view represented in a drawing in which part of the exterior is removed to reveal selected internal parts or features of an object.

ac99bb9a-ba4b-48ce-804a-0b6c2985b9e3.title: exploded view
ac99bb9a-ba4b-48ce-804a-0b6c2985b9e3.description: An image of an object with individual parts shown separately but arranged to show the relationship and position of how parts of a product fit together.

4de8a269-45f4-4eb5-99b6-0492f361afa6.title: isometric projection
4de8a269-45f4-4eb5-99b6-0492f361afa6.description: A type of pictorial drawing using vertical lines and lines drawn usually at a 30° angle to the horizontal.

7a1e7829-2562-4593-81cf-557c58ee37fd.title: oblique projection
7a1e7829-2562-4593-81cf-557c58ee37fd.description: A type of 3D drawing where the front face is shown straight on, and depth is represented with angled lines, usually 45°.

d6039baf-0b0d-4253-82a7-cdf735067003.title: rendering
d6039baf-0b0d-4253-82a7-cdf735067003.description: The process of creating realistic images by adding colour, shading and texturing to an image. Renderings can be generated using hand techniques or by using software.

d89a5d2d-3671-43e3-8fe7-19c8f5de92ee.title: rigging
d89a5d2d-3671-43e3-8fe7-19c8f5de92ee.description: Creating the digital skeleton for a character or object inside a 3D model, so an animator can move, pose and control the character or object realistically.

13552ed7-7011-4a5d-ba5d-197c61025a40.title: haptic
13552ed7-7011-4a5d-ba5d-197c61025a40.description: Refers to the sense of touch. Often used to describe a method of output from a device that can be measured by feel or touch.

6d9bfdcd-572a-495a-a893-3d5d64cd9aea.title: project management
6d9bfdcd-572a-495a-a893-3d5d64cd9aea.description: The process of planning, organising, controlling resources, monitoring timelines and activities, and completing a project to achieve a goal that meets identified criteria.

0c1fc927-1fbb-4eab-b5ae-3a782e3689d4.title: Australian Drawing Standards AS 1100 (AS 1100)
0c1fc927-1fbb-4eab-b5ae-3a782e3689d4.description: The Australian standard for technical drawing. It defines the general principles for technical drawing including both architectural and mechanical designs.

c95dc70a-595e-4c0c-826e-21501e8b2ee3.title: block-based
c95dc70a-595e-4c0c-826e-21501e8b2ee3.description: A type of programming that uses colourful, draggable shapes that represent code. Blocks are arranged and connected to write programs.

80c87e64-6474-443a-9336-fc4f02a668ba.title: object-oriented programming language (OOP)
80c87e64-6474-443a-9336-fc4f02a668ba.description: A type of programming language that organises code around data, or objects, rather than functions and logic. An object is a data field that has unique attributes and behaviour.

a7e5bbe6-594c-49ff-9d71-a6f8f926c7ae.title: abstraction
a7e5bbe6-594c-49ff-9d71-a6f8f926c7ae.description: The process by which data and programs are defined with a representation similar in form to its meaning while hiding away the implementation details. Abstraction tries to temporarily ignore details so that the programmer can focus on a few concepts at a time. Algorithms must ultimately be broken down into simple instructions for a digital system to execute.

427f914d-f96a-430b-81f6-76dc7daf1780.title: algorithm
427f914d-f96a-430b-81f6-76dc7daf1780.description: A step-by-step procedure required to solve a problem. Algorithms may be presented in many ways, e.g. written instructions, flow charts or using a computer programming language.

5ed60a49-1c00-4c78-93e7-442bcd5d2f74.title: app
5ed60a49-1c00-4c78-93e7-442bcd5d2f74.description: A software program designed for a specific purpose to run on mobile devices or on a personal computer. An abbreviation of the word ‘application’.

917110c7-1433-489d-8ae2-5350a1f6211c.title: augmented reality (AR)
917110c7-1433-489d-8ae2-5350a1f6211c.description: A technology that replicates, enhances or overlays extra information about the real-world environment, using computer-generated data such as global positioning systems (GPS), sound, videos and images. Common examples include a car windshield with a heads-up display (HUD) that projects three-dimensional navigation information and virtual lanes, or a swimming telecast using a line to indicate the position of the record holder in relation to the actual swimmers in the race.

ce2682de-3e5e-444a-b120-cf0306e70f29.title: automate
ce2682de-3e5e-444a-b120-cf0306e70f29.description: The process of transforming and manipulating data that does not require user intervention. For example, through the use of formulae in a spreadsheet, new sets of data can be processed and the results recalculated automatically, or a webcam can be turned on as a result of movement sensor input.

a30a60d4-c797-4ab0-9f31-27737f270dd5.title: biometric
a30a60d4-c797-4ab0-9f31-27737f270dd5.description: A term that describes the source of data being human or biological.

9fd279d6-aa29-4781-98bf-e32cc6c56c5e.title: branching
9fd279d6-aa29-4781-98bf-e32cc6c56c5e.description: An instruction in a computer program or algorithm that causes different actions to be performed depending on specified conditions.

adf6bba9-054f-429d-9725-7091d7f2fd3d.title: cloud computing
adf6bba9-054f-429d-9725-7091d7f2fd3d.description: Distributing computing over a network where storage of files, processing of data and/or access to software occurs automatically on interconnected server computers to which the user’s device is connected. The term refers to accessing files, software and services over the internet.

3045546d-b490-47ee-8039-dbc59b4db5ca.title: cyber safety
3045546d-b490-47ee-8039-dbc59b4db5ca.description: A term that refers to behaviour and the precautions that may be exercised when providing personal information in an online or digital environment.

b71a4bf4-f418-46e8-bafd-ed9b8852acdd.title: cybersecurity
b71a4bf4-f418-46e8-bafd-ed9b8852acdd.description: The protection of information technology elements, including hardware and software, data or network services.

82e1ac02-16cf-4159-9010-d6cba6ca5f43.title: database
82e1ac02-16cf-4159-9010-d6cba6ca5f43.description: A collection of data organised by records and fields that can be easily stored, accessed, managed and updated.

2cdd4a98-cd7b-43dc-9b65-9af4f8bd018a.title: dataset
2cdd4a98-cd7b-43dc-9b65-9af4f8bd018a.description: A collection of data combined for a specific purpose.

e09cf8e2-5767-4b9d-9c52-cbce81ea7edd.title: decompose
e09cf8e2-5767-4b9d-9c52-cbce81ea7edd.description: To break a complex problem or solution into parts that are easier to understand, design and implement.

c90b606a-8cd0-4bc3-8719-ad0bc75e23c8.title: design and production
c90b606a-8cd0-4bc3-8719-ad0bc75e23c8.description: A process that typically involves identifying and defining, researching and planning, producing and implementing, and testing and evaluating to create a designed solution that considers social, cultural and environmental factors.

7d2885b4-1b30-4cf3-97cb-df705bbeeb35.title: desk check
7d2885b4-1b30-4cf3-97cb-df705bbeeb35.description: A method used by a human to check the logic of a computer program's algorithm to reduce the likelihood of errors occurring. This may be done on paper, using a diagram, or mentally trying a sample of typical inputs to see what the outputs would be.

c976f540-bf30-46a1-a741-af3da8f0698b.title: digital citizenship
c976f540-bf30-46a1-a741-af3da8f0698b.description: An acceptance and upholding of the norms of appropriate, responsible behaviour with regard to the use of digital technologies.

ae57b345-94ad-4d4c-a8b7-bcf50e158bf4.title: digital footprint
ae57b345-94ad-4d4c-a8b7-bcf50e158bf4.description: Traces of data left behind by a person using a digital system. A person’s digital footprint includes all information actively provided by that person, such as interactions on social networks, online purchases, emails and instant messages. It also includes passive information, such as logs of software installed and used on a computer, metadata associated with files, a user’s internet protocol (IP) address, a device being used to access a webpage, and a user’s browsing history stored as cookies or by internet service providers.

bf08fb80-3c8a-4300-af22-8d94e3370cb1.title: encryption
bf08fb80-3c8a-4300-af22-8d94e3370cb1.description: A process in cryptography of encoding (converting) data, using mathematical formulas, into a form that only an intended recipient can decode, often including a personal digital signature.

3f68c8fb-41b5-450c-af43-3314bfb89399.title: enterprise
3f68c8fb-41b5-450c-af43-3314bfb89399.description: An activity that produces goods and/or services. Enterprises are run for the benefit of an individual or a group of individuals. They can range in scale from a transnational corporation to home-based economic activities.

33bee857-07c2-4436-adf5-eb0f3770c432.title: function
33bee857-07c2-4436-adf5-eb0f3770c432.description: A term used in programming to describe a self-contained sequence of instructions that performs a specific task or tasks and is designed to be able to be reused throughout the program. Functions often accept some kind of input, perform some process on that input, and return a result that can be used by other parts of a program. Most programming languages allow for user-defined functions, but will also provide pre-defined functions.

85da52d9-96fc-4cbe-9deb-5c58b94ae7c8.title: general-purpose programming language
85da52d9-96fc-4cbe-9deb-5c58b94ae7c8.description: A coding or programming language used to write computer software. It uses letters, numbers and symbols arranged in a prescribed format (language) to instruct a computer how to carry out specific tasks. Also known as text-based programming.

d5fd92ba-ec64-425e-bfa4-af1e3ccc3b35.title: hardware
d5fd92ba-ec64-425e-bfa4-af1e3ccc3b35.description: The collection of physical components that constitute a computer system, all of which are tangible objects. Hardware includes both internal and external components of the system, as well as any peripheral devices that can be connected.

faa6558e-63a5-40fe-8c38-aa1aec6adc2b.title: html
faa6558e-63a5-40fe-8c38-aa1aec6adc2b.description: Hypertext mark-up language (html) is one of the first coding systems (or languages) designed to be used for web­page files so that an internet browser can efficiently display a page and elements for that page such as text, links and media in the intended position.

ca8b9e6b-aa2f-4374-bc1c-9e1a91cb074f.title: http
ca8b9e6b-aa2f-4374-bc1c-9e1a91cb074f.description: Hypertext transfer protocol (http) is a set of rules or standards for transferring files and messages on the World Wide Web, specifically to allow linking of files and text (see file transfer protocol). It provides a standard for web browsers to render pages (that is, to present them in an intended form) and servers to communicate.

9b1fae37-bc89-4698-a748-cbc585a22cb1.title: information
9b1fae37-bc89-4698-a748-cbc585a22cb1.description: The presentation of data in a manner that is readily understood.

f93c1047-7198-4459-aa16-af15dcc4890b.title: information system
f93c1047-7198-4459-aa16-af15dcc4890b.description: The combination of digital systems, people and processes that collect, manage and analyse data.

3f6be14d-1151-4f0e-a6da-a46be5309f33.title: iteration
3f6be14d-1151-4f0e-a6da-a46be5309f33.description: A repetition of a process in computer programming where each repeated cycle builds towards a desired result.

7b07e05e-e905-4a8b-bed0-43b51f6f17c1.title: lossless compression
7b07e05e-e905-4a8b-bed0-43b51f6f17c1.description: A type of compression algorithm that retains sufficient information to allow the original data to be perfectly reconstructed from the compressed data. It is used when it is important for the original data to be accurately preserved, e.g. in text documents, programming source code, application files or for archival purposes.

b4dc3adb-d387-4823-91c4-0d938a1301da.title: lossy compression
b4dc3adb-d387-4823-91c4-0d938a1301da.description: A type of compression algorithm that compresses data by discarding information that is not necessary to reproduce the original data with sufficient detail for the user not to notice the difference. It is used primarily for reducing the size of multimedia assets such as video, audio and photographs, especially when streaming or transmitting the data over the internet.

fe61ad8a-f217-462a-adde-f1eaa59c2f87.title: malware
fe61ad8a-f217-462a-adde-f1eaa59c2f87.description: Malicious software designed to interfere with the regular operation of a computer system. Often used to gain access to computers, it is usually hidden in other software to avoid user detection.

0d4e6fc8-b02d-4488-a218-3170e9352685.title: microcontroller
0d4e6fc8-b02d-4488-a218-3170e9352685.description: A small computer built for the purpose of dealing with specific tasks, such as managing the engine in a car, displaying information in a microwave control panel or receiving information from a television remote control. Microcontrollers process data inputted by users (e.g. keypad) or sensors (e.g. light).

7587eafd-9cf4-46f8-bb18-342b2c95cf4a.title: multimedia
7587eafd-9cf4-46f8-bb18-342b2c95cf4a.description: The use of digital technologies to present combinations of text, graphics, video, animation and/or sound in an integrated way. Where there is facility for a user to interact with multimedia, the term ‘interactive multimedia’ may be used. Examples include interactive games, media-rich websites, electronic books (eBooks) and animated films.

e385e352-d59b-4fcd-9513-75349aa5c5ef.title: network
e385e352-d59b-4fcd-9513-75349aa5c5ef.description:
A system of interconnected digital devices and/or people.

See social network

93df73ad-0a0b-441c-a6a6-0a2803528912.title: object-oriented programming (OOP)
93df73ad-0a0b-441c-a6a6-0a2803528912.description: A paradigm based on the concept of ‘objects’ that can contain data and code in the form of procedures. OOP language is a language based on the principles of ‘C’.

76add0d7-3723-4c73-80a9-6e97de27fb45.title: Open Systems Interconnection (OSI)
76add0d7-3723-4c73-80a9-6e97de27fb45.description: This conceptual model standardises communications between all of the elements within an information or computer system.

0cd5340d-d166-435b-977b-1fc619fa6925.title: product
0cd5340d-d166-435b-977b-1fc619fa6925.description: The tangible end results of natural, human, mechanical, manufacturing, electronic or digital production and processes.

09524a00-62d4-452f-9c83-c8e328dc629c.title: prototype
09524a00-62d4-452f-9c83-c8e328dc629c.description:
A trial product or model built to test an idea or process to inform further design development. Its purpose is to see if and how well the design works and is tested by users and systems analysts. A prototype can be either a physical object or exist in digital form.

See model

3fbb22aa-a822-4663-9ed5-eb5d651140c0.title: sensor
3fbb22aa-a822-4663-9ed5-eb5d651140c0.description: A device that detects and responds to some type of input from the physical environment.

cf34fa27-330b-4b54-b65f-a604849c52e5.title: social network
cf34fa27-330b-4b54-b65f-a604849c52e5.description: A structure that describes the relationships that exist between individuals and/or organisations. Social networking services and tools provide a mechanism for people who share common interests or personal ties to communicate, share and interact using a range of media such as text, images and video.

e56d4ba9-cabd-4754-9af0-277be26cdc97.title: sociogram
e56d4ba9-cabd-4754-9af0-277be26cdc97.description: A diagram that describes the social links or relationships that one person has with other people.

829ab539-196e-4b57-be53-8cb10b00b32b.title: structured English/pseudocode
829ab539-196e-4b57-be53-8cb10b00b32b.description: An informal high-level description of a computer program, process or algorithm. It is intended for humans to understand the flow of operations without necessarily needing to understand a programming language.

e37446ef-283e-42f8-8988-a7ceed598182.title: structured query language (SQL)
e37446ef-283e-42f8-8988-a7ceed598182.description: Specialist programming language used to manage data and access data in relational database management systems.

b10d972d-fa41-462e-b324-f7efca6643f0.title: TCP/IP
b10d972d-fa41-462e-b324-f7efca6643f0.description: Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) is the basic communication language or protocol of the internet.

8308c057-5f77-4370-ad3a-87988ec6f6a8.title: trace
8308c057-5f77-4370-ad3a-87988ec6f6a8.description: Following an algorithm to check its logic and correctness. This may be done on paper, using a diagram, or mentally trying a sample of typical inputs to see what the outputs would be.

9b7c808d-3773-4f8e-acda-ab262bf5fb42.title: transmission media
9b7c808d-3773-4f8e-acda-ab262bf5fb42.description: The means through which data is sent from one system to another on a network.

9edb248f-caa3-45ea-a9ae-151dcefd8ccf.title: User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
9edb248f-caa3-45ea-a9ae-151dcefd8ccf.description: An alternative to TCP/IP, UDP is a method governing connections of some applications on the internet.

a16f77b1-0527-4a19-bb9b-eacfa8c6c1df.title: user experience (UX)
a16f77b1-0527-4a19-bb9b-eacfa8c6c1df.description: The usability, ease of use, and enjoyment provided in the interaction between the customer and the product.

d0964d81-e3db-4008-b6a4-00ac8284a31e.title: user interface (UI)
d0964d81-e3db-4008-b6a4-00ac8284a31e.description: The means by which users interact with computer hardware or software. In software, this usually comprises fields for text and number entry, mouse pointers, buttons and other graphical elements. In hardware, switches, dials and light-emitting diodes (LEDs) provide information about the interactions between a user and a machine.

9fb2c860-4764-4402-bb47-0654ff7f5938.title: virtual reality (VR)
9fb2c860-4764-4402-bb47-0654ff7f5938.description: The use of computing technology to create a simulated environment. Unlike traditional user interfaces, VR places the user inside an experience. Instead of viewing a screen in front of them, users are immersed and able to interact with three-dimensional worlds.

27350877-6978-422f-8a07-83e4e19d23cf.title: data
27350877-6978-422f-8a07-83e4e19d23cf.description: A discrete representation of information using number codes. Data may include characters (e.g. alphabetic letters, numbers and symbols), images, sounds and/or instructions that, when represented by number codes, can be manipulated, stored and communicated by digital systems. For example, characters may be represented using ASCII code or images may be represented by a bitmap of numbers representing each ‘dot’ or pixel.

a9160ed8-1b9a-4915-805d-3359ba109dae.title: protocols
a9160ed8-1b9a-4915-805d-3359ba109dae.description:
A set of generally accepted standards or 'rules' that govern relationships and interactions between and within information systems. In communication systems including the internet, specific protocols allow for the successful transmission of data.

See Open Systems Interconnection (OSI)

cc4395d1-87aa-4d13-8791-c1687b349862.title: visualisation
cc4395d1-87aa-4d13-8791-c1687b349862.description: The presentation of data or information through pictures or graphics to help the intended audience understand its significance.

4ab7a956-b874-42c6-970c-02f6591f2935.title: artificial intelligence (AI)
4ab7a956-b874-42c6-970c-02f6591f2935.description: Intelligence demonstrated by machines. Sometimes called machine intelligence.

ea7bc467-d689-422a-a2a9-fc833be861d8.title: CAPTCHA
ea7bc467-d689-422a-a2a9-fc833be861d8.description: Completely Automatic Public Turing Test to Tell Computers and Humans Apart.

82e29234-465d-4350-8a3a-b492c7526d32.title: digital nudging
82e29234-465d-4350-8a3a-b492c7526d32.description: The use of user-interface design elements to affect the choices of users in digital environments.

82ddc71e-b42d-4b5d-8ebd-0dd7c21b027c.title: expert system
82ddc71e-b42d-4b5d-8ebd-0dd7c21b027c.description: A computer program that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to solve complex problems and emulate the decision-making ability of a human expert.

284f4aec-65f2-48e8-8ae1-ef703f777096.title: interactive media
284f4aec-65f2-48e8-8ae1-ef703f777096.description: The use of digital technologies to present combinations of text, graphics, video, animation and/or sound in an integrated way. For example, include interactive games, media-rich websites and electronic books (eBooks).

8683e9f6-0756-4786-95c9-d0c248731a3b.title: qualitative data
8683e9f6-0756-4786-95c9-d0c248731a3b.description: Information that is expressed in words and narratives.

ea3776c2-eed5-4333-8b84-ffb4beecdf60.title: quantitative data
ea3776c2-eed5-4333-8b84-ffb4beecdf60.description: Information that can be expressed with numbers.

f105dd95-3f56-4829-ad4e-e378d4223cc8.title: social media
f105dd95-3f56-4829-ad4e-e378d4223cc8.description: Websites and applications that enable users to create and share content or to participate in social networking.

1364d352-79af-4156-967d-7b9edb316837.title: data types
1364d352-79af-4156-967d-7b9edb316837.description:
Data types used in computing are expressed as either:

  • string/text
  • character
  • integer
  • floating point or real
  • date and time
  • Boolean.

a66dd84f-a43e-4356-ba57-feae49468ec1.title: digital technologies
a66dd84f-a43e-4356-ba57-feae49468ec1.description: Refers to electronic tools, systems, devices and resources that generate, process or store data, and may include applications, games, microcontrollers, mobile devices, multimedia, networks, robotics.

3f47746f-cbcb-416a-bdf0-6030bb5d5b18.title: gamification
3f47746f-cbcb-416a-bdf0-6030bb5d5b18.description: The adjustment of a task using digital technologies into a computer game in an attempt to make it more appealing.

b5fc3a87-ae2d-4a00-8586-d17431cb7ee3.title: intelligent system
b5fc3a87-ae2d-4a00-8586-d17431cb7ee3.description: A collective term for enterprise-based information systems that have the capacity to gather and/or analyse data and communicate with other systems, learn and produce targeted output to respond to the world around them.

8143595e-2f19-4ce6-aa6e-1758c28ed306.title: Internet of Me (IoMe)
8143595e-2f19-4ce6-aa6e-1758c28ed306.description: The internet of me (IoMe) loosely refers to technology which connects our minds and bodies with the online world. It transforms our biological and cognitive life into streams of data which can be monitored, shared and shaped.

1bd2e313-54d1-44b6-9c14-7d3017dd57f3.title: Internet of Things (IoT)
1bd2e313-54d1-44b6-9c14-7d3017dd57f3.description: Internet of Things (IoT) encompasses smart devices and smart objects that send and receive information using the internet and communication infrastructure.

ae8be89c-9c57-428a-8432-bacebd5403e0.title: metadata
ae8be89c-9c57-428a-8432-bacebd5403e0.description: A set of data that describes and gives information about other data. For example, the metadata of a photograph is the set of data providing information about copyright.

7680e71d-8ad9-406f-8380-6d83b6cdbe83.title: node
7680e71d-8ad9-406f-8380-6d83b6cdbe83.description: A point of intersection or connection within a data communication network.

e4f27c29-83d2-486d-9e15-07aeb5317301.title: producing
e4f27c29-83d2-486d-9e15-07aeb5317301.description: Actively realising (making) designed solutions, using appropriate resources and means of production.

654e1c34-13dd-4cab-a2cb-9541da557922.title: structured data
654e1c34-13dd-4cab-a2cb-9541da557922.description: Data with a high degree of organisation, such that it can easily be analysed and processed using algorithms. The organisation of the data takes on a form that captures the properties and behaviours of the source the data represents.

2e3656db-ba93-49b6-b349-aff561d0da6f.title: workflow
2e3656db-ba93-49b6-b349-aff561d0da6f.description: A sequence of processes and/or activities that a document or artefact transitions through in order to reach completion.

c4ff5566-b745-485c-9c98-7ef85356a8cb.title: Aboriginal Dreaming Stories
c4ff5566-b745-485c-9c98-7ef85356a8cb.description:
Stories associated with the beginning of everything, passed down through oral traditions, songs and ceremonies over millennia. Central to Aboriginal Peoples' beliefs about creation, spiritual and physical existence.

See Dreaming

6a29ed61-c66b-4dee-9b82-233052344e8e.title: art form
6a29ed61-c66b-4dee-9b82-233052344e8e.description: A category of artistic representation in Visual Arts distinguished by specific techniques and mediums, encompassing 2D, 3D and 4D creations.

104ad5f0-f70f-4341-8b52-4269f0a25764.title: atmosphere
104ad5f0-f70f-4341-8b52-4269f0a25764.description: The feeling or mood created through dramatic action.

e1d6213a-5927-41ea-943e-fb18888b7aaa.title: dramatic elements
e1d6213a-5927-41ea-943e-fb18888b7aaa.description: Role, character, tension, situation, space, time, structure, language, symbol, atmosphere.

7350a1b6-2dae-4616-8a6b-94f3a827a879.title: elements of art and design
7350a1b6-2dae-4616-8a6b-94f3a827a879.description: Visual and multisensory conventions, including colour, line, shape, space, texture, tone.

153efe3d-3a86-4b31-8326-e88f807b1f3e.title: elements of music
153efe3d-3a86-4b31-8326-e88f807b1f3e.description: Duration, pitch, texture, performing media, timbre, dynamics, expression, structure.

16cc0b31-bef6-481a-9615-077c0a638f4f.title: improvise
16cc0b31-bef6-481a-9615-077c0a638f4f.description: Generate spontaneous actions, movement or sounds in response to a stimulus.

f3139f19-012e-4562-8473-c18ab2d72024.title: level
f3139f19-012e-4562-8473-c18ab2d72024.description: The height at which a dancer moves in a space, which may include high, medium or low levels.

827b5ee5-1f25-42f5-908f-236feb479fdc.title: rounds
827b5ee5-1f25-42f5-908f-236feb479fdc.description: A part-song in which the voices sing the same melody but enter one after the other.

0f475fe5-4109-4949-9054-ed7e4ad16125.title: still image
0f475fe5-4109-4949-9054-ed7e4ad16125.description: A freeze frame, frozen image or tableau that performers make with their bodies, facial expressions and gestures to communicate an idea or a moment in time.

a11df7a8-8a90-4b7d-9e40-e56a97ef53d7.title: subject matter
a11df7a8-8a90-4b7d-9e40-e56a97ef53d7.description: The topic, content or aspect of the world represented in an artwork, as distinguished from its form or style.

dcd37d80-1129-4b85-9aa9-d187801c5413.title: tension
dcd37d80-1129-4b85-9aa9-d187801c5413.description: The energy which drives drama. Tension can be developed through embodiment, structure, problems, tasks, conflict and manipulation of audience expectations.

4d61ae87-21c0-465d-9335-1b13e1a4e65b.title: alignment
4d61ae87-21c0-465d-9335-1b13e1a4e65b.description: An aspect of safe dance practice. The relationship of the skeleton to the line of gravity and the base of support, which makes movement more efficient and reduces the chance of injury.

84f14566-fc76-4a98-b491-cd19343d3f04.title: dynamics
84f14566-fc76-4a98-b491-cd19343d3f04.description: The release of energy, weight and/or force over a period of time to create movement qualities.

222caaa2-47f0-44ce-891b-73ac1411325d.title: intent
222caaa2-47f0-44ce-891b-73ac1411325d.description: The purpose or message a choreographer or performer aims to communicate.

fede4fda-92cb-4294-a281-e445655da8dc.title: character
fede4fda-92cb-4294-a281-e445655da8dc.description:
A dramatic role built with complexity, personality and/or background.

See role

6c576279-6047-412e-acd9-c4f0a83db36c.title: dramatic play
6c576279-6047-412e-acd9-c4f0a83db36c.description: Using imagination to explore and enact ideas, actions, roles and situations.

c911012c-7e83-4f44-857a-234807e5754b.title: elements of production
c911012c-7e83-4f44-857a-234807e5754b.description: Set, costume, lighting, props, sound and technologies.

1ea4baeb-b0bd-4432-864f-5702621ca5f2.title: enact
1ea4baeb-b0bd-4432-864f-5702621ca5f2.description: Represent or act the part of an idea or character.

fe0083c0-f52b-4539-a61f-d4aca1da855d.title: role
fe0083c0-f52b-4539-a61f-d4aca1da855d.description:
Points of view, objects or personas presented through embodiment.

See character

f9ee0064-ab21-4897-a372-9b3ece4aa20c.title: gesture
f9ee0064-ab21-4897-a372-9b3ece4aa20c.description: A nonverbal form of communication using movement of part of the body, such as a hand or the head, to express a message.

778f7b44-b97f-4c60-8484-757d1f358b2d.title: Cultural Knowledges
778f7b44-b97f-4c60-8484-757d1f358b2d.description: Information and technical Knowledge about Country/Place, Customs, Lore, ecologies, environmental management Practices, medicinal and scientific Knowledge, connected to a specific Language Group.

d5ddd904-56ae-4cbe-abc7-59e40fdf618d.title: duration
d5ddd904-56ae-4cbe-abc7-59e40fdf618d.description: The lengths of sounds and silences in music.

0a7f9b92-7b91-4a6b-8bca-a05920918cad.title: expression
0a7f9b92-7b91-4a6b-8bca-a05920918cad.description: The musical detail that articulates a style or interpretation of a style.

cda7e298-e402-4ae8-8dc1-627483a47c37.title: listening skills
cda7e298-e402-4ae8-8dc1-627483a47c37.description:
Skills used to receive sound and understand the message conveyed.

This may include accessing music through other senses and/or the use of assistive technology.

201cb26e-0486-4377-b2ef-ca3d2b744ab5.title: performing media
201cb26e-0486-4377-b2ef-ca3d2b744ab5.description: The instruments, voices or sound sources used in a piece of music.

7b787b27-5071-45e2-8699-be4cbf3506da.title: pitch
7b787b27-5071-45e2-8699-be4cbf3506da.description: The relative highness and lowness of sounds.

2d53cc60-6842-405b-b170-6a0453a02fa4.title: timbre
2d53cc60-6842-405b-b170-6a0453a02fa4.description: The distinctive and identifiable quality of a sound.

5f50139f-c370-4028-a206-4f1e82aad927.title: context
5f50139f-c370-4028-a206-4f1e82aad927.description: The circumstances that influence creative works, practices, practitioners and audiences.

225729b5-519d-4fa6-bbbd-7c28c889441f.title: abstract symbolic movement
225729b5-519d-4fa6-bbbd-7c28c889441f.description: Shapes, motifs and phrases created by a choreographer to represent ideas, emotions and intent through symbols.

97ff01d9-bd60-465c-9803-3203f00b01af.title: accompaniment
97ff01d9-bd60-465c-9803-3203f00b01af.description: The choreographer’s use of music, sounds, silence, vocalisations, the spoken word, percussion and body percussion as stimulus, or to accompany dance works to support the intent.

24e296d1-32bc-47e8-b603-2db7f775f19b.title: contrast
24e296d1-32bc-47e8-b603-2db7f775f19b.description: A tool used by the choreographer to retain viewer engagement and to communicate their intent. Contrast may be achieved by manipulating the elements of dance and structural devices.

8eb8b6d9-6d4c-416e-b276-dff6abd813a9.title: repetition
8eb8b6d9-6d4c-416e-b276-dff6abd813a9.description: A choreographic device where thematically significant motifs and/or phrases are repeated to reinforce their importance in the effective communication of the intent.

c2cd383d-601b-4aeb-ae73-3f58b35a6c96.title: sequencing
c2cd383d-601b-4aeb-ae73-3f58b35a6c96.description: The ordering of movements and structural devices in a dance work to effectively communicate the intent.

eca60553-3f91-47eb-938d-9c3836e14b4c.title: variation
eca60553-3f91-47eb-938d-9c3836e14b4c.description: A choreographic device for generating new movement based on the manipulation of existing movement.

2d449099-bf3c-4eb2-a497-dee26168926a.title: dance technique
2d449099-bf3c-4eb2-a497-dee26168926a.description: Training that physically prepares the body to dance. It is based on safe dance practices and anatomical principles to build strength, coordination and endurance.

bbc4ad08-cf46-4281-bd5f-7c2f7560d191.title: dance work
bbc4ad08-cf46-4281-bd5f-7c2f7560d191.description: A coherent organisation of phrases and sections driven by thematic considerations that create a unified whole.

dec01863-1cc0-4940-a9a4-63f5ad68b85f.title: genre
dec01863-1cc0-4940-a9a4-63f5ad68b85f.description: A category into which creative works are grouped based on similarities in style, purpose, structure and function.

b8873612-78d3-4fa1-8de4-aebb7a37f2db.title: improvise
b8873612-78d3-4fa1-8de4-aebb7a37f2db.description: Generate spontaneous movement in response to a stimulus.

9c91a139-a653-4427-86d8-807771273eec.title: interpretation
9c91a139-a653-4427-86d8-807771273eec.description: The individual choices made by a performer, choreographer or viewer that establish a personal perspective relative to the communication of the intent in dance works.

e39d68af-1ff9-479a-9dcc-0cc6d4edcf27.title: kinaesthetic awareness
e39d68af-1ff9-479a-9dcc-0cc6d4edcf27.description: Sensing or perceiving the body’s muscles, joints and tendons while in motion or while still.

4f8cdc02-9988-4de1-a1cf-def28f6c354a.title: motif
4f8cdc02-9988-4de1-a1cf-def28f6c354a.description:
A thematic device.

A distinctive, recognisable movement or pattern of movements that introduces and develops the idea and intent in a dance phrase and work.

eb4f55dd-566a-4be4-b0f7-5dce31384983.title: personalised movement vocabulary
eb4f55dd-566a-4be4-b0f7-5dce31384983.description: Individualised movements created in response to a stimulus or task that are free from misappropriation and communicate the intent.

e3cb9fca-7de1-4e7a-9fe9-d65d3c8912fc.title: phrase
e3cb9fca-7de1-4e7a-9fe9-d65d3c8912fc.description: The fundamental unit of structure in dance. It consists of a series of movements linked by thematic intent which has a beginning, middle and end.

ba1c32d1-172b-456b-9345-27afd26c7424.title: structure
ba1c32d1-172b-456b-9345-27afd26c7424.description: Part of the forming process in composition and choreography. There are 2 main parts; organising the movement; and organising the dance.

2fea459b-72d6-4b7d-82f1-71028be3faa5.title: auditory elements
2fea459b-72d6-4b7d-82f1-71028be3faa5.description: The auditory components of an accompaniment that include structure, temporal, dynamic and musical qualities, thematic material and lyrics.

34e305e5-e3bb-4866-b091-fa15b6c03f3b.title: components of appreciation
34e305e5-e3bb-4866-b091-fa15b6c03f3b.description: Includes stimulus, idea, intent, elements of dance, auditory elements, abstract symbolic movement, structure, dancers and theatrical elements.

675815b9-73f0-4ebd-b22e-1a8ce7c9220b.title: components of choreography
675815b9-73f0-4ebd-b22e-1a8ce7c9220b.description: Includes stimulus, idea, intent, elements of dance, auditory elements, abstract symbolic movement and structure.

982d5d5e-edf6-4bbf-867a-eb3e0477df03.title: components of performance
982d5d5e-edf6-4bbf-867a-eb3e0477df03.description: Includes dance technique, kinaesthetic awareness, elements of dance, auditory elements, structure and interpretation.

5ba60abb-3e0c-48a2-beae-341156c973a8.title: consent
5ba60abb-3e0c-48a2-beae-341156c973a8.description: Informed and freely given agreement to engage in an activity, or for a specific thing to happen. Consent is denied when someone does not have the capacity to give consent.

b9a6e404-27c1-4b04-abb6-d03a5c5ff979.title: dancers
b9a6e404-27c1-4b04-abb6-d03a5c5ff979.description: In the Appreciation focus area ‘dancers’ refers to the person/ people dancing, their number, role, arrangement and contribution to the dance work.

90c38093-0b2e-4130-ab2c-7fc21e27e264.title: idea
90c38093-0b2e-4130-ab2c-7fc21e27e264.description: In dance ‘idea’ is a concept which a choreographer develops from a stimulus and is explored for its choreographic potential.

1e6764f6-b0cc-4f18-a9ae-987cc8872f49.title: stimulus
1e6764f6-b0cc-4f18-a9ae-987cc8872f49.description: The motivation that provides the initial inspiration for the choreographer to make a dance work.

fab0398e-3559-4527-86ec-a92a933273b1.title: style
fab0398e-3559-4527-86ec-a92a933273b1.description: Related creative works and/or practices that share distinctive conventions and/or characteristics.

db34af5a-1bf6-4e9e-8223-d1a2fc2287b3.title: theatrical elements
db34af5a-1bf6-4e9e-8223-d1a2fc2287b3.description: Setting and environment, costume, props, lighting, stage space and technologies.

d5a6d367-a582-438b-ba88-1d02a39ec173.title: transition
d5a6d367-a582-438b-ba88-1d02a39ec173.description: Transitions are connecting movements between shapes, sequences of movement, phrases and sections in dance works.

5295abdb-9ed3-459d-b537-4430776f8e47.title: abstraction
5295abdb-9ed3-459d-b537-4430776f8e47.description: The process of generating movement that is symbolic, or changing movement from being representational to symbolic.

1580c9e0-69ad-45df-8c16-482c271c6b44.title: cool-down
1580c9e0-69ad-45df-8c16-482c271c6b44.description: To bring the body back to its normal physiological level after fast, vigorous exercise or activity by gradually slowing the pace of activity or by doing gentle exercises or stretches.

1e1d18ea-ac33-4917-bbac-37f659c74e61.title: expression
1e1d18ea-ac33-4917-bbac-37f659c74e61.description: The communication of ideas, images and emotions by the performer.

9cfe68d0-accf-4d89-b11f-f625777dee29.title: generating movement
9cfe68d0-accf-4d89-b11f-f625777dee29.description: A process that begins with stimulus, idea and intent, and is developed through improvisation, abstraction, selection and refinement.

d715afb9-a7d1-4111-95fa-45e3aedd22ac.title: performance quality
d715afb9-a7d1-4111-95fa-45e3aedd22ac.description: The dancer’s skill in applying projection, focus, musicality, quality of line, kinaesthetic awareness, commitment and confidence in order to communicate the desired intent.

10e9d88d-6af9-4fa5-bd95-03ab06f3b94e.title: sequence
10e9d88d-6af9-4fa5-bd95-03ab06f3b94e.description: A series of kinaesthetically linked dance movements not necessarily based on a compositional idea and intent.

3093cce5-1b76-4184-a4f9-2a44af7e50da.title: space
3093cce5-1b76-4184-a4f9-2a44af7e50da.description: Includes shape, level, direction, dimension, pathways, floor patterns and stage space.

38cbf0c2-3aff-4fb7-8a06-4d5cacabdeb7.title: time
38cbf0c2-3aff-4fb7-8a06-4d5cacabdeb7.description: Includes metre, rhythm, accent, tempo, duration and stillness.

0020e91c-6e1e-48d9-81e3-162bc8cfae36.title: warm-up
0020e91c-6e1e-48d9-81e3-162bc8cfae36.description: Movements and/or movement phrases designed to raise the core body temperature and bring the mind into focus for the dance activities to follow.

37cea71e-558b-44ac-80b7-1d1166c82c34.title: anatomical structure
