37cea71e-558b-44ac-80b7-1d1166c82c34.description: A specific identifiable part of the human body, such as the spinal cord, muscle tissue or skeletal system.

4913e31e-beea-4e48-b5d1-88869c761d1d.title: musicality
4913e31e-beea-4e48-b5d1-88869c761d1d.description: The attention and sensitivity to the musical elements of dance while creating or performing.

1d490e33-7945-42d5-a743-bd1f60118772.title: design solution
1d490e33-7945-42d5-a743-bd1f60118772.description: A product, service or environment that has been created for a specific purpose or intention as a result of design thinking, and design and production processes.

e58893a3-6efa-4a19-b6be-459aeab6f729.title: radical innovation
e58893a3-6efa-4a19-b6be-459aeab6f729.description: Groundbreaking innovation that creates a new product, service or process and has a significant impact on the market or ways of doing things.

889817b5-b892-4b12-9d81-5c73132bc5a0.title: disruptive innovation
889817b5-b892-4b12-9d81-5c73132bc5a0.description: Innovation that significantly changes or replaces an existing product, process or service.

fa644ea5-86f9-43cc-92a1-c45d08c13944.title: aesthetics
fa644ea5-86f9-43cc-92a1-c45d08c13944.description: Concerned with the appearance and visual impact or appeal of a product, system or environment and influenced by social, emotional and demographic factors.

826c8f14-ce2b-4bcf-b188-1c5462bbf775.title: end user
826c8f14-ce2b-4bcf-b188-1c5462bbf775.description: An individual or group who will use the final product, system, environment or event in a real-life setting.

b11c5fca-b5b1-4db9-a305-12a10c5eb45d.title: innovation
b11c5fca-b5b1-4db9-a305-12a10c5eb45d.description: The action or process of developing new items or changing existing products, systems or environment in order to improve their function, aesthetics or environmental impact.

6863b396-0266-48ed-865b-0b4005e75aab.title: incremental innovation
6863b396-0266-48ed-865b-0b4005e75aab.description: Small gradual improvements made to an existing product, service or process.

711af71f-aaad-44b5-8b18-178699f2f751.title: design brief
711af71f-aaad-44b5-8b18-178699f2f751.description: A statement clarifying a project task and defining the need or opportunity to be resolved. It usually identifies the users, design criteria, constraints, resources and timeframe.

45f2eb98-7c3d-418b-a455-8d3e98be73d7.title: universal design principles
45f2eb98-7c3d-418b-a455-8d3e98be73d7.description: Guidelines used to design products, spaces or systems that can be used by everyone, no matter their age, ability or background.

4240c557-fb6f-4166-b900-db80a406a68b.title: entrepreneurship
4240c557-fb6f-4166-b900-db80a406a68b.description: The process of starting and growing a business by turning ideas into opportunities. It involves identifying a need in the market, developing innovative solutions, and managing the risks and rewards to build a successful and profitable venture.

fe19c2de-ce21-4977-b376-7537c73a8415.title: data
fe19c2de-ce21-4977-b376-7537c73a8415.description: Information that is collected, organised and analysed for various purposes. It can be in the form of numbers, text, images or any other format that can be processed. Data can be represented using techniques such as tables, graphs and textual explanations.

7472629f-b089-4384-9fbb-f37931fe8add.title: artistic
7472629f-b089-4384-9fbb-f37931fe8add.description: Relating to the construction, deconstruction and/or expression of creative works.

e4c36b8b-50e8-42aa-a7f0-cad6eab1bdc6.title: aesthetic style
e4c36b8b-50e8-42aa-a7f0-cad6eab1bdc6.description: The visual or sensory qualities of a performance communicated though set, costume, sound, lighting and other design or performance choices.

1b452f27-90d7-422b-90eb-f7236c588132.title: audience engagement
1b452f27-90d7-422b-90eb-f7236c588132.description: The level and type of audience response developed in relation to intention and context.

5e1f0cfe-5885-4f24-be2c-7f31d92fae73.title: craft
5e1f0cfe-5885-4f24-be2c-7f31d92fae73.description: To create and shape a dramatic work using skills and intention.

56c9bd2f-bb52-416e-bcd7-9f944902e4e9.title: directorial concept
56c9bd2f-bb52-416e-bcd7-9f944902e4e9.description: The central idea or interpretation that shapes how a dramatic work is structured, staged or performed.

ca37e1aa-3469-41be-a2a8-97d39ffee07f.title: directorial vision
ca37e1aa-3469-41be-a2a8-97d39ffee07f.description: The director’s artistic perspective that guides the style, mood and overall audience experience of a performance.

959483f1-13bb-4f59-8630-c0683de8accc.title: dramatic processes
959483f1-13bb-4f59-8630-c0683de8accc.description: The ways in which dramatic practitioners shape meaning and experiences.

61ca72a8-c12e-40e7-ae91-7324ed216703.title: making
61ca72a8-c12e-40e7-ae91-7324ed216703.description: The ways in which makers create dramatic works, including their roles, responsibilities and approaches.

f9d7ddd2-b9af-461a-b7a8-5ef15333cb97.title: proxemics
f9d7ddd2-b9af-461a-b7a8-5ef15333cb97.description: The conscious use of space between actors, objects and the stage to indicate relationships, emotion and meaning.

470ca665-d8d7-469c-8017-6b83dbe9deb1.title: structure
470ca665-d8d7-469c-8017-6b83dbe9deb1.description: The way a dramatic work is shaped, which can include cause and effect, narrative, plot, and sequencing of images, motifs or ideas.

a9dac030-53be-4ea0-9fe0-a909067e60a7.title: create
a9dac030-53be-4ea0-9fe0-a909067e60a7.description: Develop and express insight, ideas or works in response to prior knowledge and new stimuli.

60658800-c531-42f1-8aa8-1036ff75543d.title: devise
60658800-c531-42f1-8aa8-1036ff75543d.description: Create through researching, experimenting, structuring and refining.

892da4d9-f7fa-44dd-ac22-dc6bcde1e369.title: dramatic action
892da4d9-f7fa-44dd-ac22-dc6bcde1e369.description: The combined moments and experiences that create meaning, tension and audience engagement.

3abdb57b-783f-4ed4-b96e-62fb01b3131f.title: dramatic forms
3abdb57b-783f-4ed4-b96e-62fb01b3131f.description: Recognisable types of drama developed, performed or staged for specific mediums, such as theatre, audio, video or multidisciplinary drama.

bcc285dd-d546-4b89-a039-6a99822f4ea8.title: dramatic journey
bcc285dd-d546-4b89-a039-6a99822f4ea8.description: The way an audience, character or narrative changes through a work or experience.

bf5cf4d9-cd23-4525-aaac-a624e2a44432.title: dramatic meaning
bf5cf4d9-cd23-4525-aaac-a624e2a44432.description: Ideas, feelings, images and stories communicated with an audience.

8306dd9b-2c3f-4076-ad7a-4b8ccb61c0d2.title: dramatic practitioner
8306dd9b-2c3f-4076-ad7a-4b8ccb61c0d2.description: Someone engaged in the practices of drama, such as an actor, playwright, director, designer, stage manager, deviser or drama student.

f7dc3e14-a90c-466f-8440-42a8d40c0451.title: dramatic works
f7dc3e14-a90c-466f-8440-42a8d40c0451.description: Dramatic performances and experiences, or materials such as scripts and designs.

9aba4c72-fb7d-43b0-a080-a38747675c3b.title: elements of drama
9aba4c72-fb7d-43b0-a080-a38747675c3b.description: Role, character, focus, tension, situation, space, time, structure, language, moment, atmosphere, belief and symbol.

954d03ec-3efb-4eaa-b366-bdcf810989d2.title: elements of performance
954d03ec-3efb-4eaa-b366-bdcf810989d2.description:
Voice and movement refined through the elements of dynamics, clarity, energy and expression. 

See voice and movement

10f2db9c-9365-4d94-999f-850d4d61248e.title: ensemble
10f2db9c-9365-4d94-999f-850d4d61248e.description: A group of people who perform together to produce a unified creative work.

08bca156-b13f-45dd-b328-530dbcfc1e5c.title: improvisation
08bca156-b13f-45dd-b328-530dbcfc1e5c.description: Spontaneous performance used as a key method of making drama, or as a rehearsal or live performance technique to communicate ideas and construct drama.

b071d38e-a8b8-4499-a773-17ba71b4eb23.title: language
b071d38e-a8b8-4499-a773-17ba71b4eb23.description: Ways of expressing and receiving images, ideas, feelings and stories using spoken, visual, written, and/or gestural communication strategies.

0de83244-8165-4d54-8a1f-5c86519063c0.title: movement
0de83244-8165-4d54-8a1f-5c86519063c0.description: The processes or results of moving performers, objects, set, lighting and/or audiences in dramatic works and experiences.

47e110e7-109d-4763-957e-edf91c89a39e.title: perspective
47e110e7-109d-4763-957e-edf91c89a39e.description: How someone perceives or considers ideas, images and experiences.

732183ca-71ef-4670-b753-5a06f6b00e4a.title: rehearse
732183ca-71ef-4670-b753-5a06f6b00e4a.description: To train, practise or refine a work before sharing it with an audience.

dd19f15b-265e-4122-8874-5b4b1da37efa.title: scripted
dd19f15b-265e-4122-8874-5b4b1da37efa.description: Drama developed or interpreted from a working text.

f7c2ebfc-93e1-42b4-952a-60722371ae4f.title: shape
f7c2ebfc-93e1-42b4-952a-60722371ae4f.description: To develop, structure and refine a creative work.

8c1e8d44-ae34-4a2e-8dee-c0725aac96a0.title: stage
8c1e8d44-ae34-4a2e-8dee-c0725aac96a0.description: To produce or perform a dramatic work for an audience.

a4c9c4de-700d-48d1-a08a-6ee7caa0365f.title: transition
a4c9c4de-700d-48d1-a08a-6ee7caa0365f.description: A change from one scene, moment or idea to another.

979c7878-768a-408d-b899-bc428f5fa34d.title: voice
979c7878-768a-408d-b899-bc428f5fa34d.description: Using speech, song, other vocal utterances, sign language or augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) technologies to communicate.

c049693c-064a-440f-889a-18eeb108cf5e.title: hybrid form
c049693c-064a-440f-889a-18eeb108cf5e.description: The combination of multiple art forms, genres or media to create innovative and interdisciplinary artworks.

dfe6f135-f9c7-48d7-9110-5d207beca261.title: audience
dfe6f135-f9c7-48d7-9110-5d207beca261.description: Individuals or groups who engage with and respond to a creative work.

c06f9499-e086-436f-a9c1-fb73894c861c.title: dramatic practices
c06f9499-e086-436f-a9c1-fb73894c861c.description: The ways in which dramatic practitioners engage in making, performing and appreciating.

779e02e6-8eb4-401a-a8cf-5f145e3a8042.title: moment
779e02e6-8eb4-401a-a8cf-5f145e3a8042.description: A point in time within a dramatic work or experience that creates meaning, engagement and impact in itself and in relation to the dramatic journey.

d2a20e4f-7d9c-44bb-b465-5a8a2fc0c7f1.title: multimodal communication
d2a20e4f-7d9c-44bb-b465-5a8a2fc0c7f1.description: Combining 2 or more expressive modes to communicate.

cf87c55e-7475-4b32-81a6-d6d77801a68b.title: offers
cf87c55e-7475-4b32-81a6-d6d77801a68b.description: Ideas or dramatic action that dramatic practitioners and/or audiences initiate and/or respond to.

e1c46fa9-3be9-4dfa-aa48-c3bf2d002cad.title: explain
e1c46fa9-3be9-4dfa-aa48-c3bf2d002cad.description: Relate cause and effect; make the relationships between things evident; or provide why and/or how.

2544ac29-0266-4bf0-96b1-357794af3a52.title: lateral continuity
2544ac29-0266-4bf0-96b1-357794af3a52.description: A geological concept that sediment layers originally spread out horizontally in all directions until they gradually thin or reach a boundary, meaning rock layers now separated by erosion or other factors were once connected.

aab12c1b-aee3-4255-8654-a63b93162707.title: absolute dating
aab12c1b-aee3-4255-8654-a63b93162707.description: The process of establishing an actual date, or date range, in numbers of years of a geological sample usually using radiometric methods.

67b2d4a5-cc55-43c2-b06d-0b1688490f20.title: adaptive radiation
67b2d4a5-cc55-43c2-b06d-0b1688490f20.description: The rapid evolutionary diversification of a single ancestral line into species which evolve different morphological features (adaptations) in response to different environmental selection pressures.

421bd312-b171-4ce6-86f2-8716e729e3d4.title: albedo (surface)
421bd312-b171-4ce6-86f2-8716e729e3d4.description: The proportion of incoming solar radiation that snow and ice reflect from Earth back into space.

69fbf05d-2a6c-4e0c-a15b-7d52031c5d9a.title: asthenosphere
69fbf05d-2a6c-4e0c-a15b-7d52031c5d9a.description: The layer underneath the lithosphere, extending between 80 to 150 km. It’s low-density and plastic.

4b85709f-8950-4236-b4b5-7c7edb079627.title: Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC)
4b85709f-8950-4236-b4b5-7c7edb079627.description: A major system of ocean currents in the Atlantic Ocean which plays a key role in redistributing heat, regulating climate and transporting nutrients and carbon across the globe.

02f0ca01-9758-48f5-a0c7-70e7658858af.title: banded iron formation (BIF)
02f0ca01-9758-48f5-a0c7-70e7658858af.description: A distinctive formation found in sedimentary rocks made of alternating layers of iron-rich minerals and silica-rich minerals.

cb587179-d3b8-4485-82e5-9b6d70fd57f5.title: basal drag
cb587179-d3b8-4485-82e5-9b6d70fd57f5.description: The friction between convection currents in the asthenosphere and ridged overlying lithosphere which affect plate movement.

36a58996-2e41-4a6b-9094-22c9005e8003.title: Cambrian event
36a58996-2e41-4a6b-9094-22c9005e8003.description: The unparalleled emergence of organisms including most ancestral lineages of present-day animal species at the beginning of the Cambrian period.

8efd9461-b2e3-4f0d-ac2b-8f14219cdb34.title: Cambrian metazoans
8efd9461-b2e3-4f0d-ac2b-8f14219cdb34.description: Complex multicellular animals that lived during the Cambrian period.

a02ad6be-1b3e-4ae1-9c9e-d78e236b526f.title: carbon footprint
a02ad6be-1b3e-4ae1-9c9e-d78e236b526f.description: The total amount of greenhouse gases, primarily carbon dioxide for which humans and/or organisations are responsible for.

262ff89a-40cf-4c8e-aa83-439073b99cfc.title: cementation
262ff89a-40cf-4c8e-aa83-439073b99cfc.description: A process in which sediment is chemically bonded together when minerals precipitate from the water they are dissolved in and fill the pore space between compressed sediment.

55317355-0783-4931-b935-eba58caf0832.title: clastic
55317355-0783-4931-b935-eba58caf0832.description: Describes rocks composed of fragments of pre-existing rocks.

0f8a22dc-0d5f-4942-ba6b-a273c0a90869.title: conquest of land
0f8a22dc-0d5f-4942-ba6b-a273c0a90869.description: The evolutionary transition of plants and animals from aquatic to terrestrial environments over hundreds of millions of years.

766f9a24-f3ae-4ea2-b55f-7040628a277a.title: contact metamorphism
766f9a24-f3ae-4ea2-b55f-7040628a277a.description: The process of igneous, sedimentary or metamorphic rock being changed from its original form due to high temperatures from being close to an intrusion of hot magma.

47794e1f-c15f-4480-a2c0-6158290820fb.title: convergent boundary
47794e1f-c15f-4480-a2c0-6158290820fb.description: A geographic location where tectonic plates are moving towards one another.

34c8447e-6486-49b4-be1a-3428fca0935d.title: critical minerals
34c8447e-6486-49b4-be1a-3428fca0935d.description: An element which plays a vital role in the operation of modern technologies, economic systems or national security and whose supply chain is vulnerable to potential disruptions.

f2726473-b4fe-426e-b114-80b550d8f5ba.title: cross-cutting relationships
f2726473-b4fe-426e-b114-80b550d8f5ba.description: A geological feature, such as a fault, intrusion, or erosion surface that disrupts or intersects another feature must be younger than the feature it alters or cuts across.

0ce3617b-7ea4-44dc-b0a6-2db4474cf9df.title: Cultural burning
0ce3617b-7ea4-44dc-b0a6-2db4474cf9df.description: Cultural burning is a Cultural Practice that draws upon the use of fire by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples to improve the health of Country and Place.

d25cc0f8-48c1-4666-b973-da809f384fee.title: dendrochronology
d25cc0f8-48c1-4666-b973-da809f384fee.description: A scientific method used to study Earth’s past climate by analysing growth rings in trees which vary in width, density and structure depending on environmental conditions.

30c5790c-f9db-470a-9492-ddf5259b0f00.title: dispatchability
30c5790c-f9db-470a-9492-ddf5259b0f00.description: A measure of how quickly and predictably a power plant or energy source can activated to maintain grid stability and meet both peak and off-peak demand efficiently.

3270dcc9-64c9-445b-bf97-a6315b41df1d.title: divergent boundary
3270dcc9-64c9-445b-bf97-a6315b41df1d.description: A geographic location where tectonic plates are moving away from one another.

737ef9e2-c861-4e55-866b-9c442296ff91.title: earthquake foci
737ef9e2-c861-4e55-866b-9c442296ff91.description: The place inside Earth’s crust where an earthquake originates.

544790ee-6976-4f79-9524-da37ffcedc2f.title: effusive eruption
544790ee-6976-4f79-9524-da37ffcedc2f.description: A type of volcanic eruption in which lava steadily flows out of a volcano onto the ground.

c590ac52-64be-434c-984a-ae97b5114e47.title: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO)
c590ac52-64be-434c-984a-ae97b5114e47.description: A natural climate pattern marked by variations in sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean, along with associated changes in atmospheric pressure and wind patterns.

1947e17f-a86b-4267-aa1c-dbcd14562a31.title: event conjunctions
1947e17f-a86b-4267-aa1c-dbcd14562a31.description: The simultaneous occurrence of multiple geophysical or environmental events, related or independent, that combined, produce greater environmental impacts than each would alone.

3d234146-3ff9-4577-8ab1-8eaa53faf391.title: extrusive igneous rocks
3d234146-3ff9-4577-8ab1-8eaa53faf391.description: Rocks that form when lava rapidly cools on the Earth’s surface resulting in fine-grained or glassy textures with microscopic crystals. Also known as volcanic rocks.

7a0f63e1-7d0f-4b4e-bf85-5c07f8725435.title: faunal succession
7a0f63e1-7d0f-4b4e-bf85-5c07f8725435.description: The principle that fossils appear in a consistent, recognisable order through geological layers over time allowing scientists to use fossil assemblages to relative date rock layers across different geographic regions.

5c4c7d19-20f3-4066-85f3-f235adc1bc48.title: feedback loops (climate)
5c4c7d19-20f3-4066-85f3-f235adc1bc48.description: Processes that amplify or reduce the effects of climate forcings. They can be either positive (amplifying) or negative (diminishing).

4d878408-123d-4403-8a1a-29ed0db77fd1.title: felsic
4d878408-123d-4403-8a1a-29ed0db77fd1.description: A group of light-coloured rocks or minerals rich in silica, low in density, high in viscosity when molten, and common in continental crust.

dc6ecb19-5565-45ae-985c-8cd0d3643cf8.title: fold belt
dc6ecb19-5565-45ae-985c-8cd0d3643cf8.description: A large geological region where crustal compression at convergent plate boundaries creates deformed and folded rock layers.

e314d054-44a7-4aef-89be-f6da25f73b22.title: geosphere
e314d054-44a7-4aef-89be-f6da25f73b22.description: The solid parts of the Earth, encompassing the crust, mantle, and core.

412c34af-7fb0-43d7-acfc-a57c5f29b17f.title: global warming potential (GWP)
412c34af-7fb0-43d7-acfc-a57c5f29b17f.description: A measure of a greenhouse gas’s heat-trapping ability compared to carbon dioxide (assigned a value of 1).

6c7285fc-aad5-4cc6-b587-902716f89072.title: greenhouse gases
6c7285fc-aad5-4cc6-b587-902716f89072.description: Gases found in the atmosphere that let sunlight in but prevent some heat from escaping back into space.

38b65df5-c54a-45b9-bc41-456d128bc3f1.title: hotspot volcano track
38b65df5-c54a-45b9-bc41-456d128bc3f1.description: A chain of volcanoes formed as a tectonic plate moves over a fixed area of intensely hot mantle that melts rock, creating magma and volcanic activity.

34f600ae-c6cc-43ea-bf98-c4f695cdf0a5.title: icehouse climate
34f600ae-c6cc-43ea-bf98-c4f695cdf0a5.description: A long-term period in Earth’s history when global temperatures are relatively low and polar ice sheets and glaciers are extensive or permanent.

b26f9510-9ba0-402d-a28e-5add6b7d5e50.title: inclusions
b26f9510-9ba0-402d-a28e-5add6b7d5e50.description: Any rock fragments found within another rock which are older than the rock they are enclosed in.

38ea108d-3472-483c-9567-35e7605a87c3.title: index fossils
38ea108d-3472-483c-9567-35e7605a87c3.description: Fossils of organisms that were abundant, widespread, and existed for a short geological timeframe, making them useful for dating and correlating rock layers.

49a0d841-bc1e-437c-b0d0-33eb550e3a26.title: inner core
49a0d841-bc1e-437c-b0d0-33eb550e3a26.description: The solid centre of the Earth, which is its hottest and densest layer, made mainly of iron and nickel.

0b426f1d-31a2-40de-bcc7-d1dea5eca666.title: isotope ratio
0b426f1d-31a2-40de-bcc7-d1dea5eca666.description: The quantitative relationship between 2 isotopes of the same element, typically expressed as a ratio.

c8724683-4d9e-4cb0-95c0-7de1701bc147.title: lahar
c8724683-4d9e-4cb0-95c0-7de1701bc147.description: A fast-moving volcanic debris flow made of mud and/or volcanic materials, such as ash, pumice and rock fragments, that flows down the slopes of a volcano.

3708b32f-7300-48ad-9dc5-e3c55c77a7e5.title: mafic
3708b32f-7300-48ad-9dc5-e3c55c77a7e5.description: Describes igneous rocks or minerals rich in magnesium and iron, typically dark-coloured and denser than felsic rocks.

7dfceec0-10ae-4b48-b0a7-feb909dd6d26.title: mantle
7dfceec0-10ae-4b48-b0a7-feb909dd6d26.description: The layer of the Earth located between the crust and the outer core.

9bccca33-7e2c-4825-af2a-5548929f89ec.title: mid-ocean ridges
9bccca33-7e2c-4825-af2a-5548929f89ec.description: Submarine mountain ranges or mountain ranges on the sea bed at divergent plate boundaries where spreading tectonic plates allow molten rock to rise, creating new ocean floor and basaltic mountain-forming eruptions.

7e40918e-23a7-4868-b637-270c82a57e82.title: non-clastic sedimentary rocks
7e40918e-23a7-4868-b637-270c82a57e82.description: Rocks formed by chemical precipitation or biological accumulation, not from fragments (clasts) of pre-existing rocks.

2294d52f-cf61-41c1-ba11-646ee0ef75af.title: non-renewable energy economy
2294d52f-cf61-41c1-ba11-646ee0ef75af.description: An economic system that relies primarily on finite energy sources.

12f3cd59-b48e-47d0-bf3a-b70dc6149e5d.title: normal faults
12f3cd59-b48e-47d0-bf3a-b70dc6149e5d.description: Fractures in the Earth’s crust where one block (the hanging wall) moves downward relative to the other block (the footwall), due to tectonic tension.

6bf51713-9c34-410f-93eb-2faa17eb3909.title: orbital eccentricity
6bf51713-9c34-410f-93eb-2faa17eb3909.description: The degree of elongation of a planet’s elliptical orbit around the Sun, ranging from 0 (circular) to 1 (highly elliptical).

ce26fce6-9427-4c78-a0de-609479330300.title: orbital obliquity
ce26fce6-9427-4c78-a0de-609479330300.description: The angle between Earth’s rotational axis and a line perpendicular to the orbital plane.

fad224ab-c056-40a3-8e75-61ff3fd27b27.title: orbital precession
fad224ab-c056-40a3-8e75-61ff3fd27b27.description: A cyclical change in the orientation of the Earth’s rotational axis causing it to trace a cone-shaped path over time, resulting in a gradual wobble of its axis.

4fec7663-ce50-4839-96b4-d6bfd401b440.title: original horizontality
4fec7663-ce50-4839-96b4-d6bfd401b440.description: The principle which states that layers of sediment are originally deposited in a horizontal or nearly horizontal position.

6ae61c1c-f047-4061-89ae-f2e2d8b03e49.title: outer core
6ae61c1c-f047-4061-89ae-f2e2d8b03e49.description: The liquid layer of the Earth located between the mantle and the inner core.

550d6245-062b-4ecb-824d-518cb65f8db5.title: photovoltaic
550d6245-062b-4ecb-824d-518cb65f8db5.description: Providing electric current using electromagnetic radiation from the Sun.

59d3556c-f836-4441-8f22-5806cae8e11e.title: planetary accretion
59d3556c-f836-4441-8f22-5806cae8e11e.description: The process by which planets form from smaller particles in a protoplanetary disk surrounding a young star. It is a key stage in the formation of planets, moons and other celestial bodies in the early solar system.

9db68716-64ee-49c2-8dc9-bbd728fc9844.title: plate tectonic supercycle
9db68716-64ee-49c2-8dc9-bbd728fc9844.description: The long-term repeating cycle of supercontinents forming, breaking apart and reassembling due to plate tectonics.

7711a7cc-b0df-42ac-9474-bbadba8831d1.title: pollen microfossils
7711a7cc-b0df-42ac-9474-bbadba8831d1.description: Microscopic fossilised pollen grains and spores from plants.

3c452fb5-e782-46b7-ba65-7e79416eb454.title: problem waste
3c452fb5-e782-46b7-ba65-7e79416eb454.description: A product that is hazardous, difficult to recycle, or harmful to the environment and human health and which requires special handling as it cannot be disposed of in regular landfill.

8dccf204-c7d2-40e5-9d4f-2fedb2de34d3.title: proxy data
8dccf204-c7d2-40e5-9d4f-2fedb2de34d3.description: Indirect evidence from natural recorders, or ‘proxies’, used to reconstruct past climates and environmental conditions before direct measurements existed.

56ba11a4-d1d3-4f73-97fe-cf5e2fae3c92.title: pyroclastic flow
56ba11a4-d1d3-4f73-97fe-cf5e2fae3c92.description: A fast-moving current of hot gas, ash, and volcanic rock fragments that flows down the slopes of a volcano during explosive eruptions.

3a49faaa-5b7e-46d2-a423-9f248e271c24.title: radioisotope decay
3a49faaa-5b7e-46d2-a423-9f248e271c24.description: The spontaneous decay of an unstable atomic nucleus into a more stable one, releasing energy or particles, and is the fundamental process behind radiometric dating.

4d94a9aa-aa8e-4b94-aedc-6375b6fc44d0.title: regional metamorphism
4d94a9aa-aa8e-4b94-aedc-6375b6fc44d0.description: A type of igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic rock that has been changed over large areas by both heat and pressure during plate collision and mountain-building.

b0554488-0534-490f-8aa6-0f3130ccc8e3.title: relative dating
b0554488-0534-490f-8aa6-0f3130ccc8e3.description: Determines the age order of rocks, fossils, or geological events by comparing their positions or relationships, to determine which are older or younger without knowing their exact age in years.

0b173c39-4436-46c7-a9b3-f4b628d71be1.title: renewable energy economy
0b173c39-4436-46c7-a9b3-f4b628d71be1.description: An economic system primarily powered by renewable energy sources such as hydroelectric, solar and wind farms.

96efbcbf-402e-4119-a65c-a3536466c5f5.title: reverse fault
96efbcbf-402e-4119-a65c-a3536466c5f5.description: A fracture in the Earth’s crust in which one block (the hanging wall) moves up and over the other block (the footwall) as a result of tectonic compression.

6d25eeee-13f0-4179-a312-ecd9eee6c905.title: ridge push
6d25eeee-13f0-4179-a312-ecd9eee6c905.description: The gravitational force exerted by the elevated mid-ocean ridge, causing the oceanic tectonic plates to slide away from the ridge towards lower elevation areas.

e8b31697-0527-4061-8ddf-8d446eb27ba4.title: seafloor spreading
e8b31697-0527-4061-8ddf-8d446eb27ba4.description: The process by which new oceanic crust is formed at mid-ocean ridges and slowly moves away from the ridge, causing the ocean floor to spread.

165d55c4-35f8-40cb-b95a-cbfd54e6b09c.title: seismic wave
165d55c4-35f8-40cb-b95a-cbfd54e6b09c.description: A vibration, typically generated by earthquakes or volcanic eruptions, that carries energy away from the source through the Earth.

500da3fd-6612-459d-b352-d7c466123e51.title: slab pull
500da3fd-6612-459d-b352-d7c466123e51.description: A tectonic force in which a dense, sinking oceanic plate drags the rest of the plate into the mantle, which is a major driver of plate tectonics.

30749dde-7652-4ed2-9552-040700023f01.title: soil profile
30749dde-7652-4ed2-9552-040700023f01.description: A vertical cross-section of soil that shows its layers (horizons) and reveals information about the composition, structure and formation of the soil over time.

ef899178-e079-475e-8ca2-9bc7388ae446.title: soil salinity
ef899178-e079-475e-8ca2-9bc7388ae446.description: The presence of dissolved salts in soil that occur naturally (primary) or as a result of human activities (secondary).

18e1feae-52c4-482b-bd0a-a0f72091419c.title: stratigraphic dating
18e1feae-52c4-482b-bd0a-a0f72091419c.description: A method for determining the relative age of rock layers and fossils by examining their position within a sequence of strata, using principles like superposition and faunal succession to establish an age order of geological events without knowing their exact age.

93e6bcdf-f636-4328-889a-cbdbfb80e198.title: strike-slip faults
93e6bcdf-f636-4328-889a-cbdbfb80e198.description: A type of fracture in the Earth’s crust where the dominant movement is horizontal and parallel to the fault line, rather than vertical.

7b80d4b0-64f4-4e5b-96c6-94ae6cc2723e.title: subduction zone
7b80d4b0-64f4-4e5b-96c6-94ae6cc2723e.description: A region of the Earth’s crust where one tectonic plate is forced beneath another.

ed3a3647-e5f1-480e-8d8b-a4de48e340c4.title: thermohaline circulation
ed3a3647-e5f1-480e-8d8b-a4de48e340c4.description: The global ocean circulation driven by differences in water temperature and salinity which affect water density and help regulate Earth’s climate.

4a57071c-c3d4-4384-82d9-0f5bf979a991.title: thrust belt
4a57071c-c3d4-4384-82d9-0f5bf979a991.description: A region of the Earth’s crust where rock layers are folded and pushed over each other along thrust faults by compressional forces.

9f3cf784-6421-40b1-ad6e-2e7ff674e743.title: tipping point
9f3cf784-6421-40b1-ad6e-2e7ff674e743.description: A critical threshold where small changes in temperature or emissions can lead to large, often irreversible shifts in the Earth’s climate system. Crossing a tipping point can trigger rapid and self-reinforcing changes.

804e696b-224e-4464-867c-8731d1ea0065.title: transform boundary
804e696b-224e-4464-867c-8731d1ea0065.description: A plate boundary where 2 tectonic plates slide horizontally past each other without creating or destroying crust.

8ac95b23-cea2-4f5d-beac-628fb1a307d2.title: unconformity
8ac95b23-cea2-4f5d-beac-628fb1a307d2.description: A surface in rock layers that represents a break or gap in the geologic record, caused by erosion or a period without deposition.

2ef52d1f-03cf-4503-9ebd-221719d22aa1.title: volcanic arc
2ef52d1f-03cf-4503-9ebd-221719d22aa1.description: A curved chain of volcanoes that have formed above a subduction zone.

0c6bf497-4621-41ff-9b47-a2d4f511f824.title: water cycle
0c6bf497-4621-41ff-9b47-a2d4f511f824.description: The biogeochemical cycle that involves the continuous movement of water on, above and below the surface of the Earth across different reservoirs.

6350fa56-c64c-4363-be17-54cf22e798da.title: uniformitarianism
6350fa56-c64c-4363-be17-54cf22e798da.description: The theory that the geological processes observed on Earth today (such as erosion, sedimentation, and volcanic activity) have operated in the same way throughout Earth’s history.

f939531c-c181-41bf-91b0-6abbf89f8468.title: climate change
f939531c-c181-41bf-91b0-6abbf89f8468.description: A long-term change in regional or global climate patterns, e.g. annual precipitation, frequency of weather events.

f394302c-53d5-4845-90a9-0ab9783894ab.title: biosphere
f394302c-53d5-4845-90a9-0ab9783894ab.description: The part of the earth that includes all plant and animal life forms.

9ff6e1c2-2d17-4895-b408-fe2c61076e7c.title: hydrosphere
9ff6e1c2-2d17-4895-b408-fe2c61076e7c.description: All water on the surface of the globe, including underground water and water in lakes, rivers and oceans.

6feaaa88-3d38-4aaf-99a6-4d9acd65a1bd.title: lithosphere
6feaaa88-3d38-4aaf-99a6-4d9acd65a1bd.description: The crust or solid part of the earth comprising the continental crust, oceanic crust and the brittle part of the upper mantle.

2bada490-d03f-4988-ae35-5fbbb26ffba2.title: Oral traditions
2bada490-d03f-4988-ae35-5fbbb26ffba2.description:
The Customs and beliefs shared through Storytelling and song.

See Oral histories

f45d56d3-f924-4e6f-831f-3e4a182970e0.title: law of superposition
f45d56d3-f924-4e6f-831f-3e4a182970e0.description: In layers of stratified sedimentary rocks, the lowest layer is the first to be deposited.

a711c60f-848f-48d1-a056-25c531ffbb91.title: igneous (rock)
a711c60f-848f-48d1-a056-25c531ffbb91.description: Rock formed from magma, either erupted from a volcano or cooled below ground in an intrusion.

dfe5bd02-78a7-4893-bcfb-20ef728ba3d0.title: introduced species
dfe5bd02-78a7-4893-bcfb-20ef728ba3d0.description: Organisms that have been intentionally or accidentally moved by humans from their natural habitat to a new location.

d3bd7ec6-2c41-4e8d-8e29-e85426d64401.title: metamorphic (rock)
d3bd7ec6-2c41-4e8d-8e29-e85426d64401.description: Describes a type of rock that has been changed from its original form by heat and/or pressure.

96acacad-2efa-491e-9742-8b160a057375.title: sustainable
96acacad-2efa-491e-9742-8b160a057375.description: Supporting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to support their needs.

4ce9a3e8-cea4-4259-b670-fcc07e8aea34.title: tectonic activity
4ce9a3e8-cea4-4259-b670-fcc07e8aea34.description: Processes and movement associated with the Earth’s tectonic plates. These movements can cause the land to be pushed upwards, sink downwards, or be translated horizontally.

0bfe08a7-4286-424c-a4cb-ae25d73893d4.title: climate
0bfe08a7-4286-424c-a4cb-ae25d73893d4.description: The average types of weather, including seasonal variations, experienced by a place or region over a long period of time.

fd74f1eb-6d9f-4e5a-aa0b-548a4d081665.title: natural hazard
fd74f1eb-6d9f-4e5a-aa0b-548a4d081665.description: Atmospheric, hydrological and geomorphic processes and events in the environment that have the potential to damage the environment and endanger communities, e.g. bushfires, tropical cyclones, floods, earthquakes.

c09f2d35-6656-4d67-b3ac-ebecf2159174.title: non-renewable (resource)
c09f2d35-6656-4d67-b3ac-ebecf2159174.description: A resource that becomes depleted or takes longer than a human life span to be restored.

4351a35e-1029-47ef-9f0e-b51dde68dbd5.title: renew/renewable
4351a35e-1029-47ef-9f0e-b51dde68dbd5.description: A resource that cannot be exhausted. A resource that can be restored in a human lifetime.

9574c063-4066-4cf2-853d-2cfdd269fe9d.title: tectonic plate
9574c063-4066-4cf2-853d-2cfdd269fe9d.description: A massive, irregularly shaped slab of solid rock, generally composed of both continental and oceanic lithosphere (also called ‘lithospheric plate’).

f38e3966-866f-4f88-9157-1e792ffdb7fa.title: absolute advantage
f38e3966-866f-4f88-9157-1e792ffdb7fa.description: A country's capacity to produce goods or services more efficiently than another country.

72e23cbc-3e09-48e1-a4d9-4a9ec21cdc0a.title: absolute poverty
72e23cbc-3e09-48e1-a4d9-4a9ec21cdc0a.description: People who cannot access the basic necessities of life, as determined by the World Bank international poverty line.

b04883b0-75cf-42d3-9b34-ae0bbaa9847f.title: actual output
b04883b0-75cf-42d3-9b34-ae0bbaa9847f.description: The total current production of goods and services in an economy, as measured by real GDP (gross domestic product).

a9c9ae1e-1d44-4f57-8894-718bd1abbadd.title: advanced economy
a9c9ae1e-1d44-4f57-8894-718bd1abbadd.description: A country with a high level of income per capita, a high level of economic development and a relatively stable economic base.

a5aac391-3171-4949-b868-6df123a21446.title: adverse selection
a5aac391-3171-4949-b868-6df123a21446.description: When a buyer or seller has more information than other party(ies), allowing them to maximise their personal benefit in a transaction.

b5695787-ba5b-408b-b96b-da2000668553.title: asymmetric information
b5695787-ba5b-408b-b96b-da2000668553.description: One party to an economic transaction who has more information than other involved parties.

446ab711-01c1-413d-a8d3-8cea11833dd0.title: automatic stabilisers
446ab711-01c1-413d-a8d3-8cea11833dd0.description: Counter-cyclical mechanisms in fiscal policy that alter spending or taxes when economic conditions change, and which do not require discretionary action from government.

f0c610e8-bdfa-47b7-8d04-f6e568500a48.title: balance of payments
f0c610e8-bdfa-47b7-8d04-f6e568500a48.description: The record of financial transactions between residents and non-residents over a given period.

32123294-ae38-4706-9873-967f7226eab2.title: binding price ceiling
32123294-ae38-4706-9873-967f7226eab2.description:
A maximum price for a good or service imposed by the government and set below the equilibrium market price.

See binding price floor

16911e90-02b0-4f16-a5ce-579c2923d0a0.title: binding price floor
16911e90-02b0-4f16-a5ce-579c2923d0a0.description:
A minimum price for a good or service imposed by the government and set above the equilibrium market price.

See binding price ceiling

c0a1262b-3b85-44ec-a215-3a908b14519f.title: bracket creep
c0a1262b-3b85-44ec-a215-3a908b14519f.description: When an increase in personal income causes an individual to pay a higher average rate of income tax because they’ve moved into a higher income tax increment.

ba2fc8db-78bf-4ede-9a1f-7e93b6cc5343.title: budget outcome
ba2fc8db-78bf-4ede-9a1f-7e93b6cc5343.description: The difference between government revenue and government expenditure in a fiscal year.

0d96a83c-fe45-4751-bb4a-a1d92cadfe8f.title: business cycle
0d96a83c-fe45-4751-bb4a-a1d92cadfe8f.description: Fluctuations in the level of economic activity (GDP) over time.

f6c5c554-d7a1-494c-b906-2df71c210f1a.title: capital
f6c5c554-d7a1-494c-b906-2df71c210f1a.description: Goods purchased for the purpose of producing other goods. It is frequently referred to as the produced means of production.

21d0bafc-4327-4174-a589-2385600e0cb6.title: capital deepening
21d0bafc-4327-4174-a589-2385600e0cb6.description: An increase in the capital to labour ratio so that each unit of labour has more capital to work with to produce output.

22fea6d2-b492-40cc-89bb-94b676c52125.title: central bank
22fea6d2-b492-40cc-89bb-94b676c52125.description: A non-commercial financial institution that manages the currency and monetary policy of a country.

dcf82732-9c1a-4759-a402-f49d0a8ac131.title: circular flow of income
dcf82732-9c1a-4759-a402-f49d0a8ac131.description: A representation of the money flows between the various sectors that compose an economy.

79253135-c72e-4d3d-a2c7-23ce58f9528f.title: command-and-control instruments
79253135-c72e-4d3d-a2c7-23ce58f9528f.description: Government policy measures that use rules and standards to limit damage to the natural environment from harmful economic activities and are enforced through penalties and legal sanctions.

f25a470e-419c-4d14-b5b6-ba6efe039bc7.title: common-pool resources
f25a470e-419c-4d14-b5b6-ba6efe039bc7.description:
Goods that are accessible to everyone, but the availability is reduced when one person uses them.

See public goods

e615c555-8f6a-4ede-bdf2-4c2abc8c4d06.title: comparative advantage
e615c555-8f6a-4ede-bdf2-4c2abc8c4d06.description: When a country can produce and export specific goods and services at a lower opportunity cost than another country.

0542b4bd-b9e1-4e52-85bc-42eb7637035f.title: consumer price index (CPI)
0542b4bd-b9e1-4e52-85bc-42eb7637035f.description: An inflation measure that captures the price change of a basket of goods and services over time which reflects the spending patterns of typical metropolitan households.

8706c312-4ec5-48ec-9b6d-1289e9320814.title: consumer sovereignty
8706c312-4ec5-48ec-9b6d-1289e9320814.description: The power of consumer demand to determine the type and quantity of goods and services produced in an economy.

959576d9-4bf9-4ac8-80c9-167373ae24eb.title: cost-push inflation
959576d9-4bf9-4ac8-80c9-167373ae24eb.description: Price rises that occur when the supply of goods and services falls, but the demand stays unchanged. As the supply can’t satisfy the demand the cost of the goods and services increases.

1976482f-6cd6-4e56-a77b-dc61af1ca8cb.title: crowding-out effect
1976482f-6cd6-4e56-a77b-dc61af1ca8cb.description: The decrease in private sector investment because of higher interest rates related to increased government borrowing.

f4b80522-a19d-4442-9bb6-585746c8467d.title: currency appreciation/depreciation
f4b80522-a19d-4442-9bb6-585746c8467d.description: The increase or decrease in the value of one currency in terms of another.

3a7f76dc-1efe-483f-bf13-2759d3059722.title: cyclical unemployment
3a7f76dc-1efe-483f-bf13-2759d3059722.description: A situation where individuals work less due to a decline in economic activity and a subsequent decrease in demand for labour.

ea47d9c3-61c7-423c-b94f-cdf05cd19cee.title: debt markets
ea47d9c3-61c7-423c-b94f-cdf05cd19cee.description: A financial market where households, businesses and governments borrow money through financial instruments.

80022fce-0aae-4b47-aada-8ca5990f0b84.title: deflation
80022fce-0aae-4b47-aada-8ca5990f0b84.description: A general decrease in the prices of goods and services over time.

7119e4d1-6446-46cb-92bd-ec7596f435cb.title: demand-pull inflation
7119e4d1-6446-46cb-92bd-ec7596f435cb.description: An increase in prices caused by aggregate demand accelerating faster than aggregate supply.

fd7a30d7-a575-4ff5-beaf-482029325f54.title: demerit goods
fd7a30d7-a575-4ff5-beaf-482029325f54.description:
Goods that, when consumed, generate more costs than benefits, and then tend to be overconsumed and overproduced.

See merit goods

ad937291-051f-47bc-8761-b7340bd52c21.title: dependency ratio
ad937291-051f-47bc-8761-b7340bd52c21.description: The number of people in a country’s population who are dependent (i.e. not working) on the working population. The dependent population includes people under 15 years of age and those over 65.

c8a357de-8668-4d43-9dca-b3eaffa5395f.title: developing countries
c8a357de-8668-4d43-9dca-b3eaffa5395f.description: Countries with low per capita incomes and low levels of economic development.

c9af2542-d141-4bc3-923e-97f7f3c6b06a.title: dumping
c9af2542-d141-4bc3-923e-97f7f3c6b06a.description: Selling goods in the international market at a price lower than the price charged in the country of manufacture.

67cd2b59-b5aa-4dc2-8f3d-7625fcc32253.title: economic agents
67cd2b59-b5aa-4dc2-8f3d-7625fcc32253.description: An individual or group that makes decisions that affect the allocation of resources in an economy.

e080414e-4380-4aad-9ae6-41b140dbc075.title: economic development
e080414e-4380-4aad-9ae6-41b140dbc075.description: The process of improving the quality of life of a population through sustained economic, social, and environmental progress.

c568e69a-bd8d-42f9-86e5-56df97e314dd.title: economic growth
c568e69a-bd8d-42f9-86e5-56df97e314dd.description: An increase in the volume of goods and services produced in an economy over a period of time.

94d61a67-23fe-4456-b985-01b74ea3bc14.title: economic model
94d61a67-23fe-4456-b985-01b74ea3bc14.description: A simple theoretical representation of real-world situations used to explain and test economic behaviour.

08d29854-8b20-4b3c-b92c-7a765665ea78.title: economic problem
08d29854-8b20-4b3c-b92c-7a765665ea78.description: The fundamental challenge of unlimited wants and scarce resources confronting any economy.

e2a5b119-6912-4c97-ace3-b9cb32c4cd8c.title: economic profit
e2a5b119-6912-4c97-ace3-b9cb32c4cd8c.description: Total revenue of a business minus the total costs, including opportunity cost.

b41b3a96-e7c5-49e9-849b-00e52bf97275.title: economic shocks
b41b3a96-e7c5-49e9-849b-00e52bf97275.description: An unexpected and sudden event that significantly affects a country’s or region’s economic conditions.

7c6ecb32-c150-48eb-bc02-88fa5d406ccd.title: economic systems
7c6ecb32-c150-48eb-bc02-88fa5d406ccd.description:
A country’s organisational structure for determining:

  • the way resources are allocated
  • how goods and services are produced and exchanged.

15861f44-1cf2-4bcc-9bd0-19742912081b.title: economies of scale
15861f44-1cf2-4bcc-9bd0-19742912081b.description: The savings made when producing a product in larger quantities allows for a lower cost per individual item.

549ef09e-310f-48a7-9797-1844d94a0af5.title: ecosystem services
549ef09e-310f-48a7-9797-1844d94a0af5.description: The direct and indirect benefits humans receive from natural ecosystems.

d03ee269-a026-4e2f-91f6-92112c7462e8.title: efficiency standards
d03ee269-a026-4e2f-91f6-92112c7462e8.description: Regulations that establish the minimum acceptable environmental performance of a good.

8c765b2b-387b-43f5-89b4-8179579d9f8d.title: emerging economies
8c765b2b-387b-43f5-89b4-8179579d9f8d.description: A country that has experienced sustained economic development and is transitioning from a developing economy to an advanced economy.

3d23c170-ff14-4d6a-b589-8602f5ed739a.title: equity markets
3d23c170-ff14-4d6a-b589-8602f5ed739a.description: The marketplace for buying and selling shares in the ownership of businesses.

750c5881-39c8-4a49-b24e-647c48696b63.title: exchange rate
750c5881-39c8-4a49-b24e-647c48696b63.description: The value of one currency expressed in terms of the value of another currency.

1b88d0e5-85a8-47e0-a149-b5585e885d19.title: excise duty
1b88d0e5-85a8-47e0-a149-b5585e885d19.description: The tax on excisable goods made in Australia (alcohol, tobacco, fuel, petroleum).

ffa392bb-5737-4b0c-9da7-15f193d18ec2.title: external shocks
ffa392bb-5737-4b0c-9da7-15f193d18ec2.description: An unexpected and sudden event that originates outside of a country that has economic impacts inside that country.

f2e981a7-ba77-49d4-8b88-dfd722c93bc4.title: externalities
f2e981a7-ba77-49d4-8b88-dfd722c93bc4.description: The costs or benefits of consuming or producing goods that affect third parties.

459e4f86-d24b-4a14-b105-9b344af09df9.title: factor markets
459e4f86-d24b-4a14-b105-9b344af09df9.description: A market for land, labour, capital or entrepreneurship.

ad646aa2-ab49-4a4a-91a6-39adeb945ff7.title: financial intermediaries
ad646aa2-ab49-4a4a-91a6-39adeb945ff7.description: An institution or agent that channels money between savers and borrowers.

78cd4b15-7a40-4c86-bcff-76981d135dc5.title: first-mover advantages
78cd4b15-7a40-4c86-bcff-76981d135dc5.description: The commercial benefit associated with taking a good or service to market before competitors.

ed9fa7e8-eaf1-44cb-b6df-92f5f9da2b4a.title: fiscal policy
ed9fa7e8-eaf1-44cb-b6df-92f5f9da2b4a.description: A government’s budgetary plan for taxation and spending.

445f12e9-7f23-4e9e-8177-5330ee70e270.title: fiscal stance
445f12e9-7f23-4e9e-8177-5330ee70e270.description: The intended impact on future economic activity of planned government spending and taxation.

19b4d920-b0dd-493b-8a94-dcc658b6e4f7.title: fiscal sustainability
19b4d920-b0dd-493b-8a94-dcc658b6e4f7.description: When a government does not need to undertake major changes to taxation or spending policies to keep meeting its debt obligations indefinitely.

6096c739-fb92-46e8-8cec-6a4bc6e5d308.title: floating exchange rate system
6096c739-fb92-46e8-8cec-6a4bc6e5d308.description: Value of a currency determined by the forces of demand and supply.

c9b3b024-7d1c-4cf4-9653-0973bbafd79d.title: foreign direct investment (FDI)
c9b3b024-7d1c-4cf4-9653-0973bbafd79d.description: The establishment of a new business or the purchase of 10 per cent or more of an existing business by a foreign entity.

b7e187e3-3888-4c6a-a097-a825e8e9b0ba.title: free trade
b7e187e3-3888-4c6a-a097-a825e8e9b0ba.description:
The buying and selling of goods and services between countries without government barriers. 

See multilateral free trade agreements

fe6bd48f-e0d2-4812-b749-ae3f7edeadb7.title: frictional unemployment
fe6bd48f-e0d2-4812-b749-ae3f7edeadb7.description: A type of unemployment that occurs as people change jobs or work status.

264c4077-f78a-469c-ae28-eedc2a0e3735.title: full employment
264c4077-f78a-469c-ae28-eedc2a0e3735.description:
A level of employment consistent with low and stable inflation that effectively equates to zero cyclical unemployment.

See cyclical unemployment

1e6ec946-5a4f-434b-8553-6b0e9f649776.title: full-time workers
1e6ec946-5a4f-434b-8553-6b0e9f649776.description:
An individual who averages 35 hours or more of work per week.

See part-time workers

4a7c9787-7705-46bc-9ea9-48e1a845f0f4.title: geographic mobility of labour
4a7c9787-7705-46bc-9ea9-48e1a845f0f4.description: The ease with which people can relocate for a job.

fbac9049-3ec4-4aab-86fd-10d448947f3c.title: Gini coefficient
fbac9049-3ec4-4aab-86fd-10d448947f3c.description: A measure of income or wealth inequality in an economy on a scale of 0 to 1.

4072ef43-dfed-4589-93ad-c07f8f07ce94.title: government failure
4072ef43-dfed-4589-93ad-c07f8f07ce94.description: Government policy implemented to address market failure which results in worse outcomes.

90fb168c-f37a-42fd-84f7-15cb74fff7e0.title: gross domestic product (GDP)
90fb168c-f37a-42fd-84f7-15cb74fff7e0.description:
The total value of all final goods and services produced in an economy over a period of time.

See national income

545cece1-de72-45a8-81a2-14db46e7df5d.title: hidden unemployed
545cece1-de72-45a8-81a2-14db46e7df5d.description:
Person(s) not in paid employment who are generally willing and able to work, but not actively seeking employment.

See underemployment

59813249-97eb-4635-8561-e4cbabc15b7b.title: imported inflation
59813249-97eb-4635-8561-e4cbabc15b7b.description: A rise in the prices of imported goods and services, commonly due to a depreciation of the currency.

aeb343ef-55b3-41bc-b543-e939e8c6a42a.title: incidence of tax
aeb343ef-55b3-41bc-b543-e939e8c6a42a.description: The entity that bears the legal or economic burden of a tax.

39a58bb4-38ef-40ae-9718-076adec0e314.title: infant industries
39a58bb4-38ef-40ae-9718-076adec0e314.description: A relatively new domestic industry vulnerable to more established and efficient international competitors.

87207d59-c122-4d9b-8450-4fdde2e1207b.title: inferior goods
87207d59-c122-4d9b-8450-4fdde2e1207b.description: Lower quality goods with demand that decreases as income rises.

1d6a63a9-c1e7-4709-b781-f7c046af302c.title: inflation target
1d6a63a9-c1e7-4709-b781-f7c046af302c.description: A central bank objective of keeping inflation low and stable.

f5a95bbf-ee07-4564-a598-0bb18df85386.title: informal economy
f5a95bbf-ee07-4564-a598-0bb18df85386.description: Unregulated economic activities that contribute to output and employment but are not captured in official data.

8cc80d4e-4f5b-44ab-832b-c0522d62858e.title: international business cycles
8cc80d4e-4f5b-44ab-832b-c0522d62858e.description: Synchronised fluctuations in the level of economic activity across countries due to increased interdependencies from trade and investment.

b889f9ee-1f52-4318-a733-ac455b0b66ba.title: labour force underutilisation rate
b889f9ee-1f52-4318-a733-ac455b0b66ba.description: The percentage of the labour force composed of people unemployed and underemployed.

3a9e43f2-0c96-4acb-9601-a658979a9549.title: labour market frictions
3a9e43f2-0c96-4acb-9601-a658979a9549.description: Impediments to the efficient allocation of workers in an economy.

b83d12ab-1dd3-418e-9aae-93c2ef63f3d6.title: law of diminishing marginal utility
b83d12ab-1dd3-418e-9aae-93c2ef63f3d6.description: The principle that the extra satisfaction a person gains from consuming an additional unit of a good or service will reduce at some point.

3b64da40-cf54-4d19-8286-8c56054e358b.title: liquidity
3b64da40-cf54-4d19-8286-8c56054e358b.description: The speed and ease with which financial assets can be converted into cash.

ce902e04-b86c-4261-a918-00b7e5ebc22f.title: local content requirements
ce902e04-b86c-4261-a918-00b7e5ebc22f.description: Government policy designed to support domestic industries by mandating the use of locally produced goods or services instead of competing imports.

c62c6567-7248-463e-932c-e1c916c806a4.title: Lorenze curve
c62c6567-7248-463e-932c-e1c916c806a4.description: A graph illustrating the distribution of income or wealth in a country by comparing the cumulative share of income received by different parts of the population.

a6d9fc7b-0c5e-485f-8bf5-fdcc350d5138.title: macroeconomics
a6d9fc7b-0c5e-485f-8bf5-fdcc350d5138.description: The study of the economy as a whole, focusing on aggregates.

3e08916c-027a-4f01-8599-0c9b52225776.title: marginal propensity to consume (MPC)
3e08916c-027a-4f01-8599-0c9b52225776.description: The proportion of each extra dollar of income that is spent.

38762fc5-78e8-43a7-bdda-a21ceda31617.title: marginal propensity to save (MPS)
38762fc5-78e8-43a7-bdda-a21ceda31617.description: The proportion of each extra dollar of income that is saved.

040891ea-c39f-44bf-9245-ea4a557a5ae2.title: market concentration
040891ea-c39f-44bf-9245-ea4a557a5ae2.description: A measure of the distribution of market share between businesses in a particular industry.

7379848a-7ba9-45bb-ad1f-af0fdf22e782.title: market economy
7379848a-7ba9-45bb-ad1f-af0fdf22e782.description: An economic system where economic decisions are mostly made by households and businesses, and economic outcomes are largely determined by the forces of demand and supply.

e759ce95-591b-47d3-80ac-8c0512500b9e.title: market failure
e759ce95-591b-47d3-80ac-8c0512500b9e.description: When demand and supply does not allocate resources efficiently or equitably, resulting in undesirable outcomes.

c326f9da-3800-4c85-b3ae-ebd5922c368d.title: merit goods
c326f9da-3800-4c85-b3ae-ebd5922c368d.description:
Goods that, when consumed, generate benefits in excess of the costs, and then tend to be under-consumed and under-produced.

See demerit goods

7bc3805a-50a6-47da-8b0e-9586fc86b85d.title: microeconomics
7bc3805a-50a6-47da-8b0e-9586fc86b85d.description: The study of the economy in its parts, focusing on individuals, businesses and industries.

fb2c72d6-ba26-4825-87f0-a94512e8e39e.title: monetary financing
fb2c72d6-ba26-4825-87f0-a94512e8e39e.description: The financing of government spending through the creation of new money by the central bank.

0ea62136-8674-4575-a405-7399ec0eea8d.title: monetary policy
0ea62136-8674-4575-a405-7399ec0eea8d.description: The actions of a central bank to influence the interest rates and manage fluctuations in the business cycle of an economy.

e6bc9b96-1f89-4d8b-b7ab-8833842001d7.title: monopolies
e6bc9b96-1f89-4d8b-b7ab-8833842001d7.description: A market structure comprised of a single seller.

8cea705c-3ed3-4f4a-9f0f-61d33a2959ea.title: monopolistic competition
8cea705c-3ed3-4f4a-9f0f-61d33a2959ea.description: A market structure with imperfect competition characterised by differentiated products, a large number of relatively small sellers and no barriers to entry.

684de7c4-c4a2-4ee6-aac6-775ed6782f61.title: multilateral free trade agreements
684de7c4-c4a2-4ee6-aac6-775ed6782f61.description:
A trade agreement between 3 or more countries.

See free trade

a46d0273-4a62-4e71-b97e-70c1e96946c7.title: multiplier effect
a46d0273-4a62-4e71-b97e-70c1e96946c7.description: The increase in national income resulting from additional spending.

c2a6d675-c106-40e2-8827-e623d395c74a.title: national income
c2a6d675-c106-40e2-8827-e623d395c74a.description:
An alternative term for gross domestic product (GDP).

See gross domestic product (GDP)

e83c73d6-056f-408b-a0f6-3b177b94b834.title: nationalisation
e83c73d6-056f-408b-a0f6-3b177b94b834.description: The government taking ownership and control of a business from the private sector.

c90be091-5e7e-4d97-b849-05aa0903d151.title: network effects
c90be091-5e7e-4d97-b849-05aa0903d151.description: The increase in value or the benefit derived from a good or service as more people use it.

2ba2ab83-dc67-4310-bf11-be1784b927f2.title: non-market sector
2ba2ab83-dc67-4310-bf11-be1784b927f2.description: The part of the economy producing goods and services that are either free or heavily subsidised, and usually produced by the government.

d791f792-8c23-4705-9dfb-3ae862824dcd.title: non-standard work arrangements
d791f792-8c23-4705-9dfb-3ae862824dcd.description: A job without an employer guarantee of stable, long-term employment.

1b6e5f1a-94c5-4b87-835f-6045fc4fcec3.title: non-wage benefits
1b6e5f1a-94c5-4b87-835f-6045fc4fcec3.description: Compensation provided by employers in addition to wages or salaries.

9e9446a6-5489-47ea-89bb-b2501332ab3a.title: normal goods
9e9446a6-5489-47ea-89bb-b2501332ab3a.description: Goods with demand that increases as income rises.

25f051b1-487a-41c3-b0f5-488e244debd7.title: nudges
25f051b1-487a-41c3-b0f5-488e244debd7.description: A behavioural strategy used to influence the decisions of consumers or businesses toward positive economic and social outcomes by changing how choices are presented.

df0b80c0-7517-447a-9831-c5eff65f0b5f.title: occupational mobility of labour
df0b80c0-7517-447a-9831-c5eff65f0b5f.description: The ease with which workers can move between different fields of employment.

63707968-2387-4018-a6dc-6a27c52834fb.title: occupational segregation
63707968-2387-4018-a6dc-6a27c52834fb.description: The distribution of jobs and industries between genders and the tendency for women to be concentrated in lower-paid employment.

93bb4603-47a5-43e0-8e31-fb8c9cf100db.title: oligopolies
93bb4603-47a5-43e0-8e31-fb8c9cf100db.description: A market structure with imperfect competition comprising few firms and significant barriers to entry.

1eb620d6-8029-4838-b86e-152aee97fb95.title: Palma ratio
1eb620d6-8029-4838-b86e-152aee97fb95.description: The proportion of income of the top 10 per cent of earners divided by the proportion of income of the bottom 40 per cent of earners.

3dabc0ed-55ef-4d18-b986-c35e4ebbf1a1.title: paradox of thrift
3dabc0ed-55ef-4d18-b986-c35e4ebbf1a1.description: The economic theory that when all individuals attempt to save more, the collective decrease in spending will cause lower production, employment and income in the economy, ultimately lowering total savings.

39fc3f6c-a9c0-4ed5-aa01-561c8f041e21.title: part-time workers
39fc3f6c-a9c0-4ed5-aa01-561c8f041e21.description:
An individual who averages less than 35 hours of work per week.

See full-time workers

de96b688-d75c-4e7e-8a6d-001f8ea0382d.title: per capita recession
de96b688-d75c-4e7e-8a6d-001f8ea0382d.description: An economic downturn defined by a fall in real GDP per capita and a decrease in living standards.

8c3d0e43-0c13-46c4-bd24-fd5b1e179405.title: perfect competition
8c3d0e43-0c13-46c4-bd24-fd5b1e179405.description: A market structure characterised by homogenous products, a large number of small sellers and no barriers to entry.

16274e73-9b23-4a72-b45f-0c478ef1f0a0.title: portfolio investment
16274e73-9b23-4a72-b45f-0c478ef1f0a0.description: The acquisition of financial assets without gaining control over management of the underlying business or entity.

0c03d2f6-8588-4c1b-ae3c-db2b7a98427b.title: potential output
0c03d2f6-8588-4c1b-ae3c-db2b7a98427b.description: The maximum sustainable level of goods and services an economy can produce when all of its available resources are used.

3bc20143-4e22-4cb9-84cd-2f26d67e935d.title: price elasticity of demand
3bc20143-4e22-4cb9-84cd-2f26d67e935d.description:
A measure of the sensitivity of the demand of a good or service to a change in its price.

See price elasticity of supply

d01db609-b83a-4344-acbf-c241974e5504.title: price elasticity of supply
d01db609-b83a-4344-acbf-c241974e5504.description:
A measure of the sensitivity of the supply of a good or service to a change in its price.

See price elasticity of demand

8412532f-072f-4fe8-ba28-0b24abb4f0a6.title: price mechanism
8412532f-072f-4fe8-ba28-0b24abb4f0a6.description: The interplay between demand and supply to determine the price of a good or service in a market economy.

dc002bd5-9b13-4086-9535-58c3026fc02c.title: private benefits
dc002bd5-9b13-4086-9535-58c3026fc02c.description: The gains of a household or business in consuming or producing a good or service.

dfaf3924-8c60-4661-af6e-1859485e6399.title: private costs
dfaf3924-8c60-4661-af6e-1859485e6399.description: The direct costs for a household or business in consuming or producing a good or service.

2d6d5443-5778-459c-b818-06c279358777.title: private sector
2d6d5443-5778-459c-b818-06c279358777.description: The part of the economy not owned and operated by the government and run for profit.

661c0a30-3945-42a2-93bc-5ec666b9a848.title: privatisation
661c0a30-3945-42a2-93bc-5ec666b9a848.description: The transfer of ownership of an asset from the public sector to the private sector.

32c33414-abdf-47b5-87bf-61a140988c8b.title: product markets
32c33414-abdf-47b5-87bf-61a140988c8b.description: The marketplace for final goods and services.

21acefc1-727a-464c-9a5c-6f454286e9db.title: productivity
21acefc1-727a-464c-9a5c-6f454286e9db.description: The volume of output produced per unit of input.

ddeb1ec1-277b-4fd6-8802-53438300b06c.title: promotion gaps
ddeb1ec1-277b-4fd6-8802-53438300b06c.description: The phenomenon of men being promoted at higher rates than women.

9dd4e532-2b93-46ca-a739-3199763c5570.title: public enterprises
9dd4e532-2b93-46ca-a739-3199763c5570.description: A business owned and controlled by the government.

88640cdc-f66b-42a5-b29d-efecb4c28d19.title: public goods
88640cdc-f66b-42a5-b29d-efecb4c28d19.description:
Goods that are freely available for everyone to use and one person’s use does not reduce the capacity for others to also use them.

See common-pool resources

a65c32a7-51c1-4a2e-830a-07f1b7724bad.title: purchasing power parity (PPP)
a65c32a7-51c1-4a2e-830a-07f1b7724bad.description: Currency conversion that equalises the buying power between countries’ currencies.

22fe4cbf-0f84-46d0-9387-96f4e70bdf3c.title: quotas
22fe4cbf-0f84-46d0-9387-96f4e70bdf3c.description: A restriction on the quantity of an imported good allowed into a country.

680a8323-eefe-4845-b778-d94aad59d9ee.title: regional trading blocs
680a8323-eefe-4845-b778-d94aad59d9ee.description: A group of countries in the same geographical area that agree to reduce or remove trade barriers between themselves to benefit from economic integration.

3fb196a1-b5ac-444c-b264-ac66398f5635.title: regulatory capture
3fb196a1-b5ac-444c-b264-ac66398f5635.description: When a regulatory agency is improperly influenced by groups who have an interest in the industry that is overseen by the agency.

8ff98c26-0b3d-4ea4-add9-f72dfad38a07.title: relative poverty
8ff98c26-0b3d-4ea4-add9-f72dfad38a07.description: A condition where a person’s income is significantly below the median income of the population, resulting in a lower standard of living and reduced ability to participate fully in society.

a7c73e0e-5364-44e9-85b3-a1c52900478b.title: rent-seeking behaviour
a7c73e0e-5364-44e9-85b3-a1c52900478b.description: Gaining a competitive advantage through manipulation or exploitation instead of through production and trade.

f0aa108f-91a5-4fc3-9c99-9b42d91f6db5.title: sludge
f0aa108f-91a5-4fc3-9c99-9b42d91f6db5.description: A process deliberately designed to be difficult, confusing and onerous, to discourage people from completing the process.

e8fe4d2b-6f4d-49fa-a259-6fbc19c5cd99.title: social benefits
e8fe4d2b-6f4d-49fa-a259-6fbc19c5cd99.description:
The total benefit to society of the consumption or production of a good or service, including private and third-party benefits.

See social costs

3a023027-ac86-4896-a602-d833613a7987.title: social costs
3a023027-ac86-4896-a602-d833613a7987.description:
The total cost to society of the consumption or production of a good or service, including private and third-party costs.

See social benefits

5de41e01-f23b-4c20-8291-4888dc7dd0a7.title: sovereign investment funds
5de41e01-f23b-4c20-8291-4888dc7dd0a7.description: A state-owned, special purpose investment vehicle funded by budget surpluses.

2a3cac93-92e1-4d2c-bc96-8cb963d48236.title: specialisation
2a3cac93-92e1-4d2c-bc96-8cb963d48236.description: The concentration of labour or other resources on a specific task or stage of production to improve efficiency.

5e0e925a-6ba1-4246-ae4d-8f78968ce0b6.title: stagflation
5e0e925a-6ba1-4246-ae4d-8f78968ce0b6.description: The phenomenon of simultaneously low economic growth and high inflation.

2cb0925a-0110-4570-b807-a5c1b3816858.title: structural unemployment
2cb0925a-0110-4570-b807-a5c1b3816858.description: People unemployed because of changes in the economy that have led to their skills becoming redundant.

6befd62d-a861-4613-9402-e6a88cb3494f.title: subsidies
6befd62d-a861-4613-9402-e6a88cb3494f.description: Government incentives provided to domestic producers, commonly in the form of payments or tax concessions, to lower the cost of production and encourage greater production.

5fbe25b8-96fe-4c31-b158-bf8d6040e65f.title: tariff
5fbe25b8-96fe-4c31-b158-bf8d6040e65f.description: A tax imposed on imports into a country.

0835c9a3-845e-4fba-9bfe-792930a1ea68.title: technical recession
0835c9a3-845e-4fba-9bfe-792930a1ea68.description: Two consecutive 3-month periods or quarters of negative growth in real GDP (gross domestic product).

97a19e8b-797a-41fa-8417-9eef41469572.title: technical specifications
97a19e8b-797a-41fa-8417-9eef41469572.description: Rules that regulate the materials, methods or technologies that must be used in production processes.

5c38f713-2d59-4d88-a459-1fa9ef89884d.title: terms of trade
5c38f713-2d59-4d88-a459-1fa9ef89884d.description: The ratio of export prices to import prices.

bccbf8c1-0d35-4b27-a45e-5589d17770d1.title: trade-offs
bccbf8c1-0d35-4b27-a45e-5589d17770d1.description: Something that is given up to gain from something else.

7d2f112a-40e7-474b-bb45-69c0f1823ffa.title: trade protection
7d2f112a-40e7-474b-bb45-69c0f1823ffa.description: Artificial barriers to trade imposed by governments to protect domestic businesses from international competitors.

4484f080-999b-489a-87e9-67dfd8b35e66.title: transnational corporations
4484f080-999b-489a-87e9-67dfd8b35e66.description: A business with operations in more than one country.

65257fb5-bd98-4a8e-ac7c-28a93b7a8eb4.title: underemployment
65257fb5-bd98-4a8e-ac7c-28a93b7a8eb4.description:
People in paid employment not working full-time hours who are willing and available to work more hours.

See hidden unemployed

a475dd0a-9a0a-4703-87d0-d68a42ab1525.title: underlying inflation rate
a475dd0a-9a0a-4703-87d0-d68a42ab1525.description: The expected level of inflation over the longer-term after accounting for the effects of volatile price movements in the economy.

7250138a-deaa-490d-9491-bc8d0255fde3.title: Veblen goods
7250138a-deaa-490d-9491-bc8d0255fde3.description: Luxury goods with demand that increases as the price rises.

d0adc7f6-4a39-49b0-8ccd-e25c2168b5cf.title: working-age population
d0adc7f6-4a39-49b0-8ccd-e25c2168b5cf.description: The civilian population of Australia aged 15 years and over.

ba4f5af6-74c7-4ef8-95dc-60a2872092de.title: inflationary expectations
ba4f5af6-74c7-4ef8-95dc-60a2872092de.description: The future price of goods and services anticipated by consumers and producers.

32511925-d893-4ce6-8390-cf758b999047.title: inflation
32511925-d893-4ce6-8390-cf758b999047.description: A general increase in the prices of goods and services over time.

6f762ae5-b1ba-47e8-9b4d-ee3e0dceea96.title: actuator
6f762ae5-b1ba-47e8-9b4d-ee3e0dceea96.description: A device that converts energy (electrical, hydraulic or pneumatic) into mechanical motion to control or move a system's components.

d2aeb645-fc70-46cb-b0c0-5b130a4c5f6f.title: closed-loop control system
d2aeb645-fc70-46cb-b0c0-5b130a4c5f6f.description: A system that uses feedback to monitor and adjust its performance automatically to achieve a desired outcome. It continuously compares the actual outcome with the desired outcome and makes corrections as needed.

897e1515-13e2-4194-88be-9ed22db6a630.title: control system
897e1515-13e2-4194-88be-9ed22db6a630.description: A system designed to manage, command or regulate the behaviour of other devices or systems using electronic, hydraulic, pneumatic or mechanical methods.

70d767a6-5478-4c43-94d6-68039451fc1a.title: dead load
70d767a6-5478-4c43-94d6-68039451fc1a.description: A permanent and immovable load, such as the weight of a structure itself.

04829a90-1026-404c-92a0-85f4d536d3a9.title: friction
04829a90-1026-404c-92a0-85f4d536d3a9.description: The resistance to motion that occurs when 2 surfaces rub against each other.

107e9518-64f0-463b-91b1-4902cf30538c.title: gear
107e9518-64f0-463b-91b1-4902cf30538c.description: A toothed wheel that engages with other wheels or parts to transfer motion. This engagement allows motion to be transferred in the same or a different direction.

283ae994-f8a9-48c4-85ae-f1c7a042efe9.title: hydraulic
283ae994-f8a9-48c4-85ae-f1c7a042efe9.description: The use of liquids, such as water or oil, to create movement or apply force, usually through pipes or cylinders.

1bd7b2b6-9d53-4dda-a35b-ec5d7745891f.title: live load
1bd7b2b6-9d53-4dda-a35b-ec5d7745891f.description: Temporary or changing weight on a structure such as people, furniture, or vehicles. These loads can move or change over time.

26bb2edb-0a4b-463b-96e1-386f90284f5a.title: load
26bb2edb-0a4b-463b-96e1-386f90284f5a.description: Any external force or weight that is applied to a structure or component.

32574166-13aa-4b9e-8773-76eadfe13f49.title: mechanical advantage
32574166-13aa-4b9e-8773-76eadfe13f49.description: The ratio of the output force to the input force in a mechanical system.

4ab42c4d-263b-4550-a540-65bf754622e6.title: mechanism
4ab42c4d-263b-4550-a540-65bf754622e6.description: A system of moving parts that work together to perform a function, often by transforming the direction, speed, or size of a force.

0142238b-acef-41db-b34c-8fec0893cdf0.title: open-loop control system
0142238b-acef-41db-b34c-8fec0893cdf0.description: A system that works without using feedback. It follows a set of instructions to produce an outcome but does not check or adjust its performance.

2006d71d-a406-4672-b28d-1102042e5d7b.title: pneumatic
2006d71d-a406-4672-b28d-1102042e5d7b.description: The use of compressed air or gas, to create movement or apply force, usually through pipes or cylinders. Pressure is often controlled by a regulator.

d098d5a2-2f0f-4c29-998c-b72c40e8a225.title: simple machine
d098d5a2-2f0f-4c29-998c-b72c40e8a225.description: A basic mechanical device that changes the direction or magnitude of a force, making work easier.

ebedd5ec-fcde-413f-9c5a-1e9105440a37.title: structure
ebedd5ec-fcde-413f-9c5a-1e9105440a37.description: A system of connected parts designed to support loads safely and perform a specific purpose.

5a588764-05c8-4215-b54d-dab414c37ecb.title: force
5a588764-05c8-4215-b54d-dab414c37ecb.description: A push or pull between objects, which may cause one or both objects to change speed, and/or direction of their motion, and/or their shape.

e7e52afe-3121-42cf-8fa5-a9f6961b0fde.title: efficiency
e7e52afe-3121-42cf-8fa5-a9f6961b0fde.description: The ratio of the work done, or energy developed by a machine or engine, to the energy supplied to it.

686f150f-c593-4681-a934-32d6daa4b15b.title: aesthetic
686f150f-c593-4681-a934-32d6daa4b15b.description: Relating to a sense of beauty or an appreciation of artistic expression.

2a8cfdcc-07df-4bff-b518-a277f1dbca1e.title: appropriation
2a8cfdcc-07df-4bff-b518-a277f1dbca1e.description: Taking a text or component of a text (such as a character or plot) from one context and using it in another context.

6ae1ef2a-e8fe-4962-a303-b0ce8b545d72.title: characterisation
6ae1ef2a-e8fe-4962-a303-b0ce8b545d72.description: The technical construction and representation of any personality or person-like figure in text, including features such as their appearance, actions, words or thoughts.

7b2c8198-09e0-4f19-b4da-346b1b16d4ae.title: compose
7b2c8198-09e0-4f19-b4da-346b1b16d4ae.description:
Develop and/or produce signed, spoken, written or multimodal texts in print, visual, oral or digital forms.

See create

31d2c434-c6b7-4575-8960-6cde8634de08.title: context
31d2c434-c6b7-4575-8960-6cde8634de08.description: The range of personal, situational, social, historical and cultural circumstances that shape how texts and their representations are conceived, constructed, understood and interpreted.

d0403b56-fb93-449d-8eed-2a3d1b2576d8.title: medium
d0403b56-fb93-449d-8eed-2a3d1b2576d8.description:
Means of communication, such as publishing, broadcasting or the internet.

Singular of media.

bb2a6925-fdfb-4052-a1fd-17f3aaba419a.title: perspective
bb2a6925-fdfb-4052-a1fd-17f3aaba419a.description: A lens through which the author perceives the world and creates a text, or the lens through which the reader or viewer perceives the world and understands a text. Readers may also temporarily adopt the perspectives of others as a way of understanding texts.

9e2df3ce-aaf0-4f77-8711-0145ac6881c7.title: reflection
9e2df3ce-aaf0-4f77-8711-0145ac6881c7.description: The thought process by which students develop an understanding and appreciation of their own learning. This process draws on both cognitive and affective experience.

24df6753-fb9f-401c-9ee0-131999e82f50.title: responding
24df6753-fb9f-401c-9ee0-131999e82f50.description: The activity that occurs when students read, listen to or view texts. It encompasses the personal and intellectual connections a student makes with texts. It also recognises that students and the texts to which they respond reflect social contexts.

e3860a76-1b18-4392-823f-c6935166b5ae.title: style
e3860a76-1b18-4392-823f-c6935166b5ae.description:
The way in which the effects of distinctive language forms and features of a text, often including those specific to its medium, combine to generate an overall impression.

Particular style elements may be observed in multiple works by the same author, from the same genre, or written during the same time period or artistic movement.

9a1148b4-41c0-432b-9005-4faf1a7a68f2.title: mode
9a1148b4-41c0-432b-9005-4faf1a7a68f2.description: A semiotic (meaning-making) resource or process of communication. For example, sounds, music, printed or spoken words, images and gestures.

d95aa9ca-b4d9-43d8-a300-a168cbb12b18.title: representation
d95aa9ca-b4d9-43d8-a300-a168cbb12b18.description: The way ideas are portrayed and represented in texts, using language devices, forms, features and structures of texts to create specific views about characters, events and ideas. Representation applies to all modes: spoken, written, visual and multimodal.

73292109-a04d-491c-9d63-94146c17a685.title: adaptations
73292109-a04d-491c-9d63-94146c17a685.description: A literary work that has been rewritten for presentation in a different medium.

fb769159-c5e4-4f58-a59f-d079bbdd93b6.title: allusion
fb769159-c5e4-4f58-a59f-d079bbdd93b6.description: A deliberate and implicit reference to a person or event, or a work of art which draws on knowledge and experiences shared by the composer and responder.

9b8c89ff-b21a-4aa4-a6f5-978077ce2073.title: critical
9b8c89ff-b21a-4aa4-a6f5-978077ce2073.description: Involving the assessment of the quality of argument, content, analysis, information or persuasion in oral, visual or written text, to assess the way in which themes, issues or ideas are presented for the audience and purposes intended.

3b4c5251-0aaa-4291-976f-08699e1f1120.title: form
3b4c5251-0aaa-4291-976f-08699e1f1120.description: The category into which a text can be classified based on its arrangement, structure and style, e.g. novel, autobiography, essay, sonnet, haiku, documentary.

e1a9f8a9-be84-48c8-879b-3ac0715748b9.title: irony
e1a9f8a9-be84-48c8-879b-3ac0715748b9.description:
A clash between what the words say and what they mean. Irony has 3 forms:

  • rhetorical irony – saying something contrary to what is meant, e.g. 'I had a great time' (I was bored)
  • dramatic irony – stating or doing something unaware of its contrast with the real situation, e.g. where the reader or watcher knows disaster is about to befall a character who says 'I've never been happier'
  • situational irony where events are opposite to expectations.

e111dddc-29f0-42ca-99b9-21af708d12ee.title: language forms and features
e111dddc-29f0-42ca-99b9-21af708d12ee.description: The symbolic patterns and conventions that shape meaning in texts. These vary according to the particular mode or media of production and can include written, spoken, nonverbal or visual communication of meaning.

e8e36251-2f0b-4d0c-a37d-d1d823b2ad74.title: sustained
e8e36251-2f0b-4d0c-a37d-d1d823b2ad74.description: When referring to texts, maintaining consistency of style, form, language features, argument and other unifying characteristics across the entire text.

76ae5929-5b39-4ba4-b390-9483e74544f8.title: syntax
76ae5929-5b39-4ba4-b390-9483e74544f8.description: The specific grammatical arrangement of words and phrases into sentences in order to make meaning.

ea294bea-b4d4-4571-84f1-da71a5a0a48b.title: values
ea294bea-b4d4-4571-84f1-da71a5a0a48b.description: These are ideas and beliefs in a text. They may be reflected in characters, through what they do and say; through the setting of the text, reflecting particular social views; and through the narrative voice of the text, perhaps through authorial comment. Values are specific to individuals and groups, and a text may contain a number of conflicting values.

a5425d86-0e74-47bc-bbb9-88459f5665c3.title: writing
a5425d86-0e74-47bc-bbb9-88459f5665c3.description:
The planning, composition, editing and publishing of texts in print or digital forms. Various methods of transcription may be used, including communication form(s) and systems.

See communication forms

c2ce09c3-3e77-4f84-9fc2-e488de2e75fa.title: discursive texts
c2ce09c3-3e77-4f84-9fc2-e488de2e75fa.description: Texts whose primary focus is to explore an idea or variety of topics. These texts involve the discussion of an idea(s) or opinion(s) without the direct intention of persuading the reader, listener or viewer to adopt any single point of view.

e4749875-a370-4fb8-817b-cf6e61bce9f0.title: speaking
e4749875-a370-4fb8-817b-cf6e61bce9f0.description:
May involve using the voice to convey meaning and communicate with purpose. Some students participate in speaking activities using communication form(s), such as sign language or augmentative and alternative communication devices.

See augmentative and alternative communication (AAC)

97b992aa-766e-455b-8103-88d21dbd8a5a.title: discursive text
97b992aa-766e-455b-8103-88d21dbd8a5a.description: Texts whose primary focus is to explore an idea or variety of topics. These texts involve the discussion of an idea(s) or opinion(s) without the direct intention of persuading the reader, listener or viewer to adopt any single point of view.

7bf161ba-06e1-4cb8-851c-85f1999c763d.title: figurative language
7bf161ba-06e1-4cb8-851c-85f1999c763d.description: Word groups/phrases used differently from the expected or everyday usage to express an idea in a non-literal way for a particular effect.

3ef06637-4339-4291-9977-a66dbc6f2ab4.title: composer
3ef06637-4339-4291-9977-a66dbc6f2ab4.description: A noun used to (collectively) describe an author, poet, playwright, director, designer and so on.

012f1967-f39b-492c-8cb8-2873e2a6cad6.title: textual integrity
012f1967-f39b-492c-8cb8-2873e2a6cad6.description: The unity of a text; its coherent use of form and language to produce an integrated whole in terms of meaning and value.

dac20c59-bb37-467b-9c69-6f58089d4676.title: authority
dac20c59-bb37-467b-9c69-6f58089d4676.description:
