Authority of a text – How trustworthy, authentic or valid an audience may find the representation of ideas, experiences, perspectives and arguments in a text.

Authority over a text – The varying degrees to which the meaning of a text is controlled or constructed by its creator(s) and by its audience.

984558ea-25ea-441a-97e4-1339b1a7e961.title: modality
984558ea-25ea-441a-97e4-1339b1a7e961.description: Aspects of language that suggest a particular perspective on subjects and/or events. Modality forms a continuum from high modality (always, must) to low modality (might, could).

db9ae8ac-68d2-497a-b92b-68d2fde638dd.title: critique
db9ae8ac-68d2-497a-b92b-68d2fde638dd.description: Comprehensive analysis and assessment of a thing, especially a literary, philosophical or political theory, which usually offers a judgement.

3000cddb-fbb5-4cd6-95f1-435d6f59d973.title: adjective
3000cddb-fbb5-4cd6-95f1-435d6f59d973.description: A word class that describes, classifies or qualifies a noun or a pronoun.

250bbc1b-6b97-48d2-a097-944e40f82944.title: adverb
250bbc1b-6b97-48d2-a097-944e40f82944.description: A word that tells something about a verb, adjective, another adverb or a whole clause. They usually indicate manner (commonly ending in -ly) or degree.

82dca4b6-d12d-4fe9-8cc5-6a330d8cb56c.title: apostrophe (’)
82dca4b6-d12d-4fe9-8cc5-6a330d8cb56c.description: A punctuation marker used to indicate possession or missing letters or numbers in a contracted expression.

5912b593-fcbf-463e-affd-2b9c5b4ffd9d.title: argument
5912b593-fcbf-463e-affd-2b9c5b4ffd9d.description:
A stated position about an idea.

The way in which various dimensions of a text (such as theme, perspective and style) can be understood to represent a particular position on an issue.

e0f08226-521f-4452-8be5-aa0f4cafaafe.title: automaticity
e0f08226-521f-4452-8be5-aa0f4cafaafe.description: The fast, accurate and effortless word recognition that comes with practice. NESA acknowledges that reading aloud may include the use of Auslan, assistive technology or AACs.

b3a1f27c-fb64-4f01-be0f-9474d8b7a0a0.title: background knowledge
b3a1f27c-fb64-4f01-be0f-9474d8b7a0a0.description: Information that is important for understanding a subject.

5e114224-7a01-43a3-8e27-1c67b0828f4b.title: base word
5e114224-7a01-43a3-8e27-1c67b0828f4b.description:
A morpheme (meaningful unit) that stands freely on its own to make a word.

See morpheme

2714f2ca-4b4d-46b6-8871-3b4f1849f51a.title: blend
2714f2ca-4b4d-46b6-8871-3b4f1849f51a.description: The act of synthesising phonemes smoothly from left to right, to read words.

c9a15e89-b114-46f3-a15a-17a75b210be6.title: voice
c9a15e89-b114-46f3-a15a-17a75b210be6.description:
The way in which language is used and/or interpreted to represent particular thoughts, opinions or perspectives. This includes the authorial voice or the voice of a narrator, character or persona within a text.

Describes the relationship between the action expressed by the verb and the subject/object of the sentence. For example, ‘active voice’ is where the subject performs the action, ‘The cat broke the vase’; ‘passive voice' is where the object is acted upon, ‘The vase was broken by the cat’.

In speaking, a description of the oral production of text.

See point of view for ‘narrative voice’

61ce24d5-3f7d-400e-ac94-11cfd5d46844.title: clause (dependent)
61ce24d5-3f7d-400e-ac94-11cfd5d46844.description: A dependent clause (also known as subordinate clause) is a group of words that cannot stand alone as a sentence.

1118121a-20b6-4770-a710-30933fb79418.title: clause (main)
1118121a-20b6-4770-a710-30933fb79418.description:
A main clause (also known as principal or independent clause) is a clause that can stand alone as a complete sentence.

See adjectival clause and adverbial clause

32a9e25e-2c84-4648-ab51-88c873b47d91.title: comma (,)
32a9e25e-2c84-4648-ab51-88c873b47d91.description: A punctuation marker used to show separation between parts of a sentence, such as clauses or phrases, where separation is important to the meaning. Commas are also used to separate words, phrases or numbers in a series.

0b098ade-644c-4112-b01d-5c21c4d844bb.title: communication systems
0b098ade-644c-4112-b01d-5c21c4d844bb.description: The range of communication forms used by a person. Communication systems are specifically designed to meet people’s individual needs.

f2386269-845a-40e1-aed3-357a2bab346b.title: complex sentence
f2386269-845a-40e1-aed3-357a2bab346b.description: Formed by adding one or more dependent (subordinate) clauses to a main (independent) clause using subordinating conjunctions and/or relative pronouns.

603cbf62-dab4-4938-b7f0-4779935a30b9.title: compound sentence
603cbf62-dab4-4938-b7f0-4779935a30b9.description: A sentence comprising 2 or more independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction.

86b5b8b2-0a17-416c-8c58-adbb8b7d4dca.title: compound word
86b5b8b2-0a17-416c-8c58-adbb8b7d4dca.description: A word consisting of 2 or more base words, e.g. farmyard = farm + yard.

37ca91f0-b451-4875-8831-405c86f352db.title: consonant digraph
37ca91f0-b451-4875-8831-405c86f352db.description:
Two consonant graphemes used to represent one phoneme.

For example:

  • th in that
  • sh in shy
  • kn in knee.

512faf88-1fa7-4201-94a4-fbc7b719869b.title: consonant phoneme
512faf88-1fa7-4201-94a4-fbc7b719869b.description: A speech sound produced with a complete or partial obstruction of the flow of air by the teeth, lips, tongue and/or voice.

07703014-1ede-46ec-b232-59a99cb8f91b.title: contraction
07703014-1ede-46ec-b232-59a99cb8f91b.description: A shortened form of one or 2 words (one of which is usually a verb). In a contraction, an apostrophe takes the place of the missing letter or letters.

dc609ac3-13a1-4967-a472-fa63aa81f1bf.title: contrast
dc609ac3-13a1-4967-a472-fa63aa81f1bf.description: Show how things are different or opposite.

90ffd55e-a3c8-412a-82c0-22298669eca3.title: coordinating conjunction
90ffd55e-a3c8-412a-82c0-22298669eca3.description:
A word or group of words that functions to link:

  • 2 words or phrases within a sentence, e.g. shoes and socks
  • 2 independent clauses within a sentence.

31c7a0af-95ed-43be-8dd2-e79fbb9b99da.title: CVC words
31c7a0af-95ed-43be-8dd2-e79fbb9b99da.description: Words formed by a consonant-vowel-consonant. For example, cat, bag, pen.

7b75b276-8346-42c8-b96f-d9895568a874.title: decodable texts
7b75b276-8346-42c8-b96f-d9895568a874.description:
Texts that are made up of grapheme–phoneme correspondences (GPCs) that students have learnt. These texts are used by beginning readers to practise segmenting and blending skills to read words, quickly and effortlessly.

See automaticity

f80314a3-8df7-4e87-8a79-7990ca19ad81.title: decode
f80314a3-8df7-4e87-8a79-7990ca19ad81.description: A process of efficient word recognition in which readers use knowledge of the relationship between letters (graphemes) and sounds (phonemes) to work out how to say and read written words.

c01ea0f2-2274-4a4e-af27-ddef3b68352c.title: dialogue
c01ea0f2-2274-4a4e-af27-ddef3b68352c.description: A conversation between 2 or more people: the conversation between characters in a text, an exchange of ideas or opinions on a particular issue, or a literary work in the form of a conversation.

665b7adf-e8a6-4b43-8c57-e37db0146ba3.title: digraph
665b7adf-e8a6-4b43-8c57-e37db0146ba3.description:
Two graphemes used to represent one phoneme.

For example:

  • consonant digraphs – sh, ck, th
  • split digraphs – a-e, i-e, o-e
  • vowel digraphs – ee, oo, ea.

8bc25711-49ff-46e4-85ae-855f29c1bb98.title: double consonant
8bc25711-49ff-46e4-85ae-855f29c1bb98.description: Two of the same consecutive letters. Also referred to as a consonant doublet.

19cdb1ae-d42e-4e4d-ad10-750f908fd376.title: adjectival clause
19cdb1ae-d42e-4e4d-ad10-750f908fd376.description: A type of dependent clause that operates as an adjective to give more information to a noun or pronoun in a sentence.

fd282e37-04e2-4b55-8caa-8a30802fd020.title: adjectival phrase
fd282e37-04e2-4b55-8caa-8a30802fd020.description:
A group of words (usually beginning with a preposition) that gives more information about a noun.

For example:

  • The girl with brown curly hair sat at the front.
  • The flowers in the vase were wilting.

ebb78527-d14d-4e40-9c7e-76dbbaccf99c.title: adverbial clause
ebb78527-d14d-4e40-9c7e-76dbbaccf99c.description: A dependent clause that modifies a verb, adjective, adverb or a main clause in a sentence.

9cbba9de-a6e0-4729-9f04-61b9ea7712b9.title: adverbial phrase
9cbba9de-a6e0-4729-9f04-61b9ea7712b9.description:
A group of words that provides information about where, when, with what, how far, how long, with whom, about what or as what.

For example:

  • He swept the floor with an old broom.
  • Throughout time people have attempted to halt old age.

af5c2bb2-5e78-4c80-b4f0-56e0acf3072c.title: analyse
af5c2bb2-5e78-4c80-b4f0-56e0acf3072c.description: Identify components and the relationship between them; draw out and relate implications.

c79c193b-4d3b-442e-ab50-cbe4471d1c7b.title: anaphor(a)
c79c193b-4d3b-442e-ab50-cbe4471d1c7b.description:
Grammar – a word or phrase that references an earlier word or phrase.

Rhetoric – the intentional repetition of a word or phrase at the beginning of several clauses, sentences, stanzas or paragraphs.

d7cb7720-5fff-41bc-9f04-ad2cb53df3f0.title: antonym
d7cb7720-5fff-41bc-9f04-ad2cb53df3f0.description: A word or phrase that has the opposite meaning of another word or phrase.

a5030df3-7641-4f63-b58e-82658f330bf6.title: appositive
a5030df3-7641-4f63-b58e-82658f330bf6.description:
A noun or pronoun that is positioned beside another noun or pronoun to explain or identify it. An appositive often includes modifiers.

See modifier

c0c32196-af38-458c-b2ca-bd8d15fd0015.title: appreciate
c0c32196-af38-458c-b2ca-bd8d15fd0015.description: Make a judgement about the value of.

fc966be7-97dc-467b-b45d-6309b7861956.title: assess
fc966be7-97dc-467b-b45d-6309b7861956.description: Make a judgement of value, quality, outcomes, results or size.

c6d9ea80-baf4-481c-ba67-6780f53f566d.title: assimilated prefix
c6d9ea80-baf4-481c-ba67-6780f53f566d.description: A bound morpheme that is added before a base word and where its last letter changes to match the first letter of the base word. For example, in + mature = immature.

59b836c6-c9c4-4fbc-a50f-db6774eb137c.title: authorship
59b836c6-c9c4-4fbc-a50f-db6774eb137c.description: Origin as to author, composer, or compiler. For example, the authorship of a book.

f6dacd8d-e722-4c74-831d-3d1ef71833e4.title: causal connective
f6dacd8d-e722-4c74-831d-3d1ef71833e4.description: A word or groups of words used as a cohesive device between sentences, when explaining how something works or why something happens.

790065e0-dc6b-4b67-a965-b2fef91e0a1c.title: character
790065e0-dc6b-4b67-a965-b2fef91e0a1c.description: A person (or animal) created in a text (usually narrative) to represent human characteristics including physical, emotional and intellectual characteristics, habits and behaviour.

69d7b06f-7095-4aca-97f1-1f82aee3403e.title: code and convention
69d7b06f-7095-4aca-97f1-1f82aee3403e.description: Agreed systems of making, communicating and interpreting meaning.

4c89fcc6-1910-4e96-acff-c38779e11ce9.title: cohesive devices
4c89fcc6-1910-4e96-acff-c38779e11ce9.description: Words or phrases that indicate a relationship with other words, phrases, clauses or paragraphs across a text.

68f4bbbc-7780-4ba1-b9f0-2136f2179ab7.title: conditional connective
68f4bbbc-7780-4ba1-b9f0-2136f2179ab7.description: A word, or groups of words, that describes the condition that needs to be met for something to happen. This may be in the form of a word ‘if’ or phrase ‘in this case’.

418161fa-23f5-4755-9d4d-c01df8f36ff1.title: conjunction
418161fa-23f5-4755-9d4d-c01df8f36ff1.description: A form of connective. A word or group of words used to link together words, phrases or clauses within sentences.

e0c5ce84-4fee-4479-9651-f4ad82be7570.title: connective
e0c5ce84-4fee-4479-9651-f4ad82be7570.description: A word or group of words used to connect sentences, clauses, phrases or words. A connective is commonly a conjunction, a preposition or an adverb.

55e646fc-d2ee-4c32-b299-582e7d49ffb7.title: connotation
55e646fc-d2ee-4c32-b299-582e7d49ffb7.description: The nuances or implied meaning attached to language, beyond that of its literal or dictionary meanings. Connotations may be positive, negative, or neutral.

e98401d6-717d-4851-bbed-d1eaa7da00e5.title: construct
e98401d6-717d-4851-bbed-d1eaa7da00e5.description: Make; build; put together items or arguments.

e7fd53b4-b8cd-4b1d-bf2c-2f3b1e3470ec.title: dash
e7fd53b4-b8cd-4b1d-bf2c-2f3b1e3470ec.description: A punctuation marker used to indicate an abrupt break or pause in a sentence, to begin and end a parenthetic clause, as an indication of omitted letters or words.

befd8205-09fa-4c4e-b4fa-dbdb331108ca.title: declarative sentence
befd8205-09fa-4c4e-b4fa-dbdb331108ca.description: A statement presented as a complete sentence to provide fact, evidence or detail. For example: Drinking water is important for your health.

24e97366-fcb8-4325-ae46-81e7d25d6ce1.title: definite article
24e97366-fcb8-4325-ae46-81e7d25d6ce1.description: In English, the definite article is the word ‘the’. It’s located before a noun to indicate that the noun is specific.

4f11844f-091a-48c1-8574-d9027b7f4a22.title: derivational word form
4f11844f-091a-48c1-8574-d9027b7f4a22.description: A new word that is formed from another word, usually by adding a derivational suffix to change its grammatical form. For example, the noun, proposition, derives from the verb, propose, and contains the derivational suffix, -ion.

0044cdd9-ea28-4968-b33c-9d3535312601.title: digital text
0044cdd9-ea28-4968-b33c-9d3535312601.description: An audio, visual or multimodal text produced by electronic technology. A digital text may be interactive and include still and/or dynamic images, animations and/or hyperlinks.

acbb9275-5db0-44df-b22e-c169c6c4e1f8.title: diphthong
acbb9275-5db0-44df-b22e-c169c6c4e1f8.description: A type of vowel phoneme, also known as a glide vowel, formed by combining 2 vowel sounds within a single syllable. For example, /oi/ in join, /ou/ in proud.

172d8e06-88ca-4de4-aef0-464724f9f099.title: discuss
172d8e06-88ca-4de4-aef0-464724f9f099.description: Identify issues and provide points for and/or against.

b797041c-a470-4105-8b82-de83a4e31861.title: etymology
b797041c-a470-4105-8b82-de83a4e31861.description:
The origins of, and changes to, words in relation to meaning.

Words derived from earlier or other languages, place names, words derived from people's names, coinages.

3817be2b-2aa6-4162-ace0-0acfe18e51a0.title: exclamation mark
3817be2b-2aa6-4162-ace0-0acfe18e51a0.description: A punctuation marker used after an exclamation.

f3bb20a3-ec50-4c86-9722-041f5b164f66.title: exclamatory sentence
f3bb20a3-ec50-4c86-9722-041f5b164f66.description: A statement expressing a strong emotion, formed as a complete sentence, and often ending with an exclamation mark.

57cf2927-d739-4fc1-a8c2-6cb33cce656e.title: expanded noun group
57cf2927-d739-4fc1-a8c2-6cb33cce656e.description: An extended group of words that provide rich or detailed information about the noun.

b10a1d16-f516-4091-8358-49aa0161555d.title: expanded verb group
b10a1d16-f516-4091-8358-49aa0161555d.description: A main verb that is preceded by one or more auxiliary or modal verbs to provide detail or precision.

4e4c9da7-2f41-42f1-9686-6b6a5070cfe2.title: gist statements
4e4c9da7-2f41-42f1-9686-6b6a5070cfe2.description: Succinct thoughts and information that capture the generalisations gleaned from what has been read, heard or viewed.

eb77d95d-fdc7-4031-ba4a-6b09d8fac264.title: home language
eb77d95d-fdc7-4031-ba4a-6b09d8fac264.description: A language acquired and used in the home or community.

73e3f0fd-b111-4742-97b4-936fd1602ecb.title: hyperbole
73e3f0fd-b111-4742-97b4-936fd1602ecb.description: An exaggerated statement not intended to be taken literally; may be used as a rhetorical device or figure of speech.

ed3ee0e5-9eb1-4ce2-90b4-04d1667417ec.title: hyphen
ed3ee0e5-9eb1-4ce2-90b4-04d1667417ec.description: A punctuation marker used to connect the parts of a compound word or the parts of a word divided for any purpose.

9bda9bb2-df51-439d-a41a-0cfabef71478.title: hyphenation
9bda9bb2-df51-439d-a41a-0cfabef71478.description: Used at the end of a line, to break a word between syllables or morphemes.

48d934e6-d6b8-4758-9417-1fe5d30acaf3.title: imaginative text
48d934e6-d6b8-4758-9417-1fe5d30acaf3.description: Texts that represent ideas, feelings and mental images in words or visual images. Imaginative texts entertain or provoke thought through their creative use of literary elements and make connections between ideas and experiences.

0cc0d7a2-81a5-4501-be9a-cbd0d067ca21.title: imperative sentence
0cc0d7a2-81a5-4501-be9a-cbd0d067ca21.description: A complete sentence conveying a direct command, request, invitation, warning or instruction, typically directed to an implied person.

ebffe324-e303-49a7-8cf0-32da95423ae8.title: indefinite article
ebffe324-e303-49a7-8cf0-32da95423ae8.description: In English, the indefinite article is either the word ‘a’ or ‘an’. It’s located before a noun to indicate that the noun is general.

9319f359-b991-4904-a3d1-cf502be61d93.title: inferencing
9319f359-b991-4904-a3d1-cf502be61d93.description:
Local inferencing requires the reader to comprehend implied information from within relatively small sections of text, such as 2 adjacent sentences.

Global inferencing requires the reader to comprehend implied information from across relatively larger sections of text and is supported by the reader’s depth of vocabulary and background knowledge.

2bb750e8-ec49-43c4-8ef7-dcaea045f2e6.title: informative text
2bb750e8-ec49-43c4-8ef7-dcaea045f2e6.description: Texts whose primary purpose is to provide information through explanation, description, argument, analysis, ordering and presentation of evidence and procedures.

ba0d0d7e-1215-41f0-9c69-a0ac330e7278.title: interrogative sentence
ba0d0d7e-1215-41f0-9c69-a0ac330e7278.description: A sentence that asks a direct or indirect question.

6d30644c-bf99-4ef1-8301-36fa193b3c47.title: intertextuality
6d30644c-bf99-4ef1-8301-36fa193b3c47.description: The various ways in which texts may be understood to draw meaning from one another, either by explicit, implied or inferred reference.

7dd60bba-85e9-418e-8ccf-221683b42bf0.title: irregular plural word
7dd60bba-85e9-418e-8ccf-221683b42bf0.description:
A noun that indicates more than one thing without requiring a plural marking suffix, -s or -es.

Mouse is a singular noun and mice is an irregular noun.

fc35de91-9d8e-4a37-a405-7f9b272a5a20.title: lexical cohesion
fc35de91-9d8e-4a37-a405-7f9b272a5a20.description: The use of word associations to create links in texts. Examples of links are the use of repetition of words, pronouns, synonyms, antonyms and words that are related, such as by class and subclass.

c6877a7d-2755-4db2-bf83-691e6202f1e3.title: literary value
c6877a7d-2755-4db2-bf83-691e6202f1e3.description:
The many ways in which audiences across time assign importance to texts. This may include the perceived authenticity, universality or significance of their representations of personal, social or cultural experiences and ideas. It may also include the aesthetic qualities and artistic significance of a text.

Specific texts that are considered to hold enduring value for society are often termed ‘canonical’ or ‘classic’ texts.

4bbbcf5d-1db6-4a27-a800-1d61a1b6460a.title: metaphor
4bbbcf5d-1db6-4a27-a800-1d61a1b6460a.description:
Linguistic – a figure of speech used for effect that implies one thing by referring to another.

Literary – an object, entity or situation that can be regarded as representing something else.

f84d2581-a180-4ded-a48f-014709bbc6c3.title: model text
f84d2581-a180-4ded-a48f-014709bbc6c3.description: A text that is studied as an example to show how specific textual features are crafted. Also known as a mentor text.

742aca59-58db-46b7-80f9-e2df86314ffd.title: modifier
742aca59-58db-46b7-80f9-e2df86314ffd.description: Words, phrases and clauses that affect and often enhance the meaning of a sentence.

8ad18ec7-400a-4da5-be4e-fb0f6921497b.title: monitoring
8ad18ec7-400a-4da5-be4e-fb0f6921497b.description: Considering meaning and/or purpose when reading and/or writing.

75e465c0-34e9-4c82-996a-e0a61bad950d.title: nominalisation
75e465c0-34e9-4c82-996a-e0a61bad950d.description: A process of transforming actions or events (verbs) or descriptions of nouns and pronouns (adjectives) into things, concepts or people (nouns). It can also refer to the process of forming noun groups from clauses. Nominalisation is often a feature of texts that contain abstract ideas and concepts.

d07817e0-ec8b-434a-8026-7358fdab4b30.title: noun group
d07817e0-ec8b-434a-8026-7358fdab4b30.description:
A group of words built around a noun.

Noun groups:

  • include a noun and any words that modify it
  • may include articles, adjectives and other modifiers
  • operate the same way as a single noun in the structure of a sentence.

7a4755b9-016e-4eca-9a67-67f75ed5ed50.title: objective language
7a4755b9-016e-4eca-9a67-67f75ed5ed50.description: Language that is fact-based, measurable and observable, verifiable and unbiased. It does not include a speaker or writer’s point of view, interpretation or judgement.

8197f3db-83d7-4a1b-acc4-9ce58bcafedb.title: paraphrase
8197f3db-83d7-4a1b-acc4-9ce58bcafedb.description: A rewording of something that has been written or spoken.

663c7090-27bd-4be5-bac0-e98ac17a390e.title: parenthesis
663c7090-27bd-4be5-bac0-e98ac17a390e.description:
A punctuation marker used to indicate an interjected explanatory or qualifying remark.

Plural: parentheses

ffa27c5b-db48-41e3-82fa-c02eca42ddd0.title: personification
ffa27c5b-db48-41e3-82fa-c02eca42ddd0.description:
Attributing human characteristics to abstractions such as love, things or animals.

See figurative language

0ca28750-7219-4be2-ac7b-3a968b7ef600.title: persuasive text
0ca28750-7219-4be2-ac7b-3a968b7ef600.description: A text designed to convince a reader of a particular opinion or way of thinking on an issue. A persuasive text may express an opinion while discussing, analysing and/or evaluating an issue.

754cc765-027d-4217-a56d-b8f580f6d768.title: poetic forms
754cc765-027d-4217-a56d-b8f580f6d768.description: Fixed forms within poetry that follow specific rules, such as ballad, sonnet, elegy, ode, dramatic monologue. The form will often be determined by the tone and subject matter. Note that some poets may deliberately subvert the fixed form.

72d631ef-df01-417d-b2a2-4134e6801053.title: point of view
72d631ef-df01-417d-b2a2-4134e6801053.description:
The position from which the information and events of a text are intended to be perceived by its audience. Point of view is constructed through the narrator, voice or images of the text and by characters or voices presented within it.

Point of view should not be confused with the term ‘perspective’ or with notions of opinion.

578666c6-5bf4-4887-a362-1d03e6b54cdc.title: predict
578666c6-5bf4-4887-a362-1d03e6b54cdc.description: Suggest what may happen based on available information.

29998ea8-ef68-4205-85f4-d1a8c74baef6.title: prepositional phrase
29998ea8-ef68-4205-85f4-d1a8c74baef6.description:
A word or group of words that indicate a circumstance such as time, place, manner or causality.

See adjectival phrase and adverbial phrase

0d0fc09b-0576-44f7-8bf3-78ccc5c1f9b7.title: prior knowledge
0d0fc09b-0576-44f7-8bf3-78ccc5c1f9b7.description: The knowledge a person already has before encountering a particular topic.

5c924f98-a7a3-4f7c-adb4-00bf9f442702.title: purpose
5c924f98-a7a3-4f7c-adb4-00bf9f442702.description: To entertain, to inform or to persuade different audiences in different contexts. Composers use a number of ways to achieve these purposes: persuading through emotive language, analysis or factual recount; entertaining through description, imaginative writing or humour, and so on.

89685fcf-a2bf-4fd8-bb52-a436b430ffd8.title: questioning
89685fcf-a2bf-4fd8-bb52-a436b430ffd8.description: A reading comprehension strategy that may occur before, during, and/or after reading. The questions a reader may ask themselves can support their literal and/or inferential understanding of a text.

0d35ef48-babc-4c26-8715-1d1ae7d3a2c6.title: quoted speech
0d35ef48-babc-4c26-8715-1d1ae7d3a2c6.description: The exact words expressed by a person, reproduced in quotation marks. For example: ‘You'll never guess what I've just seen!’ exclaimed Loreta.

4b39da3e-5d41-4d37-afcc-3ebef08e126c.title: reciting
4b39da3e-5d41-4d37-afcc-3ebef08e126c.description: Repeating a prepared text aloud, such as a published poem, to an audience. Reading should be prosodic and may occur from memory.

411f1d0b-b9be-4937-af91-7aa9369ace95.title: regular plural word
411f1d0b-b9be-4937-af91-7aa9369ace95.description: A noun comprising a free morpheme (base word) that is affixed to the inflected suffix, -s or -es, to indicate more than one.

d0c8d88d-ac6f-4179-86bf-6f5d8c835531.title: reported speech
d0c8d88d-ac6f-4179-86bf-6f5d8c835531.description:
Speech in a text used to communicate what someone else said, but without using the exact words. In reported speech the tense of the verbs is often changed.

For example:

  • She said that she was going to leave (indirect speech).
  • ‘I am going to leave', she said (direct speech).

60364505-7ff0-4c08-abc1-0209541f0b49.title: rhetorical devices
60364505-7ff0-4c08-abc1-0209541f0b49.description: Strategies used by writers and speakers to achieve particular effects, such as, to stimulate the audience’s imagination or thought processes, to draw attention to a particular idea, or simply to display wit and ingenuity in composition.

e917d051-5058-47cf-b9e4-5d08a7896a59.title: rhetorical question
e917d051-5058-47cf-b9e4-5d08a7896a59.description: A question that is asked to provoke thought rather than require an answer.

4f503c54-7cc3-4788-b23b-a23a65700fa8.title: root
4f503c54-7cc3-4788-b23b-a23a65700fa8.description: A morpheme that gives the word its core meaning. A root may or may not stand alone as a word. Many roots in Standard Australian English derive from Latin and Greek.

55a6aab7-fe89-4710-91b2-996f5d4ae8ba.title: salience
55a6aab7-fe89-4710-91b2-996f5d4ae8ba.description:
A strategy used to highlight what is important in a text.

In an image, salience may be created through framing an object in the foreground, and/or by its size or distinct colour.

In written text, salience may be conveyed by positioning the most important idea at the beginning of a sentence, or through font styling such as the use of bold, underlined or italicised text.

e7bba996-6ac3-46d1-a4a4-068d8a5c404d.title: schwa
e7bba996-6ac3-46d1-a4a4-068d8a5c404d.description: A reduced vowel phoneme occurring in an unaccented (unstressed) syllable of a multisyllabic word. For example, in the word ‘problem’ the final vowel phoneme is unstressed and is said quickly and quietly, and with less emphasis.

ce59d500-bf9d-4707-989d-191c90e5814a.title: simile
ce59d500-bf9d-4707-989d-191c90e5814a.description:
A figure of speech that compares the similar qualities of 2 different things. The comparison usually includes like, as or as if.

See figurative language

8944e9ec-0e97-4e6d-bc34-6e5390eeb8e7.title: spoonerism
8944e9ec-0e97-4e6d-bc34-6e5390eeb8e7.description:
A language device, sometimes a slip of the tongue, by which corresponding phonemes or morphemes are switched between 2 words or within a word.

For example:

  • butterfly becomes flutterby
  • It's pouring with rain becomes it’s roaring with pain.

See word play

0ebe270c-b7a0-45fa-8c20-b72a4f5cb106.title: subvert
0ebe270c-b7a0-45fa-8c20-b72a4f5cb106.description: To compose or respond to a text in ways that are different from the widely accepted reading or different from the conventional genre. For example, Roald Dahl's Revolting Rhymes provides a subverted reading of Cinderella. The purpose of producing a subverted reading of a text might be to entertain or to raise questions about the meaning or inherent values in the original text.

10909be9-90a0-47c8-8f8c-822fd4225fe1.title: synonym
10909be9-90a0-47c8-8f8c-822fd4225fe1.description: A word or phrase that has the same or a similar meaning to another word or phrase. For example, sick and ill.

3cca5be9-0aea-4f9c-826d-83c6dc7dd49c.title: temporal connective
3cca5be9-0aea-4f9c-826d-83c6dc7dd49c.description: A word or group of words that indicates when something is happening, e.g. first, next, finally, before, after, then.

75afdd74-be0e-4624-b1ef-1565067e80f3.title: theme
75afdd74-be0e-4624-b1ef-1565067e80f3.description: An overarching or recurring idea that describes attitudes or values that are perceived in a text. A theme may range from the understood ‘moral’ of a text to philosophical observations that the audience makes about the events, characters and experiences depicted in a text. A text may have more than one theme.

5809815b-7ba6-4409-b18a-df501afd40ce.title: visual texts
5809815b-7ba6-4409-b18a-df501afd40ce.description: Texts that consist of or include images. Visual elements in texts may contribute to meaning. Visual design elements in a text may include choices of lines, symbols, vectors, size and colour.

1366d67f-9f59-4f63-b7f9-a3f5bb7b621a.title: vowel digraph
1366d67f-9f59-4f63-b7f9-a3f5bb7b621a.description:
Two vowel graphemes that represent one phoneme.

For example:

  • ea in cream
  • ai in snail
  • oo in chook.

9d9e5f4c-a5c4-4443-b708-1f5d52cb7da8.title: word association
9d9e5f4c-a5c4-4443-b708-1f5d52cb7da8.description: The relationship between a word and other words that are semantically related in a text.

6fc5c459-865d-4a83-bee5-7a068e8f69d3.title: encode
6fc5c459-865d-4a83-bee5-7a068e8f69d3.description: Spell words in their visible written form.

bc6cfc10-8e8e-4a8b-8801-7c3754b331fd.title: extended phonic code
bc6cfc10-8e8e-4a8b-8801-7c3754b331fd.description: The vowel and consonant phonemes which are represented by less frequently occurring and alternative spellings.

fce9e02e-9acb-4659-9711-f50cedf9cc3b.title: fluency
fce9e02e-9acb-4659-9711-f50cedf9cc3b.description: Reading, speaking, encoding and spelling with appropriate pace and accuracy.

62bbcb35-056f-4417-adf9-507c45be4ae1.title: fluent reading
62bbcb35-056f-4417-adf9-507c45be4ae1.description: The act of identifying words accurately, effortlessly, at a contextually appropriate rate, and with phrasing and expression that reflects the meaning of the passage.

36a68f93-a2e0-4e94-8080-ed97a08a7b49.title: full stop (.)
36a68f93-a2e0-4e94-8080-ed97a08a7b49.description: A punctuation marker used to indicate the end of a sentence that is a statement or command.

f11b857b-68d9-494d-899e-ea65bec943f1.title: grammar
f11b857b-68d9-494d-899e-ea65bec943f1.description: A description of a language’s system, in regard to both structure (form) and meaning (function), at the level of a word, sentence and/or text.

2fa9ea21-c2aa-465a-80cd-1cc7d0b9eb23.title: grapheme
2fa9ea21-c2aa-465a-80cd-1cc7d0b9eb23.description:
The smallest unit of writing used to represent one phoneme. A letter or combination of letters corresponding to or representing a single phoneme.

Examples include:

  • the f in frog
  • the ph in phone
  • the gh in cough

df773cb2-6111-4b86-9f41-5e1c6f112da8.title: grapheme–phoneme correspondence
df773cb2-6111-4b86-9f41-5e1c6f112da8.description: The relationship between phoneme and its written alphabetic symbol (grapheme).

a1df7c7f-090b-45b2-b7f1-2f9c76dfd80d.title: high-frequency words
a1df7c7f-090b-45b2-b7f1-2f9c76dfd80d.description: Words that appear often in written texts.

5dec9951-c566-441b-ba6c-ccfbf26f4f36.title: homonym
5dec9951-c566-441b-ba6c-ccfbf26f4f36.description: A word having the same sound and the same spelling as another, but a different meaning.

1463ee11-a04f-495a-8e6a-ea270f0fc78d.title: homophone
1463ee11-a04f-495a-8e6a-ea270f0fc78d.description: A word having the same sound as another but different spelling and meaning.

2a2554f9-1e57-4f16-888c-34656cbde006.title: hybrid text
2a2554f9-1e57-4f16-888c-34656cbde006.description: Composite texts resulting from combining elements from different genres, styles and modes.

a144877f-dc0c-4927-b3f3-53239b616253.title: hyperlink
a144877f-dc0c-4927-b3f3-53239b616253.description: A hyperlink is a text, image, frame or button that when clicked or tapped will open another webpage, website, image, sound, document or application, such as email. Hyperlinks are often used within documents to link to other pages or sections.

6331c197-c9f0-40d8-b2d1-881635a077c0.title: imagery
6331c197-c9f0-40d8-b2d1-881635a077c0.description: Use of figurative language to represent objects, characters, actions or ideas in such a way that they appeal to the senses of the reader or viewer.

eaacdfb7-4dc4-4bc9-b218-41c61fc9defa.title: inflected word forms
eaacdfb7-4dc4-4bc9-b218-41c61fc9defa.description:
A word form that marks a distinction in tense (jump-jumps-jumping-jumped), plurality (cat-cats), and comparatives and superlatives (big-bigger-biggest).

See suffix

c94eff8f-9cb7-4d32-8818-1fe7c377087a.title: interpersonal conventions
c94eff8f-9cb7-4d32-8818-1fe7c377087a.description: Contextually purposeful language resources used for interacting; expressing ideas, opinions and feelings; and/or for taking a stance.

a6df6800-0170-49f3-aae0-8bd2e0963bd1.title: investigate
a6df6800-0170-49f3-aae0-8bd2e0963bd1.description: Plan, inquire into and draw conclusions about.

7cfeab4f-3242-42a5-af62-a7ccd71c2789.title: literature
7cfeab4f-3242-42a5-af62-a7ccd71c2789.description: An evolving category of text that is broadly seen by its audience to hold enduring personal, social, cultural or aesthetic value. Literature comprises a dynamic range of fiction and nonfiction texts from diverse historical and cultural contexts.

85723f0a-3e25-46a1-9084-a3c313960ea1.title: subjective language
85723f0a-3e25-46a1-9084-a3c313960ea1.description: Words used to communicate based on opinion, feelings or personal biases.

86fa90e2-35b6-4b8a-b1ae-a0910dc1609d.title: inference
86fa90e2-35b6-4b8a-b1ae-a0910dc1609d.description: A conclusion reached on the basis of evidence and reasoning.

fee9d479-f79f-4acc-8e44-859e76580cea.title: media
fee9d479-f79f-4acc-8e44-859e76580cea.description:
Means of communication, such as publishing, broadcasting or the internet.

Plural of medium.

32a0bfd5-c7e9-4909-8698-26da55067f18.title: mental model
32a0bfd5-c7e9-4909-8698-26da55067f18.description: A mental representation of the information in a real or an imaginary world. A student develops a mental model as the text progresses. It may include information derived from inferences and from background knowledge as well as from what is explicitly stated in the text itself.

e04f5150-df2e-444a-b55a-71132c68ac74.title: mentor text
e04f5150-df2e-444a-b55a-71132c68ac74.description: A text that is studied as an example to show how specific textual features are crafted. Also known as a model text.

42d40ac1-42e0-4f3e-a908-c5aa3a051894.title: spoken text
42d40ac1-42e0-4f3e-a908-c5aa3a051894.description: Communication produced using spoken words and delivered either face-to-face or digitally.

4111b1cd-ef5f-4049-953f-fe6410c1252c.title: morphological generalisation
4111b1cd-ef5f-4049-953f-fe6410c1252c.description: A spelling term that describes the manipulation and control of a particular base or root word when it is affixed with a prefix and/or suffix.

6689efde-45d3-4952-babe-113d6dee143f.title: navigation pathway
6689efde-45d3-4952-babe-113d6dee143f.description: A possible way to move around and locate content on a digital platform.

1f9e3149-6e85-4e0c-b9a3-0977cb217c0b.title: non-words
1f9e3149-6e85-4e0c-b9a3-0977cb217c0b.description:
Words that contain phoneme–grapheme correspondences that are plausible.

Also referred to as pseudowords. For example, drot, shann, glick.

691ed36e-4bac-49ae-8e66-6d80ea098ca0.title: noun
691ed36e-4bac-49ae-8e66-6d80ea098ca0.description:
A word used to represent people, places, ideas and things.

  • Common nouns: nouns used to name any one of a class of things, e.g. girl, classroom, egg.
  • Proper nouns: nouns used to name a place, a person or the title of something and are signalled by a capital letter, e.g. Wagga Wagga, Sam, Olympic Games.
  • Collective nouns: nouns used to name a group of things, e.g. crowd, swarm, team.
  • Abstract nouns: nouns used to name things that we cannot see but which exist in thoughts and feelings, e.g. sadness, love, wonder.

See pronoun

615e538b-5986-4a5a-acaa-a77deea7d3d3.title: noun–pronoun agreement
615e538b-5986-4a5a-acaa-a77deea7d3d3.description: Occurs where the correct pronoun is selected for the noun or noun group to which it is referring. For example: The children were looking for their father in the supermarket.

957dc754-d52a-4bca-823f-4b82ffd66d5f.title: noun–verb agreement
957dc754-d52a-4bca-823f-4b82ffd66d5f.description:
Occurs where the correct verb is selected for the noun or noun group to which it is referring.

For example:

  • A singular subject has a singular verb: the apple is cold.
  • A plural subject has a plural verb: these apples are cold.

f03ec774-556f-4a66-a8bd-588f29d6c3ca.title: object
f03ec774-556f-4a66-a8bd-588f29d6c3ca.description: The noun, noun group or pronoun in a sentence that is affected by an action. For example: The child threw the ball.

838e3e89-2db5-484b-ae4a-0287e8077927.title: onomatopoeia
838e3e89-2db5-484b-ae4a-0287e8077927.description: A word that phonetically imitates or is indicative of the sound that it describes. For example, bang, splash, oink, miaow.

410b5c6d-11bb-474f-80fc-199c8398669e.title: onset
410b5c6d-11bb-474f-80fc-199c8398669e.description:
The consonant speech sound(s) that appear at the start of a syllable and before the vowel phoneme. For example, /b/ represents the onset in the word ‘big’.

See rime

f9d9c401-7d2f-4d8b-80fc-2c95ddc445fc.title: oral language
f9d9c401-7d2f-4d8b-80fc-2c95ddc445fc.description: A system through which spoken words can be used to express, receive and understand information, ideas and feelings.

5cf09a76-cb43-4b62-a94e-4709915f301e.title: orthography
5cf09a76-cb43-4b62-a94e-4709915f301e.description: The conventional written or visible word-level system of a language.

ee988993-7fbb-4882-9a72-75d902fd1d86.title: paragraph
ee988993-7fbb-4882-9a72-75d902fd1d86.description: A sequence of sentences, grouped together and focused on a specific theme. A distinct section of writing indicated by a new line.

c526867b-5ad1-4196-ac6b-3aa2567b81c2.title: phonic knowledge
c526867b-5ad1-4196-ac6b-3aa2567b81c2.description: The ability to decode and encode words using knowledge of grapheme–phoneme relationships.

b3bef33b-f40d-4ea9-9864-53e97c812d52.title: phonological awareness
b3bef33b-f40d-4ea9-9864-53e97c812d52.description: The ability to hear, identify and say the separate parts of words (syllables, onsets, rimes and phonemes).

4bfc60ed-f347-4a3f-9441-21da9649a1d1.title: phrase
4bfc60ed-f347-4a3f-9441-21da9649a1d1.description: A group of related words that form part of a sentence and do not include both a verb and its subject.

e89b236f-a91e-4bd0-9971-4429d068cb44.title: prefix
e89b236f-a91e-4bd0-9971-4429d068cb44.description: A bound morpheme made up of letters that appear before a base word to make a new word. For example, un- in ‘unhappy’ means ‘not’ (un + happy = not happy).

5fd47bdf-e728-4429-97de-d4389e6d21ac.title: preposition
5fd47bdf-e728-4429-97de-d4389e6d21ac.description: A word that is used before a noun, noun group or pronoun that connects it to another word in the sentence, e.g. in, on, after, before, by, under, over, of.

be0925f3-a4d0-49e2-a975-4176e565cadf.title: pronoun
be0925f3-a4d0-49e2-a975-4176e565cadf.description: A word that is used in place of a noun. A pronoun may be personal (he, she, we, they), demonstrative (that, this) or relative (who).

b5dfdedc-38a7-4b5e-b9ef-fa1154c43fd3.title: prosody
b5dfdedc-38a7-4b5e-b9ef-fa1154c43fd3.description: Reading with expression using correct phrasing, intonation and attention to punctuation.

b31b8421-3fc5-4219-84f3-7187b11c41b4.title: pun
b31b8421-3fc5-4219-84f3-7187b11c41b4.description: A figure of speech where there is a play on words, usually created through the use of a homonym or homophone. Puns rely on more than one meaning of a word to emphasise the point.

3a8b153d-dbd1-4579-91ac-6e6b1a296940.title: question
3a8b153d-dbd1-4579-91ac-6e6b1a296940.description: A sentence that seeks information by asking or requesting to elicit a response.

c899c510-67f8-4956-b97b-b1d728f3e249.title: question mark (?)
c899c510-67f8-4956-b97b-b1d728f3e249.description: A punctuation marker used at the end of a sentence to indicate that a question is being asked.

84deb23f-0a4a-419c-a9a9-e926560bd24c.title: quotation marks
84deb23f-0a4a-419c-a9a9-e926560bd24c.description: Punctuation markers used to indicate: quoted or direct speech; the actual words quoted from another source in formal writing; the titles of poems, songs, short stories or articles; or, to draw attention to an unusual or particular sense or usage of a word.

fb9f4437-3745-4ca3-8bf4-8f254ffeba4a.title: reading
fb9f4437-3745-4ca3-8bf4-8f254ffeba4a.description: To process written words, to derive and/or construct meaning. It is the product of word reading and language comprehension.

806305ee-7295-464c-b8d4-a14441f9d17c.title: recasting
806305ee-7295-464c-b8d4-a14441f9d17c.description: Recasting is a teaching strategy to support students in their oral language. A recast occurs when the teacher modifies a learner’s utterance by adding new or different grammar (syntax) or by using precise words.

10b75e83-0901-406a-9dff-ae339a334afe.title: reference
10b75e83-0901-406a-9dff-ae339a334afe.description:
The use of a source of information in order to ascertain something.

The act of mentioning someone or something in speech or writing.

ddbf8ccb-6264-41ea-90c5-d96e1100edf8.title: return sweep
ddbf8ccb-6264-41ea-90c5-d96e1100edf8.description: The eye movement that takes the reader’s eyes from one end of the line of text to the start of the next line.

92f4bef9-2bdc-45a4-bab3-49a883362a42.title: rhyme
92f4bef9-2bdc-45a4-bab3-49a883362a42.description: A repetition of similar speech sounds in 2 or more words, beginning from the last stressed vowel sound and carrying through any remaining syllables.

9fb831f0-05ab-4bce-bb33-9c3c4026aaf5.title: rime
9fb831f0-05ab-4bce-bb33-9c3c4026aaf5.description: The vowel and other speech sounds that occur at the end of a syllable. For example, the /-ig/ represents the rime in the word ‘big’.

7dd0cf06-df00-4be1-b4b9-430bd0ac4fda.title: segment
7dd0cf06-df00-4be1-b4b9-430bd0ac4fda.description: The act of separating a spoken word into its syllables and/or phonemes.

937932fe-bd54-4ad9-87b7-60aeff00e6c3.title: simple sentence
937932fe-bd54-4ad9-87b7-60aeff00e6c3.description: A complete message that contains a subject and predicate, forming a single independent clause.

7372ca69-90ef-4cac-a0c4-049abb11d731.title: single-letter grapheme
7372ca69-90ef-4cac-a0c4-049abb11d731.description:
One letter used to represent one phoneme (speech sound).

See phoneme

e183ece8-23e5-43a5-98c6-d6a569aadaf6.title: split digraph
e183ece8-23e5-43a5-98c6-d6a569aadaf6.description:
Two graphemes that are split by a consonant to represent a long vowel phoneme.

For example:

  • a-e in cake
  • i-e in side
  • o-e in rope.

8f1a06f1-c126-4f68-b6cb-07ad4ea79a04.title: Standard Australian English
8f1a06f1-c126-4f68-b6cb-07ad4ea79a04.description: A system of standard English language, characterised by the perceived consistent usage of words and syntax across Australian political, business, media and education contexts. While it is always dynamic and evolving, it is recognised as the ‘common language’ of Australians.

13113bc7-6c0f-492c-985d-bcfee116c04a.title: subject
13113bc7-6c0f-492c-985d-bcfee116c04a.description: The noun (or noun group) in a sentence that conveys who or what the clause is about.

013788da-4706-4590-ab3d-e21b438445d4.title: subject matter
013788da-4706-4590-ab3d-e21b438445d4.description: The topic or content of a text. For example, an information report on marine vessels may include content about construction materials, and different types of boats and engines.

66585b2b-971f-4ea6-8074-2d260f124487.title: subject–verb agreement
66585b2b-971f-4ea6-8074-2d260f124487.description: Occurs when the writer or speaker selects the correct verb for the noun or noun group to which it is referring. For example: The bike was here (not: The bike were here).

01baae2c-2f27-4918-bf75-741608af9629.title: subordinating conjunction
01baae2c-2f27-4918-bf75-741608af9629.description: A word or group of words that function to link a dependent clause to an independent clause.

feb83ed6-a2fe-49d2-bdd8-e647b954fbaf.title: suffix
feb83ed6-a2fe-49d2-bdd8-e647b954fbaf.description:
A bound morpheme comprising a letter or group of letters that attach to a base word to make a new word.

For example:

  • The -s in dogs is an inflected suffix that marks plurality.
  • The derivational suffix, -ion can be added to the end of the verb, protect, to form the noun, protection.

See derivational word form and inflected word forms

f8406500-3483-4c7d-aa89-63d434bcf6e7.title: sustained reading
f8406500-3483-4c7d-aa89-63d434bcf6e7.description: Independently reading texts to expand and maintain comprehension.

2e419956-c96e-49a2-95b4-98498096442e.title: syllabification
2e419956-c96e-49a2-95b4-98498096442e.description: The process of segmenting a multisyllabic word into its syllables.

6a335dd5-10b6-4ea1-8bcd-bc16fb0ee662.title: syllable
6a335dd5-10b6-4ea1-8bcd-bc16fb0ee662.description: A unit of sound within a word that contains a vowel phoneme and feels like one ‘beat’. For example, a word with 3 syllables is: won-der-ful.

5bcd8411-0270-4c38-9987-a154d6b61941.title: symbol
5bcd8411-0270-4c38-9987-a154d6b61941.description: An object, character or entity that can be understood to represent a larger idea, action or feeling. Depending on context, audience and purpose, symbols can have commonly agreed or reinforced associations, or they can be dynamic. Symbols can operate within texts, or they can serve as meaning-making devices of language in the real world.

4f728aa1-8e0d-4af3-9d92-81c451304822.title: tense
4f728aa1-8e0d-4af3-9d92-81c451304822.description:
The form of the verb that indicates when something is happening in relation to the speaker’s time: past, present or future.

For example:

  • I ate bananas (past).
  • I am eating bananas (present).
  • I will eat bananas (future).

eef36231-6d80-45ef-bfa5-5eefd8cabb2a.title: Tier 1 words
eef36231-6d80-45ef-bfa5-5eefd8cabb2a.description: Basic-level, everyday words, e.g. dog, baby, happy, pretty, was, come, said.

abe3e590-77c4-4954-9ec4-a9a5c8668a5c.title: Tier 2 words
abe3e590-77c4-4954-9ec4-a9a5c8668a5c.description:
General academic words that can be used across a variety of domains. They are of high utility for mature language users and are commonly used in written language.

Tier 2 words add power and precision to written and spoken language, but many Tier 2 words are most commonly found in written language, e.g. contradict, precede, stale, awful, snuggle.

2388062a-1837-4032-a367-46b16087247c.title: Tier 3 words
2388062a-1837-4032-a367-46b16087247c.description: Words that are used rarely (low frequency) and only in highly specific situations, e.g. decibel, cataclysm, atom.

fa456a4a-7c24-4a39-9809-b27bd591fd45.title: tiered words
fa456a4a-7c24-4a39-9809-b27bd591fd45.description: Vocabulary classified according to complexity and use.

2cb5f278-c527-4b4c-8dfa-0b9ca45269ee.title: topic sentence
2cb5f278-c527-4b4c-8dfa-0b9ca45269ee.description: A sentence that usually occurs at the start of a paragraph and outlines the main idea of that paragraph.

4b35f4f0-e4d0-4b18-80cb-a50aa8af2d4b.title: trigraph
4b35f4f0-e4d0-4b18-80cb-a50aa8af2d4b.description:
Three letters used to represent one phoneme.

For example:

  • the tch in catch.
  • the igh in flight.

ecfd9f43-c3c6-4732-afa0-78667a285f47.title: upper/lower-case letters
ecfd9f43-c3c6-4732-afa0-78667a285f47.description:
Two visible forms of alphabetic letters. Lower-case letters are generally used, except when it is necessary to:

  • indicate specific names (proper nouns) such as those of people, organisations, titles or countries
  • indicate the beginning of a sentence or the initial letter of a proper noun
  • write headings
  • achieve a particular effect, such as to indicate shouting.

f8918dc9-bf2d-4641-bab7-cd1bc611be80.title: verb
f8918dc9-bf2d-4641-bab7-cd1bc611be80.description:
A word that tells what is happening. Different types of verbs include:

  • action verbs: They danced ...
  • thinking verbs: I forgot ...
  • feeling verbs: We like ...
  • saying verbs: He whispered ...
  • relating verbs: They are ....

546447e4-a127-4ed1-b244-14e99e3adf89.title: verb group
546447e4-a127-4ed1-b244-14e99e3adf89.description:
A group of words built around a verb.

Verb groups:

  • may include auxiliary verbs (‘helping’ verbs used to indicate tense or modality), e.g. I am going soon. I must leave before dark.
  • are sometimes referred to as a complex verb or compound verb.

772a7067-84e5-4c22-b7c2-fe2a066007bb.title: visualise
772a7067-84e5-4c22-b7c2-fe2a066007bb.description: A comprehension strategy used to create a mental image from a text read, viewed or heard. To visualise is to bring the text to life, engage the imagination, and use a person’s senses.

967f363e-19b0-4cff-8f13-0460a4de4d10.title: vowel
967f363e-19b0-4cff-8f13-0460a4de4d10.description:
A sound that is voiced with the mouth open and not obstructed by the lips, teeth or tongue. For example: the short /o/ phoneme in the word ‘dog’.

Often represented by the graphemes: a, e, i, o, u.

352d6c18-8354-4667-af27-3b1b2dd54fba.title: word play
352d6c18-8354-4667-af27-3b1b2dd54fba.description:
Experimenting with and manipulating language.

See pun and spoonerism

3ff9e7e8-42da-4e97-bdea-cd2d362b3ea7.title: literacy
3ff9e7e8-42da-4e97-bdea-cd2d362b3ea7.description: A synthesis of language, thinking and contextual practices through which meaning is shaped. 'Effective literacy is intrinsically purposeful, flexible and dynamic' (J Dawkins 1991, Australia's Language: The Australian Literacy and Language Policy, AGPS, Canberra) and involves interactions in a range of modes and through a variety of media.

9677f057-1b62-44f3-ae8f-4bb43e17e1fb.title: preferred communication form(s)
9677f057-1b62-44f3-ae8f-4bb43e17e1fb.description: The ways people communicate (i.e. the communicative method(s) or strategies they use) including augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems, eye gaze, objects, gestures, visuals, Key Word Sign or technology.

1c7a0a3c-cecf-4470-8af4-0dc1d76fa247.title: backward chaining
1c7a0a3c-cecf-4470-8af4-0dc1d76fa247.description:
A technique used by inference engines that determines reasoning from the knowledge base to understand how a decision was made. In backward chaining, the goal or output is used to track back to establish the steps taken.

See forward chaining

ff5cb947-6eb9-4ab9-96d8-cb5a67e7f79e.title: blockchain
ff5cb947-6eb9-4ab9-96d8-cb5a67e7f79e.description: A growing list of records, known as blocks, which are linked using cryptography. It can be used to record transactions between 2 parties efficiently and in a verifiable and permanent way.

67e32ab4-9129-495b-9e2d-e00606e36778.title: calculate
67e32ab4-9129-495b-9e2d-e00606e36778.description: Ascertain/determine from given facts, figures or information.

42f631ca-0bd6-4686-ae79-93f5703f51b5.title: Creative Commons
42f631ca-0bd6-4686-ae79-93f5703f51b5.description:
Is a non-profit organisation that enables the sharing of creative content without the need to seek legal approval.

See copyright

894a01ee-440a-4a33-8723-39398957bc67.title: data compression
894a01ee-440a-4a33-8723-39398957bc67.description: A reduction in the number of bits needed to represent data.

ad6d2496-b365-41cb-8d92-f8d10fc12b26.title: data sampling
ad6d2496-b365-41cb-8d92-f8d10fc12b26.description: The practice of analysing a subset of a larger dataset in order to determine meaningful information such as patterns and trends.

874cdca6-cf52-48aa-8509-260d6a999b36.title: edge computing
874cdca6-cf52-48aa-8509-260d6a999b36.description: A computing framework that allows for the distribution of processing capabilities and hardware so that applications can be closer to their data source.

49f593c2-50ee-4c99-8259-b828deaa6b7a.title: enterprise computing
49f593c2-50ee-4c99-8259-b828deaa6b7a.description: Refers to business-oriented information technology that is critical to a company’s operations. Enterprise computing encompasses types of information technology tools that businesses use for resource management, efficient production operations, relationship management and back office support.

2048e607-ae0b-4530-9ed4-4d9d2a49f017.title: enterprise system
2048e607-ae0b-4530-9ed4-4d9d2a49f017.description: The combination of digital systems, people and processes that collect, manage and analyse data.

57776d3c-e092-4772-8194-f584ebe50ef0.title: firmware
57776d3c-e092-4772-8194-f584ebe50ef0.description: Is the software that is installed on a small chip in almost all hardware devices that makes the hardware function as the manufacturer intended it to.

86cd626f-2ffe-485d-b25c-b879403ec196.title: forward chaining
86cd626f-2ffe-485d-b25c-b879403ec196.description:
A technique used by inference engines that applies reasoning to the knowledge base to get the information to make a decision. In forward chaining, the inference engine evaluates existing data to develop new data to make a decision.

See backward chaining

a6116292-02e1-4aa5-964a-921abc07ce90.title: informatics
a6116292-02e1-4aa5-964a-921abc07ce90.description: The science of processing data for storage and retrieval.

1c53d31d-9d4f-491c-a5b2-d02b32cf7fa9.title: interactive media systems
1c53d31d-9d4f-491c-a5b2-d02b32cf7fa9.description: Where there is facility for a user to interact with multimedia, the term ‘interactive media’ may be used. The use of digital technologies to present combinations of text, graphics, video, animation and/or sound in an integrated way. For example, interactive games, media-rich websites and electronic books (e-books).

245a753f-141f-492d-9eb0-2d7744ce9a32.title: sandbox gaming
245a753f-141f-492d-9eb0-2d7744ce9a32.description: A virtual world where players can build their playscapes, invite other players to play and test game play.

4cac79dd-f3b9-44bd-b3c0-931ede6394cd.title: system implementation
4cac79dd-f3b9-44bd-b3c0-931ede6394cd.description: The implementation method applied when introducing a new or redesigned enterprise system. Typically methods include: direct, parallel, phased or pilot.

86c43f76-7389-449d-b166-41bc62a0ee44.title: threat actor
86c43f76-7389-449d-b166-41bc62a0ee44.description: An individual or group that poses a security threat to an individual or organisation.

81f52c74-17bd-4531-975c-df53a55e5616.title: assets
81f52c74-17bd-4531-975c-df53a55e5616.description: Assets are the digital elements that can be used or incorporated into a multimedia presentation or production. They include graphics, photographs, videos, audio, animations or other artistic data.

ea541ece-530d-4f63-be37-4d51b328f624.title: big data
ea541ece-530d-4f63-be37-4d51b328f624.description: Extremely large datasets that may be analysed computationally to reveal patterns, trends and associations.

8a7cd4c1-a7fe-47f2-bb81-2bcf45546f2a.title: computational thinking
8a7cd4c1-a7fe-47f2-bb81-2bcf45546f2a.description: A process in which a problem is analysed and solved so that a human, machine or computer can effectively implement the solution. It involves using strategies to organise data logically, break down problems into parts, interpret patterns and design, and implement algorithms to solve problems.

0b654cc2-f13c-46ef-9428-2f9f84a0810c.title: data sovereignty
0b654cc2-f13c-46ef-9428-2f9f84a0810c.description: This is a global movement that refers to the right of Indigenous Peoples to determine the creation, collection, ownership and application of data that is for and about Indigenous Peoples. The term also refers to transnational data flow and a range of issues arising from the flow of data between nations.

afb786d6-a64c-43db-9e54-815fe07f1e7e.title: design thinking
afb786d6-a64c-43db-9e54-815fe07f1e7e.description: A process where a need or opportunity is identified and a design solution is developed. The consideration of economic, environmental and social impacts that result from designed solutions are core to design thinking. Design thinking methods can be used when trying to understand a problem, generate ideas and refine a design based on evaluation and testing.

89852148-dcf0-42a1-8bd0-7413564cc629.title: Object-Relational Mapping (ORM)
89852148-dcf0-42a1-8bd0-7413564cc629.description: A technique used in object-oriented programming to query and manipulate data from a database.

9827d01c-df09-4d3d-9f11-bc9fe14c4bf7.title: systems thinking
9827d01c-df09-4d3d-9f11-bc9fe14c4bf7.description: An understanding of how related objects or components interact to influence how systems function. Students are provided with opportunities to recognise the connectedness of, and interactions between phenomena, people, places and events in local and wider contexts and consider the impact of their decisions. Understanding the complexity of systems and the interdependence of components is important for scientific research and for the creation of solutions to technical, economic and social issues.

0bed88bb-f17e-4456-9a67-87782cb46471.title: food design
0bed88bb-f17e-4456-9a67-87782cb46471.description:
The creative process involved in the designing of food products, packaging, preparation methods, presentation and the spaces where food is consumed, with the aim of meeting human needs and enhancing the consumer experience.

See food systems

4fdbd0b9-c2eb-4e6f-9143-e7a1f70fdbc0.title: food practices
4fdbd0b9-c2eb-4e6f-9143-e7a1f70fdbc0.description: The patterns and behaviours involved in the selection, preparation, consumption and disposal of food, shaped by culture, religion, nutritional choices, food preparation techniques, environmental sustainability, resource availability and individual preferences.

82d68ccb-ad8b-4e35-b072-0d35f3ed01b6.title: food systems
82d68ccb-ad8b-4e35-b072-0d35f3ed01b6.description: The network of activities and resources that deal with the supply, distribution and sustainability of food, from its production and consumption to the disposal of surplus or waste.

e51213f9-af13-425d-aa3d-b4fb9d250bbf.title: food security
e51213f9-af13-425d-aa3d-b4fb9d250bbf.description: Assurances that food supplies are reliable and of a sufficient quality and quantity to maintain human life.

de5f0db6-2406-4315-81af-7a6069815b8b.title: benefit sharing
de5f0db6-2406-4315-81af-7a6069815b8b.description: Formal and mutually agreed terms for the ongoing, equitable distribution of benefits, arising from the application or commercial utilisation of knowledge, practices and/or resources. Benefit sharing agreements with Indigenous Peoples may relate to Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property (ICIP), such as knowledges and practices associated with sustainable management of land and resources.

fa5f0f0f-333e-48ce-b013-93d72f495526.title: biocapacity
fa5f0f0f-333e-48ce-b013-93d72f495526.description: The capacity of nature/ecosystems to produce and renew the resources that people use and to absorb and filter the waste generated by human activities, within a limited period of time.

ce763ded-028a-48c9-9c92-fff1cc3e3740.title: biophysical
ce763ded-028a-48c9-9c92-fff1cc3e3740.description: Biological and physical elements of the environment. It includes various life forms, both plant and animal, and elements such as temperature, light, humidity and soil nutrients.

9345bf12-f9f3-47ff-a1b6-fdbc5df6029b.title: cartographic conventions
9345bf12-f9f3-47ff-a1b6-fdbc5df6029b.description: Accepted practices associated with constructing and interpreting maps, e.g. using a border, orientation or compass point, legend or key, title, scale, giving latitude readings before longitude.

c2f5c176-bede-44b8-aa84-c54ae279a675.title: continentality
c2f5c176-bede-44b8-aa84-c54ae279a675.description: The effect of land mass on climatic conditions/patterns.

05323017-dc60-4d69-8fd2-515abbc62ab6.title: demographic transition
05323017-dc60-4d69-8fd2-515abbc62ab6.description: A model consisting of various stages used to show population change over time, including the influence of birth rates and death rates.

3e1d9c10-de2d-4e31-927a-53e9df4373da.title: diversity
3e1d9c10-de2d-4e31-927a-53e9df4373da.description: In a geographic context, diversity refers to variations within and between places, environments, natural or human phenomena, e.g. in relation to biophysical characteristics, culture, religion, settlement, economic activity.

934739f8-9b9c-4948-b1dd-01697bd8aecc.title: dynamic equilibrium
934739f8-9b9c-4948-b1dd-01697bd8aecc.description: In the context of Geography 11–12, when an ecosystem is able to maintain its natural balance and remain relatively stable, subject to gradual changes through natural succession. An ecosystem that is in a state of dynamic equilibrium is able to return to its balanced state in response to natural and/or human stresses.

c2141f10-d5f5-4936-8a9c-73bc66b7a3eb.title: ecological disturbance
c2141f10-d5f5-4936-8a9c-73bc66b7a3eb.description: Temporary changes or events in an ecosystem that cause disturbance to its functioning, e.g. increased mortality of organisms, changes in spatial patterning. Ecosystems are typically resilient to ecological disturbance.

b3ab0d0e-a377-4d5e-8185-e6c7c4587efd.title: ecological hazard
b3ab0d0e-a377-4d5e-8185-e6c7c4587efd.description: A biological hazard that has the potential to impact adversely on the wellbeing of people or the environment more generally. Examples of ecological hazards include malaria, coronavirus, Dengue fever, rabies, cholera, locust plagues, invasive species.

baea3d86-bf15-46d7-85ff-f69a18864f47.title: ecological integrity
baea3d86-bf15-46d7-85ff-f69a18864f47.description: The ability of an ecosystem to support and naturally maintain ecological processes, species, a diverse community of organisms, and other important characteristics, with minimal or no intervention through human management.

be6614fe-cf1b-414e-ba02-d995c265a045.title: economic integration
be6614fe-cf1b-414e-ba02-d995c265a045.description: The process by which places become increasingly linked and interdependent economically. This involves the reduction or elimination of the barriers to the flow of goods, services and factors of production between places and nations.

2e6cbb11-3714-4dd0-bc82-a7b4cec8cc05.title: environment
2e6cbb11-3714-4dd0-bc82-a7b4cec8cc05.description: The living and non-living elements of the Earth’s surface and atmosphere. Where unqualified, it includes human changes to the Earth’s surface, e.g. croplands, planted forests, buildings and roads.

5e56f29c-1609-42a9-87ce-614c6282f0e5.title: ethical practices
5e56f29c-1609-42a9-87ce-614c6282f0e5.description:
The application of fundamental ethical principles when undertaking research and collecting information, e.g. confidentiality, informed consent, citation and integrity of data. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • respecting confidentiality and anonymity
  • avoiding use of deception or misleading information
  • preventing physical and/or emotional risk or harm
  • obtaining permission to access private property or restricted areas
  • minimising damage to the natural environment
  • observing referencing conventions to avoid plagiarism
  • storing data appropriately, e.g. securely, depersonalising data collected
  • acknowledging the provenance of sources, e.g. information, data, visual materials.

f5b29d28-8964-408c-966e-48524defb42f.title: feedback loops
f5b29d28-8964-408c-966e-48524defb42f.description: Feedback loops are reactions in response to environmental change. Positive feedback loops cause one or more components to increase overall, creating a negative impact on the ecosystem. A negative feedback loop has a positive impact on the ecosystem because it decreases the impact of change, bringing it closer to dynamic equilibrium.

103d2e59-0b37-4eca-ba27-56ac6a8027f5.title: geographic region
103d2e59-0b37-4eca-ba27-56ac6a8027f5.description: A region exhibits shared natural or human characteristics, e.g. political, economic, social, cultural, climate, land/water cover, vegetation, that distinguishes the region from neighbouring regions. Regions can be divisions of a nation, or larger than a nation.

d27758ae-8706-4fbc-b873-1fcd935299a8.title: geographical methods
d27758ae-8706-4fbc-b873-1fcd935299a8.description: The tools and skills associated with the discipline of geography that geographers use to develop their understanding of places, environments, and geographical phenomena.

d898c4b1-0091-4a6d-a022-dd05a3cc5f4e.title: geographical processes
d898c4b1-0091-4a6d-a022-dd05a3cc5f4e.description: The physical and human processes that form and transform the world, e.g. the water cycle, erosion, migration and urbanisation. Geographical processes can work in combination and operate within and between places.

7ad3c8e0-cb96-4878-84d2-9a3c5fb386bd.title: geomorphic
7ad3c8e0-cb96-4878-84d2-9a3c5fb386bd.description: Relating to the form of the landscape and other features on the Earth’s surface.

0dacbe3b-0f3c-4bf1-a9bd-cde764c39c17.title: geomorphic processes
0dacbe3b-0f3c-4bf1-a9bd-cde764c39c17.description: Natural processes that transform the lithosphere to create distinctive landscapes and landforms e.g. tectonic activity, weathering, erosion and deposition.

c5ee1239-fa13-4073-ab80-448670880b82.title: geopolitical
c5ee1239-fa13-4073-ab80-448670880b82.description: Politics and international relations as influenced by geographical factors, e.g. related to space, place and environment.

60b40e8e-e33e-42cf-bd28-20ed96c37288.title: human diversity
60b40e8e-e33e-42cf-bd28-20ed96c37288.description: Variations in how people use the places and spaces they occupy, including the nature of their settlements, economies, cultures and societies.

1e49cef7-c897-4057-befa-cb98b9efc244.title: human wellbeing
1e49cef7-c897-4057-befa-cb98b9efc244.description: The quality of life of a population, e.g. access to opportunities, healthcare, education, infrastructure, a clean environment.

134afc7f-8f73-40e1-8016-f21aba2244ba.title: informal settlements
134afc7f-8f73-40e1-8016-f21aba2244ba.description: Areas where housing or shelter is constructed on land where the occupants either have no legal claim, occupy illegally and/or are not in compliance with planning and building regulations. These settlements typically lack provision of amenities and services.

830a74b5-c382-466e-98a0-d981c0c772ae.title: inspirational landscape
830a74b5-c382-466e-98a0-d981c0c772ae.description: Landscapes that stimulate emotional responses based on aesthetic elements, e.g. their dramatic physical form, vibrant colour, arrangement of physical features, diversity of plant species. An inspirational landscape may be experienced directly or through soundscapes and tactile representations, e.g. physical models.

82990ad7-c101-42b7-8db0-5fd138c45ef8.title: land cover
82990ad7-c101-42b7-8db0-5fd138c45ef8.description: The natural and artificial features and structures that cover the land’s surface, e.g. trees, grass, crops, wetlands, water, ice, buildings and pavement.

acdb621d-34f0-4503-bd86-d8c7d0001b2d.title: liveability
acdb621d-34f0-4503-bd86-d8c7d0001b2d.description: An assessment of the quality of a place. The concept of liveability has been linked to a range of factors, e.g. health, sense of safety, access to services, cost of living, comfortable living standards, mobility and transport, air quality and social participation.

d9b7a388-501d-42a9-8a51-b7c43a919e00.title: mega-region
d9b7a388-501d-42a9-8a51-b7c43a919e00.description: An expanding urban cluster, formed as a result of the convergence of more than one metropolitan/urban area.

5725077b-001a-4daa-9265-868a32ec5fce.title: megacity
5725077b-001a-4daa-9265-868a32ec5fce.description: In the context of Geography 11–12 and Geography 11–12 Life Skills, a megacity is a metropolitan area with a total population in excess of 10 million.

bf9de586-b54e-4c85-bfbe-c845469ca61d.title: natural system
bf9de586-b54e-4c85-bfbe-c845469ca61d.description: A combination of physical and/or biological elements, and their interconnected processes, that form an integrated whole.

e0319420-ace6-4bbf-a2dc-8df96d5ee09d.title: oceanity
e0319420-ace6-4bbf-a2dc-8df96d5ee09d.description: The effect of vast bodies of water on climatic conditions/patterns.

d4be9f67-3bb6-456c-ae42-8f8cbf946647.title: Overview Effect
d4be9f67-3bb6-456c-ae42-8f8cbf946647.description: A shift in awareness reported by some astronauts who have viewed the Earth from space, including the wonder of the Earth, the thinness of its atmosphere and the absence of national boundaries.

2cdd2cf8-7350-4259-bcf2-4b965b1d6c8d.title: primary data
2cdd2cf8-7350-4259-bcf2-4b965b1d6c8d.description: Original material collected e.g. field notes, measurements, responses to a survey or questionnaire.

d6296b8c-1a3c-4358-b4a0-8812c76eb61c.title: range of scales
d6296b8c-1a3c-4358-b4a0-8812c76eb61c.description: The varying frames of reference used for viewing and analysing the world in spatial terms. These are commonly described as local, national, regional and global. These scales can be used to develop an understanding of places, environments, natural and human phenomena, geographical patterns and processes, and management. They represent the geographical way of investigating the world.

98bbbea9-666e-4873-994d-6955e7e7e914.title: regional centre
98bbbea9-666e-4873-994d-6955e7e7e914.description: Places that have an economic and social role, servicing the area around them. They are often characterised by factors such as population growth, increasing population density and growth in employment.

d8e92261-7c61-4a1e-b297-05be4267a950.title: remote settlement
d8e92261-7c61-4a1e-b297-05be4267a950.description: A place that has less access to various goods and services because of its location and distance from larger urban settlements.

6927b295-4d06-4fd5-826c-defcb3d132a3.title: resilience
6927b295-4d06-4fd5-826c-defcb3d132a3.description: The ability of an ecosystem to tolerate and recover from natural and/or human-induced disturbance.

150b05d4-9ebb-452d-b6a7-484c382d1105.title: risk management
150b05d4-9ebb-452d-b6a7-484c382d1105.description: In the context of Geography 11–12 and Geography 11–12 Life Skills, risk management is defined in terms of preparedness, mitigation and/or prevention of a natural or ecological hazard. Preparedness involves planning the interventions needed to prevent or mitigate the effects of a hazard. Mitigation involves the implementation of strategies to eliminate or minimise the effects of these hazards. Adaptation involves adjusting to the changed environmental circumstances.

d8220f48-a464-4693-96f9-8af345ce5ebb.title: rural place/rural settlements
d8220f48-a464-4693-96f9-8af345ce5ebb.description: A reference to a settlement in the countryside typically serving a farming or agricultural area.

79aea2e5-3309-4f4a-b3aa-c23b36025a66.title: secondary sources/information
79aea2e5-3309-4f4a-b3aa-c23b36025a66.description: Sources of information that have been collected, processed, interpreted and published by others, e.g. census data, newspaper articles and images or information in a published report.

bc5a601e-7336-47b5-8bcb-bc5998f31765.title: settlement pattern
bc5a601e-7336-47b5-8bcb-bc5998f31765.description: The spatial distribution of different types of human settlement, e.g. dwellings, towns, cities. Settlements may take a range of forms, including linear, scattered, clustered, nucleated, dispersed, planned, radial.

7b8db86f-f924-48fd-adc0-2f2f50cb5c71.title: shifting baselines
7b8db86f-f924-48fd-adc0-2f2f50cb5c71.description:
A theory that describes the way changes to an ecosystem are measured against previous reference points or baselines, which themselves may represent changes from an even earlier state of the ecosystem.

It reflects the perception of each new generation that current conditions are the same as past conditions. An ecosystem may therefore be degraded successively over time, so that the extent of change from its original state, is greater than perceived. Shifting baselines describes the situation where knowledge is lost about the original state of the natural world.

1f1c3fce-ec47-41f8-ac66-ad5193be006c.title: sociocultural
1f1c3fce-ec47-41f8-ac66-ad5193be006c.description: Related to social and cultural factors that influence people and communities.

a4b7e314-bdc3-4b2e-84cd-9a6b70708a55.title: spatial change
a4b7e314-bdc3-4b2e-84cd-9a6b70708a55.description: Change in the location and arrangement of particular features, phenomena or activities across the surface of the Earth.

de5cb53d-0ae3-4c2b-938e-5bed5572a142.title: spatial distribution
de5cb53d-0ae3-4c2b-938e-5bed5572a142.description: The location and arrangement of particular features, phenomena or activities across the surface of the Earth.

9aca1813-2c16-4ac2-a13a-67db5d89574e.title: spatial technologies
9aca1813-2c16-4ac2-a13a-67db5d89574e.description: Any form of technology that interacts with place, space and location. Spatial technologies may be used to collect, organise, record, visualise, manipulate, analyse and display spatial data.

10cfa891-1ee0-4801-8ade-ad4fd6ba944e.title: spheres of influence
10cfa891-1ee0-4801-8ade-ad4fd6ba944e.description: The geographical area over which the services and functions of an urban settlement extend. Larger settlements typically have a greater sphere of influence than smaller settlements and attract people from a wider geographical area.

65e57029-b3a9-4a61-8ad6-19e272b84d30.title: students investigate
65e57029-b3a9-4a61-8ad6-19e272b84d30.description: In the context of Geography 11–12, this encompasses a broad range of learning approaches and activities, facilitated by a variety of teaching strategies.

69fe3c65-2676-4b5a-ac32-318edb570d99.title: tipping points
69fe3c65-2676-4b5a-ac32-318edb570d99.description: A critical point (often called a threshold) where a series of smaller changes become significant enough, collectively, to trigger a larger-scale change. The change is often abrupt and irreversible, permanently altering the state of the original system, leading to flow-on effects that have more widespread consequences for other natural systems, and for people.

2da90236-215c-4f26-a144-89925f6308c8.title: transformation
2da90236-215c-4f26-a144-89925f6308c8.description: In the context of this syllabus, the term transformation refers to the processes of change from which forms of environmental, social, cultural and economic relationships and patterns emerge.

48d577f2-7e25-491b-b55d-2db7f6952247.title: urban corridor
48d577f2-7e25-491b-b55d-2db7f6952247.description: A part of an urban area defined by a particular geographical feature such as a transportation route.

715682d8-8bf1-4692-8e34-d7845af810e3.title: urban hierarchy
715682d8-8bf1-4692-8e34-d7845af810e3.description: The ranking of urban places in descending order, e.g. cities, determined by population size.

50bebb28-d87a-4d04-8fc3-b321f3779863.title: urban place
50bebb28-d87a-4d04-8fc3-b321f3779863.description: A reference to a permanent settlement or built-up area with a relatively dense population.

7a128d39-ba09-4039-8de6-59c5ec3121de.title: urbanisation
7a128d39-ba09-4039-8de6-59c5ec3121de.description: The process of demographic, economic and/or social change in which an increasing proportion of the population of a country or region live in urban areas. The size and rate of urbanisation is influenced by push-pull factors.

a2a5d521-f853-4e70-af7f-93345d7e18e6.title: vulnerability
a2a5d521-f853-4e70-af7f-93345d7e18e6.description: In the context of this syllabus, the term vulnerability refers to an ecosystem’s risk of exposure or susceptibility to stress.

82304ea3-b183-4738-8809-9b8c282452ed.title: cartogram maps
82304ea3-b183-4738-8809-9b8c282452ed.description: A map in which the size of the countries are adjusted to illustrate the distribution of a feature or statistic.

b0b45646-5fa1-4a90-8a9a-5b131d2da635.title: catchment area
b0b45646-5fa1-4a90-8a9a-5b131d2da635.description: The area drained by a river or water body. Also known as a river basin.

d2d156cc-aee7-4ad0-9414-0fe6444f2f23.title: characteristics
d2d156cc-aee7-4ad0-9414-0fe6444f2f23.description: The tangible and intangible elements of a place or environment.

e300ca38-4b9f-4c31-b606-4aee68b9c8d8.title: consumption
e300ca38-4b9f-4c31-b606-4aee68b9c8d8.description: The act of using or purchasing goods and services which can impact on the environment, economy, individuals and society.

3b869a62-5ea1-4d9d-80f9-8ab50b2f80c7.title: contour lines
3b869a62-5ea1-4d9d-80f9-8ab50b2f80c7.description: Lines on a map that indicate altitude.

ce04cefa-977d-449a-93d9-d8d452ffbf6f.title: cross-section
ce04cefa-977d-449a-93d9-d8d452ffbf6f.description: A graphical representation constructed as a line graph that depicts a vertical slice through the Earth’s surface and provides a sideways view of the landscape.

c9195121-6fb8-46cd-8cb0-1c61795801cf.title: Cultural mapping
c9195121-6fb8-46cd-8cb0-1c61795801cf.description: Creating a record of a landscape that is alive with activity, including Culture, Lore, language and ethics.

384abfe6-4e8e-493a-bc8c-101be5adb34d.title: density
384abfe6-4e8e-493a-bc8c-101be5adb34d.description: The concentration of a feature in a specific area, e.g. the number of buildings per square kilometre.

6cc73f93-58ef-4a8c-9d08-0e3b9e33f508.title: deposition
6cc73f93-58ef-4a8c-9d08-0e3b9e33f508.description: The process by which eroded materials are laid down in a new location.

7180c9e2-185b-4550-b2df-88490a2fcf0e.title: development
7180c9e2-185b-4550-b2df-88490a2fcf0e.description: Economic, social and political changes that improve the wellbeing of people.

cc4a584b-3b57-4b55-8011-94957e7deaec.title: dot maps
cc4a584b-3b57-4b55-8011-94957e7deaec.description: A thematic map that uses dots to mark locations where a phenomenon occurs.

6044e09d-bc4e-490b-beab-83ccb85b0873.title: environmental change(s)
6044e09d-bc4e-490b-beab-83ccb85b0873.description: Alterations in natural environments over time, driven by both natural processes and human activities.

03f86966-4217-4f5e-906b-3a9b0ece70b4.title: environmental quality
03f86966-4217-4f5e-906b-3a9b0ece70b4.description: Characteristics of a local environment that affect human wellbeing, such as pollution, access to open space, traffic volume, and visual effects of buildings and roads.

995a94a7-7ca1-413b-b205-bc5fb871714f.title: field sketches
995a94a7-7ca1-413b-b205-bc5fb871714f.description: A type of visual representation created during fieldwork activities used to record the main geographical features observed.

cd4ee12b-d7c4-45ad-8de6-b507f6a1e594.title: fieldwork transects
cd4ee12b-d7c4-45ad-8de6-b507f6a1e594.description: A straight measured line between 2 points along which environmental features are observed and recorded. Often measured with a tape measure or rope.

b0af82f8-ae06-44bb-8969-772e7e068bc4.title: flowline maps
