ac6cf228-7912-4135-a20a-22c1341597cd.description: An amount of money that is paid into an annuity. The contribution can be made as a lump sum or as a series of payments.

226f71ee-d8e0-4e57-9012-bd680a01a5a9.title: cosine rule

6d4214ff-392f-4dfb-9b5a-684fbe455a05.title: cost
6d4214ff-392f-4dfb-9b5a-684fbe455a05.description: The price paid to acquire, produce, accomplish or maintain anything.

3218669a-0393-4020-8b4d-3783d8450da8.title: cumulative frequency
3218669a-0393-4020-8b4d-3783d8450da8.description: The accumulating total of frequencies within an ordered dataset.

5e2a7080-1595-4db4-af06-9433479f003c.title: cumulative frequency histogram
5e2a7080-1595-4db4-af06-9433479f003c.description:
A visual representation of data using bars to represent the class boundaries and the cumulative frequencies.

The area of each bar is proportional to the cumulative frequency of the observations up to the end of that class.

bc3a67e6-c02a-46e1-980c-40b7a7d3261f.title: cumulative frequency polygon
bc3a67e6-c02a-46e1-980c-40b7a7d3261f.description: A series of straight lines representing the cumulative frequency for a given dataset. Sometimes called the ‘ogive’.

b286e5f3-51c3-4187-b752-62b277fd94d7.title: discrete probability distribution
b286e5f3-51c3-4187-b752-62b277fd94d7.description: Specifies the probabilities with which a discrete random variable takes each of its values.

d520eb22-0a20-4d8f-aa42-089c594b118c.title: displacement
d520eb22-0a20-4d8f-aa42-089c594b118c.description: The change in position of an object, after a period of time, from its original position. Displacement is a vector quantity. The displacement may be positive, negative or zero.

4d56db92-5987-4aa5-acbd-e5d50071d27b.title: distance
4d56db92-5987-4aa5-acbd-e5d50071d27b.description: The length between 2 points. Distance is a positive scalar quantity.

0e8d11e5-82ca-49c5-ab38-ca167c0683ed.title: distance–time graph
0e8d11e5-82ca-49c5-ab38-ca167c0683ed.description: A line graph that relates distance and time, with time on the horizontal axis and distance on the vertical axis.

c4545a73-5327-496d-a543-1a77d88c395d.title: empirical rule (for a normally distributed random variable)

2041247c-37ab-4af7-80cc-60427220d278.title: experiment (random)
2041247c-37ab-4af7-80cc-60427220d278.description: A process with an observable result. The results of the experiment are the set of possible outcomes called the sample space.

425d527d-0db4-4948-84ad-50391a954ea1.title: identity
425d527d-0db4-4948-84ad-50391a954ea1.description: An identity is a statement involving a variable(s) that is true for all possible values of the variable(s).

3a8c851d-42ba-4cee-8e3d-24267828bd84.title: integration
3a8c851d-42ba-4cee-8e3d-24267828bd84.description: The process of finding the integral of a function. The inverse of differentiation.

12aa602f-634b-4943-b466-4867bff2af46.title: interest
12aa602f-634b-4943-b466-4867bff2af46.description: Money paid or received in return for using or lending money.

f78ff81b-acd4-43c0-ae60-10beca4bd772.title: interest rate
f78ff81b-acd4-43c0-ae60-10beca4bd772.description: A percentage at which interest is charged or paid.

cc71d1f1-60ba-4bd4-8179-5bf4c08a0b82.title: investment
cc71d1f1-60ba-4bd4-8179-5bf4c08a0b82.description: An allocation of money or capital into an asset or venture that is expected to generate a profit or return.

8e1a2b03-c4df-4f89-b65e-739660a1d226.title: linear
8e1a2b03-c4df-4f89-b65e-739660a1d226.description: Something that can be represented or modelled by a straight line.

b8dd93e6-a199-475d-a322-7eecca2f8cd8.title: loan
b8dd93e6-a199-475d-a322-7eecca2f8cd8.description: An amount of money borrowed from a bank or other financial institution.

efefa345-4a11-4e4f-85b8-6832582f7c87.title: multistage events
efefa345-4a11-4e4f-85b8-6832582f7c87.description: An event that consists of 2 or more simple experiments, e.g. tossing a coin 3 times (repeated trials), or both tossing a coin and rolling a dice (possible outcomes would be H and 5, T and 2).

06db70ad-6d65-4b8b-a34b-5e0ae02c3a13.title: normal distribution
06db70ad-6d65-4b8b-a34b-5e0ae02c3a13.description:
A type of continuous distribution whose graph looks like this:

Image long description: The horizontal x-axis is labelled from 100 to 200 in increments of 20 from left to right. The y-axis is labelled from 0 to 50 in increments of 10 from the bottom to the top. Along the x-axis is a series of columns that rise to a peak halfway along the axis and fall back towards 0 on the far right of the x-axis. An orange ‘bell curve’ is laid over the peaks of the columns.

The mean, median and mode are equal and the scores are symmetrically arranged either side of the mean.

The graph of a normal distribution is often called a ‘bell curve’ due to its shape.

a1ad5e24-fa6e-49b8-ab38-7a82aa03f32c.title: point of inflection
a1ad5e24-fa6e-49b8-ab38-7a82aa03f32c.description: A point on a curve where the concavity changes. At a point of inflection, the tangent exists and crosses the curve.

31c5c095-0e9b-4734-a16f-c9d02e4e3c3f.title: real number
31c5c095-0e9b-4734-a16f-c9d02e4e3c3f.description: A number that can be represented by a point on a number line. The set of real numbers is the set of all rational and irrational numbers.

6d9e0adf-203d-47c7-ad8b-48711513f460.title: reducing balance loan
6d9e0adf-203d-47c7-ad8b-48711513f460.description: A reducing balance loan is a compound interest loan where the loan is repaid by making regular payments and the interest paid is calculated on the amount still owing (the reducing balance of the loan) after each payment is made.

9eeb5a4e-be94-4da7-874a-2a6e7afe2e7e.title: repayment
9eeb5a4e-be94-4da7-874a-2a6e7afe2e7e.description: A set amount, paid at regular intervals over the period of a loan, to pay off a loan.

df732ff5-6c24-4d67-b463-3013cffe902a.title: sine rule

e9ee0a3a-c41b-4b13-9244-cfa2789fc9c7.title: substitution
e9ee0a3a-c41b-4b13-9244-cfa2789fc9c7.description:
The process of replacing a variable in an algebraic expression, formula, equation or function consistently with a particular value, another variable, expression or function.

Simultaneous equations can be solved using substitution by isolating one variable in one equation and using its value to replace that variable in another equation.

See simultaneous equations

Extended in Mathematics Extension 1 and Extension 2: Integration by substitution is a method used for evaluating integrals. The substitution could be expressed as a function of the variable of integration, or with the variable of integration as the subject of the substitution.

74d2b5d2-920c-417c-b649-f0287ff937dc.title: transformation
74d2b5d2-920c-417c-b649-f0287ff937dc.description:
A procedure or set of procedures that changes the size and/or shape of an image. A transformation operates on points in the plane to change aspects, such as the position, size or shape of curves and other figures.

Translations, reflections, rotations, dilations, enlargements are all examples of transformations.

d93fc40d-2a0b-4d76-a3e7-d09b94469aea.title: translation
d93fc40d-2a0b-4d76-a3e7-d09b94469aea.description: A type of transformation that moves a shape (or all the points in a plane) by the same amount to the left or right, or up or down.

c52612b3-195f-409b-8e4a-b7603a01d6fe.title: trial
c52612b3-195f-409b-8e4a-b7603a01d6fe.description:
A single performance of a random experiment. Successive trials refer to repeated performances of the same experiment, each of which will therefore have the same set of possible outcomes (sample space).

When there are only 2 possible outcomes they are known as Bernoulli trials.

fc4c1122-3652-4f70-a322-2d822d663113.title: turning points
fc4c1122-3652-4f70-a322-2d822d663113.description: Points at which the gradient of the graph of a function changes direction, so the function has either a local minimum or local maximum at those points.

e0c74bc9-1697-4481-aa15-77e76a885f26.title: revenue
e0c74bc9-1697-4481-aa15-77e76a885f26.description: The total income generated from normal business operations, such as from the sale of items produced.

03dac5f0-c5b7-458a-bec5-ad2bc86e9f40.title: vertex
03dac5f0-c5b7-458a-bec5-ad2bc86e9f40.description:
Where 2 straight sides of a two-dimensional shape meet.

Extended in 7–12: A vertex is a point in the plane where lines meet and do not extend beyond, or a point in space where several edges meet. A vertex can also refer to a node in a network. It is also the turning point of a parabola.

ddb506c9-9f51-4d20-9b2b-64cd9cc5792f.title: volume
ddb506c9-9f51-4d20-9b2b-64cd9cc5792f.description: The amount of space occupied by an object.

f9bb689f-3dc2-4289-8e22-85ef4ebc5331.title: midpoint
f9bb689f-3dc2-4289-8e22-85ef4ebc5331.description: A point on a line segment or interval that divides the segment into 2 equal parts.

9be5991c-e35d-4fea-aab6-6cad5c575f5d.title: monic
9be5991c-e35d-4fea-aab6-6cad5c575f5d.description: A polynomial in which the coefficient of the leading term is 1.

6412b1cf-d662-4599-823b-03b51cba3e0a.title: obtuse angle
6412b1cf-d662-4599-823b-03b51cba3e0a.description: An angle bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight angle (2 right angles, or 180°).

7c8313bb-a921-4a1d-b0db-a69a1e5ffba2.title: polynomial
7c8313bb-a921-4a1d-b0db-a69a1e5ffba2.description: An expression made up of non-negative integer powers of the same variable and coefficients combined using addition, subtraction and multiplication.

cb99fb2c-ea20-48bc-b40e-f8b678cafca1.title: population
cb99fb2c-ea20-48bc-b40e-f8b678cafca1.description:
The complete set of individuals, objects, places, etc., that we want information about.

Extended in Mathematics Standard and Mathematics Extension 1: In statistics it is the entire dataset from which a statistical sample may be drawn.

75e49971-05dd-4fc1-add8-557bcc1cdba2.title: quotient
75e49971-05dd-4fc1-add8-557bcc1cdba2.description: The result of dividing one number or algebraic expression by another.

552e7a6b-4b3c-430a-9b56-4fb3b6e6eccf.title: Bernoulli distribution
552e7a6b-4b3c-430a-9b56-4fb3b6e6eccf.description: A discrete probability distribution of a Bernoulli random variable.

324d9bbb-257a-4f86-a87d-e2ab0c32abaf.title: binomial experiment
324d9bbb-257a-4f86-a87d-e2ab0c32abaf.description: Performance of a fixed number of Bernoulli trials.

e8134f6a-64a6-4f12-9177-47c38daf9a62.title: directed line segment
e8134f6a-64a6-4f12-9177-47c38daf9a62.description: A part of a line between 2 endpoints, with fixed length and a direction.

f732bff0-a25c-43bd-a1ae-5dba0f977757.title: displacement vector
f732bff0-a25c-43bd-a1ae-5dba0f977757.description: Represents the displacement from one point to another.

e39ebb64-f34a-4042-a9f4-1fc3f23fc632.title: leading coefficient
e39ebb64-f34a-4042-a9f4-1fc3f23fc632.description: The coefficient of the term involving the highest power in a polynomial.

c1581701-a6fa-4438-b050-9e9b234567b7.title: leading term
c1581701-a6fa-4438-b050-9e9b234567b7.description: The term involving the highest power in a polynomial.

29756e88-0332-48ba-a79b-49de1d0f41b2.title: Pascal's triangle
29756e88-0332-48ba-a79b-49de1d0f41b2.description:
A triangular figure with rows of numbers starting and ending with 1, where each interior number is equal to the sum of the two numbers immediately above it.

See binomial coefficient

0b855ba9-424f-4a14-81b7-9b3c5c32f3a8.title: projection (vectors)
0b855ba9-424f-4a14-81b7-9b3c5c32f3a8.description: Image long description: Two vector diagrams both representing vectors, each showing 2 arrows connected at a point. In the first diagram, the angle between the arrows is acute. One arrow is labelled with boldface a, the other with boldface b, with the b arrow as the longer vector, pointing up and to the right. A dotted line perpendicular to arrow b joins the tip of arrow a. There is an arrow drawn on top of arrow b from the vertex, which is labelled proj b a, with a subscripted b and boldface a. In the second diagram the angle between the arrows is obtuse. One arrow is labelled with boldface a and the other with boldface b, with b as the longer vector, pointing up and to the right. A dotted line perpendicular to arrow b joins the tip of arrow a, pointing up and to the left, to an extension of arrow b, pointing down and to the left. The arrow drawn on top of arrow b from the vertex is labelled proj b a with a subscripted b and boldface a.

83240397-f840-4054-99cc-1e1a76285488.title: sampling distribution
83240397-f840-4054-99cc-1e1a76285488.description: The distribution of a sample statistic over all samples of the same size.

38c4e489-f95c-4841-86c9-1acebc1bb659.title: slope field
38c4e489-f95c-4841-86c9-1acebc1bb659.description: A graphical representation of the tangent lines to the solutions of a first-order differential equation.

f3f6c87e-20a9-4050-bf18-85fdaded93a2.title: triangle law
f3f6c87e-20a9-4050-bf18-85fdaded93a2.description: For vector addition, when 2 vectors are represented as 2 sides of a triangle, the third side represents the resultant vector:

61860e09-da1f-45ef-a8f5-912490482bed.title: zero polynomial
61860e09-da1f-45ef-a8f5-912490482bed.description: A polynomial that has all coefficients equal to zero.

b2049056-0bab-4f00-b142-c3f2861e8328.title: gravity/gravitational
b2049056-0bab-4f00-b142-c3f2861e8328.description: The force of attraction that objects with mass exert on each other.

958458c9-8b0c-4174-b7ce-ce348f424482.title: Cartesian equation
958458c9-8b0c-4174-b7ce-ce348f424482.description: The equation of a relation or a function expressed in terms of the Cartesian coordinates 𝑥 and 𝑦. May sometimes be formed from 2 parametric equations by eliminating the parameter.

0e052fb6-9706-4a6c-b7f7-0213c0184012.title: component
0e052fb6-9706-4a6c-b7f7-0213c0184012.description:
One of the parts of a vector that is parallel to a particular axis or lying in a specified direction.

See component form (vectors)

b29adcc8-f745-4f57-97e9-396fb364e603.title: expected frequency
b29adcc8-f745-4f57-97e9-396fb364e603.description: The number of times that a particular event or outcome is predicted to occur using theoretical probability.

d098da01-a0f0-4f6c-8480-c5f7d91a7ce9.title: one-to-one
d098da01-a0f0-4f6c-8480-c5f7d91a7ce9.description: A correspondence between 2 sets where each element of one set is paired with one, and only one, element of another set.

8e0192d4-dc84-493b-9b2d-04be552fef82.title: parallelogram law

b22074b1-7dd0-4df2-b8de-b79e18f4c9c4.title: projectile
b22074b1-7dd0-4df2-b8de-b79e18f4c9c4.description: An object initially propelled by an external force, after which the only forces acting on it are gravity and possibly a resistive force due to its motion through a surrounding medium.

bed3b584-4377-4d96-bc99-7b0815041fce.title: statement
bed3b584-4377-4d96-bc99-7b0815041fce.description:
A statement is an assertion that is either true or false but not both.

Also referred to as a proposition.

40a04368-ca9e-48cd-aef0-d27058cf058b.title: vector
40a04368-ca9e-48cd-aef0-d27058cf058b.description: A quantity having both magnitude and direction.

aa7555f6-0176-42d9-aee8-bdd4bf8c1500.title: commutativity (commutative property)
aa7555f6-0176-42d9-aee8-bdd4bf8c1500.description:
Commutativity (commutative property) of addition or multiplication means that 2 numbers can be added or multiplied in any order and the solution will be the same.

Commutative law, commutativity and turn-around facts are interchangeable terms.

fc79db7a-13ca-4fea-8704-39184946ff07.title: collinear
fc79db7a-13ca-4fea-8704-39184946ff07.description: Describes points that lie on the same straight line.

fda58619-b345-45e2-a58d-e6bb5c0e4cdc.title: unit circle
fda58619-b345-45e2-a58d-e6bb5c0e4cdc.description: A circle with a radius of 1 unit.

d61ae10b-0450-4cb1-a773-43192c141ce4.title: complex plane
d61ae10b-0450-4cb1-a773-43192c141ce4.description: A Cartesian plane in which the real part of a complex number is plotted on the horizontal axis, referred to as the real axis, and the imaginary part on the vertical axis, referred to as the imaginary axis. Sometimes called the Argand plane.

c6b7bb51-ce23-4738-80cd-3e4fbd6040c2.title: counterexample
c6b7bb51-ce23-4738-80cd-3e4fbd6040c2.description: An instance/example where the proposition is not true, thereby showing the proposition to be false.

465f8e0f-548a-453a-9cd4-497416115e05.title: direction vector
465f8e0f-548a-453a-9cd4-497416115e05.description: For a straight line or line segment, a direction vector is a vector whose direction is that of the line or line segment.

dd36d083-9204-4a27-84b9-9c4a0149fcfb.title: integrand
dd36d083-9204-4a27-84b9-9c4a0149fcfb.description: A function that is to be integrated.

d1c7294a-2133-4bf9-8de5-b177eeace47d.title: integration by parts
d1c7294a-2133-4bf9-8de5-b177eeace47d.description:
A process of transforming the integral of a product of functions into an integral which can be more easily found. It is derived using the product rule for differentiation.

See product rule

c2a8cd2b-a12d-4e37-b765-ce2b0c81c60c.title: principal argument of a complex number

46aab5ed-b4d9-4aba-836f-e416bf7baf44.title: proof by contradiction
46aab5ed-b4d9-4aba-836f-e416bf7baf44.description: The negation of an original statement is assumed but is proven false, usually by deriving a contradiction, so the negation of the original statement cannot be true, that is, the original statement is true.

76cf0d70-494b-4403-8f66-f71b3439df72.title: resisted motion
76cf0d70-494b-4403-8f66-f71b3439df72.description: Motion that encounters resisting forces such as air resistance.

6f31f330-ce81-4e71-a53d-c944e57adfd2.title: simple harmonic motion
6f31f330-ce81-4e71-a53d-c944e57adfd2.description: Motion in which acceleration is proportional to, and in the opposite direction to, displacement. It is a repetitive movement back and forth through an equilibrium, or central position, so that the maximum displacement on one side of this position is equal to the maximum displacement on the other side.

d986db77-0b4e-476f-bc7a-6797d791bba5.title: skew lines
d986db77-0b4e-476f-bc7a-6797d791bba5.description: In 3 dimensions, lines that do not intersect and are not parallel to each other.

9e1bf2f5-d745-40ee-b7ef-38fbe43f5966.title: terminal velocity
9e1bf2f5-d745-40ee-b7ef-38fbe43f5966.description: The constant velocity that a free-falling object approaches as the resistance of the medium through which the object is falling more closely cancels the downward gravitational force.

aae2635c-526b-421c-b42e-f6b474a9d2ec.title: absolute error
aae2635c-526b-421c-b42e-f6b474a9d2ec.description: In a measurement, half of the smallest unit of the measuring device. The smallest unit is called the precision of the device.

dc04d7da-cfb4-41d2-879c-041a85924fd9.title: attribute
dc04d7da-cfb4-41d2-879c-041a85924fd9.description: A quality, feature or characteristic of an object or shape.

90063adf-99e8-4ff3-9716-4c2053c9c91a.title: closed shape
90063adf-99e8-4ff3-9716-4c2053c9c91a.description: A shape enclosed by all its sides with no gaps.

c61d45d8-4a01-4611-8bd4-19deff8f2d1a.title: combinations
c61d45d8-4a01-4611-8bd4-19deff8f2d1a.description: The various ways a group of items can be arranged without regard to order.

0c689f8f-68b1-4b3a-bd27-2307e7e37465.title: constant difference
0c689f8f-68b1-4b3a-bd27-2307e7e37465.description: Constant difference refers to a common difference between pairs of numbers. For example, the difference between 3 and 7 is 4, and another pair of numbers that has a difference of 4 is 2 and 6.

524ce0f6-957c-4657-b98c-11ffbd0c9f25.title: container
524ce0f6-957c-4657-b98c-11ffbd0c9f25.description: Objects such as bottles, jars and tubs.

51af9f00-0d56-483b-acd1-c2036f92159f.title: corresponding angles
51af9f00-0d56-483b-acd1-c2036f92159f.description:
Angles that lie in the same relative position at the points of intersection where a pair of lines is cut by a transversal.

If the lines are parallel, then each pair of corresponding angles is equal.

Conversely, if a pair of corresponding angles is equal, then the lines are parallel.

3c9f6386-2d31-4fe0-b951-9e23cce06c40.title: cube
3c9f6386-2d31-4fe0-b951-9e23cce06c40.description: An object with 6 equal square faces and 12 edges.

bd2957f0-b753-4201-9380-1946e884d7e3.title: curve
bd2957f0-b753-4201-9380-1946e884d7e3.description: A one-dimensional figure that is not straight.

16d02036-24ee-4bac-9d51-96fb7d891f61.title: curved surface
16d02036-24ee-4bac-9d51-96fb7d891f61.description: Surface of an object that is not flat, e.g. a cylinder has one curved surface.

eda3acd0-2cbe-41e8-b1d7-b6b541315f92.title: data
eda3acd0-2cbe-41e8-b1d7-b6b541315f92.description: Facts or units of information collected together.

1a4c9144-b784-4329-9f9f-704acdc84176.title: difference
1a4c9144-b784-4329-9f9f-704acdc84176.description:
The difference of 2 numbers is the result of subtracting one from the other. You can use subtraction or addition to find the difference between 2 numbers.

For example, to find the difference between 15 and 21, you can:

  • add 5 up from 15 to get to 20, then add one more to get to 21, so the difference is 6
  • start with 21 and count back to find the difference of 6.

dea607d0-23b8-44d0-bf1c-b29a0cadd0bb.title: doubling and halving
dea607d0-23b8-44d0-bf1c-b29a0cadd0bb.description:
Doubling and halving is a strategy that can make solving multiplication problems easier, e.g. solving 4 x 12 is the same as solving 2 x 24.

Doubling and halving is also a strategy used to find factors of a number. For example, to find the factors of 24, start with 1 x 24 then double and halve, 2 x 12, 4 x 6, 8 x 3.

7360d2b0-84ee-4aa7-b065-fe37d093c213.title: edge
7360d2b0-84ee-4aa7-b065-fe37d093c213.description: The line segment formed by the intersection of two faces of a polyhedron, e.g. a cube has 6 faces and 12 edges.

ba48203f-e6d3-4888-a8ed-106fcc081375.title: equal-arm balance
ba48203f-e6d3-4888-a8ed-106fcc081375.description: A balance where the distance from the support point (middle) to the arms at each end is equal.

5a088d15-c4b1-4888-8bce-86f6e497d7d9.title: equals sign
5a088d15-c4b1-4888-8bce-86f6e497d7d9.description:
In mathematics, the equals sign is used to indicate equivalence, e.g. 5 + 1 = 2 + 4 and to show that two or more amounts have the same value.

See equivalent

1dc286d4-63a8-4560-abe6-3e5841c34aa1.title: face
1dc286d4-63a8-4560-abe6-3e5841c34aa1.description: A flat surface of a 3-dimensional geometric object (polyhedron) with only straight edges.

c57e2629-dc33-4989-9574-7f1cca2f5ef7.title: Gregorian calendar
c57e2629-dc33-4989-9574-7f1cca2f5ef7.description: The Gregorian calendar is the most widely used solar dating calendar. It was introduced in 1582 as a modification of the Julian calendar.

8d325c7e-2669-465d-96c9-cabf41452c91.title: grouping division
8d325c7e-2669-465d-96c9-cabf41452c91.description:
Grouping (quotitive) division requires finding how many groups are formed, e.g. if I have 12 marbles and each child gets 4, how many children will get marbles?

When grouping, the quotient represents the number of groups within the shared quantity.

7161a29a-dd1a-4e4e-b9ba-ced32e1296e0.title: hefting
7161a29a-dd1a-4e4e-b9ba-ced32e1296e0.description: Testing the weight of an object by lifting and/or balancing it.

4dc30ca6-e42d-4273-9d71-a8e6df6b5201.title: internal volume (capacity)
4dc30ca6-e42d-4273-9d71-a8e6df6b5201.description: A measure of how much a container can hold.

463c6851-b236-47ca-aea7-af7ec98cab76.title: inverse operation
463c6851-b236-47ca-aea7-af7ec98cab76.description:
The operation that reverses the effect of another operation. 

Examples:

  • Addition and subtraction are inverse operations. When you add 3 to 7 you get 10. If you then subtract 3, you get back to 7.
  • Multiplication and division are inverse operations. When you multiply 6 by 2 you get 12. If you then divide by 2 you get back to 6.

c4f4ca34-ab82-47a9-a42b-bb6897c73160.title: jump strategy
c4f4ca34-ab82-47a9-a42b-bb6897c73160.description: A mental calculation method that involves jumping from one number (usually the largest number) either forwards (addition) or backwards (subtraction) to the solution.

fbf1f919-5975-4286-b730-a2d8f01fa174.title: length
fbf1f919-5975-4286-b730-a2d8f01fa174.description: Measure of an object from end to end.

fe669b96-d317-4841-b169-2f624303c3b2.title: line
fe669b96-d317-4841-b169-2f624303c3b2.description: A one-dimensional figure that is straight, has no thickness and extends endlessly.

ac783398-7ee8-47d1-b2bc-2add10bf60dd.title: linear pattern
ac783398-7ee8-47d1-b2bc-2add10bf60dd.description: A pattern created by the regular repetition of units with the same difference between terms.

dea42c10-214b-4834-a03e-4812dcdf847a.title: list
dea42c10-214b-4834-a03e-4812dcdf847a.description: A number of items, typically presented one after the other.

994b51b1-78f4-49ab-890a-4fc59505117c.title: five (5)-number summary
994b51b1-78f4-49ab-890a-4fc59505117c.description: A method for summarising a dataset using 5 statistics: the minimum value, the lower quartile, the median, the upper quartile and the maximum value.

5de65745-eb2b-49d3-a953-e00d37576551.title: adjacent
5de65745-eb2b-49d3-a953-e00d37576551.description: Has different meanings for different mathematical contexts. For example, adjacent vertices in a network are joined by an edge and adjacent faces in a solid have a common edge. In trigonometry, the adjacent side of a right-angled triangle is the side next to the angle to which the trigonometric ratio is referring.

b68916af-de67-4de6-b109-00dc5c3b615e.title: adjacent angles
b68916af-de67-4de6-b109-00dc5c3b615e.description:
Angles that share a vertex and an arm. They do not overlap.

Extended in 7–10: Two angles at a point are called adjacent if they share a common ray and a common vertex and lie on opposite sides of the common ray.

1487efac-e1f0-4eef-b906-49d689df2a04.title: alternate angle
1487efac-e1f0-4eef-b906-49d689df2a04.description: In each diagram below, the 2 marked angles are called alternate angles (since they are on alternate sides of the transversal).

13f25252-8fee-4787-be08-ff4a0b3c2877.title: base
13f25252-8fee-4787-be08-ff4a0b3c2877.description: Has different meanings for different mathematical contexts. A base is a number that is raised to a power and the base of a solid is the face the object rests on.

cd018f7d-6bda-468a-9514-ff103536d6c4.title: bias
cd018f7d-6bda-468a-9514-ff103536d6c4.description: A systematic favouring of certain outcomes more than others, due to unfair influence (knowingly or otherwise).

ffd78fad-cfa5-40b9-bd7f-4e0119f1f617.title: bivariate data
ffd78fad-cfa5-40b9-bd7f-4e0119f1f617.description: Data relating to measurement of 2 variables. It can be categorical data, numerical data or a combination of both.

9ba4c9dd-f74f-4424-8b81-d41591d43ba2.title: box plot
9ba4c9dd-f74f-4424-8b81-d41591d43ba2.description:
A synonym for a box-and-whisker plot. A graphical display of a 5-number summary of data. The ‘box’ covers the middle 50% of scores. The ‘whiskers’ extend to the maximum and minimum values in the dataset.

In a box plot, the 'box' covers the interquartile range (IQR). A vertical line in the box is used to indicate the location of the median.

The box plot below has been constructed from the 5-number summary of the resting pulse rates of 17 students.

6cee81ee-c37e-40f6-97b3-e67768bdabdc.title: capacity (internal volume)
6cee81ee-c37e-40f6-97b3-e67768bdabdc.description:
Generally refers to the amount a container can hold.

A term used to describe how much a container will hold. It is often used in relation to the volume of fluids. Units of capacity (volume of fluids or gases) include litres and millilitres.

See internal volume (capacity)

0a2b4dda-e3fe-4555-bdf2-2b5964aba968.title: categorical variable
0a2b4dda-e3fe-4555-bdf2-2b5964aba968.description: A variable whose values belong to exactly one of a number of categories. A categorical variable describes a quality or characteristic of something. Sometimes called a discrete variable. There are 2 types of categorical variables: nominal and ordinal. For example, your home state or blood type are categorical variables.

ec75a969-94b1-4507-afe8-41061fdf4ac3.title: causal
ec75a969-94b1-4507-afe8-41061fdf4ac3.description: Two variables with a relationship which indicates that one event is the result of the occurrence of the other event.

7219a262-5549-4274-8927-cb9866551ac6.title: chord
7219a262-5549-4274-8927-cb9866551ac6.description: A line segment (interval) joining 2 points on a circle.

6b539f10-c241-4913-a4b1-1b3c5f05234a.title: circuit (networks)
6b539f10-c241-4913-a4b1-1b3c5f05234a.description: A trail that begins and ends on the same vertex. Vertices can be repeated.

1c2b0028-b4af-4393-8518-1da9490dbe3e.title: co-interior angles
1c2b0028-b4af-4393-8518-1da9490dbe3e.description:
A pair of angles that lie between a pair of parallel lines cut by a transversal and have a sum of 180 degrees or 2 right angles.

In each diagram the 2 marked angles are called co-interior angles.

If the 2 lines are parallel, then co-interior angles add to give 180° and so are supplementary.

Conversely, if a pair of angles are supplementary, then the lines are parallel.

8a9e01d1-a19a-4017-b979-3ad2f6505192.title: commission
8a9e01d1-a19a-4017-b979-3ad2f6505192.description: The sum or percentage paid for services, e.g. to an agent or salesperson.

6cf725cc-267b-46b6-be09-a0df87ac6c7a.title: composite number
6cf725cc-267b-46b6-be09-a0df87ac6c7a.description: A non-zero natural number that has a factor other than 1 and itself. For example, all even numbers besides 2 are composite numbers. Some odd numbers are composite (e.g. 21) but not all are composite (e.g. 11).

8495d0ee-248e-4ef7-a2e6-28b12e8ad2f5.title: composite shape
8495d0ee-248e-4ef7-a2e6-28b12e8ad2f5.description: A shape that is formed by combining other plane shapes. Composite shapes are often described as 'complex' when they are made up of many and different shapes.

72dd1661-1bbf-4c96-8e1d-f25d30c364d0.title: congruent
72dd1661-1bbf-4c96-8e1d-f25d30c364d0.description: An exact match between every part of one figure with the corresponding part of another figure, i.e. congruent figures can be exactly superimposed on each other.

b92b8fb4-cc66-41de-aa89-ebd793f67711.title: connected
b92b8fb4-cc66-41de-aa89-ebd793f67711.description:
In the Cartesian plane, 2 points are connected if there is a line or curve that joins them. In a network, a set of points is connected if every point can be reached from another point. A set of points that is not connected is called disconnected.

Examples of a connected network and a disconnected network respectively are shown below:

e8fc35a9-5a23-498b-8f88-2aac86fa619a.title: continuous variable
e8fc35a9-5a23-498b-8f88-2aac86fa619a.description: A numerical variable that can take any value that lies within an interval. The values taken are subject to the accuracy of the measuring instrument used to obtain these values. For example, height, reaction time to a stimulus and systolic blood pressure.

afa49629-4a81-4fd0-a46e-b79d7f18a609.title: coordinates
afa49629-4a81-4fd0-a46e-b79d7f18a609.description: A set of values that define the position of a point or an object in a space. The coordinate system being used will govern the nature of the coordinates.

a9eb4471-c365-4109-9022-0a094f237e0a.title: cross-section
a9eb4471-c365-4109-9022-0a094f237e0a.description: The intersection of a solid with a plane. May differ for a given solid depending on the orientation of the slicing plane. For example, the cross-section of a sphere will be a circle (of different radius depending on the slicing plane), while the cross-section of a cube could be a square or other polygon (e.g. triangle, hexagon) depending on the orientation of the slicing plane.

0bea1980-0e3d-4c59-ac3f-e98a5c8c1f59.title: cubic
0bea1980-0e3d-4c59-ac3f-e98a5c8c1f59.description: Having the form of a cube or being of the third power or degree.

4b64527c-d09b-448e-acc9-1e10c414dc46.title: cycle (networks)
4b64527c-d09b-448e-acc9-1e10c414dc46.description: A closed path that starts and finishes on the same vertex. No vertex is repeated.

93f41611-0f5f-4340-a5e8-7e567dbf15df.title: cyclic quadrilateral
93f41611-0f5f-4340-a5e8-7e567dbf15df.description: A quadrilateral with every vertex (corner point) on a circle’s circumference.

c69b269c-8711-4c75-8083-34a6c03cd85e.title: cylinder
c69b269c-8711-4c75-8083-34a6c03cd85e.description: An object that has parallel circular discs of equal radius at the ends that are joined by a curved surface.

0ab26200-46e9-4ae9-913e-213514aed222.title: dataset
0ab26200-46e9-4ae9-913e-213514aed222.description: A collection of numbers or values relating to a particular subject. Datasets are normally presented in tables or represented by graphs. For example, the test scores of each student in a particular class.

115a2d99-2c39-4817-8a92-eae78ce54692.title: decimal
115a2d99-2c39-4817-8a92-eae78ce54692.description: Used to describe aspects of the base-10 number system. The decimal point (. or ,) separates the whole number part of a number from its decimal part.

ef66025e-d7c4-4439-92ff-e0a97d5b8288.title: dependent events
ef66025e-d7c4-4439-92ff-e0a97d5b8288.description: An event that relies on another event to happen first. One event influences the probability of another event.

1dfdb2f3-7b63-41bd-b029-d3adc73721df.title: depreciation
1dfdb2f3-7b63-41bd-b029-d3adc73721df.description: A decrease in value due to wear and tear, decay, decline in price etc.

5e888f65-f8e7-4867-8ffc-8ffeafb72280.title: diameter
5e888f65-f8e7-4867-8ffc-8ffeafb72280.description: A chord passing through the centre of a circle. The word is also used for the length of the diameter.

0694e9d8-1fca-4789-83ac-8e44b072c216.title: distribution
0694e9d8-1fca-4789-83ac-8e44b072c216.description: The spread of data which can be shown graphically or in a table.

1a4438f6-f7c8-4d6f-92d6-d4dbf0616122.title: edge (networks)
1a4438f6-f7c8-4d6f-92d6-d4dbf0616122.description: A line that joins vertices to each other in a network diagram.

1c62625a-75ac-411d-b78f-1c6540728227.title: equiangular
1c62625a-75ac-411d-b78f-1c6540728227.description: When the angles of one polygon are equal to the corresponding angles of another polygon.

d25ab51f-2b05-4d8f-b3d6-0947d116ce28.title: exponential relationship

58825533-8eef-48cf-aff0-d8aa53ba54b4.title: extrapolate/extrapolation
58825533-8eef-48cf-aff0-d8aa53ba54b4.description: Occurs when the fitted model, such as a line of best fit, is used to make predictions using values that are outside the range of the original data upon which the fitted model was based.

d97c73a0-f53b-4c6e-9c66-ff3edb525cfc.title: factor
d97c73a0-f53b-4c6e-9c66-ff3edb525cfc.description: A number that divides another number without a remainder. For example, 1, 2, 3 and 6 are factors of 6 but 4 and 5 are not.

08b3f67c-767c-4cdf-b9ba-377cc009c96c.title: fraction
08b3f67c-767c-4cdf-b9ba-377cc009c96c.description:
The result of a division. For example, 2 divided by 4 produces quarters. Fractions also represent:

  • a relationship or ratio
  • parts when a whole is partitioned into equal parts
  • numbers between whole numbers
  • units of measure.

c495f9cb-9ca5-488e-8a62-cecfbc7c052e.title: frequency distribution
c495f9cb-9ca5-488e-8a62-cecfbc7c052e.description:
A visual display that organises and presents frequency counts of scores so that the information can be interpreted more easily.

Frequency distributions can be displayed in tabular or graphical form.

7dc53b85-c1bb-4a28-a2d6-f85465a5bd7c.title: hectare
7dc53b85-c1bb-4a28-a2d6-f85465a5bd7c.description: A common unit of land measure in the metric system equal to 10 000 square metres (approximately 2.47 acres).

e17d5091-a2c3-4489-bdb9-24c24a3a67d5.title: highest common factor (HCF)
e17d5091-a2c3-4489-bdb9-24c24a3a67d5.description: The common divisor of a given set of natural numbers that is greater than each of the other common divisors. For example, 1, 2, 3 and 6 are common factors of 24, 54, and 66, and 6 is the highest common factor.

de25262f-4863-4060-96a5-8bea87676d88.title: hypotenuse
de25262f-4863-4060-96a5-8bea87676d88.description: The longest side in a right-angled triangle that is opposite the right angle.

6e89f6f4-8163-4b70-9504-59fc833018cf.title: hypothesis
6e89f6f4-8163-4b70-9504-59fc833018cf.description: A supposition or proposed explanation made on the basis of limited evidence as a starting point for further investigation.

9310c707-d87a-46e4-806f-48d9fe3c4c12.title: infographic
9310c707-d87a-46e4-806f-48d9fe3c4c12.description: A chart, diagram or illustration (as in a book or magazine or on a website) that uses graphic elements to present information in a visually striking way.

c8f0a506-a329-40db-9872-03d80c7763d9.title: interior angle
c8f0a506-a329-40db-9872-03d80c7763d9.description:
When referring to polygons, the inner angles formed by 2 adjacent sides.

When referring to a transversal cutting through a pair of straight lines, the 4 angles formed are called interior angles.

6134b6c9-21a6-438f-a957-bedf1e1702f2.title: interpolate/interpolation
6134b6c9-21a6-438f-a957-bedf1e1702f2.description: Making predictions between known data values. For example, working between 2 known points on a graph to predict a value in between these points.

384bb686-0235-4e5a-9f0e-5639ef41bdcc.title: interquartile range (IQR)
384bb686-0235-4e5a-9f0e-5639ef41bdcc.description: The IQR is the width of an interval that contains the middle 50% (approximately) of the data values.

153c9334-b287-4b7e-a653-e704acd058ac.title: interval
153c9334-b287-4b7e-a653-e704acd058ac.description: A continuous subset of the real number line. For example, ‘the set of all real numbers greater than or equal to 10’.

2a8686b2-59c2-4244-ab74-27f92a175441.title: line of best fit
2a8686b2-59c2-4244-ab74-27f92a175441.description: A line drawn through a scatter plot of data points that represents the nature of the relationship between 2 variables.

94923987-da72-4751-a653-220933c0bbf4.title: measure of spread
94923987-da72-4751-a653-220933c0bbf4.description: In statistics, different methods of calculating the variability of a set. The most commonly used measures of spread are the range, interquartile range and standard deviation.

e816f73b-366a-431e-97ee-ae6f88535b08.title: net
e816f73b-366a-431e-97ee-ae6f88535b08.description:
A diagram showing the pattern of connected faces and the edges of an unfolded polyhedron (a solid with all faces polygons).

One possible net for a cube is shown below.

2c859575-e0ed-40aa-b9e6-58d6ab9eb9ba.title: network
2c859575-e0ed-40aa-b9e6-58d6ab9eb9ba.description: A set of points (vertices or nodes) some of which are joined by lines or curves (edges) that sometimes enclose regions (faces). For example, road networks, a family tree or the edges lining a tennis court.

343c5fe2-0f83-4eb5-914d-6547b39c7109.title: non-linear
343c5fe2-0f83-4eb5-914d-6547b39c7109.description: Functions or graphs that cannot be represented by a straight line or a linear function.

62ccfb3d-195e-4345-a255-cfa8fdba1bc4.title: numerical variable
62ccfb3d-195e-4345-a255-cfa8fdba1bc4.description:
Variables whose values are numbers and for which arithmetic processes, such as adding and subtracting or calculating an average, make sense.

A discrete numerical variable is a numerical variable, each of whose possible values is separated from the next by a definite 'gap'. The most common numerical variables have the counting numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, … as possible values. Others are prices, measured in dollars and cents. For example, the number of children in a family or the number of days in a month.

99622d1c-611c-4b90-9144-01b5e0c2f627.title: operation
99622d1c-611c-4b90-9144-01b5e0c2f627.description: The process of combining numbers or expressions. Operations are arithmetic – addition, subtraction, multiplication and division – and also include exponentiation and substitution.

f77f1a32-c27c-421e-b8cf-3d0aaaa142b2.title: path (networks)
f77f1a32-c27c-421e-b8cf-3d0aaaa142b2.description: A sequence of consecutive edges in a graph. The length of the path is the number of edges traversed.

1630d616-aaad-4fbf-b404-0c83afc33395.title: piecework
1630d616-aaad-4fbf-b404-0c83afc33395.description: Employment where a worker is paid a fixed rate for each item produced or action performed regardless of the time taken.

3fa3ee92-cd87-4ccd-ac37-ea2cb4867497.title: planar graph
3fa3ee92-cd87-4ccd-ac37-ea2cb4867497.description: A connected graph that is drawn within a plane whose edges do not cross.

671c773f-b400-40a7-b693-e7a069944b87.title: point
671c773f-b400-40a7-b693-e7a069944b87.description: Representation of a location in space that has zero dimensions. Lines, curves, shapes, surfaces and objects are constructed from sets of points. Points in the Cartesian plane are specified by coordinates.

deaac1b7-a9a7-4928-8f96-20ea59594fd1.title: pronumeral
deaac1b7-a9a7-4928-8f96-20ea59594fd1.description: A letter or symbol that is used to represent a value in a problem that can vary or change. Also known as a variable.

b7a627db-120a-40d7-b7a7-6517f53c4032.title: radius
b7a627db-120a-40d7-b7a7-6517f53c4032.description: The distance from the centre of a circle to any point on its perimeter. It is equal to half of the circle’s diameter.

897ce019-3494-4173-a21f-1bc38534890e.title: random number
897ce019-3494-4173-a21f-1bc38534890e.description: A number whose value is governed by chance. For example, the number of dots showing when a fair die is tossed. The value of a random number cannot be predicted in advance.

8168b006-1855-4979-8c70-2ec5c05c66c9.title: ray
8168b006-1855-4979-8c70-2ec5c05c66c9.description: The part of a line that starts at a point and continues in a particular direction to infinity.

9c8c7c0a-166c-4b6b-8c9c-0bbf4174a76e.title: reflex angle
9c8c7c0a-166c-4b6b-8c9c-0bbf4174a76e.description: An angle that measures between 180 and 360 degrees, i.e. between 2 and 4 right angles.

a4b6fe70-d984-4bdd-8784-6b2ceba20107.title: rounding
a4b6fe70-d984-4bdd-8784-6b2ceba20107.description: The process for approximating a value that lies between 2 known values. It is used to specify a number correct to a given accuracy. For example, 4.027 becomes 4.03 when rounded to 2 decimal places.

191248a6-090b-4762-bf88-c5b04d178719.title: sample space
191248a6-090b-4762-bf88-c5b04d178719.description: The set of all possible outcomes of a chance experiment. For example, the set of outcomes (also called sample points) from tossing 2 identical coins at the same time is {HH, HT, TT}, where H represents a ‘head’ and T a ‘tail’.

4b56fd45-d0ac-4a60-95be-762808e342b6.title: scatter plot
4b56fd45-d0ac-4a60-95be-762808e342b6.description: A visual representation of bivariate numerical data using the position of each dot on the horizontal and vertical axis to indicate the numerical values for an individual data point. Scatter plots are used to observe relationships between variables.

50ed52d5-3c79-4aa4-bbd4-cea3f26d15ca.title: similarity
50ed52d5-3c79-4aa4-bbd4-cea3f26d15ca.description: When the enlargement of one figure is congruent to another figure. Similar figures have corresponding lengths in the same proportion, are the same shape and have equal corresponding angles.

9e91e6c2-cd69-428c-a9c1-5ce4b1a93571.title: simple interest
9e91e6c2-cd69-428c-a9c1-5ce4b1a93571.description: The interest accumulated when the interest payment in each period is a fixed percentage of the principal (the initial lump sum of money).

f3eee67f-b663-4d9c-9915-66d4ce370831.title: simulation
f3eee67f-b663-4d9c-9915-66d4ce370831.description: A recreation of random phenomena used to collect probability data through either physical or virtual manipulatives such as spinners, coins and cards or computer-generated simulations that can be performed a large number of times.

4c787607-a840-4bb1-bcda-6fd950c436cf.title: simultaneous equations
4c787607-a840-4bb1-bcda-6fd950c436cf.description: A set of 2 or more equations, each containing 2 or more variables whose values can simultaneously satisfy all the equations in the set, the number of variables being equal to or less than the number of equations in the set.

4d3af9a3-96b3-40df-812c-2eb20f1ac4ed.title: skewness
4d3af9a3-96b3-40df-812c-2eb20f1ac4ed.description: A measure of asymmetry (non-symmetry) in a distribution of values about the mean of a set of data.

b5dcc8da-edf6-40a3-a150-06be303e9dcb.title: stem-and-leaf plot
b5dcc8da-edf6-40a3-a150-06be303e9dcb.description:
A method of organising and displaying numerical data in which each data value is split into 2 parts, a 'stem' and a 'leaf'. For example, the stem-and-leaf plot below displays the resting pulse rates of 19 students. The stem is on the left side of the vertical line and the leaves are on the right side.

See back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot

453a272e-0aed-4b37-b5c2-1d6f34c0f647.title: supplementary angles
453a272e-0aed-4b37-b5c2-1d6f34c0f647.description: Two adjacent angles that form a straight angle and whose sum is 180 degrees (a straight angle). For example, 45° and 135° are supplementary angles.

8813a5fb-d7ab-4ef1-8bd7-ef156e1db96b.title: surface area
8813a5fb-d7ab-4ef1-8bd7-ef156e1db96b.description: The measure of the total area of the surface(s) of a three-dimensional shape or object. For example, the surface area of a cube with side length of 5 units is 150 square units.

c13b4942-1208-49fc-95e0-b9cdebd3ee78.title: symmetrical distribution
c13b4942-1208-49fc-95e0-b9cdebd3ee78.description: When the 2 sides of the distribution are a mirror image of each other. A normal distribution is a true symmetric distribution of observed values.

3526714c-92a5-4149-b3e0-d4a0022e05e3.title: taxable income
3526714c-92a5-4149-b3e0-d4a0022e05e3.description: The amount of yearly income that is used to calculate an individual’s or company’s payable income tax.

5ed7e8f2-196f-44a0-bdab-5ed36ae7a39b.title: terminating decimal
5ed7e8f2-196f-44a0-bdab-5ed36ae7a39b.description: A decimal expansion of a number that has a finite number of non-zero digits, e.g. 3.125. Every terminating decimal represents a rational number where the denominator is a power of 10.

cc48418e-0ac2-4cc6-8447-18650746ec2f.title: trail (networks)
cc48418e-0ac2-4cc6-8447-18650746ec2f.description: A walk where no edges are repeated.

ec82eb76-475e-4619-901b-6ae5348ff5a4.title: transversal
ec82eb76-475e-4619-901b-6ae5348ff5a4.description: A line that intersects 2 other lines obliquely.

a192c48b-76f2-471b-84a2-d30ff8769259.title: vertically opposite angles
a192c48b-76f2-471b-84a2-d30ff8769259.description: Two pairs of vertically opposite angles formed at the point of intersection of 2 lines in a plane. Vertically opposite angles are equal.

cc066b07-7777-4c76-a172-b4f504d36951.title: walk (networks)
cc066b07-7777-4c76-a172-b4f504d36951.description: A sequence of edges and vertices in a network.

770d9300-0cdf-41c9-bb0a-2ed377e397ad.title: multiples
770d9300-0cdf-41c9-bb0a-2ed377e397ad.description: Products formed using the same base number multiplied by different whole numbers, e.g. 3, 6, 9, 12 …

5ad516d3-c108-483e-8ad0-ebc86b203026.title: number bonds
5ad516d3-c108-483e-8ad0-ebc86b203026.description: Combinations (pairs) of numbers that add to a given number, e.g. 8 + 2, 6 + 4, and 7 + 3 all bond to form 10.

5e15588a-4d5f-481c-a459-dc0399f9578b.title: number chart
5e15588a-4d5f-481c-a459-dc0399f9578b.description:
A table that lists numbers in numerical order. There are different types of number charts.

For example:

  • a 1–120 or 0–99 chart
  • a calendar display for a month.

b4350372-20c9-4aea-baa7-504f7241f456.title: number line
b4350372-20c9-4aea-baa7-504f7241f456.description: A number line is used to represent numbers according to their distance from a zero point. The representation of a number line can start and end on any number.

9b5e296d-9683-414c-b6be-1de33ef5dd6d.title: number sentence
9b5e296d-9683-414c-b6be-1de33ef5dd6d.description: A number sentence uses numerals and mathematical symbols. A number sentence may be used instead of the word equation. For example, instead of writing 6 apples plus 7 apples equals 13 apples, the number sentence would be 6 + 7 = 13.

94ee1886-4239-41c9-8531-cfebb2ab0473.title: one-to-one data display
94ee1886-4239-41c9-8531-cfebb2ab0473.description: Display of data using objects and pictures where one object or picture represents one data value.

f05dad5a-4b00-4a13-abf4-aaf3432446f9.title: partition
f05dad5a-4b00-4a13-abf4-aaf3432446f9.description:
Partitioning is dividing a quantity into parts.

In the early years, it commonly refers to treating whole numbers as made up of 2 parts (number bonds), e.g. 10 is 8 and 2.

In later years, it refers to dividing both continuous and discrete quantities into equal parts (equi-partitioning) when learning about fraction and division concepts.

8f9254b3-e58a-4280-92db-798c772e72a0.title: picture graph
8f9254b3-e58a-4280-92db-798c772e72a0.description: Display of data using images, symbols or pictures to represent data in categories.

1ec4e1e9-906a-4978-b87c-1060f33f81fa.title: place value system
1ec4e1e9-906a-4978-b87c-1060f33f81fa.description:
The place value system has 4 properties: positional, base-ten, additive and multiplicative.

The value of a digit is determined by its position in a number relative to the ones (or units) place. For example, in the number 924, the 4 denotes 4 ones, the 2 denotes 2 tens or 20 ones, and the 9 denotes 9 hundreds, 90 tens or 900 ones.

2254cbca-a659-47d1-bc31-17b305ad695e.title: polygon
2254cbca-a659-47d1-bc31-17b305ad695e.description: Plane shape bounded by 3 or more line segments.

2ab335be-cacf-4b60-ba71-f2f5ca8c3a46.title: quantity value
2ab335be-cacf-4b60-ba71-f2f5ca8c3a46.description: The amount a digit represents in a number. For example, the quantity value of the five in 546 is 500, and the quantity value of the four is 40.

28bfaffe-ec13-4d9c-b852-0165e763f592.title: rectangle
28bfaffe-ec13-4d9c-b852-0165e763f592.description: A four-sided shape (quadrilateral) with opposite sides of equal length and all 4 interior angles equal (right angles).

56ab6ff9-f860-4d12-b939-4474c8801378.title: regular shape
56ab6ff9-f860-4d12-b939-4474c8801378.description: A two-dimensional polygon with all sides and all interior angles equal. A square is an example of a regular shape.

899d468c-a019-49c5-92bc-16874c8fdc03.title: repeated addition
899d468c-a019-49c5-92bc-16874c8fdc03.description: An early strategy for solving multiplication problems used to add groups of the same quantity. For example, 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 to solve 4 groups of 3.

006853f4-f686-4860-95f2-bcf3e795ad96.title: rhythmic counting
006853f4-f686-4860-95f2-bcf3e795ad96.description: Rhythmic counting refers to the repeated sound pattern that students may use to vocalise the count – creating a beat to emphasise the pattern.

29312dcd-ab21-46b2-bbe7-5fee2d552cbe.title: sharing division
29312dcd-ab21-46b2-bbe7-5fee2d552cbe.description:
Sharing (partitive) division requires finding how many are in each group, eg if 12 marbles are shared between 3 students, how many does each student get?

When sharing, the quotient represents the quantity of shared objects in each group.

0faedabf-caba-4c09-8a3a-4ec3ee5fdae7.title: side
0faedabf-caba-4c09-8a3a-4ec3ee5fdae7.description: A side is the line segment joining 2 vertices of a two-dimensional shape.

d7bfcec0-d61c-4cdd-9ef2-c14d732abee3.title: skip counting
d7bfcec0-d61c-4cdd-9ef2-c14d732abee3.description: Skip counting is counting forwards or backwards in groups or multiples of a particular number, e.g. 5, 10, 15, 20 ...

3023c3d8-7948-4953-8077-252b3ab4f6eb.title: square
3023c3d8-7948-4953-8077-252b3ab4f6eb.description: A four-sided shape (quadrilateral and a parallelogram) with all sides of equal length and all 4 interior angles equal (right angles).

49d4e429-be4d-47c1-a540-015bdcd9e3cf.title: superimposed
49d4e429-be4d-47c1-a540-015bdcd9e3cf.description: To place or lay on top of.

94de8c88-7542-4e63-b464-e4dd3238d1e2.title: surface
94de8c88-7542-4e63-b464-e4dd3238d1e2.description:
The flat or curved area of an object. A surface with straight edges is called a face, a surface with a curved boundary is called a curved surface.

See face

e266ee3b-0e9f-481c-b5a9-a669abf5a97a.title: table
e266ee3b-0e9f-481c-b5a9-a669abf5a97a.description: An arrangement of information in rows and columns.

ae30576d-4867-4721-bf33-7e40f63c64ec.title: triangle
ae30576d-4867-4721-bf33-7e40f63c64ec.description: A closed shape with exactly 3 straight sides and 3 interior angles.

2edcb0f7-2a93-4420-9d30-1b31b02f9968.title: two-dimensional
2edcb0f7-2a93-4420-9d30-1b31b02f9968.description: Having length and width only (with no depth).

cc6961a8-946a-4443-8a6d-3d68791cd62a.title: uniform
cc6961a8-946a-4443-8a6d-3d68791cd62a.description: Means ‘the same as’. Used to refer to units of the same size used for measuring.

9c52aa7b-5d9e-4d94-98e4-7407672ba982.title: weight
9c52aa7b-5d9e-4d94-98e4-7407672ba982.description: The measure of the force of gravity acting on a body with a given mass. An object can be weightless without its mass being zero. The term ‘weight’ is used as a synonym for mass when the concept of gravitational force has not been introduced.

81c05bb0-0524-4be6-b4b5-e9156d00284d.title: estimate
81c05bb0-0524-4be6-b4b5-e9156d00284d.description: To judge the value, number or quantity of a calculation roughly.

394474e2-ed64-4be7-9c29-a7ec946cfaa5.title: location
394474e2-ed64-4be7-9c29-a7ec946cfaa5.description: In measurement and geometry, the relative position of an object is referred to as its location. It can be expressed in terms of a description (such as ‘next to’, ‘behind’, ‘on top of’), a grid reference (such as ‘A5’), or a coordinate (such as ‘(−2,7)’).

d8c31f6a-61fb-4d25-8b19-b9074a55402d.title: three-dimensional
d8c31f6a-61fb-4d25-8b19-b9074a55402d.description: An object is three-dimensional when it possesses the dimensions of height, width and depth. Two-dimensional objects have only length and width. A solid is any geometrical object with 3 dimensions.

a1bab5cd-c7b1-4237-89ec-1a676d35b78b.title: best buy
a1bab5cd-c7b1-4237-89ec-1a676d35b78b.description: A product or service that offers the most benefits or quality for the lowest price. It is found by comparing different purchase options and choosing the one that has the best value for money, e.g. by comparing unit prices.

1448d7fc-4543-4966-89c8-c069af7b8fc7.title: budget
1448d7fc-4543-4966-89c8-c069af7b8fc7.description: A tool for managing money and achieving financial goals. It is a list of all the expected income and costs for a certain period of time. A budget aims to balance the income and expenses, so that the expenses are less than or equal to the income.

81b8b913-da99-4d43-9d85-04ad773a3264.title: credit card
81b8b913-da99-4d43-9d85-04ad773a3264.description: A method for borrowing funds to purchase goods and services. Banks or financial institutions agree to loan an amount of money to an individual up to a pre-approved limit, and the individual agrees to pay back the amount plus any interest and fees that are charged.

680c72ed-dd61-4084-8415-85648783791c.title: goods and services tax (GST)
680c72ed-dd61-4084-8415-85648783791c.description: An indirect tax that is levied at a flat percentage (rate) on most goods and services sold in Australia.

c81c0ef3-728b-4937-a70b-9c5530c8076e.title: rate
c81c0ef3-728b-4937-a70b-9c5530c8076e.description: A comparison of 2 quantities of different kinds. For example, a speed of 60km/h is a rate because it compares quantities of distance and time.

5cc78eb6-9698-4b6a-a122-6a595416288c.title: tax
5cc78eb6-9698-4b6a-a122-6a595416288c.description: A compulsory monetary contribution required by a government for its support, levied on incomes, property value, goods purchased.

84d3e267-2727-43cc-b661-6e67e3206560.title: appreciation
84d3e267-2727-43cc-b661-6e67e3206560.description: An increase in the value of an asset over time. The appreciated value is the value an asset has increased to over that time.

b1f878f2-beec-4678-a9fa-bacf713b7a07.title: back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot
b1f878f2-beec-4678-a9fa-bacf713b7a07.description:
A back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot is a method for comparing 2 data distributions by attaching 2 sets of 'leaves' to the same 'stem'; e.g. the stem-and-leaf plot below displays the distribution of pulse rates of 19 students before and after gentle exercise.

In this plot, the stem unit is ‘10’ and the leaf unit is ‘1’. Thus, the third row in the plot, 8 8 6 2 | 8 | 6 7 8 8, displays pulse rates of 88, 88, 86, 82 before exercise and 86, 87, 88, 88 after exercise.

823c625d-eab6-4218-8c60-827373394545.title: backward scanning (networks)
823c625d-eab6-4218-8c60-827373394545.description: The process of systematically determining the latest starting time for each activity as part of critical path analysis.

59532a4f-6497-4b3f-ad49-49708e36828c.title: balance
59532a4f-6497-4b3f-ad49-49708e36828c.description: The difference between the total debit entries and the total credit entries of an account during a financial period.

a4550fd8-a754-4dc7-9aea-ddfd2f07fded.title: blood alcohol content (BAC)
a4550fd8-a754-4dc7-9aea-ddfd2f07fded.description: A measure of the amount of alcohol present in the bloodstream, which may be used for legal purposes.

d379f8b0-ccef-4b99-a39e-036e06e7b119.title: brokerage
d379f8b0-ccef-4b99-a39e-036e06e7b119.description: The commission earned by a broker when buying and selling shares. Brokerage can be charged at a flat rate or as a percentage of the sale.

aeca4a80-863f-4674-b1de-269ce40ad86b.title: buy now, pay later
aeca4a80-863f-4674-b1de-269ce40ad86b.description: A service that allows a consumer to purchase a product and pay the cost in instalments. There is no interest charged on the purchase price, but there may be fees, such as an account set-up fee and late payment fees.

0534affd-63ff-4f44-bbcf-ab21aeaa06be.title: capture-recapture technique
0534affd-63ff-4f44-bbcf-ab21aeaa06be.description: A method for estimating the size of a population that is difficult to count directly. It involves capturing a random sample of the population, marking them with tags or labels, and releasing them back into the population. After some time, a second random sample is captured, and the number of marked individuals is recorded. Based on the ratio of marked to unmarked individuals in the second sample, the total population size can be estimated.

05091caf-4bcd-458f-a515-dda7f19dd95f.title: categorical data
05091caf-4bcd-458f-a515-dda7f19dd95f.description: Data associated with a categorical variable. Also known as qualitative data.

62f34b23-187e-47fd-9bf2-217c8daff010.title: cluster
62f34b23-187e-47fd-9bf2-217c8daff010.description: A group of data points that are close together or have similar values.

6bea9ba0-297e-472f-b59d-9258c333c79e.title: constant of variation
6bea9ba0-297e-472f-b59d-9258c333c79e.description:
Also known as the constant of proportionality.

See direct or inverse variation.

bde27553-ed1a-4d91-a4d0-277f50ebd338.title: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)
bde27553-ed1a-4d91-a4d0-277f50ebd338.description: The primary time standard used across the world. It is based on International Atomic Time, which is measured by atomic clocks, with leap seconds added occasionally to keep it close to the earth’s rotation. For every 15° longitude east or west of the Prime Meridian (known as 0° longitude), the time changes by 1 hour.

52aec673-5bf9-4024-b8de-80240c2dac05.title: correlation
52aec673-5bf9-4024-b8de-80240c2dac05.description: A measure of the strength of the linear relationship between 2 variables.

ffe0ff7b-8040-48bb-ac93-3ec672e804e4.title: critical activity (networks)
ffe0ff7b-8040-48bb-ac93-3ec672e804e4.description: Activities that must be completed on time to ensure that the project is completed on schedule. These activities have zero float, meaning that any delay in these tasks will extend the project’s timeline.

b6c1f0e9-6280-48fb-b5b6-82fb69e9996c.title: critical path
b6c1f0e9-6280-48fb-b5b6-82fb69e9996c.description: The sequence of network activities that combine to have the longest overall duration so as to determine the shortest possible time needed to complete a project.

a29ffe4c-9ebb-4f5e-a1b8-c0453939a4e4.title: currency conversion
a29ffe4c-9ebb-4f5e-a1b8-c0453939a4e4.description: The process of converting the value of one currency to another currency. It is commonly used in foreign exchange markets where it is necessary to exchange one currency for another to purchase goods or services. The conversion rate between 2 currencies is the ratio between the values of the 2 currencies.

2d1497ea-d5af-49d5-963e-adcb4251c257.title: cut (networks)
2d1497ea-d5af-49d5-963e-adcb4251c257.description: In a flow network, a cut partitions the vertices of a graph into 2 separate groups so that the source is in one group and the sink in the other.

e5354d9b-c686-48f8-9191-0f747aed7417.title: daylight saving
e5354d9b-c686-48f8-9191-0f747aed7417.description: A system of setting clocks 1 hour ahead of the standard in spring to give more hours of daylight to the working day in summer months. In Australia, this practice is observed in some states from October to April.

c2e29a3c-f435-4e8b-823a-1f4110e3e47a.title: declining balance depreciation
c2e29a3c-f435-4e8b-823a-1f4110e3e47a.description: The value of an asset is depreciated by a fixed percentage of its initial value each year.

28b3bc17-8e7a-409f-945b-daa74a5013ad.title: deduction
28b3bc17-8e7a-409f-945b-daa74a5013ad.description: An expense incurred by a worker in relation to their job or profession and which can be taken away from annual earnings to obtain the taxable income. Deductions form part of an individual’s or a company’s tax return.

a878ad14-1f6e-4ab2-8c18-9534bf1663b2.title: deposit
a878ad14-1f6e-4ab2-8c18-9534bf1663b2.description: A sum of money that is used for financial reasons. An amount of money that is placed in a bank or other financial institution either as a lump sum or as a regular payment, or an initial payment when purchasing something, with the rest to be payable later.

e70060dd-e398-4b64-bd92-61a29485709f.title: directed network
e70060dd-e398-4b64-bd92-61a29485709f.description: A network whose edges have arrows and travel is only possible in the direction of the arrows.

c823ba17-3951-49e1-ae52-6c86cbca6734.title: discretionary spending
c823ba17-3951-49e1-ae52-6c86cbca6734.description: A type of spending that is not essential or mandatory. It includes expenses, such as entertainment, clothes and gifts, that can be varied based on choice and preference.

ac0dbbe4-21fd-4ac4-8e7a-c38a347a77e6.title: dividend (shares)
ac0dbbe4-21fd-4ac4-8e7a-c38a347a77e6.description: A sum of money paid by a company to its shareholders out of its profits.

3236614b-acee-4c20-8607-5b6c3b1395b2.title: dividend yield
3236614b-acee-4c20-8607-5b6c3b1395b2.description: The dividend expressed as a percentage of the current share price.

4d3de89b-7e5e-403d-a488-ab6d73d96669.title: dummy activities
4d3de89b-7e5e-403d-a488-ab6d73d96669.description: Operations in a network that require no time nor any resources. They are imaginary activities shown in a project network to identify the dependence among activities. They are usually represented by a dashed directed edge.

8007520b-27d8-4342-8efa-ccf41eeac4c1.title: earliest starting time (EST)
8007520b-27d8-4342-8efa-ccf41eeac4c1.description: The earliest time that any activity can be started after all prior activities have been completed.

f0845f75-7602-4a5a-9ac3-76fb8bdf8e50.title: exponential model
f0845f75-7602-4a5a-9ac3-76fb8bdf8e50.description: Creating an exponential model involves fitting an exponential curve or equation to a practical situation or set of data.

b32cc51e-8022-4a5f-8414-1adbfd37a5c9.title: fixed spending
b32cc51e-8022-4a5f-8414-1adbfd37a5c9.description: A type of spending that is essential or mandatory. It includes expenses like rent or board that cannot be varied or changed.

4ce94d26-6e38-40f2-9a18-f2e706fe0ce8.title: float time
4ce94d26-6e38-40f2-9a18-f2e706fe0ce8.description: Float time is the amount of time that a task in a project network can be delayed without causing a delay to subsequent tasks.

b10f989d-6825-48db-8ea5-7281819c7ce6.title: flow capacity
b10f989d-6825-48db-8ea5-7281819c7ce6.description:
The flow capacity of a network can be found using the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem and depends upon the capacity of each edge in the network.

See maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem

fb309ff0-7e89-4c99-ba99-180ed55ab7b6.title: forward scanning (networks)
fb309ff0-7e89-4c99-ba99-180ed55ab7b6.description: In critical path analysis, forward scanning identifies the earliest starting time for each activity in an activity network.

3726ff49-fa9b-49e2-b2bc-31b0193546c0.title: fuel consumption rate
3726ff49-fa9b-49e2-b2bc-31b0193546c0.description: The fuel consumption rate of a vehicle measures how much fuel it uses and is usually measured in litres per 100 kilometres (L/100 km).

fd760ea9-1817-4c7e-80e9-91a85f4022fa.title: Gantt chart
fd760ea9-1817-4c7e-80e9-91a85f4022fa.description: A bar chart showing a project schedule including a timeline and horizontal bars representing activities. The position of each bar shows the start time and duration of each activity.

cbc57d69-f75e-4ddf-85c7-5203e5397215.title: government payments
cbc57d69-f75e-4ddf-85c7-5203e5397215.description: Payments made by the government to individuals to provide financial support.

324c3e10-72be-41c9-8903-19ff712baf15.title: hyperbolic
324c3e10-72be-41c9-8903-19ff712baf15.description:
Having the shape of a hyperbola.

See hyperbola

2bc060df-b065-4a24-a5c5-f9fe1a1a575c.title: inflow (networks)
2bc060df-b065-4a24-a5c5-f9fe1a1a575c.description: The amount of flow that enters a vertex in a network flow diagram. Inflow is calculated as the total flow of the edges arriving at a vertex.

784614c4-3b6f-43bd-8a27-42568da533a1.title: interest factors
784614c4-3b6f-43bd-8a27-42568da533a1.description: The values of an investment at a specific date. A table of these factors can be used to calculate the future value of different amounts of money that are invested at a certain interest rate for a specified period of time.

23145b49-979b-4917-8c5b-4809b38e71f0.title: interest-free period
23145b49-979b-4917-8c5b-4809b38e71f0.description: A period of time during which no interest is charged or paid on a loan or a credit card. It is usually offered as an incentive for customers to borrow or spend money.

85fe44cf-81c5-4d92-bd0e-e3607a354649.title: kilowatt hour (kwh)
85fe44cf-81c5-4d92-bd0e-e3607a354649.description: A unit of energy that measures how much electricity is used or produced over a period of time. It is equal to the amount of energy delivered by one kilowatt of power for 1 hour.

66d335c6-7574-41b9-9ec4-d8d38cd81ddb.title: latest starting time (LST)
66d335c6-7574-41b9-9ec4-d8d38cd81ddb.description: The latest time an activity may be started after all prior activities have been completed and without delaying the project.

5326446b-1a8c-445d-9dbb-3b1ecbf52027.title: latitude
5326446b-1a8c-445d-9dbb-3b1ecbf52027.description: The angular distance of a point on the Earth’s surface north or south from the equator.

c805f3a2-d235-4114-aa60-7fab5bdb6b79.title: least-squares regression line
c805f3a2-d235-4114-aa60-7fab5bdb6b79.description: The line that minimises the sum of the squares of the residuals. Also known as the least-squares line of best fit.

415c9fa2-e2f3-4793-bab9-d7df9c3372cb.title: linear model
415c9fa2-e2f3-4793-bab9-d7df9c3372cb.description: A straight-line graph or equation fitted to a practical situation or set of data.

b38dc1ea-1177-4a1a-a841-e4b345176220.title: longitude
b38dc1ea-1177-4a1a-a841-e4b345176220.description: The angular distance of a point on the Earth’s surface east or west from the Greenwich meridian.

61135f3d-549f-492a-b438-c84974b4a00f.title: loss
61135f3d-549f-492a-b438-c84974b4a00f.description: The difference between the total cost and the total revenue of producing and selling goods or services where the cost is greater than the revenue.

4e7e34ee-1f3e-4cb1-870c-694a6a138884.title: lump-sum payment
4e7e34ee-1f3e-4cb1-870c-694a6a138884.description: A single amount paid instead of smaller instalments. Often used in the context of a loan or investment.

ef4f1863-d995-4105-876c-d8e04f9e7a04.title: maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem
ef4f1863-d995-4105-876c-d8e04f9e7a04.description: The maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem states that the flow through a network cannot exceed the value of any cut in the network and that the maximum flow equals the value of the minimum cut, i.e. it identifies the bottleneck in the system.

30ef5315-94d3-4e1f-99cc-6c15e88d332b.title: Medicare levy
30ef5315-94d3-4e1f-99cc-6c15e88d332b.description: A tax that finances the national health insurance program, Medicare, for all Australians, calculated as a percentage of taxable income.

cc8517ab-50bb-4563-9830-4129153448d1.title: minimum cut
cc8517ab-50bb-4563-9830-4129153448d1.description:
The smallest possible capacity of a cut that separates the source and sink vertices.


See cut (networks), maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem

49bb0a40-b3c8-4b75-b53f-f2464265952d.title: minimum payment
49bb0a40-b3c8-4b75-b53f-f2464265952d.description: The lowest amount of money required for a borrower to pay off their credit card balance each month to remain in good standing with the credit card company.

e12ad0d3-0d52-44db-b6d8-3eafc0ff23d8.title: minimum spanning tree
e12ad0d3-0d52-44db-b6d8-3eafc0ff23d8.description: A tree of minimum length in a connected, undirected network. It connects all the vertices together with the minimum total weighting for the edges.

5614f40c-eabe-47d6-bb71-e9c5d836bc09.title: net earnings
5614f40c-eabe-47d6-bb71-e9c5d836bc09.description: The amount of gross pay remaining after tax and other deductions have been made.

4b728f3d-aa9a-4d7f-b52c-00f3a7947011.title: nominal variable
4b728f3d-aa9a-4d7f-b52c-00f3a7947011.description: A type of categorical variable whose values have no natural order in which they may be placed, e.g. eye colour.

e73ceb0e-bfde-499d-aeec-ab48d0483fe6.title: non-critical activities (networks)
e73ceb0e-bfde-499d-aeec-ab48d0483fe6.description: Activities that can be delayed without affecting the project’s completion time.

df6fff22-e454-4e5e-ac63-76562836f259.title: numerical data
df6fff22-e454-4e5e-ac63-76562836f259.description: Data associated with a numerical variable. Also known as quantitative data.

3e0f724e-309e-468a-bc53-27f4c1e665c0.title: ordinal variable
3e0f724e-309e-468a-bc53-27f4c1e665c0.description: A type of categorical variable whose responses have a natural order. For example, level of happiness: very unhappy, unhappy, neutral, happy, very happy.

8005b8ec-191c-4f4e-94af-60cd84a955a7.title: outflow (networks)
8005b8ec-191c-4f4e-94af-60cd84a955a7.description: The amount of flow that leaves a vertex in a network flow diagram. Outflow is calculated as the total flow of the edges exiting a vertex.

5643d798-2435-4df7-b040-ee2277a62b09.title: overtime
5643d798-2435-4df7-b040-ee2277a62b09.description:
Time worked before or after regular scheduled working hours. A higher rate of pay is often earnt during this time, known as penalty rates.

See penalty rate

3e75ef21-1a4d-4f3c-8d6a-6d123b1a9d3d.title: path (networks)
3e75ef21-1a4d-4f3c-8d6a-6d123b1a9d3d.description: In a network diagram, it is a walk in which all of the edges and all the vertices are different. A path that starts and finishes at different vertices is said to be open, while a path that starts and finishes at the same vertex is said to be closed. There may be multiple paths between the same 2 vertices.

cbe0aeca-4704-4dd0-93d1-e865e4d1d610.title: pay as you go (PAYG) tax
cbe0aeca-4704-4dd0-93d1-e865e4d1d610.description: A system for making regular tax instalments which are removed from gross pay towards the expected income tax liability for that financial year.

412e6a30-1e51-46fa-988d-7d241f2139ee.title: penalty rate
412e6a30-1e51-46fa-988d-7d241f2139ee.description: A rate of pay determined by an award, higher than the usual rate, in compensation for working outside normal hours, such as time-and-a-half and double-time.

8f40dacd-ee66-4fb1-9468-5b01493ad861.title: position coordinates
8f40dacd-ee66-4fb1-9468-5b01493ad861.description: Used to describe the location of a point on the Earth’s surface expressed in degrees of longitude and latitude.

27aa8053-7c92-4b7d-958d-f51748e8906b.title: precedence table
27aa8053-7c92-4b7d-958d-f51748e8906b.description: A table that lists all the activities involved in a project, along with their expected durations and immediate predecessors.

2508264d-2800-4ed0-9f26-c5a53a1f65de.title: present value
2508264d-2800-4ed0-9f26-c5a53a1f65de.description: The single sum of money (or principal) that could be initially invested to produce a future value over a given period of time.

1cce93cc-8dbd-434d-a6d3-5952edae7b12.title: probability tree
1cce93cc-8dbd-434d-a6d3-5952edae7b12.description:
A diagram demonstrating all the possible outcomes of a series of events. A probability tree has branches that represent each event with the probability of each event written on the branch. The probability of each possible outcome is found by multiplying the probabilities along the branches.

See tree diagram

19bf0ce5-7693-4941-948f-444998ebb58e.title: profit
19bf0ce5-7693-4941-948f-444998ebb58e.description: The excess of total revenue above the total cost of selling goods or services.

b0854673-d42e-41d6-87be-30619427802f.title: quadratic model
b0854673-d42e-41d6-87be-30619427802f.description: A quadratic graph or equation fitted to a practical situation or set of data.

f859f550-8da4-4968-b901-0fbbc6dfc36d.title: radial survey
f859f550-8da4-4968-b901-0fbbc6dfc36d.description: A radial survey can be used to measure the area of an irregular block of land. In a radial survey, a central point is chosen within the block of land and measurements are taken along intervals from this point to each vertex. The angles between these intervals at the central point are also measured and recorded.

f3d619c6-c589-4c3d-aad2-be04940532c5.title: reciprocal model
f3d619c6-c589-4c3d-aad2-be04940532c5.description: A reciprocal graph or equation fitted to a practical situation or set of data.

1f4d6f4f-4e29-43ab-ae95-53311c384cb7.title: royalties
1f4d6f4f-4e29-43ab-ae95-53311c384cb7.description: Payment made to the owner or creator of a product or intellectual property, such as a patent, novel, song or artwork. Typically calculated as a percentage of the total sales.

038ee0c0-4575-47b8-9f84-4ca68387e90d.title: salary
038ee0c0-4575-47b8-9f84-4ca68387e90d.description: A fixed regular payment made by an employer to an employee for their work or services. The amount of salary paid is usually expressed as an annual sum, which is then divided into equal payments over the course of the year such as weekly, fortnightly or monthly.

82ab9288-cbf1-4c1f-a75e-218a0481ab20.title: salvage value
82ab9288-cbf1-4c1f-a75e-218a0481ab20.description: The value of an asset after depreciation.

09fd8d2e-70d3-4c93-952e-859bbebc1a97.title: saturated edges
09fd8d2e-70d3-4c93-952e-859bbebc1a97.description: Edges that have zero excess flow capacity.

90b9070a-aa3d-49a5-b7a1-66f51814efb2.title: scale drawing
90b9070a-aa3d-49a5-b7a1-66f51814efb2.description: A drawing of a real object with accurate sizes reduced or enlarged by the scale factor.

88e6d303-59f0-4e45-aa9b-1ffb2f8561ef.title: share
88e6d303-59f0-4e45-aa9b-1ffb2f8561ef.description: A share is one of the equal parts into which a company's capital is divided, entitling the shareholder to a portion of the company’s profits.

4d870ffe-4d65-439a-9bd7-b27a432d23b4.title: shortest path
4d870ffe-4d65-439a-9bd7-b27a432d23b4.description: A shortest path in a network diagram is a path between 2 vertices in a network where the sum of the weights of its edges are minimised.

7585bf4b-ad99-4475-8e3e-1e588a228198.title: sink (networks)
7585bf4b-ad99-4475-8e3e-1e588a228198.description: In a network flow diagram it is a vertex that has no outgoing edges and only incoming edges. It represents the destination of the flow in the network.

2f2bc0db-bdab-4b79-b87c-5842b23f19c2.title: skewed
2f2bc0db-bdab-4b79-b87c-5842b23f19c2.description: A distribution is negatively skewed when its tail is on the left side. A distribution is positively skewed when its tail is on the right side.

0b19060e-90c2-449c-8c6d-6e4033ba9cf3.title: source (networks)
0b19060e-90c2-449c-8c6d-6e4033ba9cf3.description: In a network flow diagram it is a vertex that has no incoming edges and only outgoing edges. It represents the origin of the flow in the network.

d79f8619-272f-48b7-b846-4d4679c0c0a7.title: spanning tree
d79f8619-272f-48b7-b846-4d4679c0c0a7.description: A spanning tree of an undirected network diagram is a tree that includes all the vertices of the original network connected together, but not necessarily all the edges of the original network diagram. A network can have many different spanning trees.

7e5c9d73-387e-43e3-a6d2-8ab9e311b448.title: stamp duty
7e5c9d73-387e-43e3-a6d2-8ab9e311b448.description: A tax payable to the government for transactions and documents, such as motor vehicle registrations and transfers, insurance policies and mortgages.

f58e4908-6bb8-41ed-bd69-0e3b05654835.title: straight-line depreciation
f58e4908-6bb8-41ed-bd69-0e3b05654835.description: In straight-line method of depreciation, the value of the depreciating asset decreases by the same amount during each time period.

87a0ab88-82df-419d-853e-c598a9d37053.title: superannuation
87a0ab88-82df-419d-853e-c598a9d37053.description: A retirement fund to which financial contributions are made during a person’s working life.

be90dc90-c06e-4deb-ad53-bc7b0323c10f.title: tax return
be90dc90-c06e-4deb-ad53-bc7b0323c10f.description: A tax return is an annual statement of all income, allowable deductions, PAYG tax paid and other personal financial information so as to allow the Australian Taxation Office to calculate the amount of income tax an individual should pay for the financial year.

b4774fd2-ff13-4f8d-af72-fb6c49f668e4.title: term deposit
b4774fd2-ff13-4f8d-af72-fb6c49f668e4.description: A deposit held in a bank for a fixed term to which a fixed interest rate is applied.

7900f094-f3a3-4694-9b80-d3e788138bba.title: time zones
7900f094-f3a3-4694-9b80-d3e788138bba.description: The 24 divisions of the globe, where each change of 15 degrees longitude corresponds to one hour. As time zones often align with national or regional boundaries this is an approximate relationship.

d9233a1c-4abe-45e4-b4bb-274b9be66b8a.title: transaction
d9233a1c-4abe-45e4-b4bb-274b9be66b8a.description: A purchase or payment made using a credit card. It can include purchases made in-store or online, cash advances and balance transfers.

d5db20ea-180c-47ec-ae6c-0169708c8cd0.title: tree (networks)
d5db20ea-180c-47ec-ae6c-0169708c8cd0.description: A tree is an undirected network in which any 2 vertices are connected by exactly one path.

6081095d-09eb-4ab8-b219-7fa2e20b3335.title: unit price
6081095d-09eb-4ab8-b219-7fa2e20b3335.description: The price per agreed unit of a product or service, such as per kilogram, per dozen or per item. It is used to compare the cost of different quantities or packages of the same product or service.

88eac527-5743-407d-b4f5-7295d34418e6.title: value-added tax (VAT)
88eac527-5743-407d-b4f5-7295d34418e6.description: A type of sales tax that is added to the purchase price of each item. VAT is used in many countries, usually as a percentage of the purchase price.

833dca5b-8f63-437e-aacc-a2c8ea5d76a5.title: vertex (networks)
