833dca5b-8f63-437e-aacc-a2c8ea5d76a5.description: A vertex is a point in a network diagram at which lines of pathways (called edges) intersect or branch. Also called a node.

a7a88002-5862-4608-a89d-467c1483986b.title: wage
a7a88002-5862-4608-a89d-467c1483986b.description: An amount of money that is paid for work or services, based on the time spent or the work done. It is usually calculated by the hour, day or week, and paid at regular intervals, such as daily, weekly or fortnightly.

34bd7751-e805-412b-925c-867b4ca9479e.title: weighted edges
34bd7751-e805-412b-925c-867b4ca9479e.description: A weighted edge is an edge of a network diagram that has a number assigned to it, which implies some numerical value, such as cost, distance or time.

a00c33e5-e5c6-411a-814b-1c649bb234ab.title: withdrawal
a00c33e5-e5c6-411a-814b-1c649bb234ab.description: The act of taking money out of a bank account or an investment.

53b9ed18-3d7e-4462-9abf-51ccac557c4a.title: dictatorship
53b9ed18-3d7e-4462-9abf-51ccac557c4a.description: A form of government in which one person, or group of people, holds absolute power.

1f7b2ed8-15b0-47d2-a45c-8c26d99f25c1.title: accent
1f7b2ed8-15b0-47d2-a45c-8c26d99f25c1.description:
A manner of pronunciation of a language which marks speakers as belonging to identifiable categories such as geographical or ethnic origin, social group or generation.

The stress placed on the syllable.

b0a658d6-036d-40e1-b6bc-c971a0ac45af.title: communicative purpose
b0a658d6-036d-40e1-b6bc-c971a0ac45af.description: The reason for which the text is created; the context, purpose and audience enables meaningful communication.

2bf78f46-60ef-4a08-8721-a6059163a226.title: intercultural understanding
2bf78f46-60ef-4a08-8721-a6059163a226.description: A capacity to understand the relationship between language, culture and people with diverse backgrounds and experiences. This involves understanding the dynamic and interdependent nature of both language and culture, that communicating and interacting in different languages involves interacting with values, beliefs and experiences as well as with words and grammars. It involves being open to differing perspectives, being, responsive and reflective; being able to de-centre, to look objectively at one’s own cultural ways of thinking and behaving, and at how these affect attitudes to others, shape assumptions and shape behaviours.

de4962d5-d74c-40f8-b97a-a5d0a8ac1a7f.title: manipulate
de4962d5-d74c-40f8-b97a-a5d0a8ac1a7f.description: To change the vocabulary or syntax of a sentence to suit the purpose.

059076a9-4f78-495a-b536-2eb078e8a0e3.title: modern language
059076a9-4f78-495a-b536-2eb078e8a0e3.description:
Any language that is currently in use.

Aboriginal Languages are the oldest continuous languages and as they are still in use today, they are considered modern languages. Many Aboriginal Languages are in various stages of reclamation and revitalisation. Study of an Aboriginal Language in the NSW Curriculum is through Aboriginal Languages syllabuses.

Auslan is the language of the Australian Deaf community and is a visual gestural language. Study of Auslan in the NSW Curriculum is through the Auslan syllabus.

51dcc260-6147-4fbe-bcc6-7531cbcf84b4.title: written text
51dcc260-6147-4fbe-bcc6-7531cbcf84b4.description: A text produced using written language. It is one-way information giving, such as a handwritten or digital text.

e235a6e9-4adb-4c8c-b4ee-26f6bd88b1df.title: rehearsed language
e235a6e9-4adb-4c8c-b4ee-26f6bd88b1df.description: Language that has been practised by the student. It is used in structured and familiar situations. Students usually learn the language by heart, e.g. a role play.

6c6eb773-7ab8-4e3f-9807-56c2a166f74b.title: digital technique
6c6eb773-7ab8-4e3f-9807-56c2a166f74b.description: Digital processes to generate, modify or shape musical material.

c2a4d014-2875-4be3-8918-21cb917a2fe3.title: waveforms
c2a4d014-2875-4be3-8918-21cb917a2fe3.description: A representation of sound showing changes in amplitude over time.

b2ca70a4-f7d1-494e-a3d0-0610ad7abe0b.title: performance practice
b2ca70a4-f7d1-494e-a3d0-0610ad7abe0b.description: Established approaches and stylistic conventions that shape how musicians realise and interpret music in performance.

105489de-4ed5-4294-b08f-0512a03bfa12.title: aural skills
105489de-4ed5-4294-b08f-0512a03bfa12.description: Skills used to identify, discriminate between and interpret musical features. These skills may be developed through auditory, visual, tactile and kinaesthetic modalities.

c73eb839-e6c9-4d2a-87ce-b4790cc16d6e.title: electroacoustic
c73eb839-e6c9-4d2a-87ce-b4790cc16d6e.description: The manipulation or transformation of acoustic sound through electronic or digital processes.

19a192e1-f69e-4cd3-a354-b9c296f2622f.title: spectral visualisation
19a192e1-f69e-4cd3-a354-b9c296f2622f.description: A representation of the frequency spectrum of sound over time, often through visual displays such as spectrograms.

13805053-0efa-44f5-aa40-a9a239b61dd5.title: beat grid
13805053-0efa-44f5-aa40-a9a239b61dd5.description: A framework of evenly spaced divisions that represents the pulse of music, against which the positions of other sounds are indicated.

537b1e18-cce8-4e9a-b99b-814250436b8e.title: pitch shifting
537b1e18-cce8-4e9a-b99b-814250436b8e.description: The alteration of a sound’s pitch without changing its duration, using digital processes.

2ef1df5f-6617-44d3-90b6-f7c85b5e1ac4.title: piano roll
2ef1df5f-6617-44d3-90b6-f7c85b5e1ac4.description: A digital representation of musical notes on a grid against an image of piano keys or a keyboard. Pitch is shown vertically and time is shown horizontally.

4d0b864b-6b89-44c8-9e97-a86122fb825a.title: groove
4d0b864b-6b89-44c8-9e97-a86122fb825a.description: Rhythmic quality that produces a strong sense of flow or physical response in music.

3e934611-852c-4eef-8927-268da66806e0.title: altered chord
3e934611-852c-4eef-8927-268da66806e0.description: A chord in which at least one note is modified from its usual pitch within the key.

6a0f72fe-a0a8-4c4c-b06c-8486cc6e20c3.title: nonlinear scoring
6a0f72fe-a0a8-4c4c-b06c-8486cc6e20c3.description: Representation of music which allows for flexible reorganisation, layering, or adaptation in performance.

07d8af85-4c66-4b88-a937-9d6af71e17e2.title: digital music documentation
07d8af85-4c66-4b88-a937-9d6af71e17e2.description: Representation of musical ideas using digital technologies.

ea977a4f-6751-4424-87b6-f45a36544d22.title: spatial scoring
ea977a4f-6751-4424-87b6-f45a36544d22.description: Scoring that visually conveys the placement, movement and relationships of performers or sound sources.

55244030-b579-4335-910b-e9e375d9a91b.title: pre-notation
55244030-b579-4335-910b-e9e375d9a91b.description: Simplified notation system(s) used to represent sound. Pre-notations system(s) are symbolic in nature and may be based around objects, shapes or colours.

6ba0399f-9fe0-4d67-8f44-422491021295.title: articulation
6ba0399f-9fe0-4d67-8f44-422491021295.description: The way a note is sung or played.

079b500b-d7f3-42eb-a7fa-2f1676901ba7.title: improvisation (music)
079b500b-d7f3-42eb-a7fa-2f1676901ba7.description: The simultaneous creation and performance of music.

54b204e8-ebae-4f6e-aa2c-bf57f724f44e.title: notate
54b204e8-ebae-4f6e-aa2c-bf57f724f44e.description: Record a piece of music in written form.

0c64b8f6-0b65-4547-9349-71662b90912d.title: notation
0c64b8f6-0b65-4547-9349-71662b90912d.description:
A written means of documenting musical thought through signs and symbols.

Notation forms may include staff notation, pre-notation, graphic notation, notations drawn from global music cultures, instrument-specific notations, braille, scores, charts, lead-sheets.

ffb8542c-e3a7-4447-856d-68c20e1c5442.title: record
ffb8542c-e3a7-4447-856d-68c20e1c5442.description: Transfer sounds onto a recording medium for the purpose of reproduction.

5a454a44-5284-4f1e-b9d2-d39e01cbdf3a.title: repertoire
5a454a44-5284-4f1e-b9d2-d39e01cbdf3a.description: A collection of pieces of music within a particular social or cultural context, genre, style or tradition.

69d5b168-7652-4175-888b-d9cf101c6ac3.title: score
69d5b168-7652-4175-888b-d9cf101c6ac3.description:
A collection of notated representations of sound used to communicate musical information.

See notation

79d36fea-5332-4df9-8c7f-77918d35c73f.title: sensory score
79d36fea-5332-4df9-8c7f-77918d35c73f.description: The communication of musical information recorded through adapted media including modified stave notation, braille notation and graphic notation. It may also include sensory cues (such as visual, auditory, gestural and/or kinaesthetic stimuli) to assist the sequencing of musical material.

c575eb92-29ca-42fb-b00d-b20edcae3ced.title: stylistic awareness
c575eb92-29ca-42fb-b00d-b20edcae3ced.description: Responsiveness to the characteristics that define musical style(s).

d88fc854-bd33-43e3-8a7b-3aabdd4dd7b1.title: stylistic understanding
d88fc854-bd33-43e3-8a7b-3aabdd4dd7b1.description: The conscious application of stylistic features to create expressive works.

33c5cdcb-1b6a-45e8-a2af-473ae1fa5fa3.title: texture
33c5cdcb-1b6a-45e8-a2af-473ae1fa5fa3.description: The way layers of sound are combined in a piece of music.

f2d3df11-33ec-40f6-b989-1e2327d86757.title: dampen
f2d3df11-33ec-40f6-b989-1e2327d86757.description: Muffle or deaden the sound of an instrument by reducing vibrations.

8a65d5d4-bb4d-42ae-92e7-04a58708e02e.title: belonging
8a65d5d4-bb4d-42ae-92e7-04a58708e02e.description: A strong feeling of being happy or comfortable as part of a group, place or experience.

8e292473-1063-485d-89bc-5a1efbfa7c77.title: consent
8e292473-1063-485d-89bc-5a1efbfa7c77.description:
Informed and freely given agreement to engage in an activity, or for a specific thing to happen. Consent is denied when someone does not have the capacity to give consent.

According to the Commonwealth Consent policy Framework, sexual consent is a free, voluntary and informed agreement between people to participate in a sexual act. This agreement is only present when these people mutually and genuinely want to engage in that sexual act and actively make sure their partner does too.

In NSW, consent is a fundamental part of sexual offence law.

3ff71a10-2224-4c5d-8254-99c203bae254.title: contextual factors
3ff71a10-2224-4c5d-8254-99c203bae254.description: Factors that can influence health, safety, wellbeing and participation in physical activity including personal, social, cultural, economic, environmental and political factors that exist in differing ways and have varying impacts across population groups.

651929f3-be05-4de2-85af-7b18ca86e283.title: cyberbullying
651929f3-be05-4de2-85af-7b18ca86e283.description: The use of electronic communication and technology to bully or harass a person.

cc0f1db5-77cb-4a6e-9700-012f55dc4d9d.title: dynamic movement environments
cc0f1db5-77cb-4a6e-9700-012f55dc4d9d.description: Situations that are constantly changing and are more unpredictable.

bbef7d59-8a93-4ad2-8fc6-d61c8baa6c02.title: effort
bbef7d59-8a93-4ad2-8fc6-d61c8baa6c02.description: Refers to the dynamics and quality of movement. Effort awareness refers to understanding the muscular effort required to produce, sustain, stop or regulate a movement.

1fa40c88-6401-4349-9e5b-2c53158f9bce.title: grooming
1fa40c88-6401-4349-9e5b-2c53158f9bce.description: The process of someone building a relationship with a child or vulnerable person with the intention of manipulating, exploiting and/or abusing them, typically for sexual purposes.

e2055dcd-9c37-4f8d-a149-5658d53514a2.title: health-related components of fitness
e2055dcd-9c37-4f8d-a149-5658d53514a2.description: Cardiovascular fitness, flexibility, muscular endurance and strength.

30962aa7-4ffc-4056-b5c8-9b0978f82f6f.title: image-based abuse
30962aa7-4ffc-4056-b5c8-9b0978f82f6f.description: The act of sharing or threatening to share sexual or intimate images or videos of a person without their consent, often with the intention of causing distress or harm.

a9ea2df4-2dc5-4928-becf-1f668e1a22a6.title: initiative games
a9ea2df4-2dc5-4928-becf-1f668e1a22a6.description: Physical activities designed to challenge individuals that require critical and creative thinking, promote cooperation or encourage the solving of problems or movement challenges.

6aba71e2-ee40-4204-ba84-25bea92c01e8.title: intimate relationships
6aba71e2-ee40-4204-ba84-25bea92c01e8.description: Close, personal connections between individuals characterised by deep affection and emotional closeness.

ad879ea1-8208-498a-a674-6a79041e671b.title: movement challenges
ad879ea1-8208-498a-a674-6a79041e671b.description: Tasks that require individual students or groups of students to use a problem-solving approach to successfully complete the task.

4d4e6427-ba5d-400e-befa-ab18d2d34ba0.title: movement concepts
4d4e6427-ba5d-400e-befa-ab18d2d34ba0.description: Movement concepts (or elements of movement) explored in the content include body awareness; spatial awareness; effort awareness; and the relationship to or with objects, people and space.

9977a2e4-859d-4102-8707-11e75ab04a31.title: movement sequences
9977a2e4-859d-4102-8707-11e75ab04a31.description: A combination of movement skills and movement concepts to enable a body and/or objects to move in response to a stimulus; or a planned order of movements.

3c916549-b863-4252-8d5a-0b76445a8308.title: rhythmic movement sequences
3c916549-b863-4252-8d5a-0b76445a8308.description: Movement that is composed and performed in response to stimuli such as equipment, beats and sounds, images, words or themes. It includes creative movement, movement exploration, dance styles and dance elements.

ea50b4a0-7688-47c4-909a-92fc4b5bf6f5.title: sexual relationship
ea50b4a0-7688-47c4-909a-92fc4b5bf6f5.description: Involves interactions between individuals that include sexual activities or behaviours.

266b8185-a16e-478f-96da-4d82d07165cf.title: sexually transmissible infections (STI)
266b8185-a16e-478f-96da-4d82d07165cf.description: Any infection that can be passed from one person to another during sexual activity. Sexually transmissible infections include chlamydia, herpes, gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, scabies, pubic lice, hepatitis and HIV.

5c573563-3e15-4ff1-90c5-4c6dae7a986a.title: skill-related components of fitness
5c573563-3e15-4ff1-90c5-4c6dae7a986a.description: Includes agility, balance, coordination, reactions, power and speed.

0f4553c9-132c-4f59-8c32-f73498e1cfb1.title: specialised movement skills
0f4553c9-132c-4f59-8c32-f73498e1cfb1.description: Movement skills that are task-specific and are required in more organised games and activities.

d4672909-1609-4229-b36f-7863e611b6d9.title: bullying
d4672909-1609-4229-b36f-7863e611b6d9.description: Ongoing misuse of power through repeated behaviour that causes harm to a person or group of people.

4a32e084-e9e2-47f8-b193-979a3792f36c.title: coercion
4a32e084-e9e2-47f8-b193-979a3792f36c.description: The act of persuading or compelling someone to do something through the use of intimidation or force.

8bdd97f5-5445-4db4-b71f-d7dcfe8d7098.title: fundamental movement skills
8bdd97f5-5445-4db4-b71f-d7dcfe8d7098.description: A specific set of gross motor skills.

f74c5d48-ec10-44e8-b66c-8373586b1282.title: consent
f74c5d48-ec10-44e8-b66c-8373586b1282.description: Informed and freely given agreement to engage in an activity, or for a specific thing to happen.

529b9cf0-b1fc-494f-834d-7cf6551ae4b6.title: fair play
529b9cf0-b1fc-494f-834d-7cf6551ae4b6.description: Play that is free from any bias and includes the application of rules and/or etiquette.

5cb26ddb-690b-4237-8753-7182f39d4655.title: analogue
5cb26ddb-690b-4237-8753-7182f39d4655.description: A method of capturing images using chemical processes on film, a hard plate, or paper.

c5cfe55b-4168-42e3-8f42-58f75c5a0ebc.title: aperture
c5cfe55b-4168-42e3-8f42-58f75c5a0ebc.description: The adjustable opening in a camera lens that controls how much light enters when taking a photograph, measured in f-stops.

eef3239e-616d-4638-bec3-5ae0a71fbda3.title: cyanotype
eef3239e-616d-4638-bec3-5ae0a71fbda3.description: A photographic printing process using sensitised, precoated paper to create white forms on deep blue backgrounds; also the resulting print.

a0a5cf70-c68d-406c-8779-a21946f6775d.title: exposure
a0a5cf70-c68d-406c-8779-a21946f6775d.description: The amount of light that reaches a camera’s sensor or sensitive film, plate or paper, determined by the aperture, shutter speed and ISO settings on a camera that control its sensitivity to light.

dfc3e7ab-0cee-45dc-8230-cb8f7e2cd371.title: frame rate
dfc3e7ab-0cee-45dc-8230-cb8f7e2cd371.description: The number of images, or frames, captured or displayed per second in film or video, measured in frames per second (FPS).

5106d783-a70f-4b00-b524-910edb0df3f9.title: gimbal
5106d783-a70f-4b00-b524-910edb0df3f9.description: A stabilising device that uses pivoted supports to keep a camera steady and level while filming, even when the operator or platform is moving.

09d51e68-c252-4868-88d0-d2b209542e17.title: hyperlapse
09d51e68-c252-4868-88d0-d2b209542e17.description: A type of time-lapse video created by moving the camera through space between each shot, producing a dynamic sense of motion and accelerated time.

50e5767a-b937-4a0d-95bc-9b43c002243c.title: iconography
50e5767a-b937-4a0d-95bc-9b43c002243c.description: A visual code used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples that connects art to ancestral Cultural Knowledge systems, Country and Cultural identity.

e5f0f61c-bf72-467d-bcac-923b330e26ca.title: layering
e5f0f61c-bf72-467d-bcac-923b330e26ca.description: The process of combining or stacking multiple images, videos, or graphic elements to build depth, texture, or meaning.

17528b41-ae2a-4c6b-89fe-218b91ffb567.title: long exposure
17528b41-ae2a-4c6b-89fe-218b91ffb567.description: A photographic technique that keeps the camera’s shutter open for an extended time to capture motion, light trails, or low-light scenes.

c5401e83-55ac-4f39-82bd-a965d4d835c7.title: masking
c5401e83-55ac-4f39-82bd-a965d4d835c7.description: Controlling what is visible or exposed by limiting light, or hiding parts of an image or layer.

7396116e-5a3e-4690-8730-c5824ee95d8e.title: montage
7396116e-5a3e-4690-8730-c5824ee95d8e.description: A technique that combines multiple photographic images or shots, placed side by side or layered, to convey a single idea, compress time, or create new meaning.

99da6ce4-af92-416d-a3ee-4d292b8f3e22.title: photogram
99da6ce4-af92-416d-a3ee-4d292b8f3e22.description: An image made without a camera by placing objects on light-sensitive paper and exposing it to light to produce silhouettes and tonal shapes.

c1becca7-87dc-4237-9711-8c8df56dbb37.title: photomedia artist
c1becca7-87dc-4237-9711-8c8df56dbb37.description: A person who makes photomedia artworks as an individual, as part of a group, at a school, as part of a company, or by enlisting others to produce their photomedia artwork.

0ba92482-46a8-4c05-98e0-d41149f2d75f.title: photomedia form
0ba92482-46a8-4c05-98e0-d41149f2d75f.description: A category of artistic representation in Photography, Film and Digital Media distinguished by specific techniques and mediums in still, moving or emerging fields.

047abd98-5c63-40c5-9249-30d686bb3050.title: photomedia practice
047abd98-5c63-40c5-9249-30d686bb3050.description: The application of skills and knowledge to make, represent, respond to and interpret photomedia artworks.

3cd92dd3-48be-4406-8503-bc179903981c.title: photomedia practitioner
3cd92dd3-48be-4406-8503-bc179903981c.description: Individuals, such as photomedia artists, curators, writers, critics and historians, who engage in the making, curation, critique and/or historical explanations of photomedia artworks.

8ddc40f3-2b7c-4968-b34f-3142cac9984a.title: retouching
8ddc40f3-2b7c-4968-b34f-3142cac9984a.description: Correcting or improving images, negatives or moving image footage by removing blemishes or distractions and fixing imperfections.

d1fc8179-658e-4b07-af83-7c7b77ce5ee6.title: shutter speed
d1fc8179-658e-4b07-af83-7c7b77ce5ee6.description: The time the camera shutter stays open to light during an exposure which determines image brightness and whether motion appears sharp or blurred.

cfc9bf50-cd2d-4af4-af5a-7a362a371904.title: synthetic
cfc9bf50-cd2d-4af4-af5a-7a362a371904.description: A style where images are created or shaped by computational digital processes, often including AI, rather than traditional or manual methods.

6ebeacd8-9cd5-4d5b-a7f8-044d36d87920.title: time lapse
6ebeacd8-9cd5-4d5b-a7f8-044d36d87920.description: A photographic or filming technique that records frames at spaced intervals and plays them at normal speed to compress time and accelerate motion; the camera remains fixed.

c2c9068b-e3cf-4637-8b9f-276bdde1ddd5.title: title sequencing
c2c9068b-e3cf-4637-8b9f-276bdde1ddd5.description: The opening segment of a film or video that uses images, motion and sound to present the title and credits, and set the tone and mood.

73cc8ffa-f454-4638-8abf-044d2cc73f95.title: code(s)
73cc8ffa-f454-4638-8abf-044d2cc73f95.description: Agreed systems of making, communicating and interpreting meaning through signs and symbols.

a444fe4e-cd9a-4b2b-b263-a209bbc31c5c.title: expressive
a444fe4e-cd9a-4b2b-b263-a209bbc31c5c.description: The use of artistic methods and techniques to convey emotions, intentions and meanings in a personal, imaginative and intuitive manner.

22e15fca-e0c8-47c0-9fe1-1c19b6a4a9ce.title: intention
22e15fca-e0c8-47c0-9fe1-1c19b6a4a9ce.description: The purpose and motivation behind a person’s choices and actions.

b15318c4-9f70-4e83-8437-dd564c48798e.title: material
b15318c4-9f70-4e83-8437-dd564c48798e.description: Encompasses physical forms, such as paint, clay, a printed photograph or ready-made objects. Virtual forms include digital projections, virtual reality and interactive installations.

9d91aecd-3011-4686-b6ec-cfb9d2cb3256.title: multisensory
9d91aecd-3011-4686-b6ec-cfb9d2cb3256.description: The process of engaging at least 2 senses to communicate or experience the same thing simultaneously.

1f9aa75c-1672-4418-a03b-ae1e4c54152a.title: symbol
1f9aa75c-1672-4418-a03b-ae1e4c54152a.description: That which represents ideas, beliefs or concepts beyond the physical form and carries inferred meanings or messages.

e1edb86e-a8af-4616-8f74-8cef8a624794.title: virtual properties
e1edb86e-a8af-4616-8f74-8cef8a624794.description: Characteristics of an artwork that exist in virtual or digital environments.

6af08b61-4013-41e3-a061-6f58659ee0dd.title: visual language
6af08b61-4013-41e3-a061-6f58659ee0dd.description: Communication using conventions, codes, symbols, signs and forms in artworks.

054fc581-f24a-49c9-97a2-3d093ec90265.title: tactic
054fc581-f24a-49c9-97a2-3d093ec90265.description: A specific action or response to a particular situation, designed to implement or support a strategy.

16a2eb6b-8db6-4b14-b398-db50474837c1.title: repulsion (electrical)
16a2eb6b-8db6-4b14-b398-db50474837c1.description: The force that pushes 2 like electric charges away from each other.

7f0421e6-f7d4-4e24-bdfa-9235938d5204.title: wasted energy
7f0421e6-f7d4-4e24-bdfa-9235938d5204.description: The energy that is lost during a process or energy conversion usually as heat.

dc9f4528-4def-44a1-ac41-627a98cf41c6.title: echolocation
dc9f4528-4def-44a1-ac41-627a98cf41c6.description: A biological sonar system used by some animals to navigate, hunt, and understand their surroundings by emitting sounds and listening to the echoes that bounce back from objects.

878609cb-e320-45d4-b210-34205ee3032c.title: longitudinal (wave)
878609cb-e320-45d4-b210-34205ee3032c.description: A type of wave in which the disturbance or oscillation of the medium occurs in the same direction as the direction of propagation of the wave.

2631fb33-3175-4e82-a798-4fe1369f95cf.title: mechanical wave
2631fb33-3175-4e82-a798-4fe1369f95cf.description: A type of wave that requires a medium, such as air, water or a solid material, to travel through.

dda1b03e-25d7-43e4-aec1-fa45280434dc.title: reflection
dda1b03e-25d7-43e4-aec1-fa45280434dc.description: The changed direction of a wave when it bounces off a surface.

5a44043d-a05e-4d04-9dcb-c17ff248e7b0.title: refraction
5a44043d-a05e-4d04-9dcb-c17ff248e7b0.description: The changed direction (bending) of a wave when it passes through one transparent substance into another.

0cccc69a-f355-4c20-977f-ebced2543a8b.title: transverse (wave)
0cccc69a-f355-4c20-977f-ebced2543a8b.description: A wave motion in which all points of the wave oscillate along paths perpendicular to the direction of the wave's movement, e.g. surface ripples on water, seismic S (secondary) waves, and electromagnetic waves like radio and light.

f281a41d-4440-4829-9f91-cee224dc4ed4.title: wavelength
f281a41d-4440-4829-9f91-cee224dc4ed4.description: The distance between successive peaks (or troughs) of a wave, measured in metres (m) in the International System of Units (SI).

9db91ef7-cc02-4c5c-810a-1a656c3b6d05.title: attraction (electrical)
9db91ef7-cc02-4c5c-810a-1a656c3b6d05.description: The force that pulls opposite electric charges toward each other.

a1dbc71e-7cf4-4e12-9cd4-048d524050d4.title: diffraction
a1dbc71e-7cf4-4e12-9cd4-048d524050d4.description: The bending and spreading of waves when they encounter an obstacle or pass through a narrow opening.

ff201db7-4427-468b-8af7-9f455a549148.title: electric circuit
ff201db7-4427-468b-8af7-9f455a549148.description: A closed path through which electric current flows. It typically consists of a power source, conductive wires, and electrical components.

657d6d32-c001-482b-8cc8-de9a24100a03.title: electromagnetic spectrum
657d6d32-c001-482b-8cc8-de9a24100a03.description: The complete range of electromagnetic waves arranged by frequency or wavelength, spanning from low-frequency radio waves to high-frequency gamma rays.

8c1cdb39-7d1e-4c1f-a21b-6ad09bd77791.title: radioactivity
8c1cdb39-7d1e-4c1f-a21b-6ad09bd77791.description: The spontaneous emission of particles or energy from the unstable nucleus of certain atoms as they decay into more stable forms.

1878d8a8-a2b2-4064-bf70-373ea59da4d5.title: antinode
1878d8a8-a2b2-4064-bf70-373ea59da4d5.description: A point in a standing wave where the amplitude of oscillation is at its maximum, which occurs halfway between 2 nodes.

52936186-cf24-4311-a22c-5b27d35d255f.title: area vector (normal)
52936186-cf24-4311-a22c-5b27d35d255f.description: A vector that is perpendicular to a surface and whose magnitude equals the area of that surface. It’s used to calculate electric flux or magnetic flux through a surface.

4082efad-2047-43a1-aa8a-4a7aec737533.title: back emf (back electromotive force)
4082efad-2047-43a1-aa8a-4a7aec737533.description: The voltage that is induced in a motor's coil when the motor is running. It opposes the applied voltage and is a direct consequence of the Law of Electromagnetic Induction.

ae692f0f-f489-4c5a-b3de-509af6c8a174.title: baryon
ae692f0f-f489-4c5a-b3de-509af6c8a174.description: A type of subatomic particle made up of 3 quarks and are part of the hadron family – particles that experience the strong nuclear force.

ff8c3a7a-d4c4-4110-947f-fbb4ae0c36db.title: beta-minus decay
ff8c3a7a-d4c4-4110-947f-fbb4ae0c36db.description: A type of radioactive decay in which a neutron inside an unstable atomic nucleus transforms into a proton and, in the process, emits a beta particle (which is an electron) and an electron antineutrino.

941a4162-45eb-4ec7-9ca2-5ca55e5d1061.title: beta-plus transformation
941a4162-45eb-4ec7-9ca2-5ca55e5d1061.description: A type of radioactive decay where a proton in an unstable nucleus is transformed into a neutron and emits a positron and an electron neutrino.

0de72ad6-e9ca-4569-b369-75116d3cf220.title: binding energy
0de72ad6-e9ca-4569-b369-75116d3cf220.description: The energy required to split a nucleus of an atom into its individual protons and neutrons.

4c982d82-cb2e-4ec9-9749-c1c617645963.title: black body (ideal)
4c982d82-cb2e-4ec9-9749-c1c617645963.description: An object that absorbs all incident electromagnetic radiation, regardless of wavelength or angle, and emits radiation with a characteristic spectrum that depends only on its temperature, not its material or surface.

cdf457a6-383b-4b81-bfdf-a23b52568d30.title: blueshift
cdf457a6-383b-4b81-bfdf-a23b52568d30.description: A phenomenon where light from a distant object in the universe shifts to shorter (bluer) wavelengths, indicating it is moving toward the observer.

56af4354-5495-402d-a070-b4f12f338197.title: boson
56af4354-5495-402d-a070-b4f12f338197.description: A type of fundamental particle that carries forces in nature.

5e55cb73-a711-469f-a3b6-cd2bdbbe1004.title: cathode ray
5e55cb73-a711-469f-a3b6-cd2bdbbe1004.description: A stream of electrons observed in vacuum tubes which are emitted from the cathode (the negatively charged electrode) and travel toward the anode (the positively charged electrode).

cf326d2b-e328-47e0-8ff3-01f479a8b0bd.title: centripetal acceleration
cf326d2b-e328-47e0-8ff3-01f479a8b0bd.description: The acceleration directed toward the centre of a circular path that keeps an object moving in a uniform circular motion.

f650e902-e920-4dcd-b0e2-182258709df1.title: centripetal force
f650e902-e920-4dcd-b0e2-182258709df1.description: The net force that acts toward the centre of a circular path, causing an object to move in uniform circular motion.

2aef3c42-9155-49d4-af02-fdf6166ebd64.title: conservative forces
2aef3c42-9155-49d4-af02-fdf6166ebd64.description: Forces where work done on an object depends only on initial and final positions, not the path taken.

53e951f0-8ff8-456f-8b3a-05766467881e.title: constructive interference
53e951f0-8ff8-456f-8b3a-05766467881e.description: Occurs when 2 or more waves combine in phase, causing their amplitudes to add together to produce a wave with a larger amplitude than the original waves.

93939159-c383-4100-a693-6196099087ab.title: conventional current
93939159-c383-4100-a693-6196099087ab.description: The flow of positive charge from the positive terminal to the negative terminal of a power source in a circuit.

d0814d25-5646-4071-80ea-a5307f2cd6ac.title: decay constant
d0814d25-5646-4071-80ea-a5307f2cd6ac.description: Represents the probability per unit time in which a given nucleus will decay.

ad4ff06e-bee0-4da4-9253-2e454fcae215.title: destructive interference
ad4ff06e-bee0-4da4-9253-2e454fcae215.description: Occurs when the crests and troughs of 2 interfering waves of equal frequency and opposite phase meet, and their amplitudes cancel out.

3fcad099-19d1-40ee-b1b7-f4299820c175.title: elastic collision
3fcad099-19d1-40ee-b1b7-f4299820c175.description: A type of collision where both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.

f5b11534-2cda-47ce-87a1-3b8cd652ed68.title: electric permittivity
f5b11534-2cda-47ce-87a1-3b8cd652ed68.description: A measure of how much resistance is encountered when forming an electric field in a medium.

a57d13c4-7b5c-4b7c-97d3-96f8e6cd2b6e.title: electric potential energy
a57d13c4-7b5c-4b7c-97d3-96f8e6cd2b6e.description: The energy in charged objects as a result of their position in an electric field.

7061bb88-7281-40b4-b141-9f8e902b20ca.title: electromagnetic induction
7061bb88-7281-40b4-b141-9f8e902b20ca.description: The production of an electromotive force (emf) across an electrical conductor in a changing magnetic field.

bbde0a68-f2fc-46c3-a124-567277c66d98.title: electromotive force (emf)
bbde0a68-f2fc-46c3-a124-567277c66d98.description: The energy supplied per unit charge by an energy source such as an electric generator or a battery.

60055c52-023b-4296-9e6c-092f4a1b0de4.title: equipotential
60055c52-023b-4296-9e6c-092f4a1b0de4.description: Refers to a region in an electric or gravitational field where the potential is the same at every point, meaning that no work is done when moving a charge or mass along an equipotential.

4d6a4b38-4577-4a6e-a6e9-686f0c4dff68.title: frequency shift phenomenon
4d6a4b38-4577-4a6e-a6e9-686f0c4dff68.description: The observed change in the frequency of a wave when there is relative motion between the source and the observer.

81efc72e-ba52-4270-be68-9547d073f72e.title: geostationary orbit
81efc72e-ba52-4270-be68-9547d073f72e.description: A geosynchronous orbit of a satellite where a satellite orbits directly above the equator in the same direction as Earth’s rotation and has an orbital period equal to Earth’s period of rotation.

ef02fa62-1ba0-40fd-9940-e06a5091dd18.title: gravitational potential energy
ef02fa62-1ba0-40fd-9940-e06a5091dd18.description: The energy possessed by a mass due to its position in a gravitational field.

08e05fc4-207c-4b5a-9bf7-6d7d458fe34d.title: half-life
08e05fc4-207c-4b5a-9bf7-6d7d458fe34d.description: The time it takes for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay.

91b427b4-c76b-40be-adbf-ff55d2f484e2.title: inelastic collision
91b427b4-c76b-40be-adbf-ff55d2f484e2.description: A type of collision where momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not, as some of the kinetic energy is converted into other forms of energy.

e5051639-a9e0-4c71-8a2f-4996bc2d1b6b.title: inertial frame of reference
e5051639-a9e0-4c71-8a2f-4996bc2d1b6b.description: A viewpoint in which Newton’s First Law (the law of inertia) holds true.

ece39451-ac9c-4571-bcdf-978108742416.title: inverse square law
ece39451-ac9c-4571-bcdf-978108742416.description: A physical quantity, like light, sound, or gravity, that diminishes in intensity in proportion to the square of the distance from its source, so doubling the distance reduces the intensity to one-fourth.

b945e030-df79-44a6-871e-0100041a7229.title: length contraction
b945e030-df79-44a6-871e-0100041a7229.description: A relativistic phenomenon where an object moving at a high velocity appears shorter along the direction of motion to a stationary observer.

15dd6470-b1da-441f-a3a7-839d614d1443.title: lepton
15dd6470-b1da-441f-a3a7-839d614d1443.description: A type of fundamental particle that does not experience the strong nuclear force.

848853c5-4f97-409c-aa7c-706d054ca640.title: magnetic permeability
848853c5-4f97-409c-aa7c-706d054ca640.description: A measure of how readily a material can support the formation of a magnetic field within itself when exposed to an external magnetic field.

41444562-8942-4ec8-bb35-21e88f82ae4d.title: mass defect
41444562-8942-4ec8-bb35-21e88f82ae4d.description: The difference between the total mass of the individual nucleons in a nucleus and the actual mass of the nucleus itself.

d1f853ce-5b18-4f42-84a4-bf18364b391d.title: mechanical energy
d1f853ce-5b18-4f42-84a4-bf18364b391d.description: Is the energy of an object due to its kinetic energy and potential energy.

1db03f8b-9972-4100-9bf0-cd5c3586e8ce.title: monochromatic light
1db03f8b-9972-4100-9bf0-cd5c3586e8ce.description: Light that consists of a single wavelength or frequency – meaning it is pure light of one colour of one specific energy.

16a9ddc7-113b-4205-bc00-c46270a2fb89.title: muon
16a9ddc7-113b-4205-bc00-c46270a2fb89.description: Part of the lepton group which are a type of fundamental particle.

20291bf6-8d88-4d60-8354-92deb232c4c5.title: node
20291bf6-8d88-4d60-8354-92deb232c4c5.description: A point along a standing wave in a vibrating medium where the amplitude is always zero meaning no movement occurs at that position.

c08be185-ca3f-4654-bc7c-a266b625f394.title: non-conservative forces
c08be185-ca3f-4654-bc7c-a266b625f394.description: Forces that dissipate mechanical energy from a system, usually by converting it into other forms like heat, sound or deformation; the work done by non-conservative forces depends on the path taken.

c7bb3105-a790-45c5-8797-5f094be2427d.title: non-inertial frame of reference
c7bb3105-a790-45c5-8797-5f094be2427d.description: A viewpoint that is accelerating relative to an inertial frame and to which Newton’s laws of motion do not apply directly.

6048467d-4d22-43da-a9ee-114d75d5438d.title: nucleosynthesis
6048467d-4d22-43da-a9ee-114d75d5438d.description: The process by which new atomic nuclei are formed from pre-existing protons and neutrons.

9e40e317-c41a-4727-9738-08136c8492d9.title: orbital velocity
9e40e317-c41a-4727-9738-08136c8492d9.description: The velocity at which a satellite must travel to maintain a particular orbit at a given altitude under the influence of gravity alone.

e00cd226-e287-41a4-a4be-0c923a75bec8.title: photoelectric effect
e00cd226-e287-41a4-a4be-0c923a75bec8.description: The process in which a photon ejects an electron from an atom so that all the energy of the photon is absorbed in separating the electron and imparting kinetic energy to it.

af40ab2b-3523-49ac-949d-f1bbca9a72a8.title: photoelectron
af40ab2b-3523-49ac-949d-f1bbca9a72a8.description: An electron that is ejected from a material, usually a metal, when it absorbs energy from incident light (photons) as a result of the photoelectric effect.

634f3953-ff8a-4c43-b3f0-faf63d7cf1c8.title: photon
634f3953-ff8a-4c43-b3f0-faf63d7cf1c8.description: A massless, chargeless particle that represents a quantum with its energy being proportional to the frequency of the radiation.

c39d5784-712e-4029-be64-fa5f97398449.title: quantised energy
c39d5784-712e-4029-be64-fa5f97398449.description: The concept that energy in a physical system can only exist in discrete, fixed amounts, rather than any arbitrary value.

8339a136-59ac-496f-87e5-b4595ad4832a.title: quark
8339a136-59ac-496f-87e5-b4595ad4832a.description: A fundamental subatomic particle that experiences all 4 fundamental forces (including the strong nuclear force) and combines to form hadrons.

0fb0099d-ed8d-43e9-9011-a2760514d5f9.title: redshift
0fb0099d-ed8d-43e9-9011-a2760514d5f9.description: A phenomenon where light from a distant object in the universe shifts to longer (redder) wavelengths, indicating it is moving away from the observer.

695d5d0c-d8e4-4633-ba11-ffffa7636b5b.title: relativistic momentum
695d5d0c-d8e4-4633-ba11-ffffa7636b5b.description: The momentum of an object moving close to the speed of light, where classical momentum formulas no longer apply: momentum increases more rapidly than classical momentum as an object’s speed approaches c.

4a76bbb0-ab24-4f5f-9400-c12900b7ece8.title: simultaneity
4a76bbb0-ab24-4f5f-9400-c12900b7ece8.description: The concept that 2 events that occur at the same for one observer may not appear to do so for another observer, depending on their relative motion.

1881fd2f-5a9c-43fe-8af8-c0eae13e43ee.title: standing wave
1881fd2f-5a9c-43fe-8af8-c0eae13e43ee.description: A wave in which the nodes appear to remain stationary, while the antinodes oscillate with maximum amplitude.

218e2c53-6e7f-4d28-9170-069cd94f2a17.title: superposition
218e2c53-6e7f-4d28-9170-069cd94f2a17.description: Two or more waves meet at a point, the total displacement of which is equal to the algebraic sum of the displacements of the individual waves.

84f1ef83-a812-4326-8dfd-62ff6806d26d.title: thermionic emission
84f1ef83-a812-4326-8dfd-62ff6806d26d.description: The release of electrons from the surface of a heated metal.

9db64b5d-29d4-4d75-8d9b-3311e3f34b69.title: time dilation
9db64b5d-29d4-4d75-8d9b-3311e3f34b69.description: The relativistic effect where time passes at different rates for observers in relative motion.

9302b841-1784-4f7a-a7f5-67f52ab34d06.title: torque
9302b841-1784-4f7a-a7f5-67f52ab34d06.description: The tendency of a force to cause rotation about a point or axis.

78dc515e-1508-4a3c-91ab-9e04ba83f58d.title: translational velocity
78dc515e-1508-4a3c-91ab-9e04ba83f58d.description: The rate at which an astronomical object changes position in space.

f62b5d13-5e24-4d39-b484-37ea771109ff.title: transmutation
f62b5d13-5e24-4d39-b484-37ea771109ff.description: The process by which one chemical element or isotope is converted into another when the number of protons in a nucleus changes.

e4e5ac3c-52a8-47da-890a-8d857bec1563.title: uniform circular motion
e4e5ac3c-52a8-47da-890a-8d857bec1563.description: The movement of an object along a circular path at a constant speed, with its direction continuously changing and causing a centripetal acceleration directed toward the circle's centre.

4f90d26b-df6e-4975-ba09-2ee1d28cc977.title: weak force
4f90d26b-df6e-4975-ba09-2ee1d28cc977.description: One of the 4 fundamental forces of nature responsible for processes that change one type of particle into another, particularly within the nuclei of atoms.

1f6ac8a5-79c3-4d38-874d-ca520b68e424.title: work
1f6ac8a5-79c3-4d38-874d-ca520b68e424.description: The transfer of energy that occurs when an external force is applied to an object, causing it to move in the direction of the force.

4cb2a8b6-7d87-4103-97d0-6616cb71f996.title: work function
4cb2a8b6-7d87-4103-97d0-6616cb71f996.description: The minimum energy required to liberate an electron from the surface of a material (typically a metal) into a vacuum.

2362ade3-0901-4c60-ad47-e05ce9e15fe4.title: alpha (decay)
2362ade3-0901-4c60-ad47-e05ce9e15fe4.description: Radioactive disintegration in which positively charged particles composed of 2 protons and 2 neutrons (and therefore equivalent to the nucleus of a helium atom) are emitted.

f9920a6e-ee9f-42a4-b476-992ab6922b0b.title: beta (decay)
f9920a6e-ee9f-42a4-b476-992ab6922b0b.description: A radioactive transformation in which high-energy, high-speed electrons are emitted.

d4e66540-4c4d-4f60-96f9-3c22475b5d59.title: fusion (nuclear)
d4e66540-4c4d-4f60-96f9-3c22475b5d59.description: A process in which 2 or more atomic nuclei combine to form a single, heavier nucleus, releasing a large amount of energy in the process.

23de3221-6a77-43ff-b038-d8e429afbe1c.title: potential energy
23de3221-6a77-43ff-b038-d8e429afbe1c.description: The energy that an object possesses due to its position in a force field or that is stored in a system by virtue of the configuration and interaction between bodies in that system, e.g. elastic potential energy.

dffd273a-c2a0-494c-819a-ce60a684977b.title: rarefactions
dffd273a-c2a0-494c-819a-ce60a684977b.description: Regions in a longitudinal wave where the particles of the medium are spread apart, resulting in decreased density and pressure compared to the surrounding areas.

f0dc1e40-8f3c-4a25-9adc-dfc07856c8cf.title: habitat
f0dc1e40-8f3c-4a25-9adc-dfc07856c8cf.description: The place where an animal or plant can live.

c6c90e5f-aa1a-4e05-819f-9ce3a238f00b.title: absorption
c6c90e5f-aa1a-4e05-819f-9ce3a238f00b.description: The process of the energy of a wave being taken in or assimilated by the medium it travels through, causing a decrease in the wave's intensity.

21538d64-8d8b-4974-ab8d-db9f5a3ed287.title: adapted
21538d64-8d8b-4974-ab8d-db9f5a3ed287.description: Able to survive and reproduce in a changed environment because of modified physical, behavioural or physiological characteristics.

d7100dc2-ac29-4eee-b35f-f7f0948f38dd.title: alkane
d7100dc2-ac29-4eee-b35f-f7f0948f38dd.description: An organic compound that consists entirely of single-bonded carbon and hydrogen atoms having the general formula CnH2n+2, as methane (CH4), ethane (C2H6), and that lacks any other functional groups.

e3290501-df41-4d50-a811-61c0f78b1596.title: alloy
e3290501-df41-4d50-a811-61c0f78b1596.description: A substance composed of 2 or more metals (or, sometimes, a metal and a nonmetal) mixed together.

660cb735-f372-4fef-9ec7-1192efe5b983.title: amplitude
660cb735-f372-4fef-9ec7-1192efe5b983.description: The maximum value of an alternating quantity measured from its mean or base value.

f0d471b0-f230-470b-aa01-a30c28b9d72f.title: analyse (scientifically)
f0d471b0-f230-470b-aa01-a30c28b9d72f.description: To consider in detail for the purpose of finding meaning or relationships, and identifying patterns, similarities and differences.

12ab36e0-a974-486b-b286-544a49c34b04.title: atomic number
12ab36e0-a974-486b-b286-544a49c34b04.description: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom; used to order the chemical elements in the periodic table.

24dc7803-980c-4c4e-a0a1-bec9c6d30318.title: bioaccumulation
24dc7803-980c-4c4e-a0a1-bec9c6d30318.description: (Of a substance, especially a toxin) The build-up of substances (especially toxins) in an organism over time.

533a51aa-479c-4d57-a05d-119a16ee281d.title: biodegradability
533a51aa-479c-4d57-a05d-119a16ee281d.description: The ability of a material to decompose as a result of the action of living organisms, especially bacteria.

ecce3979-0391-4908-85ca-818d29983046.title: bivariate analysis
ecce3979-0391-4908-85ca-818d29983046.description: A type of statistical analysis involving 2 variables which aims to explain how changes in one variable affect the other.

dbebb9a0-95ba-4d9d-963b-5bcb32abdfec.title: boiling (point)
dbebb9a0-95ba-4d9d-963b-5bcb32abdfec.description: The temperature at which the vapour pressure of the liquid equals the pressure surrounding the liquid, and the liquid changes into a vapour.

ab83688f-bb91-4291-bda1-7994b9072eb7.title: buoyancy
ab83688f-bb91-4291-bda1-7994b9072eb7.description: The tendency of an object to rise upward or float in a fluid.

01b53f54-20e4-4742-a368-b9e3b9bca9c4.title: catalyst
01b53f54-20e4-4742-a368-b9e3b9bca9c4.description: A substance that changes the speed of a chemical reaction but is itself unchanged at the end of the reaction.

b0f4fd99-6dde-458c-824b-a3fe81e432d3.title: characteristic
b0f4fd99-6dde-458c-824b-a3fe81e432d3.description: A distinguishing aspect (including features and behaviours) of an object, material, living thing or event.

b2a97340-ed3f-4d6d-b47f-c200ec142870.title: chloroplast
b2a97340-ed3f-4d6d-b47f-c200ec142870.description: The chlorophyll-containing structures in the cells of plants and algae where photosynthesis occurs.

b9029188-755c-4bfb-b050-70ad7435ec09.title: compound
b9029188-755c-4bfb-b050-70ad7435ec09.description: A substance containing 2 or more atoms of different elements bonded together in a fixed ratio.

f42390e3-e7d0-4fa9-8242-e7bbe802db22.title: conduction
f42390e3-e7d0-4fa9-8242-e7bbe802db22.description: The transfer of heat or electricity through a substance or between substances that are in direct contact with each other.

ad15d313-fcab-4193-a9b2-9a391b0cd448.title: convection
ad15d313-fcab-4193-a9b2-9a391b0cd448.description: The movement of a gas or fluid by the transfer of heat energy through the gas or fluid itself.

7dff2563-1d51-4862-903f-758848ea1b82.title: correlational relationship
7dff2563-1d51-4862-903f-758848ea1b82.description: A relationship that measures the strength of interdependence of 2 variables.

ca866e99-de3b-422f-bc5f-9c004f4b480a.title: covalent (bond)
ca866e99-de3b-422f-bc5f-9c004f4b480a.description: A chemical bond formed by the sharing of electrons between 2 atoms, each of which donates an equal number of electrons.

bd83ea5c-7d4d-4f4f-92ce-5fbac8c302ed.title: current (electric)
bd83ea5c-7d4d-4f4f-92ce-5fbac8c302ed.description: The flow of electric charge, usually through a conductor or resistor.

d0efa49a-f8d9-42ef-b52b-0cd957218238.title: data science
d0efa49a-f8d9-42ef-b52b-0cd957218238.description: A field of study which involves collecting, analysing and interpreting large amounts of data to gain insights and make decisions.

080ba7e9-7b47-4368-9b43-b36021577e65.title: decomposers
080ba7e9-7b47-4368-9b43-b36021577e65.description: Living things such as fungi and bacteria that break down dead organic material.

8e219456-10c7-4367-8604-a99e15132363.title: density
8e219456-10c7-4367-8604-a99e15132363.description: A measure of how tightly packed the particles in a substance are. Density is calculated by dividing the mass of the substance by its volume (measured as grams per centimetre cubed, or g/cm3).

73428c0e-ad62-4025-9a84-e2d6494cfdbe.title: descriptive analysis
73428c0e-ad62-4025-9a84-e2d6494cfdbe.description: The analysis of statistics that quantitatively describe or summarise features of a collection of information.

d0da0a42-0573-4192-bace-c99c9e0a33db.title: descriptive statistics
d0da0a42-0573-4192-bace-c99c9e0a33db.description: Statistics that quantitatively describe or summarise features of a collection of information.

2b469e89-aa81-4064-af3e-7074ffffc950.title: disease
2b469e89-aa81-4064-af3e-7074ffffc950.description: An illness or condition of the body affecting the way an organism, or parts of an organism, or its organs, function.

b17e0d72-1f25-41d1-b70e-7620838ff1a5.title: disorder
b17e0d72-1f25-41d1-b70e-7620838ff1a5.description: A disturbance of physical, mental or genetic health.

696407b2-c814-49b4-a23e-d906e79f6529.title: displacement (reaction)
696407b2-c814-49b4-a23e-d906e79f6529.description: A chemical reaction in which one atom (or group of atoms) is replaced by another atom (or group of atoms) in a compound.

52cd51a4-c5b2-4ff9-a92b-a557874caa0b.title: ecological energy pyramid
52cd51a4-c5b2-4ff9-a92b-a557874caa0b.description: A graphical representation of the flow of energy through different trophic levels in an ecosystem.

d5ac1e02-b22a-4d0a-b4d4-03917b287c55.title: electromagnetic (EM) radiation
d5ac1e02-b22a-4d0a-b4d4-03917b287c55.description: Describes the electrical currents and magnetic forces produced by an electrical current, as in electromagnetic radiation, electromagnetic waves, electromagnetic spectrum.

6cef21bf-3246-4758-b921-cbccff1988a3.title: endangered (species)
6cef21bf-3246-4758-b921-cbccff1988a3.description: Facing a very high risk of extinction in the wild due to rapid population decline or loss of habitat.

3631949c-f71f-4f04-87c9-7c1801e168ea.title: endemic
3631949c-f71f-4f04-87c9-7c1801e168ea.description: Of a disease, commonly found in a particular community or locality.

eb9a5c63-b394-4d84-9d37-6384eedbe483.title: epidemic
eb9a5c63-b394-4d84-9d37-6384eedbe483.description: A temporary occurrence of a disease which spreads rapidly and extensively within a specific population, community, or region, typically affecting a significantly higher number of individuals than expected.

bf573360-1777-466f-9325-e4dba9abf4d2.title: error
bf573360-1777-466f-9325-e4dba9abf4d2.description: The difference between an observed result and an expected or theoretical result. Systematic errors are often due to limitations in equipment or procedure and will be consistently different from the expected result.

d2b65a68-fb17-4860-9196-70c739123b78.title: evaporation
d2b65a68-fb17-4860-9196-70c739123b78.description: The process by which a liquid, such as water, changes into a gas or vapor state, usually due to an increase in temperature.

a3283141-b64c-490b-adb6-15d1165207c7.title: evidence
a3283141-b64c-490b-adb6-15d1165207c7.description: Valid and/or reliable data that can be used to support a particular theory, hypothesis, idea or conclusion.

f658ab2c-5548-4758-9a04-b326f855b8cd.title: evolution
f658ab2c-5548-4758-9a04-b326f855b8cd.description: The gradual process by which living things change over time.

62d4ca1c-1eb1-4162-b456-fa0cf4043a82.title: explanation
62d4ca1c-1eb1-4162-b456-fa0cf4043a82.description: A scientific explanation provides an account of a phenomenon through descriptive statements about how that phenomenon came to be.

1d4cf1a0-fb54-45c9-905a-f59df3a914bc.title: extinct
1d4cf1a0-fb54-45c9-905a-f59df3a914bc.description: No longer existing because all members of the species have died.

1f532c6d-0ea2-4e93-b977-7f6bc35edf58.title: first-hand (data)
1f532c6d-0ea2-4e93-b977-7f6bc35edf58.description: Information or data which has been directly observed or measured.

be85686a-07b3-4ce7-bdc4-02c119ed2d87.title: fission
be85686a-07b3-4ce7-bdc4-02c119ed2d87.description: A process where the nucleus of an atom splits into two or more smaller nuclei, releasing a large amount of energy in the form of heat and radiation.

45d281f3-81db-4df0-aea5-08625a4ea899.title: frequency
45d281f3-81db-4df0-aea5-08625a4ea899.description: The number of times a light, sound or radio wave passes a fixed point in unit time; the SI unit used to measure frequency is the hertz.

82498627-8d65-4cb1-a56d-5f40e1d29a54.title: gene
82498627-8d65-4cb1-a56d-5f40e1d29a54.description: A gene is a segment of DNA that contains the instructions for building and maintaining an organism. Genes determine the traits and characteristics of living organisms, and are passed from parents to their offspring during reproduction.

b8934cf7-9128-41cc-aedd-6b82f0451502.title: gene-trait relationship
b8934cf7-9128-41cc-aedd-6b82f0451502.description: The relationship between specific genes and the observable characteristics, or traits, they control in an organism.

e38bcc6e-a7fb-4c8d-8c2b-6eb6429b70ca.title: genome
e38bcc6e-a7fb-4c8d-8c2b-6eb6429b70ca.description: The complete set of genetic material, including all of the genes and non-coding sequences, found within an organism's DNA.

cf4ec4c3-0e80-4b56-a478-82aca9405cef.title: geological processes
cf4ec4c3-0e80-4b56-a478-82aca9405cef.description: Natural phenomena that shape and change the Earth's surface and interior over time. These processes include erosion, weathering, volcanic activity, the movement of tectonic plates, and sedimentation.

f6d0dadd-4abe-48a7-8bf1-006041b2dfa7.title: geological timescales
f6d0dadd-4abe-48a7-8bf1-006041b2dfa7.description: The divisions of time used by geologists to describe the history of the Earth. These timescales are typically divided into different units, such as eons, eras, periods, and epochs, which help organise and understand the sequence of events in Earth's history spanning millions to billions of years.

f63bf863-70b2-41f5-a5c9-e0922b8a023e.title: greenhouse effect
f63bf863-70b2-41f5-a5c9-e0922b8a023e.description: Heating effect due to heat rays from the ground being absorbed by some of the gases in the atmosphere.

7f3d8d5d-be0f-41b8-bd9b-a12b168707e3.title: HeLa stem cell line
7f3d8d5d-be0f-41b8-bd9b-a12b168707e3.description: A group of immortal cells derived from cervical cancer cells taken from Henrietta Lacks in 1951 without her consent. These cells have been used extensively in scientific research and have contributed to numerous medical advancements.

42e2b63d-637d-411a-99e0-5bab2b9d15d6.title: infectious (disease)
42e2b63d-637d-411a-99e0-5bab2b9d15d6.description: Able to be passed from one living thing to another.

f0edee39-eaa1-4408-9d43-855acbe44446.title: interactions
f0edee39-eaa1-4408-9d43-855acbe44446.description: Actions or influences between components and within and between systems.

937c5ddd-11a8-4ca3-b4e4-063343d4daf5.title: interdependency
937c5ddd-11a8-4ca3-b4e4-063343d4daf5.description: The condition of being dependent on each other. The state of being mutually dependent or dependent on each other.

1156da67-4f88-477b-9448-64f8e397fe85.title: isolation (geographic)
1156da67-4f88-477b-9448-64f8e397fe85.description: Populations that are separated by a physical barrier, such as a mountain range, river, or ocean so that interbreeding is no longer possible.

474e78a7-4891-4465-a5bb-785e77bcd82d.title: IUPAC
474e78a7-4891-4465-a5bb-785e77bcd82d.description: Acronym for the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, an authority on chemical terminology and nomenclature.

eeea91c7-25cd-4211-9494-5adc3e8a72d5.title: kinetic energy (KE)
eeea91c7-25cd-4211-9494-5adc3e8a72d5.description: The energy that an object possesses by virtue of its motion; the energy an object gains by being in motion.

b45b7ea3-3f33-48bc-95be-fba10aa3e736.title: large dataset
b45b7ea3-3f33-48bc-95be-fba10aa3e736.description: A dataset that must be of a size to be statistically reliable and require computational analysis to reveal patterns, trends and associations.

ed1d3b2c-67a0-43a9-bd00-34660b8f56b9.title: law
ed1d3b2c-67a0-43a9-bd00-34660b8f56b9.description: A statement that describes a relationship or phenomena that does not change under the same conditions.

36c5ddde-5167-4f50-a87d-347fa71f20a1.title: law of conservation of energy
36c5ddde-5167-4f50-a87d-347fa71f20a1.description: States that energy cannot be created or destroyed.

159621c8-ee69-49a9-819e-12e84c1a8b02.title: law of conservation of mass
159621c8-ee69-49a9-819e-12e84c1a8b02.description: States that matter cannot be created or destroyed.

2e7e3c33-40ff-40b4-90dd-94fb89ab76d3.title: megafauna
2e7e3c33-40ff-40b4-90dd-94fb89ab76d3.description: A group of large or giant animals, typically vertebrates, that lived during prehistoric times or still exist today. Some examples of extinct megafauna include the woolly mammoth, sabre-toothed tiger, Irish elk, giant ground sloths and the dodo bird.

97c0ae54-1116-45de-bc1a-d4c3d9b3e266.title: melting point
97c0ae54-1116-45de-bc1a-d4c3d9b3e266.description: The temperature at which a substance transitions from a solid phase to a liquid phase under standard atmospheric pressure.

8d4d0f14-b4c9-4aa8-93f2-d5167e32983c.title: metalloid
8d4d0f14-b4c9-4aa8-93f2-d5167e32983c.description: An element that has properties intermediate between those of metals and nonmetals, such as arsenic, silicon or bismuth.

deeed48a-2fd0-42b7-bdeb-dd7b0669dd52.title: microplastics
deeed48a-2fd0-42b7-bdeb-dd7b0669dd52.description: Small particles of plastic in the environment, generally smaller than 5 millimetres in size.

184255bb-3058-430e-a206-9be8373940ba.title: monogenic
184255bb-3058-430e-a206-9be8373940ba.description: A trait or characteristic that is determined by a single gene.

30ddf257-e85c-4ce8-b1a5-463c3117dd3c.title: noble gas configuration
30ddf257-e85c-4ce8-b1a5-463c3117dd3c.description: When an atom has a complement of electrons in its outer shell, such that it is completely filled and resembles one of the noble gases such as helium, neon or argon.

52842a4e-428b-4042-b0ec-20ac84706479.title: non-infectious (disease)
52842a4e-428b-4042-b0ec-20ac84706479.description: A medical condition that cannot be transmitted from one person to another. These diseases are typically caused by genetic factors, lifestyle choices, environmental factors, or a combination of these factors, e.g. heart disease, cancer, and asthma.

08e65ec4-80bb-4583-b9a8-96c31c227f7f.title: orbit
08e65ec4-80bb-4583-b9a8-96c31c227f7f.description: Moving in a curved path around a body such as the Earth, an atom or the Sun.

ba96d5c1-755a-4aaa-ae9d-4e68b4519d03.title: pandemic
ba96d5c1-755a-4aaa-ae9d-4e68b4519d03.description: A disease prevalent throughout an entire country or continent, or the whole world.

6371cd44-134d-42fb-a22b-1f8196e33f2f.title: pedigree
6371cd44-134d-42fb-a22b-1f8196e33f2f.description: A diagram or chart that shows the relationships between individuals in a family, typically across generations, and may include information about inherited traits or genetic conditions.

01bacf6c-ca3c-4c21-a319-9e24a56bdfc9.title: peer review
01bacf6c-ca3c-4c21-a319-9e24a56bdfc9.description: The process of other experts in a field reading, checking and giving their opinion on someone else’s research.

b7869b6b-d399-4025-a124-5569f7aa7412.title: pH
b7869b6b-d399-4025-a124-5569f7aa7412.description: A measure of the acidity or alkalinity of a solution.

e1bcd367-55dc-44e6-9401-9f0744d6ca66.title: phenomenon
e1bcd367-55dc-44e6-9401-9f0744d6ca66.description: An observable event or process that occurs in the natural world, such as weather patterns, geological events, astronomical events or biological processes.

3d96bb79-798c-4bb8-9d8a-072fa3948c42.title: phenotype
3d96bb79-798c-4bb8-9d8a-072fa3948c42.description: Observable traits produced by genes in a living thing.

2d5ebf64-69f2-4a38-8dc2-9e22569dee4e.title: physical quantities
2d5ebf64-69f2-4a38-8dc2-9e22569dee4e.description: Characteristics that can be seen or measured.

16df90df-ff26-4c66-b334-df230bcde17c.title: pitch
16df90df-ff26-4c66-b334-df230bcde17c.description: The relative highness and lowness of sounds. Can be heard or felt through vibrations.

a8613d2f-88ad-40a4-87be-1615e5c6fcb1.title: polluted
a8613d2f-88ad-40a4-87be-1615e5c6fcb1.description: Contaminated or made impure by harmful substances.

cc658cc9-419b-4b97-bf90-5a8626381c86.title: properties
cc658cc9-419b-4b97-bf90-5a8626381c86.description: Attributes of an object or material normally used to describe attributes common to a group.

b9637cff-7281-4c52-aae4-3f5d47d73463.title: Punnett square
b9637cff-7281-4c52-aae4-3f5d47d73463.description: A graphical representation used to predict the possible genetic outcomes of a cross between 2 individuals.

c1bc00bb-6726-4d9d-b3c7-c1ef5513b616.title: radiation
c1bc00bb-6726-4d9d-b3c7-c1ef5513b616.description:
The emission of energy as electromagnetic waves or as moving subatomic particles.

OR

The energy or particles that are released during radioactive decay.

b0929951-569c-4e56-98bd-27c56440bf1e.title: radioactive
b0929951-569c-4e56-98bd-27c56440bf1e.description: A substance that emits radiation as its nucleus decays.

4595e45a-943a-44ab-82f0-72d083f6583a.title: relate
4595e45a-943a-44ab-82f0-72d083f6583a.description: To establish a connection or association between 2 or more things, often by identifying similarities, connections or shared characteristics.

a42ce152-0882-4edf-8d93-8ebb6c8d4559.title: resistance (electrical)
a42ce152-0882-4edf-8d93-8ebb6c8d4559.description: Opposition to the flow of electrical current. Measured in Ohms.

c75f7333-d451-45d1-86be-f6c470333ab7.title: risk (assessment)
c75f7333-d451-45d1-86be-f6c470333ab7.description: The determination of quantitative or qualitative estimate of risk related to a well-defined situation and a recognised threat (also called hazard).

1f33d2ca-4433-475b-a5fc-6d1dfe73f5ac.title: scattering
1f33d2ca-4433-475b-a5fc-6d1dfe73f5ac.description: When any beam of radiation, electromagnetic or particle, is dispersed or redirected by particles or objects in its path, causing it to spread out in different directions.

b05c7923-f112-4c6d-9786-3b1e99a17fed.title: senses
b05c7923-f112-4c6d-9786-3b1e99a17fed.description: Perceptions that a living organism uses to take in information about its surroundings. The 5 main senses are hearing, sight, touch, taste and smell.

905796a2-7480-4a84-bea4-b8fc57a90b44.title: SI
905796a2-7480-4a84-bea4-b8fc57a90b44.description: The International System of Units (SI) is a system of measurement based on agreed standards units, such as metre, second and gram.

f0b26c47-f20e-4716-a18e-0b0de818222a.title: solubility
f0b26c47-f20e-4716-a18e-0b0de818222a.description: The ability of a solute to dissolve.

7fd64c5e-122d-4b36-99d8-919509c46e9c.title: statistical analysis
7fd64c5e-122d-4b36-99d8-919509c46e9c.description: The collection, organisation and interpretation of data to develop patterns and trends.

ea7ca130-964e-474b-bb4b-586099e1a1a2.title: statistics
ea7ca130-964e-474b-bb4b-586099e1a1a2.description: A collection of numerical facts or other data.

8b8c23f0-9a52-40ca-b28a-be4dff496c04.title: subatomic
8b8c23f0-9a52-40ca-b28a-be4dff496c04.description: Denoting a particle which is smaller than an atom.

74b75bbf-8417-4175-9434-4d158e3f5515.title: supersaturated
74b75bbf-8417-4175-9434-4d158e3f5515.description: A chemical solution which contains more than the maximum amount of solute that can be dissolved in a solution.

75fe13eb-1e41-46f3-abdb-9a3a5ba6ac8c.title: surface tension
75fe13eb-1e41-46f3-abdb-9a3a5ba6ac8c.description: The effect caused by molecular cohesion that makes a liquid seem as though it has a skin on its surface.

c8a63b9b-8105-4798-862a-935fd72d9ae9.title: synthesis
c8a63b9b-8105-4798-862a-935fd72d9ae9.description: A reaction in which a more complex compound is produced from simpler compounds (also called ‘combination reaction’).

fcfd23ff-66a5-41e1-a9b0-da4eb222453a.title: system
fcfd23ff-66a5-41e1-a9b0-da4eb222453a.description: A set of components in the natural and made environments that interact. An understanding of natural complex systems requires the integration and application of concepts from more than one science discipline.

705871b7-b386-421a-b271-8ddff504c435.title: systematic observations
705871b7-b386-421a-b271-8ddff504c435.description: Following a valid scientific method to carry out observations.

32d3e4ee-4dfd-4a64-bba4-95fb9e25e4cd.title: theory
32d3e4ee-4dfd-4a64-bba4-95fb9e25e4cd.description: A formal explanation, based on evidence and reviewed by the scientific community. Predictions can be tested by comparing actual observations with the theory.

77f5d329-d203-4a9a-97c7-48d3d313fc1c.title: thermal
77f5d329-d203-4a9a-97c7-48d3d313fc1c.description: Properties or phenomena associated with heat, temperature, or the transfer of energy due to temperature differences.

6647a97d-0540-420c-9396-5400a7548208.title: transdisciplinary
6647a97d-0540-420c-9396-5400a7548208.description: The integration of different disciplines with science.

a52a12fe-0615-4d17-bfa5-3e327abcf082.title: trophic level
a52a12fe-0615-4d17-bfa5-3e327abcf082.description: The hierarchical position of organisms in a food chain or food web based on their feeding relationships and energy transfer.

1f1c72a3-f103-4ee8-97e5-0bd9c30a5c99.title: univariate
1f1c72a3-f103-4ee8-97e5-0bd9c30a5c99.description: An analysis, study, or dataset that involves only one variable.

4ea39dd8-d3f6-4b70-b848-fb2f4621bb96.title: vaccination
4ea39dd8-d3f6-4b70-b848-fb2f4621bb96.description: The process of administering a vaccine with the aim of stimulating the immune system to develop immunity against a specific infectious disease, resulting in protection from future infections.

19e65c36-9e55-4f32-9528-be5a43d97e4b.title: valency
19e65c36-9e55-4f32-9528-be5a43d97e4b.description: The number of chemical bonds that an atom can make with a univalent atom such as hydrogen.

f1350174-5caf-43a6-ad55-8ab045a7c8b4.title: vector analysis
f1350174-5caf-43a6-ad55-8ab045a7c8b4.description: The analysis of a quantity which possesses both magnitude and direction. Two such quantities acting on a point may be represented by the 2 sides of a parallelogram, so that their resultant (or sum of vectors) is represented in magnitude and direction by the diagonal of the parallelogram.

8878952c-7d9c-4630-aceb-ba59d7c81f2a.title: voltage
8878952c-7d9c-4630-aceb-ba59d7c81f2a.description: A measure of the electrical potential difference between 2 points. The SI unit for voltage is the volt (equivalent to joule/coulomb).

1af4e6a5-033a-4393-9276-b5933fde1759.title: work health and safety (WHS)
1af4e6a5-033a-4393-9276-b5933fde1759.description: The requirements include safe practices in the laboratory and in the field.

a0f3d0fe-074f-4739-8f9b-17f91e57024b.title: xylem
a0f3d0fe-074f-4739-8f9b-17f91e57024b.description: A type of plant tissue responsible for transporting water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.

5596cf4f-56be-4c09-82e5-64c8dafd5ea8.title: binary code
5596cf4f-56be-4c09-82e5-64c8dafd5ea8.description: Binary digit (or bits) in digital technologies which describes a numbering scheme with either 0 or 1.

971838c3-31ae-4d36-a8be-59e1f92ee5b1.title: black hole
971838c3-31ae-4d36-a8be-59e1f92ee5b1.description: A region in space of such immense gravity that nothing – not even light – can escape from it.

a14edf7f-883e-4f46-b042-7cc7715bcf94.title: convection
a14edf7f-883e-4f46-b042-7cc7715bcf94.description: Heat energy transferred by its movement through liquids or gases.

60810604-d580-449d-aff3-6ade5a8701de.title: exoplanet
60810604-d580-449d-aff3-6ade5a8701de.description: A planet found outside our solar system.

64c45afd-c128-4bc5-bd62-1c87023450e2.title: food chain
64c45afd-c128-4bc5-bd62-1c87023450e2.description: A sequence of organisms that begins with a producer and ends with a consumer that shows the flow of energy and matter.

8f288d67-7eb8-4b54-a932-3f45bff453ce.title: galaxy
8f288d67-7eb8-4b54-a932-3f45bff453ce.description: A collection of gases, dust, and billions of stars and their solar systems, all held together by gravity.

b9e3519e-accb-4837-adc5-872f2217e8fb.title: insulator
b9e3519e-accb-4837-adc5-872f2217e8fb.description: A material which inhibits the transfer of heat, sound or electrical energy.

6501ee9f-b437-4b65-925d-e3f045326308.title: lunar cycle
6501ee9f-b437-4b65-925d-e3f045326308.description: The pattern of changes seen in the appearance of the Moon's shape over time.

8e611a14-b8a6-4be7-aed2-5942a7c11d18.title: nebula/nebulae
8e611a14-b8a6-4be7-aed2-5942a7c11d18.description: A giant cloud of dust and gas in space.

8bc4e9be-fe5c-4499-b86b-364d585414f2.title: opaque
8bc4e9be-fe5c-4499-b86b-364d585414f2.description: The quality of a material which means that light does not pass through it.

befb6961-b34e-4c02-9a17-efdc0a2cda5b.title: radiation
befb6961-b34e-4c02-9a17-efdc0a2cda5b.description: Transfer of energy between objects that are not in contact with each other.

170e627a-c243-418d-9801-95bbf6358b96.title: translucent
170e627a-c243-418d-9801-95bbf6358b96.description: Allowing some light to travel through, but not clear.

7e7c1f74-2565-467d-b924-6533ed71fb96.title: transparent
7e7c1f74-2565-467d-b924-6533ed71fb96.description: Allowing all light to travel through so objects behind can be clearly seen.

b1116918-20a5-4222-b925-4cb4b3d2152d.title: application programming interface (API)
b1116918-20a5-4222-b925-4cb4b3d2152d.description: An interface that allows an application or website to plug into another program or website.

3a899869-67da-47d4-8b69-362d0ab2ccaf.title: black box testing
3a899869-67da-47d4-8b69-362d0ab2ccaf.description: A testing technique where there is no knowledge of the internal workings of an application. A user will provide inputs and observe the outputs in order to determine functionality of the program.

0ef99a44-7f95-44c0-99fc-c2f06c70ae6f.title: grey box testing
0ef99a44-7f95-44c0-99fc-c2f06c70ae6f.description:
A testing technique where there is a partial knowledge of the internal workings of an application. Its purpose is to search for defects related to improper code structure or the improper use of functions. This technique gives the ability to test both the code and the presentation layer of an application.

Note: grey box testing and gray box testing mean the same.

7a63af0d-1e1c-45ba-ac78-2d2f7d12dddd.title: procedural programming
7a63af0d-1e1c-45ba-ac78-2d2f7d12dddd.description: A method of programming where the program is divided into functions. A program consists of data and procedures (modules) that operate on the data. Data and procedures are treated as separate entities.

1ae8f9ba-43ba-42f1-9866-eb9a6fee6a4c.title: pseudocode
1ae8f9ba-43ba-42f1-9866-eb9a6fee6a4c.description: A form of algorithm description that uses English-like statements with defined rules of structure and keywords.

046ed056-8ee9-4e88-84d7-fafb947d1fdc.title: refinement charts
046ed056-8ee9-4e88-84d7-fafb947d1fdc.description: A diagrammatic model that breaks down the steps of an outline solution into smaller and smaller steps.

78c7b053-6f81-4d48-ab4c-ec23679d75cb.title: scripting language
78c7b053-6f81-4d48-ab4c-ec23679d75cb.description: A programming language designed for integrating and communicating with other programming languages.

93524b66-c5db-4d8d-a1f9-1c173e2635f6.title: W3C
93524b66-c5db-4d8d-a1f9-1c173e2635f6.description: The World Wide Web Consortium is the international standards organisation for the world wide web. All of the standards used for web development are defined by this organisation.

57009ccd-f577-4762-9ec4-c02b82355d3c.title: white box testing
57009ccd-f577-4762-9ec4-c02b82355d3c.description: A testing technique used to examine the internal workings of an application including the design, code and inner workings of software. This technique gives the ability to verify the flow of inputs and outputs through the application.

b05b4fbc-4aa1-425f-a21c-0f8fed38a432.title: technological literacy
b05b4fbc-4aa1-425f-a21c-0f8fed38a432.description: The ability to select, use, manage, create and evaluate technology for specific purposes. This includes using safe practices and considering ethical implications.

9c3ce582-7747-4f43-80a1-6fde2eea5fb2.title: notions
9c3ce582-7747-4f43-80a1-6fde2eea5fb2.description: The small objects or accessories, including items that are sewn or otherwise attached to a textiles article, such as buttons, ribbon, zippers, hooks and eyes.

ac97d171-a356-4629-952a-7f916e75bb4f.title: physical properties
ac97d171-a356-4629-952a-7f916e75bb4f.description: The tangible characteristics of an artwork, such as texture, shape, size and material, which contribute to its overall meaning and impact.

a79292ee-21f3-4343-b732-5c44b5acc17a.title: symbolic
a79292ee-21f3-4343-b732-5c44b5acc17a.description: Pertaining to the use of symbols in artworks to represent ideas, beliefs or concepts. Communicates deeper meanings to audiences through material, physical and visual elements.

4415cc8b-bf58-427f-b5be-168eeb59a188.title: design form
4415cc8b-bf58-427f-b5be-168eeb59a188.description: A category of artistic representation in Visual and Motion Design distinguished by specific techniques and mediums.

11c8f196-3776-468d-b459-fcd60072e42d.title: design practice
11c8f196-3776-468d-b459-fcd60072e42d.description: The application of skills and knowledge to make, represent, respond to and interpret design artworks.

a5b6487d-4a08-4216-b961-5dcca54b2faf.title: design practitioner
a5b6487d-4a08-4216-b961-5dcca54b2faf.description: Individuals or groups such as designers, agencies, curators, critics and historians, who engage in the designing, making, curation, critique and/or historical explanation of design artworks.

e9db194a-5d38-4d09-92b4-b74031fd53b8.title: art form
e9db194a-5d38-4d09-92b4-b74031fd53b8.description: A category of artistic representation in Visual Arts distinguished by specific techniques and mediums, which encompasses 2D, 3D and 4D creations.

f7d95776-2d67-4cfb-b85f-830a1db4ebcb.title: art movement
f7d95776-2d67-4cfb-b85f-830a1db4ebcb.description: A group of artists with a shared style or philosophy, typically emerged during a specific time period.

c43b9ba1-62f0-4746-8902-2f4563796bdb.title: art period
c43b9ba1-62f0-4746-8902-2f4563796bdb.description: A span of time characterised by distinctive styles, techniques and conventions in Visual Arts, often aligned with broader historical and cultural contexts.

8f8456ba-1074-400f-84d3-9dfd8610571e.title: artist
8f8456ba-1074-400f-84d3-9dfd8610571e.description: A person that makes artworks individually, as a group, at a school, as part of a movement or by enlisting others to produce their artwork.

6b90dda8-8d81-48bf-ab33-86af6491ee92.title: artworld
6b90dda8-8d81-48bf-ab33-86af6491ee92.description: The community and system that encompasses artists, artworks, audiences, galleries, museums, collectors, and the practices and theories of producing, promoting and distributing art.

64aa7244-3fd1-4ba5-9757-4549b64e46a0.title: Artworld concepts
64aa7244-3fd1-4ba5-9757-4549b64e46a0.description: A framework for understanding the functions and roles in the artworld, through the interrelated concepts of artist, artwork, world and audience.

634aa9ec-e83b-4ef6-bc38-3896fa0dda1c.title: artworld practitioner
634aa9ec-e83b-4ef6-bc38-3896fa0dda1c.description: Individuals, such as artists, curators, critics and historians, who engage in the making, curation, critique and/or historical explanations of artworks.

8b8a0f3e-1b1b-43ae-b539-ae309a1ce513.title: body of work
8b8a0f3e-1b1b-43ae-b539-ae309a1ce513.description: A collection of artworks produced by an artist over time, which reflects their evolving artistic practice.

c2412e13-2c3b-4298-8998-d97f46ffe0f1.title: contemporary viewpoint
c2412e13-2c3b-4298-8998-d97f46ffe0f1.description: A creative and interpretative tool that guides students in art making or interpreting artworks, and which reflects current and emerging art theories and innovative practices.

d94b9470-6c79-4e25-aabb-e1e0d8fc4e57.title: conventions
d94b9470-6c79-4e25-aabb-e1e0d8fc4e57.description: Established rule, method or practice in the artworld that guides the making, presentation and interpretation of artworks.

17b9184d-c81d-4671-b8eb-c0e2674b56e2.title: cultural viewpoint
17b9184d-c81d-4671-b8eb-c0e2674b56e2.description: A creative and interpretative tool that guides students when art making or interpreting artworks that reflect social ideologies, beliefs, values, conditions and shared understandings in specific communities or societies.

438d49a9-38b2-489b-a5e3-6e8148783607.title: curatorial
438d49a9-38b2-489b-a5e3-6e8148783607.description: A way to select, organise and present material and artworks for exhibition or informal sharing.

9943c1e2-6425-4754-bfb7-573dc0c3fa34.title: decode
9943c1e2-6425-4754-bfb7-573dc0c3fa34.description: The process of interpreting and understanding the meanings conveyed by structured systems of conventions, signs and symbols in artworks.

5697473d-9b5f-432e-acde-a2a2a0679200.title: practice
5697473d-9b5f-432e-acde-a2a2a0679200.description: The application of skills and knowledge to make, represent, respond to and interpret artworks.

931436e2-6c21-450b-867d-729d549552ce.title: representation
931436e2-6c21-450b-867d-729d549552ce.description: The depiction or portrayal of subjects, ideas and themes in artworks, using various techniques and materials to convey meaning and context to audiences.

a041a5c2-84b9-4036-890e-fca24a9188e9.title: signs
a041a5c2-84b9-4036-890e-fca24a9188e9.description: A visual or multimodal element in an artwork that directly represents or points to a specific meaning or idea, often understood immediately and literally, or through cultural and contextual knowledge.

97fd92b5-0d93-41ee-bb86-1b9b910389f1.title: structural viewpoint
97fd92b5-0d93-41ee-bb86-1b9b910389f1.description: A creative and interpretative tool that guides students when art making or interpreting artworks as forms of visual and multimodal language.

3967ff47-0a30-4eca-8a19-d2c16653758b.title: stylistic conventions
3967ff47-0a30-4eca-8a19-d2c16653758b.description: Established rules, methods and techniques used in the artworld that create a recognisable style.

bc94e36a-bb52-4adc-b0a8-e273997047c0.title: subjective viewpoint
bc94e36a-bb52-4adc-b0a8-e273997047c0.description: A creative and interpretative tool that guides students when art making or interpreting artworks as expressions of deeply personal and emotive perspectives, experiences and associations.

1e6cf9c7-25a6-4c99-aaac-7abbafcff03e.title: viewpoints
1e6cf9c7-25a6-4c99-aaac-7abbafcff03e.description: Represents the different perspectives, values and beliefs about visual arts. Viewpoints, including Structural, Subjective, Cultural and Contemporary, function as means for generating alternative interpretations of the artworld.

4e30157c-b0e1-4849-ab94-d042bdd4f3d0.title: employment contract
4e30157c-b0e1-4849-ab94-d042bdd4f3d0.description: An agreement between an employer and employee that sets out the terms and conditions of employment.

75aa7ca5-4d33-4abd-9a0f-e51c11de7825.title: entrepreneurial behaviours
75aa7ca5-4d33-4abd-9a0f-e51c11de7825.description: Behaviours that are applicable in a range of contexts and demonstrate confidence, initiative, innovation and creativity, global competency, empathy, a willingness to take risks and the ability to act on identified opportunities.

3c5c5b7a-3a2d-4210-a159-14bb9512ffd3.title: entrepreneurial mindset
3c5c5b7a-3a2d-4210-a159-14bb9512ffd3.description: A set of attributes that orient individuals and organisations toward recognising opportunities and approaching challenges with an innovative and solution-focused perspective.

340ac789-8d2a-487d-ad99-7638309da32a.title: job portfolio
340ac789-8d2a-487d-ad99-7638309da32a.description: A collection of materials presented to potential employers that serves as evidence of a person's knowledge, skills and work experience.

2949508a-59a4-437c-af33-602e95777e39.title: lifelong learning
2949508a-59a4-437c-af33-602e95777e39.description: Intentional and continuous learning throughout a person's life, aimed at enhancing knowledge, skills and abilities through education, training, professional development and life experience.

3d0b7c9b-789f-4b0b-b5f5-33ac8af78d61.title: open employment
3d0b7c9b-789f-4b0b-b5f5-33ac8af78d61.description: When people with and without disability work together in the same workplace.

7e6c09b5-b408-4d3b-9b64-5d989c8b993f.title: social capital
7e6c09b5-b408-4d3b-9b64-5d989c8b993f.description: Networks of relationships among people in a society that enable cooperation, trust and mutual support to help individuals and groups pursue their goals.

bd4161ec-826f-4265-a73c-1348aa4427b4.title: superannuation guarantee
bd4161ec-826f-4265-a73c-1348aa4427b4.description: A mandatory system in which employers are legally required to contribute a percentage of an employee’s gross salary or wages into a superannuation fund.

b47f748d-b286-4fc4-a4b0-e14ceb7da692.title: technical skills
b47f748d-b286-4fc4-a4b0-e14ceb7da692.description: Skills gained through education, training and/or experience that are directly linked to a specific job and required to perform specialised tasks.

10c421f2-a130-4681-b584-88e940edc4e1.title: transferable skills
10c421f2-a130-4681-b584-88e940edc4e1.description: Skills that are generic in nature, rather than job specific, and that can be applied across a variety of work roles, for example communication, teamwork and problem-solving.

22903b1a-c160-4e4a-a32e-78d72b44c147.title: workplace code of conduct
22903b1a-c160-4e4a-a32e-78d72b44c147.description: A set of guidelines and principles that outline the expected behaviours, responsibilities and ethical standards in an organisation.
